guide.title: About 3G2 files
guide.markdown:
### What is a 3G2 file?

3G2 is a video container defined by 3GPP2, the standards group behind CDMA mobile networks, for clips shot and sent on phones. It uses the ISO media file format family as its foundation, and RFC 4393 registered its media types in March 2006. The preferred extension is .3g2, and .3gpp2 is also recognized.

A 3G2 can carry sound, moving pictures and timed text. The type video/3gpp2 is valid even when the file holds only audio, while audio/3gpp2 is reserved for files with nothing visual, and timed text counts as visual content. So a 3G2 that plays without a picture is not always broken.

You meet these files on older CDMA phones and in their MMS video. The format keeps files small, and its video is H.264 or MPEG-4. Recognizing the container does not guarantee that a player has a decoder for the video or sound inside it, which is the usual reason a 3G2 opens on one device and not on another.

### Programs that open 3G2 files

VLC media player and QuickTime Player both open 3G2 clips. These programs also handle the format:

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FFmpeg: registers .3g2 with its QuickTime and ISO base media demuxer.
- ffplay: the FFmpeg player, which uses the FFmpeg demuxers and decoders.

**Windows and Mac**

- Adobe After Effects: recognizes .3g2 as an import extension.

### 3G2 and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .3g2 or .3gpp2 with video/3gpp2, where audio/3gpp2 is kept for files with nothing visual; .mp4 for MPEG-4 Part 14.
- **Standards**: 3G2 comes from 3GPP2 and is based on the MPEG-4 container. MP4 is defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14.
- **Video codecs**: a 3G2 holds H.264 or MPEG-4 video. MP4 takes H.264, H.265 and AV1.
- **Extras**: MP4 can carry subtitles and chapters.
- **Reach**: MP4 plays on nearly every device. The older 3G2 is kept small and was made for phones.

What this page does is decode the clip and write a new MP4. The picture is re-encoded by x264 using CRF 32 and its ultrafast preset, while the soundtrack is re-encoded as 96 kbps AAC. An oversized picture is scaled down to 1920 pixels along its longer edge, and playback speed tops out at 30 frames per second. Your 3G2 itself is never changed; you download a new file next to it.

Conversion happens in your browser, one clip at a time, with no file-size cap from the page. Pick several files and they queue, each saved under its own name with the .mp4 ending. No stream-selection options are passed, which leaves FFmpeg's defaults to pick the streams that reach the MP4. An audio-only 3G2 gives an MP4 with sound and no picture.

### Other ways to convert 3G2 to MP4

- **FFmpeg with a re-encode:** on Windows, Mac or Linux, run `ffmpeg -i handset.3g2 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac handset-share.mp4`. It encodes video with libx264 and audio with aac, and the result is lossy.
- **FFmpeg, copy the streams:** run `ffmpeg -i archive-phone.3g2 -c copy archive-phone.mp4`. Nothing is re-encoded, but it works only when MP4 accepts the streams inside.
- **Prism (Windows):** click Add File(s), set Output Format to MP4, check Encoder Options, pick a folder under Save to Folder and click Convert. NCH lists 3G2 input for Windows only.

### Problems with 3G2 files

- **No picture**: a video/3gpp2 file may be audio only, so a missing picture is not always a playback failure.
- **Won't play on a phone or in an editor**: the app in question may not have a decoder for the picture or sound stored in the file. Converting here writes new H.264 and AAC streams, provided FFmpeg can decode the original.
- **Corrupt after a transfer**: a text-style transfer that changes line endings or strips high bits can corrupt this binary format.
- **A damaged or cut-short clip**: a clip like this usually still converts, giving a shorter MP4, so compare the running time with the original.
- **A soft or blocky result**: encoding uses CRF 32 with the ultrafast preset and offers no quality control, so the MP4 can look worse than the 3G2.
- **An odd .3gpp2 ending**: it is the second registered extension for the same format. Rename it to .3g2 if a program only looks for that one.

guide.title: About 3GP and MOV
guide.markdown:
### What is a 3GP file?

The 3GP format comes from 3GPP, a specialization of ISO's media file layout, for messaging, downloads and packet-switched streaming on phones. A clip can combine video, speech, other sound and timed text. Video may be H.263, MPEG-4 Visual, AVC or HEVC, and sound may be an AMR variant or AAC. The extension doesn't tell you which a given clip uses, and a conforming parser may ignore boxes or codecs outside the spec. The media types are video/3gpp, and audio/3gpp for sound only.

A MOV is QuickTime's own container. It keeps video, audio, text and timecode in separate tracks and can hold many codecs, ProRes among them. Changing the ending doesn't transcode anything or install a missing decoder, which is why a real conversion is the safer route when an editor refuses the clip.

### Programs that open 3GP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC lists 3GP among its inputs, and FFmpeg reads 3GP containers. For the finished MOV, mpv plays it on the desktop.

### 3GP and MOV compared

- **Purpose**: 3GP was built for small phone clips. MOV is a general container used in editing.
- **Lineage**: 3GP is a simplified version of the MP4 container. MOV, the QuickTime container, is what MPEG-4's file format grew from.
- **Codecs**: a 3GP can carry H.263 and AMR audio. This converter writes H.264 and AAC.
- **Size**: the output keeps the frame size up to 1920 pixels and the frame rate up to 30 fps.

### Other ways to convert 3GP to MOV

- **FFmpeg transcode:** run `ffmpeg -i handset.3gp -c:v libx264 -c:a aac editable.mov` for new H.264 and AAC streams.
- **FFmpeg remux:** run `ffmpeg -i handset.3gp -c copy rewrapped.mov` to rewrap the streams without re-encoding. It works only if the original codecs fit MOV and your editor.

### Problems with 3GP files

- **No video in the file**: a 3GP may be sound only, and there is nothing to recover.
- **The editor rejects the MOV**: QuickTime containers can use codecs your editor lacks. Convert it, so the streams are H.264 and AAC.
- **Renamed file won't open**: the old codecs are still inside. Convert instead of renaming.
- **A MOV that stopped mid-write**: an ordinary MOV can be left unusable by a write that was cut short.

guide.title: About 3GP and MP3
guide.markdown:
### What is a 3GP file?

The 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), which writes the standards for mobile networks, defined 3GP as a container. MP4 grows from the same ISO base media file format; 3GP is a slimmed-down branch of it that keeps files small. Mobile messaging, downloads and packet-switched streaming are the services it was written for.

Inside one 3GP you may find video, speech, other sound and timed text. For the picture the specification registers H.263, MPEG-4 Visual, AVC and HEVC, and for the sound AMR variants and AAC. Brands in a file-type box tell a reader which profile a file follows, and the media type is video/3gpp when pictures are present or audio/3gpp when only sound is. You will mostly meet 3GP as video from older mobile phones and as MMS video.

Nothing in the extension tells you which permitted codec a recording uses. A parser that follows the specification may also skip boxes or codecs it does not define, so two files ending in .3gp can behave differently in one player.

### Programs that open 3GP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - VLC media player lists 3GP among the input formats it opens.
  - FFmpeg reads 3GP containers.

A 3GP made of sound alone has no picture to recover, and the format expressly allows such files.

### 3GP and MP3 compared

- **Names and types**: .3gp (video/3gpp, or audio/3gpp for sound only) becomes .mp3.
- **Contents**: a 3GP can combine video, speech, sound and timed text, whereas an MP3 holds audio alone.
- **Compression**: sound in a 3GP is coded as an AMR variant or AAC. MP3 uses lossy audio coding, with constant or variable bitrate.
- **Metadata**: tags in an MP3 are stored as ID3 data.
- **Standard**: the MPEG group standardized MP3 as ISO/IEC 11172-3.
- **Support**: MP3 plays on nearly every device, including in any web browser.

The job is done by FFmpeg built for WebAssembly, running as a background worker in your tab, so the clip stays on your device. The command skips the video and hands the sound to LAME with a request for 192 kbps. Below 32 kHz sampling that request cannot be met: the ceiling is 160 kbps at 16 to 24 kHz and just 64 kbps at 8 to 12 kHz. Because the page leaves the sample rate alone, a narrowband recording produces a low-bitrate MP3. Channel count and stream choice are not set either, so FFmpeg's defaults apply, and with several tracks in a file the page does not tell you which one is taken.

Select as many 3GP files as you like. They are handled in sequence, and each MP3 arrives as its own download, with the original name plus .mp3. No ZIP is made, and the 3GP itself is left as it was. When a file is damaged or cut short, FFmpeg reports the error but still writes what it managed to read, so the MP3 is usually just shorter. If the 3GP has no audio track, the attempt ends in an FFmpeg exit-code error on the page.

Pulling out the sound cannot be undone in the MP3. It holds the audio and nothing else, so the picture stays behind in the 3GP. The encode is one more lossy step and cannot restore detail the original never held. The gain is a file that plays almost anywhere and is simple to share. For listening, that is a fair trade; for a recording you care about, keep the 3GP.

### Other ways to convert 3GP to MP3

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i input.3gp -vn -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k output.mp3` mirrors what this page runs. FFmpeg's documentation lists -vn as the switch that disables video, -c:a as the audio codec option and -b:a as the audio bitrate option; swap 192k for another number to choose your own rate. The 3GP needs an audio stream that FFmpeg can decode.

### Problems with 3GP files

- **The conversion fails**: the likely cause is a 3GP with no audio track, which leaves nothing to extract. Play it in VLC first to check.
- **The extension does not reveal the codec**: a .3gp may hold AMR or AAC sound. If a tool refuses the file, a conforming parser is allowed to ignore codecs outside the specification.
- **A player shows no video**: an audio-only 3GP has no video track, which the format permits.
- **You also want the picture**: convert to MP4 instead, which keeps the video.
- **The MP3 is shorter than the clip**: with a cut-short file, only the part FFmpeg could read is converted.
- **The MP3 bitrate is under 192 kbps**: the recording's sample rate causes that, as described earlier, and nothing has gone wrong.

guide.title: About 3GP and MP4
guide.markdown:
### What is a 3GP file?

3GP is a container format defined by the 3rd Generation Partnership Project for video on mobile phones. It specializes the ISO base media file format, the same family MP4 belongs to, and it is a simplified version of the MP4 container that keeps files small. It serves mobile messaging, downloads and packet-switched streaming, and a single presentation may mix video, speech, other audio and timed text.

The standard registers several video codecs, including H.263, MPEG-4 Visual, AVC and HEVC. For sound it registers AMR variants and AAC. A file extension does not identify which of the permitted codecs a 3GP recording contains, which is why two .3gp files can behave very differently. You meet 3GP files from older mobile phones and in MMS video. A conforming file includes a file-type box whose brands identify its profile.

### Programs that open 3GP files

- **Linux, Mac and Windows:** FFmpeg reads 3GP containers, and VLC media player accepts 3GP input.
- **Windows:** Windows Media Player opens 3GP.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player opens 3GP.

The codecs inside the file decide what a player can do with it.

### 3GP and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .3gp with video/3gpp for visual content and audio/3gpp for purely audio content; .mp4 with video/mp4 and audio/mp4.
- **Container family**: both descend from the ISO base media file format, itself an outgrowth of Apple's QuickTime format. MP4 is ISO/IEC 14496-14, first published in 2003.
- **Video codecs**: 3GP registers the four listed above. MP4 commonly holds H.264 (AVC), and can also carry H.265, AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus.
- **Audio**: 3GP registers AMR variants and AAC. MP4 commonly carries AAC.
- **Extras**: MP4 can hold subtitles and chapters. Its boxes nest inside one another, a structure QuickTime knows as atoms.
- **Used for**: 3GP serves video on older mobile phones and MMS video. MP4 is used for online video and streaming, for phone and camera recordings, and for passing video around.
- **Files**: video MP4 files use .mp4 or .m4v, and audio-only MPEG-4 files often use .m4a.
- **Reach**: every major browser plays MP4, and it plays on nearly every device. Android 5.0 added HEVC playback inside MP4 files.

Your browser runs FFmpeg as WebAssembly to decode the 3GP and encode the result. Video becomes H.264 with libx264 at CRF 32, using the ultrafast preset, and audio becomes AAC at 96 kbps. This page always re-encodes and never copies the streams, and no stream mapping is passed, which leaves FFmpeg's defaults to choose the streams. Frame size carries over unless the long side exceeds 1920 pixels, and frame rate carries over unless it exceeds 30 fps. Interlaced frames, if any, are deinterlaced first. The MP4 is written with the index at the front (faststart).

Several 3GP files can be chosen at once. They are processed in sequence, and every result downloads separately, with no ZIP, under your file's name and the .mp4 ending. Your original 3GP is not changed.

### Other ways to convert 3GP to MP4

- **FFmpeg (command line):** enter `ffmpeg -i phone.3gp -c:v libx264 -c:a aac phone.mp4`. FFmpeg's mov demuxer lists the 3gp extension, and both streams are re-encoded.
- **VLC (Windows, Mac, Linux):** choose Media > Convert/Save, click Add and pick the 3GP, type the destination file name, choose a conversion profile from the Profile drop-down and click Start. VLC lists 3GP among its input formats.

### Problems with 3GP files

- **The file won't open on a modern device**: the .3gp ending doesn't show which codecs are inside, so the device may lack one of them. Converting writes H.264 video and AAC sound.

- **There is sound but no picture**: an audio-only 3GP has no video track to recover, and the format explicitly permits pure sound.
- **The MP4 is larger than the 3GP**: the page encodes the MP4 to a fixed quality (CRF 32) instead of a target size, so the size can go either way.

guide.title: AAC files and FLAC output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AAC file?

Advanced Audio Coding, or AAC, is a lossy, perceptual audio coding family standardized through MPEG. It is specified in MPEG-2 Part 7 and placed in MPEG-4 Part 3. AAC can sit in MP4, QuickTime or other wrappers, and a standalone .aac file commonly carries ADTS framing. The media type audio/aac covers ADTS and LATM/LOAS transport. LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2 are among its profiles, and it serves streaming and delivery to listeners.

### Programs that open AAC files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC media player reads raw AAC files and decodes MPEG-4 AAC.
- FFmpeg decodes AAC and also has its own AAC encoder.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Audition imports AAC, including HE-AAC.

### AAC and FLAC compared

FLAC squeezes integer PCM audio and throws no samples away. It supports one through eight channels, carries metadata such as seek points, pictures and Vorbis comments, and uses the audio/flac media type. RFC 9639 standardized its description in December 2024. FLAC is an open, royalty-free codec developed by Xiph.Org, and people use it for music archiving, audiophile listening and lossless backups of CDs.

This page decodes the AAC and writes FLAC with FFmpeg in your browser, without a picture stream. The FLAC is lossless only from the point of decoding. The page has no settings, and a batch yields one FLAC per AAC.

### Other ways to convert AAC to FLAC

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i speech.aac -vn -c:a flac speech-decoded.flac`. With `-vn` no video stream is written, and `-c:a flac` picks the FLAC encoder.
- **VLC:** choose Media > Convert/Save, add the AAC, click Convert, pick the Audio - FLAC profile, set a .flac destination and click Start.

### Problems with AAC files

- **The sound is not as good as hoped**: a lossy AAC already lost detail, and changing it to FLAC cannot recreate the samples that were removed.
- **A decoder rejects it**: an MPEG-2 AAC decoder may not follow the MPEG-4 variants.
- **Renaming did nothing**: giving the file an .m4a name leaves the ADTS framing as it was; no MP4 wrapper appears.
- **The decoded file is much larger**: once decoded, the audio can need far more space than the compressed original did.

guide.title: About AAC files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AAC file?

AAC (Advanced Audio Coding) belongs to the MPEG family of perceptual audio codecs. MPEG-2 defines it in Part 7 and MPEG-4 in Part 3, under the ISO/IEC numbers 13818-7 and 14496-3. The profiles you will meet are LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2. It carries streaming audio and music downloads, the sound in MP4 videos and audio on mobile devices. It was designed as MP3's successor and generally sounds better at the same bitrate.

AAC names the coding alone, which is why it travels in different wrappers. Inside MP4 or QuickTime it becomes an .m4a-style file, while a standalone .aac file commonly uses ADTS framing. The registered media type audio/aac spans ADTS and LATM/LOAS transport. Two files with the .aac name can therefore behave differently in different players.

### Programs that open AAC files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FFmpeg: includes AAC decoding and an internal AAC encoder. It is a command-line tool, and it is also the engine this page runs.
- VLC media player: accepts raw AAC input and decodes MPEG-4 AAC audio. It is free and plays the file without converting it first.

**Windows and Mac**

- Adobe Audition: imports AAC, including HE-AAC. It is a paid editor, useful when you want to trim or clean the recording before exporting.

**Web**

- Firefox and Chrome play AAC in the browser, though availability can depend on system codecs.

### AAC and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .aac with audio/aac; .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **Origin**: MP3 (MPEG-1 Audio Layer III) became ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993, and ISO/IEC 13818-3 extended it in 1995. Fraunhofer IIS and fellow MPEG audio group members started development in the late 1980s.
- **Compression**: both formats are lossy and lean on a model of hearing to drop sound you are unlikely to miss. An MP3 at 128 kbit/s is about an eleventh of the size of the CD audio behind it.
- **Bitrates**: the sample rate is 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz and the bitrate runs from 32 up to 320 kbps.
- **Metadata**: MP3 keeps titles and other tags in ID3 blocks inside the file.
- **Patents**: licensing for MP3 patents ended on 23 April 2017.
- **Container**: AAC is only the coding, so it can sit in an MP4 or QuickTime wrapper or stand alone with ADTS framing. MP3 is its own stream format, with ID3 blocks for tags.
- **Support**: every major browser plays MP3. For AAC, Firefox availability can depend on system codecs, so an AAC file that plays on one computer may stay silent on another.
- **Efficiency**: AAC generally sounds better than MP3 at the same bitrate.

In this converter, FFmpeg runs in your browser, decodes the AAC, then LAME encodes an MP3, asking for 192 kbit/s. Below 32 kHz, MP3 can't reach 192 kbit/s, so LAME writes a lower rate. The MP3 is a second lossy generation of the sound. The page does not pick audio tracks, trim or change volume. Each AAC is converted by itself in turn, and the MP3 download takes the AAC's name; the original stays as it was. The page sets no size limit, so a long recording only takes longer.

### Other ways to convert AAC to MP3

- **FFmpeg in a terminal:** enter `ffmpeg -i lecture.aac -codec:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k lecture.mp3`. FFmpeg does the AAC decoding. The -codec:a option picks the audio encoder, and -b:a sets its bitrate.

### Problems with AAC files

- **One .aac opens and another doesn't**: the audio/aac media type covers both ADTS and LATM/LOAS transport, so two files with the same name can need different support from the player.
- **A player won't open it**: an MPEG-2 AAC decoder can fail on MPEG-4 variants. Try VLC, or convert the file to MP3.
- **Renaming to .m4a doesn't help**: changing .aac to .m4a does not replace ADTS framing with an MP4 wrapper. The file still holds the same data.
- **The decoded copy is huge**: AAC stores compressed audio, so decoding it to an uncompressed form, as an editor does while you work, takes far more space.
- **Zipping saves almost nothing**: ZIP compression usually offers little extra reduction for AAC streams, because the audio is already compressed.

guide.title: About AAC files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AAC file?

AAC is a lossy audio codec developed by MPEG as MP3's successor; the name stands for Advanced Audio Coding. It is defined in MPEG-2 Part 7 and again in MPEG-4 Part 3. For a given bitrate it tends to sound better than MP3, so streaming, music downloads and phones lean on it.

The codec and the file are two things. AAC audio can sit inside an MP4 or QuickTime wrapper, which is what an .m4a file is. A standalone .aac file is different: it commonly carries ADTS framing, with no track information around it. The registered audio/aac media type covers that stream form, along with LATM/LOAS framing. Profiles such as LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2 describe how the audio was coded, and a player has to support the profile as well as read the file.

A raw .aac stream can also start or end with ID3v1, ID3v2 or APE tags, which FFmpeg's aac demuxer reads along with the ADTS frames. The ADTS frame header holds a version bit that marks the stream as MPEG-2 or MPEG-4 AAC; FFmpeg's adts muxer writes 0, meaning MPEG-4, unless told otherwise. That bit is one reason a decoder built for one flavor can stumble on the other.

Because the same codec can live in either wrapper, moving between them is mostly a question of packaging.

### Programs that open AAC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player takes raw AAC as input and decodes the MPEG-4 version of AAC.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg includes an AAC decoder and its own AAC encoder.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Audition imports AAC, including HE-AAC.

### AAC and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .aac and audio/aac for a raw stream; .mp4 and video/mp4 for the container. Audio-only MPEG-4 files often use .m4a and the audio/mp4 type.
- **What each is**: AAC compresses sound. MP4, defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14 and first published in 2003, holds sound, video, subtitles and metadata in separate tracks.
- **Wrapper**: a raw .aac stream has none. Under the hood the container is ISO base media, an offshoot of QuickTime, and its track and timing data sit in nested boxes.
- **Video**: MP4 mostly holds H.264 video together with AAC audio, and other codecs, among them AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus, can be stored in it as well. It does not need any video.

The wrapper changes, and so does the audio. On the page, FFmpeg decodes the AAC and encodes it again as AAC at 96 kbps inside an MP4. FFmpeg then makes a second pass that relocates the moov atom, its name for the index, to the front so players find the track information without reading the whole file. No picture is added, so you get an MP4 with sound only. The conversion runs entirely in your browser, so the recording is not uploaded anywhere, and each file in a batch becomes its own MP4.

### Other ways to convert AAC to MP4

Both methods copy the frames instead of encoding them again.

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i voice.aac -c:a copy voice-container.mp4`. Its documentation describes stream copy as no decoding or encoding, and its aac demuxer reads ADTS AAC, with any ID3v1/2 or APE tags in it. Nothing is re-encoded, so the audio keeps the bitrate it already had.
- **Bento4:** run `mp4mux --track aac:voice.aac voice-muxed.mp4`. Its documentation lists AAC input as ADTS format, and says that when you give no type before the colon, the type is inferred from the file extension. The output is the last name on the command line.

### Problems with AAC files

- **A file plays in one program and not another**: some decoders are built for MPEG-2 AAC only and cannot read the MPEG-4 variants. VLC accepts raw AAC input, so open the file there.
- **Renaming to .m4a did not help**: a new extension leaves the ADTS framing where it was and adds no MP4 wrapper. Only a real conversion changes the container.
- **The file is much larger once decoded**: AAC stores compressed audio, so an editor that unpacks it to raw samples uses far more space.
- **A ZIP does not shrink it**: AAC streams are already compressed, and zipping them usually saves little.

guide.title: Understanding AAC for WAV output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AAC file?

AAC stands for Advanced Audio Coding, a family of lossy audio codecs standardized by MPEG. It is specified in Part 7 of MPEG-2 and again in Part 3 of MPEG-4, and the MPEG-4 form is a further refinement of the MPEG-2 one. It can travel inside MP4, QuickTime or other wrappers. A bare .aac file normally uses ADTS framing, and the registered type audio/aac covers both ADTS and LATM/LOAS transport. Its profiles include LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2. The ADTS form uses the .aac extension, the LATM/LOAS form uses .loas, and receivers recognize ADTS by a 12-bit syncword at the start of the data. The audio/aac registration, written by an author at Fraunhofer IIS, lists multimedia, HLS audio-only streams and SHOUTcast or Icecast2 streams as applications.

AAC is used for streaming audio and music downloads, for the audio in MP4 videos and on mobile devices. WAV suits recording and editing, so people convert to it when they want to work on the sound.

The Library of Congress says AAC supports up to 48 channels and 5.1 surround, and reports it as beating MP3 at a given data rate. In wrappers, the MP4 file format uses .mp4 and .m4a, QuickTime AAC uses .m4p, and Apple's Core Audio Format can carry AAC too.

Two things get confused with it. A .m4a file holds AAC too, but inside an MP4 wrapper rather than as a bare stream. And a decoder written for the older MPEG-2 form of AAC may not understand the MPEG-4 variants, which is one reason a loose file plays in one app and not another.

### Programs that open AAC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player opens raw AAC streams and decodes MPEG-4 AAC audio.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg ships its own AAC decoder along with a built-in AAC encoder.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Audition imports AAC, including HE-AAC.

### AAC and WAV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .aac with audio/aac; .wav with audio/wav or audio/x-wav.
- **Compression**: AAC is lossy. The WAV made here is 16-bit linear PCM, one full value for every sample.
- **Size**: decoded AAC can occupy much more space than the file it came from, because the original was compressed. The registration for audio/aac adds that lossless compression such as ZIP typically yields little benefit on an AAC stream.
- **Wrapper**: a raw AAC stream is a run of ADTS frames, and its ID3v2 frames may appear at any frame boundary. WAV is the RIFF-based container that Microsoft and IBM documented in 1991.
- **Metadata**: WAV files differ in where they keep text fields, since plain INFO chunks and the Broadcast WAVE extensions hold different information.
- **Compatibility**: a decoder built only for MPEG-2 AAC can stumble on MPEG-4 variants. The Library of Congress names WAVE among its recommended formats for audio collections.
- **Licensing**: royalties apply to the sale of AAC encoders and decoders, with no use-based fees, according to the Library of Congress. WAV needs no licensing or patents. AAC itself is an open standard developed by ISO JTC 1/SC 29 Working Group 11, which is MPEG.

Converting leaves the sound where AAC left it. The WAV is a bigger container for the same information.

### Other ways to convert AAC to WAV

- **FFmpeg (command line):** `ffmpeg -i interview.aac -c:a pcm_s16le interview.wav` decodes it. The `-c:a` option selects the audio codec, and FFmpeg's documentation lists raw ADTS AAC and PCM signed 16-bit little-endian among the formats it supports for both decoding and encoding. The command sets no sample rate of its own.

### Problems with AAC files

- **The file won't play**: a decoder for one AAC variant may not understand another. Try VLC, which accepts raw AAC.
- **Renaming to .m4a fixed nothing**: renaming .aac to .m4a leaves the bytes untouched, so the ADTS stream is not wrapped in MP4 and the file is still not an M4A.
- **ZIP didn't shrink it**: an AAC is already compressed, so ZIP gains little.
- **Private data inside the stream**: the audio/aac registration warns that private-use tags such as the Data Stream Element could carry arbitrary material, and that executable tagged content must not be executed if it is received. It also notes the data is neither signed nor encrypted.

Illustrator's own file format, AI, stores vector artwork such as paths, shapes and text, and can mix in pixel images. - **Mac:** ImageMagick names AI as Illustrator CS2 and can read it, though it renders the artwork rather than editing it.
- **Linux:** Inkscape opens AI artwork from Illustrator 9.0 onward, though some document features may be unavailable.

CompuServe introduced GIF in 1987 as a raster format using LZW compression, with no more than 256 colors per picture. It can't keep vector paths, and soft transparent edges can't retain partial opacity. PDF.js draws each page of the embedded PDF at up to twice its size, capped near 16.8 megapixels, and ImageMagick then encodes it as a GIF.

Pages become separate files, never an animation. A file without an embedded PDF is refused, and the message says to re-save it in Illustrator with Create PDF Compatible File switched on.

- **Inkscape and ImageMagick:** export the PNG from Inkscape the same way, then run `magick emblem.png emblem.gif`.
- **ImageMagick:** `magick emblem.ai emblem.gif`. Its format list shows AI as readable and writable, and says PDF needs Ghostscript to be installed.

Reading the embedded PDF does not give you Illustrator's editable objects. A copy saved without the PDF-compatible option can fail in third-party software. Older Illustrator releases can have trouble with newer artwork, and Adobe advises using the same version or a newer one. guide.title: About AI files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AI file?

A file ending in .ai is Illustrator's native document. Inside are paths, shapes and text drawn as vectors, along with layers, artboards and live effects, and placed raster images can sit among those objects. Logos, illustrations and print layouts are the usual jobs, and brushes, effects and transparency stay editable inside the file.

The format has been through changes: Illustrator 9 reworked it in 2000, and older files used PostScript. Newer files can carry a PDF-compatible copy beside Illustrator's private data, added when you save with the PDF-compatible option. That copy is how other software can draw the artwork without knowing Illustrator's internals.

Illustrator also lets an AI document mix vector objects with pixel images. Two AI files can look alike in a folder and differ inside: one carries the PDF-compatible rendition and the other does not. Third-party software can fail on a file saved without that rendition, because this converter draws the embedded PDF.

### Programs that open AI files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick lists the format as Illustrator CS2 and renders it to a picture instead of editing it.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Illustrator opens native artwork with every object still editable, and it preserves the effects, brushes, layers and transparency stored in the document.
- **Linux:** Inkscape's manual says it imports AI artwork saved by Illustrator 9.0 or later, and some document features may not come across. The same manual notes that an import can open a dialog of options, and that some import formats depend on other programs installed on your computer.

### AI and JPEG compared

- **Extensions**: an Illustrator file ends in .ai; the picture ends in .jpg or .jpeg, two spellings of one format with the image/jpeg media type.
- **Kind of image**: an AI file is mostly vector artwork that can be scaled without losing sharpness. A JPEG is a raster, a fixed grid of pixels, at 8 bits for each color channel.
- **Compression**: JPEG is lossy. In its baseline mode a picture is cut into eight by eight pixel tiles. Each tile is run through a discrete cosine transform before entropy coding with Huffman tables. Progressive files differ by storing several passes, so a viewer can paint a low-detail picture early while downloading continues.
- **Origin**: the format is named for the committee that wrote it. Its core specification is ITU-T T.81, dated 1992, with ISO/IEC 10918-1 as the matching ISO text.
- **Quality**: programs usually expose a 0 to 100 slider, though one number can give different results from one program to the next.
- **Reach**: browsers all show JPEG, and cameras and scanners commonly produce it.
- **Transparency**: Illustrator keeps transparency. JPEG has none and cannot store layers.
- **Editing**: the AI file keeps layers, artboards and live text. A JPEG keeps none of that.

An editable document becomes a flat picture. The page takes the PDF stored inside your AI file, has PDF.js draw each page onto an opaque white background, and writes each one out as a JPEG. The size limits are in the FAQs below. An AI file with no PDF inside cannot be drawn, and the page tells you so.

### Other ways to convert AI to JPEG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick brand.ai brand-proof.jpeg`. ImageMagick's format list shows AI as readable and says its PDF support requires Ghostscript.

### Problems with AI files

- **An error about a missing PDF**: Illustrator saved the file without its PDF-compatible copy. Reopen it there, turn the PDF-compatible saving option on, and convert the new copy.
- **An old file is refused**: a file from before Illustrator 9 was PostScript-based, so it has no embedded PDF to draw, and this page answers with the no-PDF message. Open it in Illustrator and save it again.
- **Part of the artwork is missing in Inkscape**: Inkscape imports only a subset of the features of some formats, and its manual lists AI files from Illustrator 9.0 onward.
- **Another program draws it wrong**: programs that read only the embedded PDF never see Illustrator's native objects. For editing, use Illustrator.
- **An older Illustrator opens it badly**: Adobe recommends opening artwork in the version that saved it or a newer one.
- **Linked images are missing**: they stay external unless Include Linked Files was selected while saving.

### What is an AI file?

Adobe Illustrator saves its artwork natively as AI. A single document may combine vector objects and pixel images, and Illustrator keeps effects, brushes, layers and transparency editable inside it. Typical AI documents are logos, illustrations and print layouts.

Adobe changed the AI format with Illustrator 9 in 2000, and earlier files used PostScript. Saving with the PDF-compatible option puts a PDF rendition next to the Illustrator data, and that PDF part is all other apps can open. A program that reads the embedded PDF does not necessarily expose native Illustrator objects for editing. That rendition is also what this converter reads.

### Programs that open AI files

- **Windows and Mac:** Native artwork opens in Adobe Illustrator with its Illustrator objects still editable.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads the AI format its list calls Adobe Illustrator CS2, so it renders the artwork but does not edit it as Illustrator does.
- **Linux:** Inkscape's manual says it imports AI artwork from Illustrator 9.0 onward, with some document features possibly unavailable.

Affinity Designer and CorelDRAW are also listed among the programs that open AI files.

### AI and JPG compared

- **Content**: AI holds vector paths, text, layers and artboards. JPG holds a grid of pixels.
- **Editing**: a JPEG has no editable layer stack, so keep the AI if the artwork will change later.
- **Transparency**: with no alpha channel in JPEG, transparent pixels can't make it through the export. This page draws each page on white.
- **Compression**: JPEG is a lossy format with 8 bits for every color channel. A progressive JPEG displays a rough picture right away, and later data sharpens it.
- **Standards**: image/jpeg is the registered media type, and the specification is ITU-T T.81 from 1992, also published as ISO/IEC 10918-1 in 1994.
- **How JPEG compresses**: in the baseline form, 8x8 pixel blocks of the image each get a discrete cosine transform, followed by Huffman coding.
- **Support**: most digital cameras and scanners have JPEG built in, all major browsers display it, and 27 October 2006 is when the US patents ran out.
- **Print and screen**: AI is aimed at logos, illustrations and print layouts, while JPG is built for photographs and displays in every major browser.
- **Size**: vector artwork can be drawn at any size, while a JPG is fixed at the pixel size it was rendered at.

On this page, PDF.js reads the PDF inside the AI file and renders every page. PDF.js draws each page at a scale of up to 2, reduced for a big page so its area stays within 16,777,216 pixels. Each page becomes its own JPG at quality 0.9 on a white background, and the pages arrive as separate images, not one combined file. The AI file itself is not changed.

Because the page reads only the embedded PDF, the JPG shows the page as that PDF draws it. Keep the AI for any later edit, because the JPG holds only pixels.

### Other ways to convert AI to JPG

- **ImageMagick (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `magick -density 150 input.ai output.jpg`. ImageMagick's format list shows AI as a format it reads, and the -density option sets the canvas resolution while rendering vector formats such as PostScript and PDF.
- **Ghostscript (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `gs -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -sDEVICE=jpeg -r150 -sOutputFile=page-%d.jpg input.ai`. The -r option takes the resolution, and %d in the output name is replaced with the page number, so each page gets its own file. It reads the PDF part of a PDF-compatible AI, not Illustrator's editable objects.

Both commands render at the resolution you set, unlike this page, which chooses its own scale.

### Problems with AI files

- **Other software can't open it**: third-party software may fail on an AI file that was saved with no PDF-compatible representation. Save it again from Illustrator with that option on.
- **Opening in an older Illustrator**: an older Illustrator version may run into compatibility problems with the artwork, so Adobe recommends the same or a newer version.
- **A linked image is missing**: the artwork may point at an external image instead of holding it, so a moved or absent file leaves a gap.
- **A very old file has no PDF**: files from before Illustrator 9 were based on PostScript, so there is no PDF rendition for other software to read.

guide.markdown:
### What is an AI file?

Artwork made in Adobe Illustrator is saved as AI. Vector objects and pixel images can share a document, and the editable effects, brushes, layers and transparency all remain in the file. Designers use AI source files for logos, illustrations and print layouts, which is where most people meet one: a logo or layout arrives from a designer, and the person receiving it does not own Illustrator.

Files from before 2000 were PostScript, and Illustrator 9 moved the format on. A file saved since can also include a PDF copy of the page next to Illustrator's own data, provided the PDF-compatible save option was switched on. That PDF copy is what other software reads. An AI saved without it may fail in third-party programs.

The .ai ending does not say whether the PDF is there. Two files called logo.ai can behave very differently: one opens in a print shop's software, and the other opens only in Illustrator. This page is built around that difference. It checks for the PDF and returns it, so whether a file converts here depends on how it was saved.

### Programs that open AI files

**Windows & Mac**

- Adobe Illustrator: opens native artwork with editable Illustrator objects.

**Windows, Mac & Linux**

- ImageMagick: its format list names AI as Illustrator CS2 and reads it. The artwork is rendered rather than kept editable.

**Linux**

- Inkscape: imports Illustrator artwork from version 9.0 onward, according to its manual, though a few document features may not come across.

Software that reads just the PDF part shows the page faithfully but without Illustrator's native objects. For editing, Illustrator remains the reference.

### AI and PDF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .ai and .pdf. PDF's registered media type is application/pdf.
- **Origin**: Adobe created PDF, and the goal was a file that shows or prints a document the same way anywhere. AI is Illustrator's working format.
- **Content**: a PDF combines text, vector shapes and raster pictures, plus links, bookmarks and form fields. An AI combines vector objects with pixel images.
- **Standards**: ISO adopted PDF 1.7 as 32000-1 in 2008. ISO 32000-2, from 2017, covers PDF 2.0. PDF/A (archiving) and PDF/X (printing) are narrower profiles.
- **Editing**: only Illustrator keeps every object editable. Software working from the stored PDF may not offer them.

For this conversion the two overlap completely. When the AI has a PDF inside, the page returns that PDF as it is, under a .pdf name. Nothing is redrawn or resized.

The page cannot improve what Illustrator stored. If a linked picture was left outside the file, the PDF lacks it too, because a picture linked rather than embedded stays out of the PDF unless the AI file was saved with Include Linked Files. Check the result in a PDF viewer before you send it on.

### Other ways to convert AI to PDF

- **Inkscape:** open the AI, choose File > Save a Copy, and select Portable Document Format from the file type list. The dialog then offers text output options (embed fonts, convert text to paths, or omit text), a rasterize filter effects choice, and the output page size.
- **Affinity Designer:** open the AI, go to File > Export, and choose PDF from the format row at the top of the dialog. Adjust the file settings, click Export, then enter a name and location. Affinity's file-format table marks AI as importable and notes that text will be rasterized on PDF export.

Both programs open the artwork and write a new PDF, unlike this page, which returns the stored one. Compare the new file with the original when the artwork uses features the program does not support.

### Problems with AI files

- **The page reports no PDF inside**: the AI has no PDF-compatible content, or it is an older PostScript file. In Illustrator, save it again as AI with Create PDF Compatible File turned on.
- **Third-party software cannot open it**: an AI saved without its PDF-compatible representation may fail outside Illustrator. Ask the sender to save it again with the option on.
- **Linked images are missing**: Illustrator only packs placed pictures into the AI when Include Linked Files is chosen, so save once more with it chosen.
- **A program shows the artwork but will not edit it**: the stored PDF is a view of the page, and the native objects may be missing from it. Edit in Illustrator.
- **An older Illustrator has trouble with the file**: Adobe advises opening artwork in the same or a newer version of Illustrator than the one that saved it.

faqs.question: Does the PNG keep my layers?

faqs.question: What happens to a multi-page AI file?

faqs.question: Is my artwork uploaded when I convert it?

guide.title: Understanding AI for PNG output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AI file?

AI is Adobe Illustrator's native artwork format. An AI document can hold vector objects next to pixel images, and Illustrator keeps editable effects, brushes, layers and transparency inside the file. AI source files are what designers work from for logos, illustrations and print layouts.

Illustrator 9 changed the AI format in 2000; earlier files used PostScript. The PDF-compatible saving option includes a PDF rendition alongside the Illustrator data, and that rendition is what this page draws. Modern files embed that PDF-compatible stream, which is why other programs can often read an AI file without owning Illustrator.

You will usually receive an AI file from a designer or a brand kit. To put the artwork in a slide, a web page or a document, you need a picture instead. Keep the AI itself if the artwork may need editing.

### Programs that open AI files

- **Mac and Windows:** Adobe Illustrator opens native artwork and keeps its Illustrator objects editable.
- **Linux, Mac and Windows:** ImageMagick can read the AI format that its format list calls Illustrator CS2, but it renders the artwork rather than editing it as Illustrator does.
- **Linux:** Inkscape's import manual lists Illustrator files from version 9.0 onward, though not every document feature is available.

### AI and PNG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .ai, a proprietary Adobe format; .png with image/png.
- **What is stored**: an AI keeps vector artwork, layers and artboards. A PNG keeps pixels as indexed, grayscale or truecolor samples of 1 to 16 bits each.
- **Compression**: PNG compression is always lossless, using the DEFLATE method, so a rendered logo stays crisp at the size it was drawn.
- **Transparency**: PNG supports an optional alpha channel, but this page paints a white background.
- **History**: PNG was designed as a patent-free alternative to GIF, and RFC 2083 and ISO/IEC 15948:2004 later defined it.
- **Structure**: the first thing in a PNG is a fixed signature, and after it come chunks: the header sits in IHDR, the image data in IDAT, and IEND ends the file.
- **Standards**: October 1996 saw PNG published as the first format to become a W3C Recommendation.
- **Support**: PNG is displayed by every major browser, and no known patents on it require royalties.
- **Editing**: the AI can be reopened and changed. The PNG is a final picture, and changing it means editing pixels.

The page renders each page of the embedded PDF with PDF.js. A page is drawn at up to twice its size, and scaled down if it would pass 16,777,216 pixels, about 16.8 megapixels. The cap is on area, not on each side. Pages are drawn onto opaque white and are not merged into one picture. Each page downloads as its own PNG, named after the file with _page1, _page2 and so on, and your AI is never changed. Because only the embedded PDF is drawn, the result shows the artwork as it was saved into that rendition, not as a live document.

### Other ways to convert AI to PNG

- **Inkscape (Windows, Mac, Linux):** bring the AI file into Inkscape and use File > Export PNG Image, or press Shift+Ctrl+E. Choose what to export from Page, Drawing, Selection or Custom, under Image Size set the pixel dimensions or the resolution, pick a file name and press Export.
- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick artwork.ai artwork.png`. ImageMagick's format list marks AI as both readable and writable, under the name Adobe Illustrator CS2. The result is a rendering, not an editable file.

### Problems with AI files

- **"This AI file has no PDF inside"**: the file was saved without a PDF-compatible representation. In Illustrator, save it again with Create PDF Compatible File turned on. Older PostScript-based files don't have it.
- **Third-party software can't read the AI**: a file saved without its PDF-compatible representation may fail in other programs as well.
- **Linked pictures are missing**: Illustrator leaves linked images outside the file unless Include Linked Files is chosen when saving.
- **Illustrator reports a compatibility problem**: opening artwork in an older Illustrator version can cause them, so Adobe advises matching or newer versions.
- **You need to edit the design**: a program that reads the embedded PDF doesn't necessarily expose the native objects. Keep the AI.
- **Several pages came out**: that is expected when the embedded PDF has more than one page. Each is its own PNG.

guide.title: About AI files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AI file?

Illustrator's own format is AI. What an AI document stores is paths, shapes and text, and pixel images can sit alongside them. Illustrator keeps layers, brushes and transparency in it as editable parts, which makes AI the working file behind many logos, illustrations and packaging layouts.

Before 2000 the format was PostScript-based, and Illustrator 9 changed that. When Create PDF Compatible File was on at save time, a newer AI also holds a PDF of the page beside the Illustrator data, and other software can read that PDF.

People search for AI to SVG when they want a design on a website, in a cutting machine or in a program other than Illustrator. SVG is the format those places accept. This page helps when you need an SVG that looks like the artwork. It does not help when you need to edit the shapes afterward, because the SVG it makes contains a picture of the page.

### Programs that open AI files

**Mac & Windows**

- Adobe Illustrator: the program that wrote the format, with every object editable.

**Linux, Mac & Windows**

- ImageMagick: its formats page lists AI as Illustrator CS2. It draws the artwork and does not keep the objects.

**Linux**

- Inkscape: opens AI files made by Illustrator 9.0 or later, per its manual, though not every document feature survives.

Browsers display SVG but do not open AI files, so the SVG from this page works in them while the original does not. Use the SVG when the destination wants a web-friendly picture, and keep the AI as the source for any later change.

### AI and SVG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .ai, and .svg with the type image/svg+xml.
- **Structure**: SVG is XML text that describes shapes, paths and text. AI is Adobe's own format with layers and artboards.
- **Scaling**: real SVG paths stay sharp at any size. An SVG that wraps a picture does not.
- **Standard**: SVG is a W3C standard, written as XML text, and it can be styled with CSS and scripted. AI is proprietary to Adobe.
- **Fonts**: SVG text depends on the viewer's fonts unless it is turned into outlines.
- **Embedded pictures**: an SVG can embed pixel images, and they keep their own resolution when enlarged.

That last point describes what this page produces. It draws each page of the AI's PDF and embeds the picture in an SVG, so the result is a picture of each page and nothing stays an editable vector.

The scale matters too. Pages are drawn at up to twice their size, and a page is shrunk when that would pass about 16.8 megapixels. An Illustrator artboard can be thousands of points across, so a large one comes out smaller than twice its size. The background is opaque white.

### Other ways to convert AI to SVG

- **Inkscape:** open the AI and save the drawing with a .svg ending. Choose Plain SVG for sharing, or Inkscape SVG to keep Inkscape's own editing information.
- **Affinity Designer:** open the AI, then File > Export with SVG as the type. Set the area and options, press Export, and name the file. Affinity's file-format table lists AI as importable.

Unlike this page, both can keep paths and text as vector objects, so check fonts and effects in the result before you use it.

### Problems with AI files

- **You see the no-PDF message**: save the AI again from Illustrator with Create PDF Compatible File turned on.
- **The font cannot be swapped**: the lettering is fixed inside the picture, whereas a true vector SVG uses installed fonts unless the text is outlined.
- **Linked pictures are missing**: if Include Linked Files was off when the AI was saved, the placed pictures never made it into the file, so nothing here can draw them.
- **The SVG pixelates when enlarged**: it contains a picture. Make a vector SVG in Inkscape or Affinity Designer.
- **The SVG has a white box behind it**: pages are drawn on white, so transparency in the artwork is not kept.
- **The SVG is large**: the picture is stored as text inside the file, so it outweighs a PNG of the same page.
- **You cannot select the words**: they are baked into the picture. Keep the AI or a PDF for that.

guide.title: AI files and TIFF output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AI file?

AI is Adobe Illustrator's native artwork format. Inside it sit vector paths, shapes, text and effects arranged in layers and artboards, and pixel images can sit among the vector objects. Illustrator 9 changed the format in 2000, and earlier files used PostScript. This page reads the PDF rendition that the PDF-compatible saving option stores next to the Illustrator data. Logos, illustrations and print layouts are typical AI source files.

### Programs that open AI files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- ImageMagick reads AI as Illustrator CS2. That is rendering, not Illustrator editing.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Illustrator opens native artwork with its editable objects.

**Linux:**

- Inkscape imports AI artwork from Illustrator 9.0 onward, and some document features may be unavailable.

### AI and TIFF compared

TIFF is a tag-based raster wrapper developed by Aldus and Microsoft. Revision 6.0 appeared in 1992, and Adobe now controls the specification. Compression methods and color representations vary between TIFFs, and one file can hold several images, as in a scanned page sequence. Its extensions are .tif and .tiff, with the media type image/tiff.

Here PDF.js draws each page of the PDF inside the AI, and the pixels are written as a TIFF on an opaque white background. Each page is drawn at up to double its size, and a very large artboard is scaled down to stay within a pixel budget of about 16.8 megapixels. Every page is a separate file with no ZIP, named name_page1, name_page2 and so on. You can choose several AI files at once, and they run one after another. The page sets no print resolution, so artwork meant for a printer's dpi spec should be exported from Illustrator. A file with no PDF inside fails with a message telling you to resave it with Create PDF Compatible File turned on.

### Other ways to convert AI to TIFF

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick -density 300 artwork.ai artwork.tiff`. The -density option sets the canvas resolution used when a vector format is rendered to a raster image.

### Problems with AI files

- **No PDF inside**: other software can fail on an AI that lacks its PDF-compatible representation. Resave it from Illustrator with that option on.
- **Not editable afterwards**: reading the embedded PDF gives no native Illustrator objects, so the AI stays your editable master.
- **Missing links**: a linked image stays outside the file unless Include Linked Files was ticked when saving, so the TIFF can lack it.
- **Older Illustrator versions**: opening artwork in an older version can cause compatibility problems, so match or exceed the saving version.
- **Blurry when enlarged**: the TIFF is pixels, so render again at the size you need.
- **Layers are gone**: the TIFF is flattened.

guide.title: About AIF and MP3
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIF file?

An AIF file is an Audio Interchange File Format recording. The .aif extension is the short form of .aiff, and both name the same format. AIFF was Apple's creation, based on Electronic Arts' IFF family, and version 1.3 of its specification carries the date January 4, 1989. Uncompressed linear PCM samples are the usual contents, while AIFF-C widens the family to compressed audio. An AIFF can also include named chunks for the author, copyright and annotations.

Masters and working recordings in professional audio are a typical use, and macOS audio production is where AIFF is best known. Because the samples are usually uncompressed and lossless, the files are large, and a recording is often turned into an MP3 before it is shared. Common media-type labels are audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff.

### Programs that open AIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports most AIFF files, every PCM variant included, without its optional FFmpeg library. It is the choice for trimming or cleaning a recording before you export it.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg lists AIFF encoding and decoding support in its format table, and it runs from the command line.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** AIFF is among the files VLC media player opens.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Audition opens uncompressed AIFF and most of the common compressed variants, which suits professional editing.
- **Mac:** Apple Music plays AIFF, and Logic Pro, Apple's music production app, opens it for editing.

### AIF and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .aif and .aiff are common audio/aiff, with audio/x-aiff also seen. MP3's registered media type is audio/mpeg.
- **Compression**: AIFF is normally uncompressed PCM. MP3 is a lossy format, and it plays in every major browser; it shrinks audio by dropping sounds that a model of human hearing says listeners won't notice.
- **Standards**: MP3 is MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, standardized as ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993 and extended by ISO/IEC 13818-3 in 1995. The late 1980s saw Fraunhofer IIS start the work on MP3, joined by other members of the MPEG audio group.
- **Size**: compared with the same audio on a CD, an MP3 at 128 kbit/s takes roughly one eleventh of the space.
- **Bitrate**: an MP3 can be written at 32 to 320 kbps, at a 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz sampling rate. This page asks for 192 kbps, so a source below 32 kHz gets a lower rate.
- **Metadata**: AIFF has its own chunks for author, copyright and annotations. ID3 structures, separate from the audio, hold an MP3's song titles and other tags.
- **Playback**: every major browser plays MP3, so the converted file works almost anywhere.
- **Licensing**: the MP3 patent licensing program ended on 23 April 2017.

This page re-encodes the audio with FFmpeg's LAME encoder and discards any picture track. The result is a standard MP3 that is not identical to the AIF. Global tags from the AIF are carried over by FFmpeg wherever the MP3 has a matching field.

### Other ways to convert AIF to MP3

- **FFmpeg (command line):** encode with `ffmpeg -i input.aif -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k output.mp3`. FFmpeg's documentation lists AIFF among the formats it reads, describes the LAME encoder, and sets the bitrate with the b option. Replace input.aif with the name of your own file, and the result is written next to it as output.mp3 in the folder where you ran the command.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** use File > Import > Audio to load the AIF, then File > Export Audio with MP3 chosen as the format. The bit rate modes are Preset, Variable, Average and Constant, and the Standard preset is the default.

Each route makes a lossy MP3, so keep the AIF as your master.

### Problems with AIF files

- **One AIF plays, another doesn't**: AIFF-C compression requires a decoder for the actual encoding, and the family name alone does not establish support.
- **Author field missing**: Adobe Audition can file an AIFF's author under Dublin Core: Creator, not under a field called Author.
- **The AIF is too big to email**: a long recording in uncompressed PCM gets very large, and a compressed copy of it takes less storage.
- **The extension misleads**: .aif and .aiff are the same format, but a file ending in either may hold AIFF-C, so the ending does not tell you how the audio is encoded.

guide.title: About AIFC and MP3
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIFC file?

Apple developed the Audio Interchange File Format family, and AIFF-C, usually written AIFC, extended it to compressed sound in August 1991. A file stores sampled audio in an AIFF-related wrapper, described by its channel count, sample width and sampling frequency. It can also include markers that identify positions within the recording.

Despite the C in the name, an AIFC may hold plain uncompressed samples. Python's documentation lists the compression identifiers NONE, ULAW, ALAW and G722. The format shares the AIFF container but allows optional compression, and it carries metadata chunks. People use it for compressed audio on macOS and in audio production workflows.

That flexibility is also the source of most trouble. A recognized AIFC wrapper can still contain a codec that a reader does not implement, so two files with the same extension may behave differently in the same program.

### Programs that open AIFC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - FFmpeg reads AIFF-C through its AIFF demuxer, though decoding depends on the stored encoding.
  - ffplay uses FFmpeg libraries for playback.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - Adobe Audition opens AIFC, including common compressed AIFF variants and files with up to 32 channels, but it does not promise every variant.

### AIFC and MP3 compared

- **Names and types**: .aifc, the compressed AIFF-C file, becomes .mp3.
- **Compression**: an AIFC may be plain PCM or use an encoding such as ULAW or ALAW. MP3 is lossy, so some information is always discarded.
- **Metadata**: AIFC supplies markers and metadata chunks; an MP3 keeps its tags as ID3 data.
- **Standard**: ISO/IEC 11172-3 is the MPEG specification for MP3, which most devices can play.
- **Bitrate**: MP3 can hold audio at one fixed rate or at a rate that varies.

Here FFmpeg is built for WebAssembly and executes inside a browser worker, which means your audio never leaves the device. Video is switched off, and LAME aims for a 192 kbps encode. Sound sampled under 32 kHz limits what MP3 can do, giving a ceiling of 160 kbps for 16 to 24 kHz material and 64 kbps for 8 to 12 kHz material. The page keeps the sample rate as it is, and it does not set the channel count or a stream either, so FFmpeg's defaults decide.

Several AIFC files can go in together and are processed in turn. Every MP3 downloads on its own under the original name with .mp3 added, nothing is zipped, and the AIFC stays untouched. File size is not capped and no timeout is set, so how long a lengthy recording takes depends on your device. When an AIFC is cut short, FFmpeg usually still produces output, since it logs the problem and writes whatever it could read; expect an MP3 shorter than the source.

Moving from AIFC to MP3 trades fidelity for convenience. An AIFC holding PCM keeps every sample, while the MP3 discards some information for good. The loss is permanent, so convert a copy and keep the AIFC if you ever intend to edit or master the audio. Editing an MP3 and exporting another MP3 adds a second lossy stage, which is why the original is worth keeping. If the recording will only be listened to, the MP3 is the more widely playable file.

### Other ways to convert AIFC to MP3

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i input.aifc -b:a 192k -c:a libmp3lame output.mp3` produces an MP3 aimed at the same 192 kbps this page requests. In FFmpeg's documentation -c:a is the option for the audio codec and -b:a the option for its bitrate, so another value in place of 192k gives you a different rate. Whether FFmpeg can read the file still depends on the compression type inside the AIFC.

### Problems with AIFC files

- **FFmpeg stops with an error**: the AIFC may use an encoding its reader lacks. Re-export it from an audio editor as uncompressed audio.
- **The MP3 sounds slightly different**: MP3 is lossy, so keep the AIFC for editing and convert a copy.
- **You want a lossless copy**: choose an uncompressed format from an audio editor, because this MP3 is not lossless.
- **You need to edit the audio later**: work from the AIFC, then make the MP3 as the last step. A second lossy encode adds more loss.
- **Only part of the file converted**: a cut-short AIFC converts what could be read. Compare the lengths of both files before deleting the original.
- **Audition will not open it**: Audition opens common compressed AIFF variants but does not promise every one.
- **The MP3 comes out under 192 kbps**: a low sample rate causes it, as covered earlier, and nothing is broken.

guide.title: Understanding AIFF for FLAC output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIFF file?

Audio Interchange File Format came from Apple and descends from the IFF wrapper created at Electronic Arts. In its common form the file holds uncompressed linear PCM plus optional chunks naming the author, copyright and annotations, and studios often keep masters in it. A compressed variant, AIFF-C, extends the family to other encodings. Common media-type labels are audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff.

### Programs that open AIFF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity brings in nearly any AIFF, PCM variants included, and FFmpeg both reads and writes the format.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Audition handles uncompressed AIFF plus the common compressed kinds.

### AIFF and FLAC compared

- **Size**: AIFF is large, since PCM is uncompressed. FLAC compresses the same samples without loss.
- **Fidelity**: both keep every sample when the AIFF holds PCM.
- **Video**: neither is meant for it, and the page discards any video stream.
- **Metadata**: AIFF uses chunks. FLAC relies on Vorbis comments and may embed cover art.
- **Openness**: FLAC's specification is open, and its reference encoder comes from Xiph.

The page runs `-acodec flac -vn` in FFmpeg, so the audio is encoded as FLAC and any video is dropped. Stream choice and tags follow FFmpeg's defaults.

### Other ways to convert AIFF to FLAC

- **flac:** run `flac session.aiff` with the Xiph reference encoder. It reads linear PCM AIFF with 4 to 32 bits per sample, not A-law or mu-law, and writes session.flac in place of the .aiff ending.
- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i take.aiff -c:a flac take.flac` on the command line.
- **Audacity:** open the AIFF, choose File > Export Audio, pick FLAC, and set 16-bit or 24-bit and a compression level from 0 to 8.

### Problems with AIFF files

- **The conversion fails**: the file may be an AIFF-C that uses a compression type FFmpeg cannot decode.
- **You expected better sound**: FLAC cannot restore detail that a lossy step removed before the recording became an AIFF.
- **The author looks misplaced**: Audition may list an AIFF's author under Dublin Core: Creator rather than Author.
- **A file over 4 GB**: AIFF stores its length in 32 bits, so very large files are malformed.

guide.title: AIFF files and M4A output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIFF file?

Apple developed the Audio Interchange File Format in 1988 on top of the IFF container. It usually stores uncompressed PCM audio, so it is lossless and large, with metadata chunks. It serves for macOS audio production and professional sound editing.

### Programs that open AIFF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Audacity brings in AIFF recordings, every PCM variant included, with no extra library.
- VLC media player opens AIFF.
- FFmpeg includes both AIFF encoding and decoding.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Audition opens uncompressed AIFF and most compressed variants.

**Mac:**

- Apple Music and Logic Pro open it.

### AIFF and M4A compared

An M4A is audio only, stored in the MPEG-4 container. It usually holds AAC, or lossless Apple Lossless (ALAC), and it supports tags and cover art. It is widely supported, and is the usual form for podcasts and music from the Apple stores.

FFmpeg runs in your browser here with `-acodec aac -b:a 192k -vn`, which writes AAC at 192 kbps and drops any video stream. The result is lossy and far smaller than the AIFF. Choose several AIFF files and each is encoded in turn into a separate M4A. No sample rate or channel setting is passed, so there is no control for either. Before you delete the AIFF, play the M4A through once, because AAC discards some detail.

### Other ways to convert AIFF to M4A

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i master.aiff -c:a aac -b:a 192k listening-from-aiff.m4a`.
- **Audacity:** after installing the optional FFmpeg library, open the AIFF, then File > Export Audio and M4A (AAC) Files (FFmpeg). Its AAC export has a quality setting for the bit rate.

### Problems with AIFF files

- **A huge file**: PCM audio takes up space by design, so size alone does not mean damage.
- **Lossless is required**: AAC discards detail, so keep the AIFF as the master.
- **Tracks sound different**: AAC is lossy, so compare the M4A with the AIFF before deleting anything.
- **You need an editable file**: edit the AIFF first and convert last.
- **Metadata**: AIFF carries metadata chunks, so look at the tags in your player after converting.

guide.title: Understanding AIFF for MP3 output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIFF file?

AIFF stands for Audio Interchange File Format. Apple developed it, and it is an audio wrapper derived from Electronic Arts' IFF family. Apple's AIFF 1.3 specification is dated January 4, 1989.

An AIFF often carries uncompressed linear PCM samples, which is why professional audio users have long used it for masters and intermediate recordings. The AIFF-C extension covers compressed audio, so not every AIFF-family file is plain PCM. The format can also hold named chunks for author, copyright and annotations. Common media-type labels are audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff. It is used for audio production on macOS and professional sound editing.

You meet AIFF files in recording sessions, sample libraries and projects exported from Mac audio software. They are lossless but large, so an MP3 is the lighter copy for sharing, uploading or playing on a device that doesn't read AIFF.

### Programs that open AIFF files

**Linux, Mac and Windows**

- Audacity: imports most AIFF files, including all PCM variants, without its optional FFmpeg library.
- VLC media player plays AIFF.
- FFmpeg: lists AIFF encoding and decoding support.

**Mac and Windows**

- Adobe Audition: handles uncompressed AIFF as well as most common compressed variants.

**Mac**

- Logic Pro and Apple Music open AIFF.

### AIFF and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .aiff or .aif with audio/aiff; .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **Compression**: AIFF is usually uncompressed PCM and lossless. MP3 is lossy: its encoder models human hearing and drops sound that most listeners would not miss.
- **Size**: uncompressed PCM needs more storage than a compressed copy of the same recording. A 128 kbps MP3 needs roughly an eleventh of the space the matching CD audio does, so 192 kbps lands near one seventh for a CD-rate source.
- **Metadata**: an AIFF stores author, copyright and annotations in named chunks, while an MP3 puts song titles and other tags into ID3 structures kept apart from the audio.
- **Editing**: each time you edit an MP3 and export it again, you add another lossy encoding stage. The AIFF has no such stage.
- **Support**: every major browser plays MP3. MP3 became ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993, and the license program for its patents closed on 23 April 2017.

This page asks LAME for 192 kbps, which a source at 32 kHz or more gets, and keeps only the audio. You can't pick a bitrate here, so if a delivery spec asks for a different one, use a desktop tool from the next section. The AIFF you chose is never changed, and you download a new file named after it with the .mp3 ending. Files chosen together are encoded in sequence, and each produces its own MP3.

### Other ways to convert AIFF to MP3

Each of these re-encodes the audio as a new MP3, as this page does.

- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** begin with File > Import > Audio and pick the AIFF, then File > Export Audio, select MP3 in the format list, set the channels and sample rate, choose the entire project or the current selection, and press Export. The MP3 encoding settings sit on a separate MP3 Export Options page.
- **SoX (command line):** run `sox session.aiff -C 192 session.mp3`. A positive integer after -C is taken as the bitrate in kbps. SoX can only write MP3 if it was built with the LAME library.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i session.aiff -c:a libmp3lame session.mp3`. FFmpeg's format list includes AIFF, and its MP3 encoder comes from the external LAME library. FFmpeg falls back on a default bitrate of its own when none is given, so add `-b:a 192k` for the bitrate this page uses.

### Problems with AIFF files

- **An editor rejects the file**: it may be AIFF-C, which extends the family to compressed audio. The family name alone doesn't promise support, because a decoder for the actual compression is needed.
- **The file is huge**: that is normal for uncompressed PCM, which takes plenty of room on a drive or a phone. Make an MP3 for sharing and keep the AIFF as the master.
- **Credits look different in another program**: the author field can show in Audition under Dublin Core: Creator instead of a field called Author.
- **Renaming did nothing**: changing .aif to .mp3 leaves the PCM data inside, because only the label changes. Converting is the only way to make a real MP3.

guide.title: Understanding AIFF and WAV
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIFF file?

AIFF, Audio Interchange File Format, is an audio format developed by Apple. It is derived from the IFF family from Electronic Arts, and it stores sound in named chunks that can also hold an author, copyright and annotations. AIFF usually carries uncompressed linear PCM. Its sibling AIFF-C extends the format to compressed audio.

Producers and sound designers keep masters and intermediate recordings in AIFF. The AIFF 1.3 specification from Apple carries the date January 4, 1989, and the format is still common on Macs and in audio software.

Audio people care about three settings: sample rate, bit depth and channel count. This page offers none of them as a choice; the WAV it writes is always 16-bit.

People convert to WAV because a program, device or collaborator asks for it. WAV is the other widely used uncompressed wrapper, and a request for one over the other is usually about compatibility, not sound. Archives and delivery specifications often name WAVE for that reason, and the Library of Congress lists it among its recommended audio formats.

### Programs that open AIFF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity is a free editor that imports AIFF files, including all PCM variants, without any extra library; its manual lists AIFF among the uncompressed formats it opens directly, while an optional FFmpeg add-on covers a wider range. FFmpeg's format table lists AIFF for both decoding and encoding, and third-party builds exist for all three systems.

### AIFF and WAV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: AIFF files end in .aiff or .aif and use audio/aiff or audio/x-aiff; .wav with audio/wav and audio/x-wav.
- **Structure**: AIFF descends from IFF. WAVE is RIFF-based, documented by Microsoft and IBM in August 1991.
- **Contents**: both usually hold linear PCM. AIFF-C adds compressed encodings, and WAV can carry compressed ones too.
- **Metadata**: AIFF has chunks for author and copyright. Broadcast WAVE extends WAV with production and preservation metadata.
- **Bit depth**: both can hold 16-bit, 24-bit and higher PCM. The WAV written here is 16-bit whatever the AIFF held.
- **Large files**: a very large recording may need the RF64 extension instead of the original RIFF size fields.

On this page the WAV is signed 16-bit PCM, written by FFmpeg inside your browser. Any picture or video stream in the source is left out, and the original AIFF stays untouched because you download a new copy. A 16-bit AIFF converts with its samples unchanged. A 24-bit AIFF has its precision reduced to 16 bits.

Uncompressed audio takes the same room per second whichever wrapper holds it, so the two files land near each other in size. In a test with a short mono sample, a 16-bit AIFF and its WAV differed by a few bytes, while the WAV from a 24-bit AIFF came out a third smaller.

### Other ways to convert AIFF to WAV

- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** bring the AIFF in with File > Import > Audio, then run File > Export Audio, pick WAV and set the sample rate and channels. Tracks that are muted or soloed out are not exported, so check the project before you export. Audacity also shows the sample rate and channel choices in the same dialog, which this page does not offer.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i studio.aiff -c:a pcm_s16le delivery.wav` for 16-bit PCM. FFmpeg's codec table lists signed 16-bit little-endian PCM as supported for encoding.

### Problems with AIFF files

- **A program rejects the AIFF**: the file may be AIFF-C with a compressed encoding. the program needs a decoder for the specific encoding inside; the AIFF-C name alone does not guarantee support.
- **The AIFF is large**: raw PCM takes more disk than a compressed delivery copy of the same recording, so pick a compressed format if space matters.
- **Tags look different in the WAV**: formats store descriptive fields differently, since standard INFO chunks and Broadcast WAVE extensions hold different information. Open the WAV in your editor and confirm the fields you rely on.
- **A very large recording**: once a recording outgrows the classic RIFF size fields, WAV needs the RF64 extension. If a program won't accept the result, keep the AIFF.
- **The sound has less depth**: a 24-bit original was reduced to 16 bits in the WAV. Keep the AIFF as your master.
