guide.title: About DXF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a DXF file?

DXF, Drawing Exchange Format, is a format Autodesk publishes to exchange AutoCAD drawing data with other programs. The first DXF documentation appeared in 1982, and the media type registered for it is image/vnd.dxf.

A DXF is either text or binary. The text kind is a long run of group codes, every one followed by its value. New drawing capabilities have introduced additional codes and format versions.

DXF is used to exchange CAD drawings, for CNC, laser cutting and plotting work, and for architectural and engineering drawings. It carries 2D and 3D geometry and layers.

JPEG is the output here: a raster image format with lossy compression, the Joint Photographic Experts Group standardized it in ISO/IEC 10918-1. It fits web photos, pictures from cameras, emailed attachments and photo sharing, with a quality that can be set.

### Programs that open DXF files

Inkscape and FreeCAD also open DXF. The fact sheet for the format lists these programs by platform:

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- LibreCAD: opens DXF drawings in its 2D CAD workspace.
- QCAD Community Edition: a free 2D CAD application that supports DXF; QCAD Professional is where advanced interchange features live.

**Windows and Mac**

- Adobe Illustrator: brings in DXF written by AutoCAD releases 2.5 to 2007, and offers unit and scale settings.

**Windows**

- AutoCAD: use Open Drawing and select DXF in the file-type list.

**Web**

- Autodesk Viewer: Autodesk offers browser viewing for CAD interchange files, DXF among them.

### DXF and JPG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .dxf has the registered type image/vnd.dxf. JPEG takes the ending .jpg or .jpeg.
- **Kind**: DXF exchanges AutoCAD drawing data. JPEG is a raster format designed for photographs.
- **Geometry**: layers, flat shapes and 3D shapes can all live in a DXF. This page makes one flat picture of the drawing.
- **Transparency**: JPEG has no alpha transparency, and this page draws on white.
- **Output size**: the JPG is 2048 pixels on its longer side, and no side goes over 4096 pixels.
- **Fonts**: TEXT and MTEXT are set in DejaVu Sans, whichever font your drawing names.

The page uses the dxf-viewer library, which draws with three.js and WebGL. It paints the drawing on a white background and scales it to 2048 pixels on the longer side, with no output side over 4096 pixels. TEXT and MTEXT objects are set in DejaVu Sans. The picture is then encoded like any other image. If your browser has no WebGL, the page says it is unavailable. Nothing is uploaded, and your DXF is not changed. Pick several drawings and they convert in turn, one JPG each, named after the DXF with the .jpg ending.

The pixel size comes from the page, not from the drawing's units. The longer side is always set to 2048 pixels, so a small part and a large site plan end up at the same picture size. The page has no size setting, so use the CAD program or one of the methods below if you need a specific size.

### Other ways to convert DXF to JPG

- **LibreCAD (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the DXF and choose File > Export. The list of image formats includes JPEG.
- **LibreOffice Draw:** LibreOffice's guide lists AutoCAD Interchange Format (*.dxf) among the formats Draw opens, and lists JPEG among the graphics formats Draw exports.
- **QCAD Professional (command line):** run `dwg2bmp -o plan-review.jpg -x 2400 plan-review.dxf` to render a picture 2400 pixels wide. The tool reads DXF or DWG, and QCAD's page lists it as dwg2bmpPRO in Professional installs.

### Problems with DXF files

- **LibreCAD misses features**: it does not implement every DXF feature, and it lists supported versions through DXF 2007.
- **Illustrator refuses the file**: drawings saved after the 2007 AutoCAD format are rejected, so you need an older export.
- **Illustrator asks for missing files**: a drawing that points at separate files can make the import ask for those missing external references.
- **The scale is wrong in Illustrator**: scale and unit mapping need attention when moving a CAD drawing there.
- **The page says WebGL is unavailable**: try another browser or device.
- **This JPG does not match another program's output**: identical quality settings in different programs do not assure identical compression or looks.
- **Lettering looks different**: text objects of both kinds use DejaVu Sans here, so the typeface may not match your CAD view.

guide.title: About DXF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a DXF file?

DXF is Autodesk's drawing exchange format, published so that AutoCAD drawing data can move to other programs. The first documentation appeared in 1982. A DXF exists in a text form and a binary form, and a text DXF pairs numeric group codes with values to describe each part of the drawing. New drawing capabilities have added codes and format versions over the years. The registered media type is image/vnd.dxf.

A DXF describes a drawing rather than holding a picture, so a program has to draw it before anyone can look at it. This page makes a PNG from the drawing: a grid of colored pixels.

### Programs that open DXF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- LibreCAD reads DXF drawings in its 2D workspace.
- QCAD Community Edition is a free 2D CAD program with DXF support. Advanced interchange features belong to QCAD Professional.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Illustrator imports DXF from AutoCAD 2.5 through 2007, with unit and scale settings.

**Windows:**

- AutoCAD opens it from Open Drawing with DXF chosen in the file-type list.

**Web:**

- Autodesk Viewer shows CAD interchange files, DXF included, in the browser.

LibreCAD does not implement every DXF feature and lists support through DXF 2007. Illustrator refuses AutoCAD drawings saved later than the 2007 format, so an older export is needed.

### DXF and PNG compared

- **What it holds**: a DXF describes a drawing with group codes and values. A PNG holds a grid of colored pixels.
- **Where it opens**: every major browser displays PNG. A DXF opens in CAD programs and viewers.
- **Measuring**: a PNG has only the picture, with no drawing units, so distances cannot be read from it.

This page draws the DXF in your browser with the dxf-viewer library, which uses three.js and WebGL. The whole drawing is fitted into the picture with a 5 percent margin on a white background. The longer side is 2048 pixels, and the shorter side follows the drawing's proportions but is never under 128 pixels. Entities drawn in white are shown black so they stay visible on the white page. TEXT and MTEXT are drawn in DejaVu Sans instead of the fonts named in the drawing, so labels can differ from the CAD original.

The result is one PNG per file. A browser without WebGL cannot draw the file and says so. A drawing with nothing in it stops with the message "This DXF file has nothing drawn in it."

### Other ways to convert DXF to PNG

- **LibreCAD:** open the drawing and choose File > Export, which exports the current drawing as a CAM, PDF or image file. The menu reference lists PNG among the supported bitmap formats.
- **QCAD Professional:** run `dwg2bmp -o plan.png plan.dxf` from the command line. The dwg2bmp tool converts a DXF or DWG file into a bitmap file. The `-r` option sets the resolution in pixels per drawing unit and `-b` sets the background color. Every QCAD Professional installation includes some command line tools.

### Problems with DXF files

- **The image looks empty**: the drawing may hold nothing, or the page reports "nothing drawn in it". Open the file in LibreCAD to see whether it has any entities.
- **Labels sit differently**: TEXT and MTEXT use DejaVu Sans here, so labels can differ from the original fonts.
- **"This DXF file couldn't be read"**: the viewer could not parse the file. Try re-exporting it from your CAD program.
- **The browser cannot draw it**: WebGL is off or unavailable there. Check that hardware acceleration is on, or try another current browser.
- **A newer DXF fails in Illustrator or LibreCAD**: both list support only through the 2007 format, so save an older version.
- **Missing linked files in Illustrator**: the import can ask for external references because the drawing points to separate files.
- **Scale and units in Illustrator**: moving a CAD drawing into Illustrator needs attention to scale and unit mapping.
- **A big plan comes out small**: the picture always has a 2048-pixel long side, so fine detail in a large drawing is easier to inspect by zooming in a CAD program.
- **A line you drew in white**: white entities appear black, because the page behind them is white.
- **You need exact distances**: send the DXF, because a PNG has no units.

guide.title: About EMF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an EMF file?

EMF, Enhanced Metafile, is Microsoft's format for storing graphics as recorded drawing operations. Instead of pixels, the file holds a header, a series of drawing records and an end record. The records describe graphics objects, property changes and drawing orders.

Its device-independent design keeps drawing proportions across output devices. The first extension to the format added a pixel-format record and OpenGL command support. RFC 7903 identifies image/emf and the older image/x-emf media type.

EMF is used for charts and diagrams pasted into Office documents and for Windows printing and clipboard graphics. Bitmaps can be embedded too, so a single file may hold both kinds.

The target, PNG, is a lossless raster picture format. Created in the mid-1990s as a GIF successor free of patent trouble, PNG is covered by ISO standard 15948 and by a W3C Recommendation. It is used for screenshots and interface graphics, for logos and images with transparency, and for web graphics that must stay sharp. It has 8-bit and 16-bit channels.

### Programs that open EMF files

Microsoft Office and IrfanView also open EMF. Two more programs come from the fact sheet for EMF:

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- LibreOffice Draw: lists Enhanced Windows Metafile among its import formats.
- Inkscape: its format matrix lists EMF input and output support.

### EMF and PNG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .emf with image/emf, or the older image/x-emf. The .png ending names a PNG, the lossless raster format.
- **Kind**: EMF stores drawing commands. PNG is a raster picture.
- **Scaling**: EMF scales without loss. A PNG has a fixed pixel size.
- **Compression**: PNG compression is lossless, so the pixels you export are kept exactly.
- **Transparency**: PNG supports alpha transparency.
- **Bitmaps**: an EMF can embed bitmaps, while a PNG is nothing but a bitmap.
- **Typical use**: EMF serves graphics inside Windows and Office. PNG is for screenshots, logos and sharp web graphics.
- **Support**: EMF is a Windows format that records Windows GDI drawing commands, while PNG is supported by every browser.

This page cannot do the conversion. It decodes images with the browser's own image decoder, and in a test that decoder could not read an EMF, so the attempt ends in an 'Image decode failed.' error. The file stays on your device and is not changed. Use one of the programs below. Both LibreOffice Draw and Inkscape run on Windows, Mac and Linux, so you do not need Windows to open an EMF.

LibreOffice Draw's guide names PNG among the graphics formats it exports. Check any imported result against the original. A browser works for viewing the exported PNG, as do GIMP, Windows Photos and Preview on macOS. Inkscape's wiki format matrix lists EMF among the formats it can both read and write, which is why it also appears in the list of programs above. A PNG from either program is a fixed grid of pixels, so export at the size you need, since enlarging the PNG later will not restore sharp edges.

### Other ways to convert EMF to PNG

- **ImageMagick on Windows:** run `magick office-diagram.emf office-diagram.png`. The command reads the EMF and writes a PNG. The ImageMagick formats page marks EMF as readable on Windows only, with the size option supported.
- **Inkscape (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the EMF, press Shift+Ctrl+E or use File > Export PNG Image, choose the export area (Page, Drawing, Selection or Custom), set a size and a file name, and click Export.
- **LibreOffice Draw:** open the EMF, then export it as PNG. LibreOffice's guide gives no menu path for this.

### Problems with EMF files

- **A damaged file will not draw**: if a record length is damaged, the reader cannot find the next record.
- **A newer EMF looks wrong in an old program**: older EMF readers may not implement records introduced by the format's extensions.
- **Inkscape output differs from the original**: features Inkscape cannot import are lost, so compare the two.
- **Only part of a chart appears**: choose the Drawing export area in Inkscape instead of Page or Selection.
- **ImageMagick cannot read it on Mac or Linux**: EMF reading is listed as Windows only.
- **'Image decode failed.' shows on this page**: in a test the browser's decoder could not read the EMF.

faqs.question: Why does Ghostscript come up for EPS?

faqs.question: Why can't my ImageMagick read an EPS?

faqs.question: How does an EPS differ from a PDF?

guide.title: About EPS files
guide.markdown:
### What is an EPS file?

EPS stands for Encapsulated PostScript. Adobe developed it in the late 1980s for placing illustrations in printed documents. An EPS represents one rectangular graphic through PostScript instructions, and the format can combine vector drawing commands with raster images. EPS version 3 appeared in 1990, and Adobe published its separate specification in 1992. Its MIME type is application/postscript.

Because an EPS wraps a PostScript program, something has to interpret the instructions before you can see the artwork. This page reads images with your browser's decoder, or with ImageMagick for a set of formats that leaves EPS out. Its test run of an EPS failed during decoding, so the page makes no promise about converting one.

Many publishing workflows moved from EPS to PDF, though EPS remains relevant to legacy artwork. The tools in the next sections are the route to a PDF. PDF is the paged format that now does that job.

### Programs that open EPS files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- ImageMagick: reads EPS through Ghostscript, and the installed policy and delegates determine whether it is available.
- Ghostscript: interprets the PostScript instructions used by EPS.

**Windows & Mac**

- Adobe Illustrator: can open EPS or place it as linked artwork. Unfamiliar objects can be lost during import.

No browser or phone app is listed for EPS. A program that renders it needs a PostScript interpreter, and Ghostscript is the one named here.

### EPS and PDF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .eps with application/postscript, and .pdf with application/pdf.
- **Pages**: an EPS is one rectangular graphic, while a PDF is organized in pages that each mix text, vector drawing and raster images.
- **Origin**: Adobe created both. The way PDF describes a page is inherited from PostScript, and it is independent of device and resolution.
- **Transparency**: EPS cannot retain live transparency, and Adobe recommends PDF 1.4 when placing transparent artwork.
- **Fonts**: embedding the fonts is what lets a PDF look identical on every machine.
- **Standards**: the 2008 ISO 32000-1 edition standardized PDF 1.7, and a 2017 edition, ISO 32000-2, did the same for 2.0. Profiles such as PDF/A and PDF/X serve archiving and print.

Those differences are why the move from EPS to PDF is common. Which route to take depends on what you have installed.

If you only need to look at the artwork, Illustrator or Affinity Designer can show it. If you need a PDF to send on, converting once with Ghostscript is a short command. Check the result in a PDF viewer afterward, looking at the page area, the fonts and any images, since those are the places a conversion can change the artwork.

### Other ways to convert EPS to PDF

- **Ghostscript (command line):** run ps2pdf input.eps output.pdf. The usage guide explicitly allows EPS with its PostScript utility scripts. Inspect the page area and resolve missing fonts in the source.
- **Affinity Designer:** open the EPS, choose File > Export, select PDF, adjust the settings and export area, then export and save. Compare the imported artwork and the final PDF, since font and feature interpretation can affect the result. Affinity's file-format table lists EPS as importable.

Both write a new PDF and leave the EPS untouched. Ghostscript works from the command line and has no editing view, while Affinity Designer opens the artwork on a canvas first, so you can look at it before exporting. Affinity's table also notes that text is rasterized when a PDF is exported, which is worth checking if you need selectable text in the result.

### Problems with EPS files

- **No preview on a Mac**: Apple's support notes list EPS preview only for older releases such as macOS 12 and earlier, so the Preview app no longer shows it on current macOS.
- **Objects missing after opening in Illustrator**: an object the importer does not recognize is left out, so check the result against the original.
- **ImageMagick cannot render it**: the Ghostscript it relies on is missing, so the artwork cannot be drawn. Install Ghostscript and try again.
- **Transparency looks flattened**: the EPS never held it live, so the effect is flat before conversion starts.
- **This page reports Image decode failed**: the page could not read the file. Use one of the programs above.

guide.title: About EXR files
guide.markdown:
### What is an EXR file?

OpenEXR is an image format for scene-linear, high-dynamic-range imagery, hosted by the Academy Software Foundation. An EXR can carry named channels besides red, green, blue and alpha, with samples stored as half floats, full floats or unsigned integers. The display window and the region that holds the stored pixels can differ, and the pixels can be laid out in scanlines or tiles. It is used in rendering, compositing and texture work.

### Programs that open EXR files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP has read and written high-bit-depth EXR since version 2.10. Krita opens and saves EXR too, for painting and interchange.

### EXR and JPEG compared

- **Samples:** an EXR keeps floating-point values with no upper limit. A JPEG stores 8 bits per color channel.
- **Compression:** EXR offers lossless and lossy compression. JPEG is lossy and meant for viewing.
- **Channels:** extra named channels have nowhere to go in a JPEG.

The page reads the EXR with ImageMagick compiled to WebAssembly, in your browser, and reads one image. Every value brighter than white is clamped to white, so the picture stays at the exposure stored in the file. The linear values are then encoded to sRGB, because otherwise the picture would look dark. They are rounded to 8 bits before that step. No JPEG quality is chosen by the page. The page refuses anything above roughly 537 megapixels because it is too large to convert.

### Other ways to convert EXR to JPEG

- **GIMP:** open the EXR, use File > Export As, finish the name with .jpeg, and click Export. The JPEG dialog sets the quality from 0 to 100.
- **OpenImageIO:** run `oiiotool lighting.exr -o review.jpg`. Its --colorconvert option converts between color spaces before the output.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick lighting.exr -quality 91 review.jpeg` to choose the JPEG quality yourself.

### Problems with EXR files

- **It looks dark in a viewer:** scene-linear values need display processing, and treating them like a display-ready JPEG changes the appearance.
- **The crop looks wrong:** a reader may show the display window differently from the stored data window.
- **The colors shift in an editor:** color interpretation can change when an editor assigns a different working space. Krita documents OCIO and profile workflows.

guide.title: EXR to JPG: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an EXR file?

ILM created OpenEXR and released it as open source in 2003, and the Academy Software Foundation now hosts the project. It is designed for scene-linear, high-dynamic-range pixels, stored as 16-bit half floats or 32-bit floats. An EXR can hold named channels beyond red, green, blue and alpha, such as depth, and it supports scanline and tiled layouts. The window that holds stored pixels can differ from the display window.

Renderers and compositors write EXR for rendering, compositing and texture work. People convert to JPG when they need a preview to send around, because a JPG opens almost anywhere.

### Programs that open EXR files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP has imported and exported high-bit-depth EXR since version 2.10, and Krita loads and saves EXR for painting and interchange. EXR has no internal color management, so Krita assigns its default color space on loading, usually Rec 709 Linear, and the picture may change visually.

### EXR and JPG compared

EXR keeps scene values that can be brighter than white, so it can be regraded later. JPG is lossy, stores 8 bits per channel and carries no alpha channel, which suits a preview and nothing more. Treating raw linear values as a display-ready JPG changes the look, which is why this page encodes them to sRGB first. Keep the EXR as your master.

### Other ways to convert EXR to JPG

- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick render.exr render.jpg`. ImageMagick reads and writes EXR when it is built with the OpenEXR library.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux):** GIMP loads and exports basic OpenEXR files. GIMP exports a JPEG through File > Export As… once the EXR is open; a dialog then opens where you set the quality from 0 to 100.

### Problems with EXR files

- **Brightness differs from your renderer**: scene-linear values need display processing. This page encodes the linear values to sRGB and clips anything above 1.0, so check the JPG against the EXR.
- **Highlights are flat white**: values above 1.0 clip here. Lower the exposure in an EXR editor first.
- **The conversion fails**: the image may be over about 537 megapixels. Render a smaller version.
- **Colors shift in another program**: a program that assigns its own working space reads the EXR differently. Krita documents OCIO and profile workflows for this.
- **A reader shows the wrong area**: the display window and the data window can differ in an EXR.

guide.title: Understanding EXR for PNG output
guide.markdown:
### What is an EXR file?

EXR is the file extension of OpenEXR, a high-dynamic-range raster format created by Industrial Light & Magic and released as open source in 2003. It stores 16-bit half-float or 32-bit float pixel values. The project is now part of the Academy Software Foundation, and its documentation points to strong support for multi-part, multi-channel files, which is why one EXR can hold more than a single picture's worth of data.

EXR shows up in visual effects, film compositing and 3D render output. Few ordinary programs show one correctly. Because the values are scene-referred and can go above white, numbers above 1.0 are normal inside the file and do not mean it is overexposed. Treating such data like a display-ready JPEG changes how it looks, which is why a converter has to decide what to do with the bright values.

This page makes that decision for you, and the decision is described below. If you want to pick an exposure yourself, use a program that can edit floating-point images.

### Programs that open EXR files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- GIMP loads and exports OpenEXR. Version 3.1.2 added loading of multi-layer files, which show up as individual layers, and the EXR export has no settings dialog.
- Krita loads and saves EXR for paint-over work and for exchange with apps such as Blender, Nuke and Natron. EXR stores no color space, so Krita assigns a default on load, usually Rec 709 Linear.
- ImageMagick lists EXR as read and write, and its notes say it requires the OpenEXR library.

### EXR and PNG compared

- **Extensions and MIME types**: .exr for OpenEXR; .png with image/png.
- **Numbers**: EXR stores half or full floats, so values can go far above white. PNG samples are integers from 1 to 16 bits, and this page writes 8.
- **Light**: EXR holds scene-linear values. A PNG is normally display-encoded, and this page applies the sRGB encoding.
- **Channels**: EXR can carry many named channels. A PNG holds color and, optionally, alpha.
- **Compression**: PNG compression is always lossless and DEFLATE-based.
- **Alpha**: both formats can have it, and the page leaves alpha as it is.
- **Typical use**: EXR serves rendering and compositing, while a PNG is a display-ready picture that browsers show.

The page reads the EXR into an 8-bit build of ImageMagick. That build clamps each value above 1.0 as it reads, so highlights brighter than white become white and cannot be recovered afterward. After that the linear values are converted to sRGB, since otherwise the PNG would appear dark. Before the conversion each is rounded to one of 256 levels, which is why dark gradients can band. Several EXR files can be selected together, each downloading as its own PNG, and the EXR files themselves are left as they were.

### Other ways to convert EXR to PNG

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the EXR, use File > Export As, and name the file with a .png ending. The PNG dialog offers a pixel format of 8 or 16 bits per channel, with or without alpha, plus a compression level.
- **Krita (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the EXR, choose File > Export and pick PNG. Decide the color transform before you export, because Krita assigns a color space on load.
- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick render.exr preview.png`.

### Problems with EXR files

- **The picture looks dark in a viewer**: the data is linear. Convert it here to get an sRGB PNG.
- **Highlights are blown out**: values over 1.0 clip to white in this conversion. Use an editor that handles floating point to pick an exposure first.
- **Colors shift in an editor**: an editor that assigns a different working space changes color interpretation, and Krita documents an OCIO option that overrides its assigned profile.
- **Channels are missing**: a PNG holds color and alpha, so keep the EXR for passes and layers.
- **The EXR came from a 3D package**: a render can include extra named passes, and none of them reach the PNG.
- **A very large frame fails**: a header declaring above 537 megapixels makes the page report that it is too large.
- **Banding in dark areas**: this comes from the rounding to 256 levels, so a workflow with more than 8 bits suits gradients better.
- **You need more than 8 bits**: GIMP's PNG dialog offers 16 bits per channel, while this page writes 8.
- **The PNG has to go back into a render pipeline**: clipped highlights cannot be restored, so keep the EXR as the master and treat the PNG as a preview.

guide.title: Understanding F4V to MP4
guide.markdown:
### What is an F4V file?

Adobe documents F4V among files derived from the MPEG-4 container structure. It is a container rather than the H.264 video codec itself. Adobe's playback API accepts H.264 video and HE-AAC v2 audio in these files, and Adobe AIR and Flash Player 9.0.115.0 added that support. F4V playback can deliver metadata and cue-point events. Flash Player support ended in 2020, so a browser no longer plays these files. Moving an archived clip to MP4 gives current players, editors and web pages a file they can open, provided they support H.264 and AAC.

### Programs that open F4V files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg, whose MOV-family demuxer recognizes the .f4v extension, opens F4V. VLC media player reads MP4 and MOV containers and decodes H.264 and AAC, so test the particular file.

### F4V and MP4 compared

- **Video**: encoded again as H.264 with the x264 encoder.
- **Audio**: AAC at 96 kbps.
- **Dimensions**: the longer side tops out at 1920 px; rounding then takes both sides down to an even number.
- **Frame rate**: held to 30 fps, with a deinterlacing pass for interlaced frames.
- **Layout**: the MP4 index is moved to the start so playback can begin before the whole file loads.
- **Tags and tracks**: no mapping or metadata flags are passed, so FFmpeg picks the streams on its own.
- **Original**: your F4V is not changed. The download is a new file with the same name and an .mp4 ending.
- **Speed**: encoding runs in a single browser thread and has no size cap or timeout, so duration depends on your hardware.

### Other ways to convert F4V to MP4

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i archive.f4v -c copy migrated.mp4` to copy the streams without encoding again.
- **Shotcut:** open the F4V, choose File > Export Video and click Export File. The Default settings make an H.264 MP4.

### Problems with F4V files

- **An old Flash embed stops working**: Adobe blocked Flash Player content after its retirement.
- **A codec is not supported**: the archived Adobe player API covers the documented codec combinations, not every stream a container might hold.
- **Cue points are missing**: some AIR iOS playback APIs omit the metadata and cue-point events available elsewhere.

guide.title: About FLAC files
guide.markdown:
### What is a FLAC file?

The name FLAC expands to Free Lossless Audio Codec. Integer PCM goes in, a smaller stream comes out, and decoding returns the identical samples. Anyone can read the specification, and the reference code is open source. A native FLAC stream is labeled audio/flac, and the format description was issued as RFC 9639 in December 2024.

Channel counts run from one to eight and bit depths from 4 to 32. FLAC metadata can include seek points, pictures and Vorbis comments. Storage corruption can make a frame fail its checksum, since lossless encoding gives no protection against it.

Because it is lossless, FLAC is also a good source to convert from: the encoder starts with the full audio, not a file that has already been through a lossy pass. The format reference names music archiving, audiophile listening and CD backups as typical uses.

### Programs that open FLAC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports FLAC with its built-in importer, which also covers Ogg Vorbis, MP2, WAV and AIFF, so no FFmpeg add-on is needed.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player counts FLAC among its input formats and audio codecs, and AAC appears on its features page too.

### FLAC and AAC compared

- **Extensions and media types**: FLAC files end in .flac and use audio/flac; a raw AAC stream ends in .aac.
- **Compression**: FLAC is lossless. AAC is lossy, so it discards detail to make the file smaller.
- **Channels and depth**: FLAC goes up to eight channels and 32-bit samples.
- **Wrapper**: AAC can be a raw .aac stream or sit inside an MP4 container.
- **Support**: some devices lack a FLAC decoder, while AAC is widely supported.
- **Use**: AAC serves streaming audio and music downloads, audio in MP4 videos and mobile devices. FLAC serves music archiving and lossless backups of CDs.
- **Players**: VLC media player, Apple Music, Windows Media Player and any web browser open AAC.

The big change is that lossless audio turns lossy. In a worker, FFmpeg built for WebAssembly encodes the audio to AAC at 192 kbps with its own encoder and skips video streams. The page passes no option for sample rate or channel layout, so FFmpeg decides them. Several files can be chosen at once. Files are handled in turn, and every one is downloaded separately as an .aac, with no ZIP. The page sets no size limit or timeout of its own, so a long track takes as long as your device needs. Your original file is not changed, because you download a new copy. Hold on to the FLAC if you will want full quality later.

### Other ways to convert FLAC to AAC

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i album.flac -c:a aac -b:a 192k album-listen.aac`. The FFmpeg codec documentation describes its native AAC encoder as the default one, and the adts muxer writes a single AAC stream.
- **Audacity and qaac:** qaac takes WAV, so first export a WAV from Audacity: open the FLAC, choose File > Export Audio and pick WAV, whose default encoding is Signed 16-bit PCM. The dialog can export the whole project or only a selection, so you can bridge just the part you need. Then run `qaac --adts -V 90 bridge.wav -o alternate.aac`. The qaac wiki describes `--adts` as ADTS output for AAC only and `-V` as a True VBR quality scale from 0 to 127, with -V90 as the default for the LC profile. It is a Windows console tool and needs Apple Application Support.

### Problems with FLAC files

- **It will not play on a phone**: a player without a FLAC decoder cannot open the file at all. Android documents native FLAC playback that is narrower than the format itself, which makes an AAC copy the safer pick for phones.
- **A file stops partway**: a bad disk or interrupted download can break a frame's checksum, and FLAC cannot repair that. Transfer the file again.
- **The FLAC came from an MP3 or AAC**: such a FLAC is only a bigger file, and the earlier loss stays. Converting it to AAC adds a second lossy pass.
- **The FLAC takes a lot of room**: the format reference says FLAC typically halves uncompressed audio, which is still bulky beside a lossy copy.
- **You need full quality**: AAC is lossy, so pick FLAC again if you need the audio for editing or archiving.

guide.title: About FLAC files
guide.markdown:
### What is a FLAC file?

Free Lossless Audio Codec, or FLAC, squeezes integer PCM audio and returns every sample on decoding, since nothing about the samples is discarded. Its specification is public and the reference code is open source; December 2024 saw the format description published as RFC 9639. A native FLAC stream carries the media type audio/flac.

A FLAC can hold between one and eight channels at depths from four to 32 bits per sample. Seek points, embedded pictures and Vorbis comments live in its metadata blocks. Lossless coding cannot stop a damaged frame from failing its checksum when the storage corrupts it.

A FLAC makes a good source for a conversion, since the converter begins with the complete audio and not with something a lossy pass has already trimmed. Bit depth matters for this pair, because the AIFF written here is 16-bit. The format reference lists music archiving, audiophile listening and CD rips kept lossless as typical uses, and says FLAC typically shrinks files to about half the size of uncompressed audio.

### Programs that open FLAC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports FLAC with its built-in importer, so the optional FFmpeg library is not needed.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player lists FLAC as both an input format and an audio codec.

### FLAC and AIFF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .flac with audio/flac on one side, .aiff with audio/aiff or audio/x-aiff on the other.
- **Compression**: FLAC is lossless compression. AIFF often carries uncompressed linear PCM, and its AIFF-C extension can hold compressed audio.
- **Size**: expect the AIFF to dwarf the FLAC, because uncompressed PCM takes more storage than a packed copy.
- **Support**: Audacity reads FLAC directly and imports most AIFF files, all PCM variants among them, with no optional FFmpeg library.
- **Metadata**: FLAC stores Vorbis comments and pictures, while AIFF can add named chunks holding author, copyright and annotation text.
- **Use**: AIFF turns up in masters and intermediate recordings made by professional audio users, while FLAC turns up in music archives.
- **Origin**: Apple built AIFF as an audio wrapper from Electronic Arts' IFF family. Its AIFF 1.3 specification carries the date January 4, 1989.

Two things change: how the audio is stored, and on this page the bit depth. FFmpeg built for WebAssembly decodes your FLAC, leaves out any video stream, and writes signed 16-bit big-endian PCM inside an AIFF wrapper. The page passes no sample-rate or channel option, which leaves both to FFmpeg. A FLAC at 16 bits comes through sample for sample, and a deeper one is cut to 16. You download a new copy and your original stays untouched; a long file takes whatever time your device needs.

### Other ways to convert FLAC to AIFF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i master.flac master-work.aiff`, and FFmpeg picks the AIFF muxer from the extension. FFmpeg's general documentation lists AIFF muxing and demuxing, as well as FLAC.
- **SoX:** run `sox master.flac master-working.aiff`. The SoX manual says the file type comes from the file extension, so the .aiff name in the command is what selects the output format. Its format page says FLAC support is optional and that its AIFF support does not include multiple audio chunks.

### Problems with FLAC files

- **It will not open in my program**: not every program reads FLAC. Convert to AIFF here, or open the file in VLC or Audacity.
- **The file is cut off**: storage errors can break a frame's checksum, and lossless coding cannot undo damage to the file. Download or copy it again from wherever it came from, then convert the fresh copy.
- **The FLAC was made from an MP3**: the detail that MP3 discarded is gone, and the AIFF stays just as limited.
- **A player rejects an AIFF-C file**: its compression scheme may be one the player lacks, because the family name alone proves nothing about support. This page writes plain PCM.
- **ID3 tags are absent in the AIFF**: FFmpeg's AIFF muxer writes ID3v2 tags only when its write_id3v2 option is enabled, and the command used here does not enable it. Raw PCM muxers in FFmpeg store no metadata at all.
- **The AIFF is huge**: nothing in it is compressed. Store the FLAC and use the AIFF only while editing.

guide.title: Understanding FLAC to ALAC
guide.markdown:
### What is a FLAC file?

No sample information is thrown away when FLAC compresses integer PCM audio. The specification and the reference implementation are both open, and the IETF published the format as RFC 9639 in December 2024. Streams can have anywhere from one to eight channels at depths of four to 32 bits. A native FLAC stream uses the audio/flac media type, and the metadata blocks can hold seek points, cover pictures and Vorbis comments.

Those metadata blocks are why a FLAC can carry artwork, and why the cover picture needs separate handling during conversion. Because FLAC is lossless, decoding gives back the samples that went in, which is the reason this conversion can keep the sound identical. A damaged frame can still fail its checksum, since lossless encoding does not prevent storage corruption.

### Programs that open FLAC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity reads FLAC without an FFmpeg add-on. VLC accepts FLAC as input, and FFplay plays it using the decoders built into your FFmpeg.
- **Web:** Mozilla Firefox decodes FLAC audio, and Google Chrome's FLAC decoding is listed in Mozilla's browser support comparison.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android brings over the desktop player's decoders, while VLC for iOS has its own player for local media.

### FLAC and ALAC compared

ALAC is Apple's lossless audio codec. It is a codec, not a standalone file format, and it usually sits inside an MPEG-4 container. Apple's reference implementation supports 16-, 20-, 24- and 32-bit samples, one to eight channels and integer sample rates through 384,000 Hz, and Apple distributes source for both encoding and decoding. Lossless listening in Apple Music is built on Apple Lossless audio technology, and the lossless downloads need more device storage than compressed ones. Nondefault ALAC packet sizes are not guaranteed to work on every supporting hardware device, and some Mac playback setups need an external DAC for sample rates above 48 kHz, so test one converted track on the device that matters. Apple's alacconvert utility implements fewer channel and file-layout combinations than the codec itself, so it is no test of whether your file is valid.

This page runs FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly in your browser. The `-acodec alac` setting selects the Apple Lossless encoder, and `-f ipod` writes an MPEG-4 audio container. The container is MPEG-4 audio, the family .m4a files belong to, so the download is named .m4a. `-vn` leaves out video streams, and FFmpeg holds a FLAC's embedded cover picture as one, so artwork is not carried over.

No sample rate, bit depth or channel option is passed, so those follow your source. No `-map` is set either, so FFmpeg's defaults choose the streams, and the title and artist tags are normally carried across. Because both formats are lossless, the sound is the same, and the things that change are the codec, the container and the cover picture.

### Other ways to convert FLAC to ALAC

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i album.flac -vn -c:a alac album.m4a` selects Apple Lossless and uses the usual MPEG-4 audio name, as this page does. FFmpeg's codec list shows encoding and decoding support for both FLAC and ALAC. Keep `-vn`: in a test, a FLAC with an embedded cover picture failed to convert without it, because FFmpeg treated the picture as a video stream the MPEG-4 audio file could not hold.

### Problems with FLAC files

**The file is damaged.** A corrupt frame can fail its checksum, and lossless encoding does not protect against storage corruption. Copy the file again or re-rip it before you decide ALAC cannot hold it.

**The source was lossy.** A lossy file turned into FLAC has already lost its detail, and ALAC cannot bring it back. If a FLAC came from an MP3, keep expectations to that level and find the original if you can.

**It does not play on Android.** Android's documented native FLAC support covers less than the format does: mono or stereo, with 16-bit samples recommended. A multichannel or high-depth file may need a different player.

**The cover art is gone.** The conversion leaves out the embedded picture. Put the artwork back in your music app or tag editor, and keep the FLAC files until you have checked the migrated library.

guide.title: Understanding FLAC for M4A output
guide.markdown:
### What is a FLAC file?

FLAC, the Free Lossless Audio Codec, compresses audio without losing information, so decoding returns exactly the samples that went in. Its format description is RFC 9639, published in December 2024 as a Standards Track document. Streams can carry from one up to eight channels, at four to 32 bits per sample. Its metadata blocks can carry seek points, pictures and Vorbis comments, and the Vorbis comment block is where title, artist and album tags live.

People keep FLAC for ripped CDs, music archives and purchases from lossless stores. It is the master copy, and the usual reason to convert is to get a file that plays on a phone or a player that doesn't take FLAC.

Lossless doesn't mean indestructible. Each frame ends with a 16-bit CRC, and the stream info block stores an MD5 checksum of the audio, so a decoder can detect errors in the data. Detecting damage is not the same as repairing it. A FLAC made from an MP3 or another lossy source also holds only that source's sound, since samples that were thrown away cannot be recreated.

### Programs that open FLAC files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Audacity lists FLAC among the formats it imports as shipped, with no need for the optional FFmpeg library.
- VLC media player lists FLAC among the audio it plays.
- FFplay, the player from the FFmpeg project, decodes FLAC through FFmpeg's decoders.

**Web:**

- Mozilla's codec guide lists FLAC support in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Opera and Safari.

**Mobile:**

- Android's media documentation lists FLAC in .flac files, in mono or stereo only, with 16-bit samples recommended.

### FLAC and M4A compared

- **Extensions and MIME types**: .flac with audio/flac; .m4a with audio/mp4 for sound without pictures.
- **Compression**: FLAC is lossless. The M4A here is lossy AAC, because the page asks FFmpeg for its aac encoder.
- **Bitrate**: this page encodes AAC at 192 kbps for every file.
- **Container**: .m4a is an MPEG-4 audio-only file, that follows the ISO base media file format, organized in boxes. According to the Library of Congress, Apple took up the extension for files without copy protection. It can hold lossless ALAC too, but this page doesn't write it.
- **Metadata**: FLAC uses Vorbis comments. The page maps nothing itself, so FFmpeg's defaults decide what carries over.
- **Pictures**: FLAC can embed a picture. The page's command disables video, so don't count on artwork arriving in the M4A.

Converting is a one-way trade of exactness for a different format. You can't recover the FLAC from the M4A. The page also uses one fixed bitrate for every file, so a quiet spoken-word FLAC and a dense orchestral one both come out at 192 kbps. You can select several FLAC files; the files are handled sequentially, and every M4A downloads separately, without a ZIP.

### Other ways to convert FLAC to M4A

- **FFmpeg (command line):** use `ffmpeg -i master.flac -c:a aac -b:a 192k portable-copy.m4a`. FFmpeg's format table lists FLAC decoding and AAC encoding with its internal encoder. The command makes AAC, not ALAC.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** import the FLAC, choose File > Export Audio and select M4A (AAC) Files (FFmpeg) as the format. The manual says FFmpeg is required for AAC export and isn't shipped with Audacity. Its bit rate setting is not always honored, according to the same page.

### Problems with FLAC files

- **Won't play on a device**: Android documents FLAC playback as mono or stereo, and recommends 16-bit samples. Convert to M4A for devices that balk.
- **A damaged frame**: a FLAC frame can fail its CRC check. Lossless coding doesn't protect against corruption on disk, so keep a backup.
- **A cut-short or damaged FLAC**: FFmpeg usually reports the error and saves the part it could decode, so the M4A may end up shorter than the original.
- **The M4A sounds worse**: AAC is lossy. If you can hear the difference, keep the FLAC and use it as the source.
- **The source was already lossy**: FLAC made from an MP3 holds only that MP3's sound. Converting it again adds a second loss.
- **Tags are missing**: check the M4A in your player and re-enter them in a tag editor.
- **A very large file**: the page sets no size limit, but the work happens locally, so a long album track simply takes more time on a slow phone.
- **A renamed file**: calling a FLAC .m4a changes the label, not the data. Convert it.
- **You wanted lossless M4A**: this page writes AAC. For Apple Lossless you need a tool that offers ALAC, and the FFmpeg command above won't make it.

guide.title: About FLAC files
guide.markdown:
### What is a FLAC file?

FLAC stands for Free Lossless Audio Codec. It compresses integer PCM audio without discarding any sample information, so decoding gives back exactly what went in. December 2024 brought RFC 9639, which standardized the format description. The specification is open, and the reference implementation is open source.

A FLAC stream holds one to eight channels at sample depths of 4 to 32 bits. Metadata blocks can carry seek points, pictures such as album art, and Vorbis comments for tags, and the media type is audio/flac. It suits music archiving, audiophile listening and lossless CD backups, since the files are about half the size of uncompressed audio and lose nothing.

### Programs that open FLAC files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- foobar2000 and Apple Music: also open FLAC.
- VLC media player: FLAC is on its list of input formats.
- Audacity: reads FLAC on its own; the optional FFmpeg library isn't needed.
- ffplay: the FFmpeg player, which plays FLAC through FFmpeg decoders.

**Web**

- Firefox decodes FLAC, and Chrome lists FLAC decoding in Mozilla's browser support comparison.

**Mobile**

- On Android and iOS, VLC opens FLAC files as they are, without converting.

### FLAC and WAV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .flac and audio/flac; .wav, with audio/wav and audio/x-wav in common use.
- **What they are**: FLAC is a codec with its own stream format. WAV is a RIFF-based wrapper for sound that can carry several encodings.
- **Fidelity**: both keep every sample. FLAC compresses without discarding any, and the linear PCM in a WAV is exact, so neither is a lossy format.
- **Compression**: FLAC compresses. WAV usually holds linear PCM, which is uncompressed, although compressed encodings can appear too.
- **Bit depth**: FLAC covers 4 to 32 bits. This converter writes 16-bit PCM.
- **Metadata**: FLAC uses Vorbis comments and can embed pictures. WAV uses INFO chunks, and Broadcast WAVE adds production and preservation metadata.
- **Size**: FLAC typically halves the size of the audio. WAV has a 4 GB file size limit, and very large recordings need RF64.
- **Use**: for digital audio collections the Library of Congress recommends WAVE.

WAV opens in Audacity, VLC media player, Windows Media Player and any web browser, which is part of why it works as a common handoff format. The conversion changes the packing and fixes the depth at 16 bits: FFmpeg in your browser decodes the FLAC and writes 16-bit PCM into the WAV. A 16-bit source loses nothing, while a 24-bit source drops to 16 bits.

### Other ways to convert FLAC to WAV

- **flac command-line tool:** run `flac -d album-track.flac`. Decoding creates a WAV by default. The flac tool reads FLAC natively.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the FLAC, choose File > Export Audio, pick WAV and choose the PCM encoding you need. The Encoding menu defaults to Signed 16-bit PCM.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i album-track.flac -c:a pcm_s24le album-track.wav` for 24-bit PCM output. Pick the encoding that matches your source.

### Problems with FLAC files

- **A device won't play it**: Android's documented native FLAC support covers mono or stereo and recommends 16-bit samples, which is less than the format allows. VLC for Android copes with more.
- **The file reports an error or skips**: FLAC checks each frame, so damage shows up as a checksum failure. Lossless coding can't protect against a bad disk or a broken download, so copy the file again.
- **The music sounds the same as an MP3**: if the FLAC was made from a lossy file, the removed samples are gone for good. A FLAC is only as good as what went into it.
- **A program needs WAV**: convert here, or in Audacity if you need to choose the encoding.
- **The WAV is too big to store or send**: WAV is large but exact. Keep the FLAC for storage, which is about half the size, and make the WAV only when a program needs it.
- **The WAV stops at 4 GB**: that is the original limit of the format. For a recording that long, use a tool that writes RF64.
- **Some tags are missing in the WAV**: A WAV has no Vorbis comments, so some fields may have nowhere to go. Keep the FLAC, and tag the WAV in your editor.

guide.title: About FLAC files
guide.markdown:
### What is a FLAC file?

FLAC stores integer PCM audio and compresses it without losing any sample information. The specification is open, the reference encoder is open source, and RFC 9639 standardized the format description in December 2024. Channels run from one to eight and sample depths from four to 32 bits, and metadata blocks can store seek points, cover pictures and Vorbis comments. The media type is audio/flac. It is used for music archiving and lossless backups of CDs.

### Programs that open FLAC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity opens FLAC natively, with no FFmpeg add-on required. VLC media player lists FLAC among its inputs, and FFplay decodes it through FFmpeg.
- **Web:** Firefox decodes FLAC, and Mozilla's browser support comparison also lists Chrome.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android and VLC for iOS.

### FLAC and WMA compared

- **Compression:** FLAC is lossless. The WMA made here is lossy.
- **Container:** WMA is stored in Microsoft's ASF container.
- **Variants:** a .wma name alone does not say which kind of Windows Media Audio a file holds.
- **Use:** WMA serves Windows media libraries and older portable music players.

An FFmpeg WebAssembly build handles the conversion on your device. It encodes with wmav2, the standard WMA codec, at 192 kbps and discards any video stream, so the result is lossy and not WMA Lossless. No stream or tag mapping is passed, so FFmpeg's defaults pick the streams and copy the global tags.

### Other ways to convert FLAC to WMA

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i album.flac -b:a 160k -c:a wmav2 album.wma` for the same codec at a different bitrate.
- **WavePad for Windows:** open the FLAC with File > Open, choose File > Save As and pick WMA as the format. WavePad saves WMA only on Windows.

### Problems with FLAC files

- **A player rejects it:** Android's documented native FLAC playback covers less than the format does: it expects mono or stereo audio, and 16-bit samples are recommended.
- **A damaged frame:** it can fail its checksum. Lossless coding does not prevent storage corruption.
- **A FLAC made from a lossy source:** turning a lossy file into FLAC does not bring back the audio data the lossy encoder threw away.

guide.title: About FLV files
guide.markdown:
### What is an FLV file?

FLV is a binary format associated with Macromedia Flash video delivery. FLV allows no more than one picture track and one sound track. Pictures use Sorenson or On2 VP6, sound uses MP3, PCM or ADPCM. ActionScript in a Flash SWF could point to a separate FLV file. Adobe ended Flash Player support on 31 December 2020, yet saved lectures and downloaded clips still sit around as FLV files.

### Programs that open FLV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player lists FLV input along with Sorenson and VP6-family decoding, and FFplay uses FFmpeg decoders for FLV.
- **Mobile:** Android gets the desktop player's decoding features through VLC for Android, while VLC for iOS bypasses the system player for local files.

### FLV and AVI compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .flv; .avi, which goes with video/x-msvideo.
- **Container**: FLV was built for Flash delivery and carries a single video and a single audio stream. AVI is a RIFF file that Microsoft introduced in 1992 to interleave video and audio.
- **Codecs**: an AVI may hold raw, lossless or lossy pictures, which is why the extension never reveals what a player must decode.

The output is MPEG-4 video tagged Xvid with no B-frames, plus MP3 audio at 96 kbps. Interlaced frames are cleaned up, any side over 1920 px is shrunk to fit with even dimensions, and 30 fps is the ceiling. Everything runs in your browser, and your file stays on your device.

### Other ways to convert FLV to AVI

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i lecture.flv -c:v mpeg4 -q:v 4 -c:a libmp3lame lecture.avi` to choose the quality scale yourself. It re-encodes both streams.

### Problems with FLV files

Adobe retired Flash Player, so hunting for a copy of it will not help with an old FLV. Use a player that ships decoders of its own, such as VLC.

The FLV extension does not identify a single video codec; a reader also needs the decoder for the stream. A player that opens the file but shows no picture is missing that decoder.

FLV offers one audio stream, so alternative language tracks have nowhere to go inside it.

When the AVI is ready, watch for lip-sync drift and readable screen text, and keep the FLV until you have checked.

guide.title: About FLV and MOV
guide.markdown:
### What is an FLV file?

Macromedia's Flash video delivery gave us FLV, a binary container. The picture is typically Sorenson or On2 VP6, and the sound is MP3, PCM or ADPCM. Through ActionScript, a Flash SWF could point at an outside FLV, which is why many clips sat in separate files.

Adobe stopped supporting Flash Player at the close of 2020, yet the recordings live on in archives, interview downloads and course libraries. The .flv ending names no codec, so a program also needs whichever decoder the stream inside requires.

### Programs that open FLV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player handles FLV, with Sorenson and VP6 decoding on its feature list. FFplay decodes through FFmpeg.
- **Mobile:** On phones, the Android port of VLC shares the desktop player's decoding, and VLC for iOS opens local files in its own player.

### FLV and MOV compared

- **Origin**: FLV is a Flash-era delivery format. MOV is Apple's QuickTime container, built from atoms.
- **Codecs**: a MOV may carry H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG pictures beside AAC or PCM sound.
- **Support**: MOV works best in Apple's own software and many editors; for the web, MP4 travels further.
- **Types**: video/quicktime for MOV.

Here the FLV is decoded and new H.264 video goes into the MOV with AAC sound at 96 kbps. Anything over 1920 px shrinks to fit, 30 fps is the frame-rate ceiling, and frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced first. The result is an access copy for watching or sharing, not an editing master.

### Other ways to convert FLV to MOV

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i interview.flv -c:v libx264 -c:a aac interview.mov` makes an H.264 and AAC MOV. FFmpeg lists FLV and MOV for both reading and writing, takes the output format from the .mov extension, and gets H.264 from the external library libx264.

### Problems with FLV files

- **The FLV won't play**: the stream may need a decoder your player lacks. Try VLC rather than hunting for a Flash Player download.
- **The editor refuses the MOV**: a QuickTime file can use codecs that the destination editor lacks. Check which codecs it imports before converting again.
- **Soft picture**: Flash-era video was often small and heavily compressed, and the MOV can't be sharper than the FLV it came from.
- **Several audio tracks**: the one-audio-stream FLV model cannot keep alternative audio tracks, so none are waiting to be recovered.

guide.title: About FLV and MP3
guide.markdown:
### What is an FLV file?

Flash Video, or FLV, is a container format created by Macromedia and later Adobe for delivering video through Flash Player. A single FLV carries no more than one video stream plus one audio stream. Its video is Sorenson or On2 VP6, and its sound may be MP3, PCM or ADPCM. A Flash SWF can point at a standalone FLV via ActionScript.

Support for Flash Player ended on December 31, 2020, which leaves FLV a legacy format. Older web video and archived Flash content is where you still meet it. The .flv ending does not identify a unique video codec, so two FLV files can need different decoders.

### Programs that open FLV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** playback is covered by VLC media player, which lists FLV input plus Sorenson and VP6-family decoding, and by FFplay, which uses FFmpeg decoders for FLV.
- **Phones and tablets:** VLC exists for Android and for iOS, and both open files stored on the device.

Reinstalling Flash Player is not a way to play an old FLV, since it is discontinued.

### FLV and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .flv for Flash Video; .mp3 for MP3.
- **What it holds**: an FLV is a video container with at most one video and one audio stream. An MP3 is audio only.
- **Compression**: sound inside an FLV may be MP3, PCM or ADPCM; the MP3 you get is lossy either way, with constant or variable bitrate possible.
- **Tags**: an MP3 stores metadata as ID3 tags.
- **Typical uses**: an MP3 suits music libraries and downloads, podcasts, and audio for portable players, which is why pulling the sound out of an old Flash clip often ends in this format.
- **Playback**: an MP3 plays on nearly every device and in any web browser, whereas an FLV needs a player with the right decoders.
- **Standards**: MP3 is MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III, standardized by MPEG as ISO/IEC 11172-3, with major contributions from the Fraunhofer Society. It can use constant or variable bitrate.

Here is what happens when you convert, step by step. A worker in your browser runs FFmpeg as WebAssembly. It reads the FLV, ignores the video and has the LAME encoder write an MP3 with a requested rate of 192 kbps, which LAME lowers for sources with a low sample rate. Even when the FLV's sound was already MP3, it is decoded and encoded again, not copied. The file picker accepts .flv files only. The MP3 is named after your file, with the .mp3 extension, and your FLV is not changed.

Because of that second encode, the MP3 is not a bit-for-bit copy of the original sound. Several files can be queued together. They run one by one, and each finished MP3 downloads on its own, with no ZIP. If you only need the picture, use the [FLV to MP4 converter](/flv-to-mp4/) instead.

### Other ways to convert FLV to MP3

- **FFmpeg (command line):** the command is `ffmpeg -i archive.flv -vn -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k archive.mp3`. FFmpeg's documentation lists FLV among the formats it demuxes, and the FLV needs an audio stream.
- **GStreamer (command line):** use `gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location=archive.flv ! decodebin ! audioconvert ! audioresample ! lamemp3enc ! filesink location=archive.mp3`. Its flvdemux element demuxes FLV files, decodebin builds the decoding pipeline, and lamemp3enc writes the MP3.

### Problems with FLV files

- **The FLV does not play**: the extension does not identify the codec, and Sorenson or VP6 video needs a decoder. Try VLC, not a Flash Player reinstall.
- **No MP3 appears**: the FLV may have no audio track, in which case the converter shows an FFmpeg failure message.
- **The MP3 has no title or artist**: the FLV probably carried none, since FFmpeg copies the FLV's tags where MP3 has fields for them. Add them in a tag editor.
- **You need several audio tracks**: an FLV holds one audio stream, so a workflow with alternative audio tracks cannot keep that structure inside it.
- **The picture is gone and you want it**: an MP3 holds sound only. Go back to the FLV, or convert it to MP4.
- **A Flash page can't find its video**: a SWF can point to a separate FLV file, so move the FLV and the SWF together.

guide.title: About FLV files
guide.markdown:
### What is an FLV file?

FLV is a binary format created at Macromedia for delivering Flash video, later maintained by Adobe. One file can carry only a single video stream and a single audio stream. Video is usually Sorenson or On2 VP6, with MP3, PCM or ADPCM for sound. Flash movies in SWF files could pull in a separate FLV through ActionScript.

Flash Player support from Adobe stopped on December 31, 2020, so the browser plug-in that once played these files no longer exists. FLV lives on as older web video and as archived Flash content. Nothing in the extension tells you which codec is inside, and a program needs the matching decoder to show the picture.

### Programs that open FLV files

**Linux, Mac, Windows, Android and iOS**

- VLC media player: lists FLV (Flash) among its input formats, and its video decoders include Sorenson and On2 VP6.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- mpv: opens FLV files.

### FLV and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and standards**: .flv for Flash Video, .mp4 for MPEG-4 Part 14, which is ISO/IEC 14496-14, first published in 2003. MP4's media types are video/mp4 and audio/mp4.
- **Streams**: an FLV is limited to one video and one audio stream. MP4 is a container for several codecs.
- **Codecs**: the usual FLV contents are Sorenson or VP6 video with MP3, PCM or ADPCM sound. This page writes H.264 and AAC, the common MP4 pair.
- **Streaming**: FLV was designed for streaming. The MP4 written here has its index placed first (the faststart option), so playback can begin before the download ends.
- **Players**: FLV opens in VLC and mpv today. Every major browser plays MP4, depending on the codecs inside.

Converting trades the original encoding for a format that current software expects. The video is decoded and encoded again, so quality drops a little, the audio becomes AAC at 96 kbps, and the settings are fixed: the ultrafast preset at CRF 32, shrunk to fit 1920 px and held to 30 fps at most.

### Other ways to convert FLV to MP4

- **FFmpeg stream copy (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i input.flv -c copy output.mp4`. This moves the streams into an MP4 without re-encoding them, so it is fast and loses nothing. It only works when MP4 can carry the source codecs: in a test, an FLV with H.264 video copied, but one with Sorenson video was refused.
- **FFmpeg transcoding (command line):** the command `ffmpeg -i input.flv -c:a aac -c:v libx264 output.mp4` encodes new H.264 and AAC streams, so both the picture and the sound are re-encoded.
- **HandBrake (desktop app):** open the FLV with the Open Source button, pick a preset such as Fast 1080p30, make sure the container is MP4, type a file name in Save As and press Start. HandBrake can open web videos in FLV and create MP4 files.

### Problems with FLV files

- **An old web page won't play its video**: the Flash player is retired. Convert the FLV itself; the MP4 doesn't bring back the page's Flash interface.
- **Stream copy fails or gives an MP4 that won't play**: the FLV's codecs aren't ones MP4 carries. Re-encode with this converter or the transcoding command.
- **The picture is smaller than the source**: a frame wider or taller than 1920 px is scaled down to fit, and an odd dimension loses a pixel. Keep the FLV if you need the exact original dimensions.
- **Motion looks less smooth**: a source above 30 fps is brought down to 30. Keep the FLV if the original timing matters. A clip at 25 or 30 fps is not affected.
- **The MP4 has no sound**: check whether the FLV had an audio stream. Play it in VLC first; a conversion can't add sound that was never there.
- **A SWF file won't play**: an old Flash movie (SWF) loaded its FLV through ActionScript. Converting the FLV does not rebuild that movie, so only the video comes across.
- **The FLV plays with no picture**: the video codec may be one your player has no decoder for. Try VLC, which decodes Sorenson and VP6.
- **A partial FLV gives a short MP4**: a download cut off midway has no data past that point, so the MP4 ends there too. Fetch the whole file again.

guide.title: About FLV files
guide.markdown:
### What is an FLV file?

Macromedia's Flash video delivery relied on FLV, a binary format. No more than one video and one audio stream fit in an FLV: Sorenson or On2 VP6 pictures, with MP3, PCM or ADPCM sound. A Flash SWF can reference a separate FLV through ActionScript. Adobe stopped supporting Flash Player on December 31, 2020, which leaves FLV mostly in older web video and Flash archives.

### Programs that open FLV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player lists FLV input and decodes Sorenson and the VP6 family. FFplay opens FLV through FFmpeg decoders.
- **Mobile:** phones run VLC through its Android and iOS ports.

### FLV and MPEG compared

- **Streams:** an FLV has one video stream and one audio stream. In an MPEG file, MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 video and audio share a program stream.
- **Names:** MPEG is another name for MPG, and .mpeg and .mpg are interchangeable.
- **Use:** MPEG video was the basis of VCD and DVD discs, and the format is now dated.
- **Quality:** lossy MPEG encoding drops some detail.

Your browser runs FFmpeg as WebAssembly to re-encode the video as MPEG-2 at quality scale 6, with MP2 audio at 96 kbps. A frame whose longer side tops 1920 pixels shrinks, and a rate above 30 fps is cut by dropping frames. A larger frame shrinks, a faster source has frames dropped, and a smaller or slower source is not scaled up or sped up. Width and height are floored to even values, so an odd size gives up one pixel.

### Other ways to convert FLV to MPEG

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i lesson.flv -c:a mp2 -c:v mpeg2video -q:v 4 lesson.mpeg` to name the encoders and a different quality. FFmpeg reads FLV and writes MPEG-PS, MPEG-2 video and MP2 audio.

### Problems with FLV files

- **The video stops early:** an interrupted download leaves a file that opens but ends short. Compare its length with the original.
- **Flash Player will not help:** Adobe discontinued Flash Player, so reinstalling it will not make an old FLV play.
- **A player cannot decode it:** the .flv name does not say which video codec is inside, so the player needs that stream's decoder as well.
- **Several audio tracks:** a workflow that needs alternative audio tracks cannot keep them inside the one-audio-stream FLV model.

Macromedia built FLV, a binary format, for delivering Flash video. A file carries one video stream and one audio stream at most. Video is Sorenson or On2 VP6, and audio is MP3, PCM or ADPCM. - **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player decodes FLV with Sorenson and VP6-family video, and FFplay plays it through FFmpeg's decoders.

- **Playback:** Flash Player no longer runs Flash content. Ruffle is an emulator that plays SWF.

Conversion happens locally with FFmpeg's WebAssembly build. The command names no video or audio encoder for the SWF, so FFmpeg's defaults decide: Sorenson Spark video at 200 kbit/s and MP3 audio. A larger frame shrinks and a faster source has frames dropped, while a smaller or slower one is not scaled up or sped up. An odd width or height gives up one pixel.

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i legacy.flv -ar 44100 -c:a libmp3lame -c:v flv legacy.swf`. The SWF muxer takes FLV1 video and MP3 audio at 11025, 22050 or 44100 Hz, and `-ar 44100` picks the highest.

### FLV and WMV compared

- **Container**: a .wmv file is Windows Media content inside ASF, a container designed for synchronized media storage and network delivery.
- **Codecs**: Windows Media Video 7, 8 and 9 all fit the extension, so the extension alone doesn't say which one you hold.
- **Types**: video/x-ms-wmv is what the Library of Congress records for WMV, since IANA has no registration.

FFmpeg picks the codecs for the .wmv here: MS-MPEG4 v3 for the picture, which is not Windows Media Video, and WMA v2 for the sound. Its default bitrates stay in place, so fine lettering and busy scenes blur. Deinterlacing comes first, then oversized pictures shrink and a fast source is thinned without being shortened. Several files run one after another with no size or time limit.

### Other ways to convert FLV to WMV

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i lesson.flv lesson.wmv`. FFmpeg lists Flash Video and ASF for both reading and writing, and it takes the output format from the .wmv extension, so no codec options are needed.

### Problems with FLV files

- **Player coverage**: In FFmpeg's documentation the Windows Media Video 9 decoder is not marked as completely working, so test the WMV in the player that will use it.
- **Quality**: the WMV ending alone does not establish image quality. It depends on the codec and compression settings.
- **A reader is not a decoder**: a program may read ASF without having every codec inside it, so a WMV can open and still show no picture.
- **Another generation of loss**: start each attempt from the FLV, not from a previous WMV.

guide.title: About GIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a GIF file?

CompuServe produced the Graphics Interchange Format in 1987; people call it GIF. It packs data with lossless LZW coding and gives each frame a palette of up to 256 colors. It also offers simple animation and 1-bit transparency.

A single GIF can hold several frames, which is how a simple animation is stored. Transparency here means one palette entry is declared fully clear, so there is no partial opacity. A disposal setting on each frame controls how the next image covers the one before it.

People use GIFs as brief looping animations, small graphics and icons, reaction images and stickers. The AVI side is a RIFF-based video container that arrived with Windows in 1992, and you meet it in video archives and legacy desktop editing.

### Programs that open GIF files

Any web browser, Preview on macOS, Windows Photos and GIMP open GIF files. Sorted by platform, the format's fact sheet names these:

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- GIMP: writes still pictures or multilayer animations.
- ImageMagick: reads GIF; ask your install which formats it supports.

**Web and Mobile**

- Google Chrome: GIF display.

**Web**

- Mozilla Firefox: GIF display.

**Mobile**

- Safari: GIF display.

For the AVI you get, ffplay and mpv play it on Windows, Mac and Linux, Adobe Premiere opens AVI on Windows and Mac, and VLC plays it on Android and iOS.

### GIF and AVI compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .gif for GIF; .avi for AVI, commonly labeled video/x-msvideo.
- **Kind**: GIF is a raster image format with simple animation. AVI is a video container that can hold many different codecs.
- **Compression**: GIF uses lossless LZW with at most 256 colors per frame. The AVI from this page holds MPEG-4 video, which is lossy.
- **Looping**: GIFs are typically used as short looping animations. This page passes no loop setting to the AVI.
- **Transparency**: GIF has 1-bit transparency. The AVI is yuv420p video, and that pixel format carries no alpha.
- **Typical use**: GIFs are reaction images and stickers. AVI turns up in older Windows video, capture output and archives.

Inside your browser, a WebAssembly build of FFmpeg does the encoding. It writes MPEG-4 video tagged xvid at a fixed -q:v 10 with B-frames off, and MP3 at 96 kbps is named in the command as well. No GIF side goes past 1920 pixels, and a side that is odd gets trimmed by a pixel. The AVI never exceeds 30 fps, so a quicker GIF sheds frames but plays for the same length of time. No stream mapping is passed. The upload never happens, the GIF stays untouched, and the result is saved as the same name ending in .avi. With a batch of GIFs, the page converts them one after another, each into its own AVI. There is no cap on file size from this page.

### Other ways to convert GIF to AVI

- **FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `ffmpeg -i reaction-loop.gif -c:v mpeg4 -q:v 5 reaction-clip.avi` for MPEG-4 video at a -q:v value you choose. FFmpeg's manual describes the -q:v scale as codec-dependent.
- **ImageMagick plus FFmpeg (command line):** run `magick diagram-motion.gif -coalesce diagram-frame-%04d.png`, then `ffmpeg -framerate 10 -i diagram-frame-%04d.png -c:v mpeg4 diagram-motion.avi` to control the frame rate yourself. The -coalesce option expands the frames into full images first.

### Problems with GIF files

- **Gradients look banded**: what GIMP writes as GIF is limited to 256 colors at most, so smooth gradients can shift.
- **Soft edges turn jagged**: a GIF cannot hold partial opacity along a soft transparent edge.
- **Frames overlap wrongly**: disposal choices determine what an earlier image leaves behind, so pick combine or replace to suit the animation.
- **A GIF comment is missing**: GIMP leaves out a comment containing characters beyond seven-bit ASCII.
- **Colors differ in the AVI**: lossy video at a fixed quality cannot match the GIF pixel for pixel.
- **The AVI is bigger than the GIF**: in a test, a tiny GIF became a larger AVI. The page sets no size target.
- **The AVI does not loop**: no loop setting is passed. Loop it in your player.
- **There is no sound**: the GIF is silent, and the test AVI had no audio stream.
- **An editor will not open the AVI**: an editor may recognize AVI but not include the decoder a given file needs. Play it in ffplay, mpv or VLC to check the file.
- **The speed looks different**: the AVI never runs above 30 fps, so a faster GIF loses frames and cannot be matched exactly.

guide.title: Understanding GIF to AVIF
guide.markdown:
### What is a GIF file?

GIF is a raster image format introduced by CompuServe in 1987. It uses LZW compression and a palette capped at 256 colors per frame, and supports simple animation. It is used for short looping animations, simple graphics and icons, and reaction images.

AVIF is an image format built on AV1 compression. This page reads one frame of a GIF and writes it as a still AVIF. A moving GIF therefore becomes a single picture, which suits a poster image or a thumbnail but not a reaction clip.

### Programs that open GIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP exports one frame of a GIF or a multilayer animation, and ImageMagick reads GIF files too.
- **Web:** Chrome, Firefox and Safari display a GIF picture directly.

### GIF and AVIF compared

- **Frames**: only the first frame is used. Timing, looping and disposal are not carried over.
- **Quality**: the AVIF is lossy.
- **Color**: pixels pass through 8-bit RGBA, and the GIF's palette is not restored.
- **Metadata**: left behind; EXIF, ICC and XMP data is not written.
- **Support**: still AVIF arrived in Safari on iOS 16 and in Firefox 93, with Chrome earlier.
- **Size**: the picture keeps its pixel width and height. Nothing is resized.
- **Errors**: a GIF the browser cannot decode stops with the message "Image decode failed."
- **Privacy**: the GIF stays on your device.

### Other ways to convert GIF to AVIF

- **GIMP:** open the GIF, go to File > Export As, save under an .avif name and set the AVIF dialog's options, such as Quality, Lossless and Encoder speed.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick "animation.gif[0]" cover.avif` to pick the first frame.
- **Pillow:** open the GIF, call `seek(0)` and save a file ending in .avif. Pillow reads and writes AVIF and picks the format from the extension.

### Problems with GIF files

- **Soft transparent edges**: GIF cannot keep partial opacity.
- **GIMP reduces a GIF export to 256 colors**: gradients can change.
- **Frame disposal changes the picture**: later frames cover earlier ones, so a first frame alone may look incomplete.
- **Older browsers fail to show AVIF**: supply a JPEG, PNG or WebP fallback.

guide.markdown:
### What is a GIF file?

CompuServe introduced GIF in 1987. It compresses with LZW, draws each frame from a palette of up to 256 colors, and can do simple animation. Transparency is one-bit: a palette entry is either clear or solid, so soft edges cannot keep partial opacity. Short looping animations are the format's usual job.

Because of the palette, the colors in a GIF are already limited before any conversion happens.

### Programs that open GIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP exports GIF as a single still or as an animation made from layers. ImageMagick reads GIF, but check which formats your install supports.
- **Web browsers:** Firefox and Chrome display GIF.
- **Mobile:** Safari and Chrome display GIF.

### GIF and BMP compared

- **Frames**: a GIF can hold many, a BMP only one.
- **Compression**: GIF is lossless through LZW, while a BMP commonly stores its pixels uncompressed, although lossless compression is available.
- **Color**: Version 5 of BMP arrived with Windows 98 and can record an ICC profile and an alpha channel.
- **Types**: image/gif and image/bmp.

This page decodes the first GIF frame in the browser as 8-bit RGBA, leaves metadata behind, and has ImageMagick write the BMP. The rest of the animation is ignored, and so are its delays and loop count.

### Other ways to convert GIF to BMP

- **ImageMagick:** `magick badge.gif'[0]' badge.bmp` saves the first frame. The page on image indexes says the first image is index 0, the second is 1, and so on, and the output format comes from the .bmp suffix.
- **Pillow:** `from PIL import Image; Image.open("badge.gif").convert("RGB").save("badge.bmp")` converts the picture to RGB, which BMP writing supports, and takes the BMP format from the filename extension.

### Problems with GIF files

- **The BMP is very large**: a BMP with uncompressed pixels can be bulky, which makes PNG or JPEG the more practical choice for handing files around.
- **An older program rejects the file**: software expecting an older bitmap header may need BMP3 or BMP2 output rather than ImageMagick's default BMP version.
- **Jagged transparency**: GIF transparency has no partial opacity, so soft edges were already hard before converting.
- **Gradients look different**: the small palette can change how a gradient is drawn.
