guide.title: JXL to PNG: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is a JXL file?

JPEG XL is an image coding system from the JPEG committee, standardized as ISO/IEC 18181. It offers lossy and lossless coding, alpha channels, animation, progressive decoding, and support for HDR, wide gamuts and high bit depth. It can also losslessly recompress an existing JPEG file. A .jxl file may hold just a codestream, or wrap one in a box-based container that also carries Exif, XMP and JUMBF metadata. The registered media type is image/jxl.

People convert JXL to PNG when a program cannot decode JPEG XL.

### Programs that open JXL files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP has had stable JXL import support since version 2.10.32, and ImageMagick reads JXL when it has a JPEG XL delegate.
- **Web:** Safari 17 added JPEG XL, and on iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 it decodes JPEG XL web images, which does not establish a separate photo-library editor.

### JXL and PNG compared

PNG is lossless, supports alpha transparency and stores 8-bit or 16-bit channels. A JXL can also be animated. This page decodes the JXL to one picture at 8 bits per channel, so any extra bit depth is lost. ImageMagick compiled to WebAssembly does the decoding, and the result is a PNG named after your file.

### Other ways to convert JXL to PNG

- **djxl (command line):** run `djxl image.jxl image.png`. The extension of the output file picks the format, and an animation writes one numbered file per frame.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the JXL, then use File > Export As… in GIMP to save it as PNG.
- **ImageMagick (command line):** type `magick image.jxl image.png`. JXL is listed as readable and writable, and it needs a JPEG XL delegate library.

### Problems with JXL files

- **A program rejects the JXL**: its decoder may lack support for the profile or level the file needs.
- **Metadata is missing**: a bare codestream lacks the container boxes that carry extra metadata.
- **Only one frame appears here**: this page reads a single image. Use djxl for each frame of an animation.
- **A large image fails**: pictures over about 537 megapixels do not fit here.

guide.title: About KTX and PNG
guide.markdown:
### What is a KTX file?

Khronos Texture version 1, KTX, is a container for OpenGL and OpenGL ES textures. A file records the texture dimensions and the GL format that its loader needs. It can hold cubemap faces and texture arrays, stores mipmap levels from largest to smallest, and may carry named metadata such as texture orientation. KTX2 is a separate container whose structure is incompatible with the first.

### Programs that open KTX files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** KTX Software with its libktx library reads KTX 1 and 2, though it is a developer library and not a photo viewer. FFmpeg reads KTX 1.0 files that use ASTC formats, and kram is a command-line utility that decodes supported KTX and KTX2 textures.
- **Windows and Linux:** PVRTexTool is a texture GUI and command-line tool that lists KTX and KTX2 among its inputs.
- **Mac:** kramv is a viewer for supported KTX and KTX2 textures on Apple Silicon Macs.

### KTX and PNG compared

- **Purpose**: KTX feeds a GPU, while PNG is a lossless picture meant for people.
- **Contents**: KTX can hold mipmaps, cubemap faces and arrays. A PNG holds one picture.
- **Compression**: a KTX may use a GPU compression format, but a PNG is always lossless.

This page reads only the original KTX format, and only when the texture is uncompressed 8-bit RGB or RGBA. It takes the first image in the file and writes its pixels as a PNG. A compressed or non-8-bit texture is refused with a message, and nothing is saved. An RGBA texture keeps its transparency, and an RGB texture has none to keep.

### Other ways to convert KTX to PNG

- **PVRTexToolCLI:** `PVRTexToolCLI -i texture.ktx -d extracted.png -noout` decodes the texture and writes a PNG. The -i option accepts KTX and KTX2 files, -d saves a decompressed file with the extension you give it, and -noout stops the .pvr file from being written.
- **Tacent View:** `tacentview -c texture.ktx --out png` converts from the command line without opening the GUI. Tacent View loads KTX and KTX2 and saves PNG, on Windows and Linux.

### Problems with KTX files

- **The picture is upside down**: a texture may look upside down when its coordinate origin differs from the viewer, so inspect KTXorientation and flip the PNG in an editor.
- **The suffix was changed**: renaming a KTX2 file to .ktx does not convert it.
- **Unsupported internal format**: a KTX texture does not guarantee that every OpenGL implementation supports its internal image format.
- **Compressed texture**: decode it first in a tool such as PVRTexTool, which can save a decompressed copy.

guide.title: About KTX2 files
guide.markdown:
### What is a KTX2 file?

KTX2 is the second-generation texture container from Khronos. It holds image data for graphics APIs such as Vulkan and OpenGL, and it supports mipmap levels, texture arrays and cube maps. The data inside can be supercompressed or universal, meaning it is transcoded into whatever format the destination GPU uses. Its media type is image/ktx2, and its layout is incompatible with the original KTX container.

### Programs that open KTX2 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** KTX Software, whose ktx info and ktx extract command-line tools inspect KTX2 metadata and extract images, with libktx for developers; and kram, a command-line utility that decodes supported KTX2 textures.
- **Windows and Linux:** PVRTexTool, with a GUI and a CLI, lists KTX2 among its inputs.
- **Mac:** kramv views KTX2 textures on Apple Silicon Macs.
- **Web:** developer code such as the Three.js KTX2Loader reads the format in a browser.

### KTX2 and PNG compared

A KTX2 can carry many images: mip levels, faces, layers and depth slices. A PNG holds exactly one, so exporting one picture does not keep the whole texture.

This page decodes in your browser and works only on uncompressed textures. It reads 8-bit RGB or RGBA pixels and writes the first image of the top mip level as a PNG. Compressed textures stop with an error, so a Basis Universal texture needs one of the tools below first. Nothing is uploaded, because the whole conversion runs on your device.

### Other ways to convert KTX2 to PNG

- **KTX Software:** run `ktx extract --level 0 --face 0 --layer 0 texture.ktx2 preview.png` to pick one image. PNG output applies to _UNORM formats, and other data types are written as EXR.
- **ktx extract --all:** run `ktx extract --all texture.ktx2 extracted` to write every slice into the extracted folder, one file each, named by level, face and layer.
- **PVRTexToolCLI:** run `PVRTexToolCLI -i texture.ktx2 -d preview.png -noout`. Cube maps and arrays give separate files named with Face and Array numbers.

### Problems with KTX2 files

- **A loader for the old format fails**: KTX 1 loaders cannot read KTX2, and renaming the file changes nothing.
- **A compressed texture must be transcoded**: universal data has to become a format the GPU supports before it can be shown.
- **One picture is not the texture**: mipmaps, array layers and cube faces are separate images, so a single export does not preserve the whole structure.

guide.title: About M2TS files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M2TS file?

An .m2ts file carries the video, audio and extra streams used by Blu-ray BDAV discs and AVCHD camcorders. It does not pick one codec. Instead it changes the MPEG-2 transport stream layout so that each source packet has a 188-byte transport packet plus four extra bytes, which makes 192 bytes in all.

Blu-ray allows MPEG-2, AVC and VC-1 video in this wrapper, and the format supports HD video. AVCHD was announced by Sony and Panasonic in 2006. The related MPEG type video/mp2t is shared by plain transport streams, so it does not point to M2TS alone.

An .m2ts file is used on Blu-ray discs and for AVCHD camcorder recordings. On a disc or a camera card it sits beside separate clip-information files, and copying the stream by itself leaves those files and the disc organization behind.

Because the wrapper allows several video codecs, a clip being .m2ts does not tell you what you need to decode it. VLC media player, MPC-HC and Adobe Premiere Pro all open the format, and a camcorder or a disc is where most M2TS files come from.

### Programs that open M2TS files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Playback of M2TS in FFplay comes from the FFmpeg libraries it is built on, and the tool is free.
- FFmpeg reads MPEG transport streams.

### M2TS and MKV compared

- **Layout**: M2TS is a stream of fixed-size source packets, each a transport packet with four extra bytes. Matroska is built on EBML, a binary structure derived from XML.
- **Registration**: the IANA media type for Matroska video is video/matroska, while video/mp2t, which is shared with plain transport streams, is the nearest type for M2TS.
- **Origin**: Matroska developed from the earlier MCF project, and IANA registers video/matroska for it.
- **Codecs**: M2TS permits MPEG-2, AVC and VC-1 picture streams. Matroska leaves the choice of compression method and level open.
- **Extras**: one Matroska file can combine streams of video, audio and subtitles, and the design also includes chapters and descriptive tags.
- **Typical source**: M2TS comes from camcorders and Blu-ray discs.
- **Wrapper content**: an M2TS file wraps video, audio and additional streams, and a Matroska file can hold the same kinds of stream.

This page does not repackage the stream. FFmpeg decodes the clip in your browser, and the x264 encoder rewrites the picture (CRF 32, ultrafast preset). Audio is written as 96 kbps AAC, and anything flagged as interlaced is deinterlaced. A side beyond 1920 pixels is brought down to fit, odd dimensions become even, and the output never runs faster than 30 frames per second.

To copy the streams without re-encoding, use the methods below.

You can choose several clips at once. They are processed one after another, each result is downloaded as its own file named after the original with the .mkv extension, and no ZIP is made. Your original M2TS files are never modified, and nothing is uploaded, because FFmpeg runs inside the browser as WebAssembly.

A long clip needs time because the work happens in the tab, on your own hardware. The page sets no size or time limit, and an exit-code message means FFmpeg stopped with an error.

### Other ways to convert M2TS to MKV

- **MKVToolNix (mkvmerge):** run `mkvmerge -o archive.mkv recording.m2ts`. The documentation names .m2ts among the transport-stream file types mkvmerge parses, and mkvmerge copies tracks instead of re-encoding them. The same documentation says -o names the file to write.
- **mkvmerge with chosen tracks:** run `mkvmerge --identify recording.m2ts` to list track IDs, then `mkvmerge -o archive.mkv --audio-tracks 1 --no-subtitles recording.m2ts` to copy a chosen audio track and skip subtitles. The documentation says --identify probes the file and reports its type, its tracks and their track IDs, --audio-tracks copies the audio tracks whose IDs you give, and -S or --no-subtitles leaves out subtitle tracks.
- **FFmpeg, copy everything:** run `ffmpeg -i recording.m2ts -map 0 -c copy archive.mkv`. The -map 0 option selects every stream, and -c copy leaves them unchanged. FFmpeg's documentation describes that setting as stream copy, with no decoding or encoding.

### Problems with M2TS files

- **Missing clip information**: copying only the stream omits its clip-information files and disc organization.
- **The extension does not name the decoder**: .m2ts does not tell you which supported video decoder the recording needs.
- **Protected disc content**: Blu-ray content can have AACS protection even though M2TS itself supplies no encryption.

guide.title: About M2TS and MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M2TS file?

M2TS is the stream file of Blu-ray discs and AVCHD camcorders. It packages video, audio and additional streams in a modified MPEG-2 transport stream: each source packet is a 188-byte transport packet with four extra bytes. Its transport structure modifies MPEG-2 TS rather than prescribing one video codec. Blu-ray allows MPEG-2, AVC and VC-1 pictures in this wrapper, so the extension does not tell you which video codec is inside. Sony and Panasonic announced AVCHD in 2006.

An M2TS usually turns up on a camera card or in a copied disc folder. A stream copied alone leaves behind its clip-information files and the disc organization, so archive the whole folder and treat the MP4 as a viewing copy. The video/mp2t media type is shared with other transport-stream formats, so it does not identify M2TS by itself.

### Programs that open M2TS files

**Windows**

- FFmpeg: reads MPEG transport streams; installed decoder support still matters.

**Mac**

- FFplay: FFmpeg's free playback utility for the command line.

**Linux**

- HandBrake: lists M2TS among the common video file types it reads from discs and cameras, and TS, MTS and M2TS under broadcast TV recordings.

### M2TS and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .m2ts, whose transport-stream type video/mp2t is shared with other formats; .mp4 and video/mp4.
- **Container**: M2TS is built from transport-stream packets. MP4 is an ISO base media file, ISO/IEC 14496-14, organized as tracks.
- **Video codec**: M2TS carries MPEG-2, AVC or VC-1. The MP4 made here carries H.264.
- **Audio**: the MP4 made here carries AAC at 96 kbps.
- **Protection**: M2TS adds no encryption, but commercial Blu-ray content often has AACS protection.
- **Output**: each M2TS file gives its own MP4 download, and only the stream file you choose is converted.

The conversion changes both wrapper and pictures. FFmpeg decodes the stream and re-encodes it with libx264, using the ultrafast preset, CRF 32 and the faststart flag. Video is held to 1920 pixels on its longer side and to 30 frames per second, and sides round down to even numbers, so an odd size loses a pixel. Frames marked as interlaced are deinterlaced.

A smaller frame is never scaled up and a slower frame rate is never raised. A faster source has frames dropped and keeps its length, so it is not slowed down.

The result is not a copy of the original quality: a fine trade for sharing and a poor one for archiving, so keep the M2TS if the footage matters. Several M2TS files are converted in sequence, and each downloads as a separate MP4 without a ZIP. The disc or camera folder around the file is not converted, only the stream you pick.

### Other ways to convert M2TS to MP4

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i input.m2ts -c:v libx264 -c:a aac output.mp4`. This re-encodes. With `-c copy` instead, a stream the MP4 cannot hold may be dropped or carried as a data stream without any error.
- **HandBrake:** choose Open Source or drag the M2TS onto the main window, select a preset (its quick start suggests Fast 1080p30 as a general choice), set the destination with Save As and Browse, then click Start. HandBrake creates MKV and MP4 files. HandBrake's documentation warns that AVCHD playlists get incomplete support and that single stream files may open unreliably when one stream spans several files.

### Problems with M2TS files

- **The file will not play**: the extension does not say which video decoder the recording needs, so the player may lack the one inside, as Blu-ray permits three different picture codecs here. Convert it, or try FFplay, which plays through FFmpeg's libraries.
- **Only part of the recording converted**: a single video stream can span several files, and converting one file gives just that part.
- **A disc file will not convert or shows no picture**: commercial Blu-ray content is often AACS protected, and M2TS itself supplies no way around that.
- **HandBrake opens only part of a camera folder**: AVCHD and AVCHD Lite playlists are not fully supported, though it may open individual video files from the Stream folder inside the BDMV folder.
- **Clips are missing their structure**: a stream copied alone omits its clip-information files and disc organization, so keep the whole folder.

guide.title: About M2V and MP4
guide.markdown:
### What is an M2V file?

A file ending in .m2v is an MPEG-2 video elementary stream: the picture data of MPEG-2 (ITU-T H.262, also called MPEG-2 Part 2) with nothing else attached. Sound lives elsewhere. A program stream bundles one video with its audio, and a transport stream can multiplex several channels, so an M2V on its own naturally gives a silent result. These streams mostly come out of DVD authoring tools and MPEG-2 encoders.

### Programs that open M2V files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg and ffplay decode MPEG-2 video and name .m2v for raw MPEG-2 output. VLC media player reads this kind of stream through its MPEG-I/II elementary-video demuxer.
- **Windows and Mac:** Telestream Switch documents M2V input.

### M2V and MP4 compared

- **Contents**: an M2V stream holds video only, whereas an MP4 can hold video, audio, subtitles and metadata.
- **Codec**: MPEG-2 (H.262) goes in and H.264 comes out.
- **Reach**: every major browser plays MP4.

Encoding is done by libx264 (ultrafast preset, CRF 32, zerolatency tune). Width and height are limited to 1920 pixels and the frame rate to a ceiling of 30. A smaller picture is never enlarged, so a standard-definition stream keeps its size apart from rounding an odd side down to even. The source never had audio, so the MP4 has none.

### Other ways to convert M2V to MP4

- **FFmpeg video only:** `ffmpeg -i pictures.m2v -c:v libx264 -an viewing.mp4` writes H.264 video and requests no audio, which suits a source that has none.
- **FFmpeg separate audio:** `ffmpeg -i pictures.m2v -i soundtrack.wav -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -shortest complete.mp4` brings in a separate audio file as a second input, and -shortest ends the output with the shorter input. Check that the start and end line up before you share the result.

### Problems with M2V files

- **The MP4 is silent**: the M2V had no audio to begin with. Add the soundtrack separately, as the second method above shows.
- **A stream looks wrong in a player**: program and transport streams are built differently from an elementary stream, so choose the stream type your player expects.
- **The file is cut off or damaged**: FFmpeg usually still converts what it can read, so the MP4 can come out shorter than you expect.

guide.title: About M4A and AAC
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

An M4A file is MPEG-4 audio with nothing else inside. Apple took up the extension for its unprotected music files. Most carry AAC audio, specified in ISO/IEC 14496-3, while some hold lossless Apple Lossless (ALAC), so the extension doesn't name one codec.

The wrapper can carry metadata tags and cover art, and its media type is audio/mp4. Typical sources are music from iTunes and Apple Music, podcasts and iPhone voice memos. Android plays AAC in .m4a files on every version.

### Programs that open M4A files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity brings in M4A audio after you install its optional FFmpeg library, and leaves out protected files.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play M4A audio directly.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android and mpv for Android play it.

### M4A and AAC compared

- **Layer**: M4A is a container. AAC is the coding inside it. A .aac file is the stream itself, commonly with ADTS headers.
- **Contents**: an M4A can hold AAC or ALAC and carries tags and cover art. The .aac file this page writes holds the audio stream and nothing else.
- **Profiles**: AAC profiles include LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2.
- **Media type**: audio/aac is registered for ADTS and LATM/LOAS transport.

AAC, Advanced Audio Coding, is a lossy codec standardized through MPEG: Part 7 of MPEG-2 and Part 3 of MPEG-4. It succeeds MP3 and covers sample rates between 8 and 96 kHz. You hear it in streaming audio, music downloads and the soundtracks of MP4 videos and on mobile devices.

### Other ways to convert M4A to AAC

- **FFmpeg re-encode:** in a terminal, `ffmpeg -i library_item.m4a -c:a aac -b:a 192k elementary.aac` writes a new lossy AAC stream.
- **FFmpeg rewrap:** the command `ffmpeg -i library_copy.m4a -c:a copy -f adts extracted.aac` keeps AAC as it is, without re-encoding, and can't turn ALAC into AAC.

### Problems with M4A files

- **Audacity shows no import**: the program asks for its optional FFmpeg library first.
- **DRM-protected files stay closed**: Audacity's FFmpeg route can't import them.
- **Tags get overwritten**: when several recordings go into one Audacity window, the project tags become those of the last file.

faqs.question: Can I queue several M4A files?

### What is an M4A file?

An M4A is MPEG-4 audio on its own, with no picture track. Inside you normally find AAC sound or lossless ALAC, plus tags and artwork. Songs from Apple's music apps, podcasts and iPhone voice memos are common examples. The extension alone does not establish quality, because the same .m4a ending covers both lossy and lossless sound.

### Programs that open M4A files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports M4A through its optional FFmpeg library and skips protected files, and FFplay plays the container.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly, with AAC availability depending on system codecs, while Chrome plays supported MP4 audio and the codec inside still matters.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is free and decodes whatever the container holds, and so does the mpv port for Android, which the mpv project links to.

### M4A and AIFF compared

- **Names and media types**: .m4a; .aiff with audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff.
- **Origin**: Apple created AIFF as a relative of the IFF wrapper family from Electronic Arts. Its specification is dated 4 January 1989.
- **Compression**: M4A is usually lossy AAC, or lossless ALAC. AIFF often carries uncompressed linear PCM, and AIFF-C extends the family to compressed audio.

The page decodes the M4A and writes 16-bit big-endian PCM, dropping any video stream. FFmpeg runs inside your browser as WebAssembly, so the audio is not uploaded, and a long recording simply takes longer on a slower device.

### Other ways to convert M4A to AIFF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i interview.m4a -vn -c:a pcm_s24be interview.aiff` for 24-bit audio. It decodes the same way but keeps more bits per sample, and it cannot restore detail the M4A already lost.

### Problems with M4A files

Audacity cannot read M4A until its optional FFmpeg library is installed, and protected recordings are refused on that route. Opening several recordings in a single Audacity window leaves the project with the last file's tags.

A very large AIFF is expected here. If you need only part of a recording, trim it in an editor before exporting.

Listen for clipping and compare the length of the new AIFF with the original.

guide.title: About M4A files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

An M4A is an audio-only file wrapped in the MPEG-4 container, the same one MP4 video uses. The ending names the container, not the codec. AAC is what most M4A files contain, and it is lossy. But the same container can hold Apple Lossless (ALAC). You will find M4A in music libraries, podcast downloads, voice recordings and audio exported from Apple apps.

Besides the sound, an M4A can carry descriptive tags and cover art. FFmpeg reads embedded cover art as a video stream, which is why a conversion that switches video off also leaves the picture behind.

The codec decides what a conversion to FLAC is worth. AAC is lossy. It saves space by discarding detail, and once discarded it is gone. ALAC stores every sample, so an ALAC file already holds everything FLAC would. Knowing which one you have tells you whether FLAC buys anything beyond compatibility with a player or library that wants it.

### Programs that open M4A files

- **Windows, Mac, Linux:** Audacity imports M4A only with its optional FFmpeg library, and it can't import DRM-protected recordings. ffplay, FFmpeg's player, includes the M4A demuxer.
- **Web:** Firefox plays the formats it supports on its own, while AAC can lean on your system's codecs. In Chrome the codec inside the file decides whether it opens, since only some audio and MP4 combinations play.
- **Mobile:** On Android, VLC is a free player and opens whatever codecs the file holds that it supports. mpv for Android also plays it.

The FLAC you make opens in Audacity without any extra library.

### M4A and FLAC compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .m4a, usually audio/mp4; .flac and audio/flac.
- **Compression**: AAC is lossy. ALAC and FLAC are lossless.
- **Metadata**: FLAC can carry Vorbis comments, embedded pictures and seek points. M4A carries metadata tags and cover art.
- **Open format**: FLAC's reference implementation is open source.
- **Size**: a lossless file is larger than its lossy counterpart.

The command this page runs is `-acodec flac -vn`: decode the audio, write FLAC, ignore video. It names no sample rate, channel count, stream or tag mapping, so FFmpeg's defaults settle those. An AAC source gives a FLAC with the same sound and no more detail. Converting a lossy file to FLAC cannot recreate samples that were removed earlier. Either way, keep the M4A until you have played the FLAC and checked its length. FLAC can carry embedded pictures too, so cover art can go back in with a tag editor.

### Other ways to convert M4A to FLAC

- **FFmpeg (command line):** enter `ffmpeg -i recording.m4a -vn -c:a flac recording.flac`. `-vn` disables video, and a file with several audio streams needs a `-map` option such as `-map 0:a:1` to choose one.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** after installing its optional FFmpeg library, import the file with File > Import > Audio and export it with File > Export Audio, choosing FLAC as the format. In the FLAC dialog you can choose mono, stereo or custom channels, a sample rate, 16-bit or 24-bit output and a compression level between 0 and 8.
- **fre:ac (Windows, Mac, Linux):** the project's site says it converts freely between M4A/AAC and FLAC. Add the file, choose the FLAC encoder and start the conversion.

### Problems with M4A files

- **Audacity can't import it**: install the FFmpeg library, or convert here.
- **A purchased file won't convert**: it is protected. Audacity can't import protected files, and this page refuses a FairPlay-protected one. Use an unprotected copy.
- **The cover art is missing from the FLAC**: it is read as a video stream and left out. Add it back in a tag editor.
- **Several recordings in one Audacity window**: importing multiple files replaces the project tags with the last file's tags.
- **The FLAC is much larger**: FLAC stores every decoded sample, and the AAC it came from did not.
- **"FFmpeg failed with exit code"**: a file with no audio stream ends this way. A damaged or cut-short file usually converts to a shorter FLAC instead, so check the length.
- **The FLAC won't play on an Android phone's built-in player**: Android's built-in player handles FLAC in a narrower range than the format allows: mono or stereo, with 16-bit samples recommended. VLC for Android is an alternative player.
- **The recording sounds the same as before**: that is the expected result. FLAC repeats the sound without improving it.

guide.title: About M4A and M4R files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

Apple adopted the M4A extension, which MPEG-4 audio-only files use, for unprotected music. Container and codec are separate things: most M4A files hold AAC audio, which MPEG-4 Part 3 defines, yet an M4A can also contain lossless ALAC, so two files with one extension can have very different histories. MPEG-4 keeps the container structure apart from the encoding of its tracks, and files can carry track metadata beside the sound.

The media type is audio/mp4. AAC is lossy, and its aim was to outdo MP3 on sound quality at a given bitrate. It tops out at 512 kbps, with sample rates between 8 and 96 kHz. iTunes songs were sold as AAC, and every version of Android plays AAC held in .m4a files. Every major browser plays AAC audio in an MP4 container.

### Programs that open M4A files

**Windows**

- Audacity: it imports M4A once its optional FFmpeg library is installed; protected files are excluded.

**Mac**

- FFplay: FFmpeg's player, which comes with FFmpeg and is run from the command line.

**Web**

- Firefox and Chrome: play M4A directly, though AAC availability can depend on system codecs.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android: opens M4A.
- mpv for Android: opens M4A too.

### M4A and M4R compared

- **Extensions**: .m4a and .m4r.
- **Purpose**: the WavePad manual from NCH names M4R as the iPhone ringtone type, and MediaInfo files .m4r in the same MPEG-4 family as M4A.
- **Container**: both are MPEG-4 family files, so M4R is mainly a label for ringtone use.
- **Codec**: M4A can hold AAC or lossless ALAC. The M4R made here holds AAC.
- **Length**: Apple's GarageBand ringtone export limits the selected sound to 30 seconds. This page does not cut anything.
- **Metadata**: FFmpeg copies the M4A's global tags into the M4R where it has fields for them.

What changes in this conversion is the encoding. FFmpeg decodes the M4A, drops any video stream, encodes the sound with its AAC encoder at 192 kbps and writes it in the iPod-style MP4 container with an .m4r name. An AAC source goes through a second lossy encode, and a lossless ALAC source becomes lossy.

The converter also leaves out video, including cover art. That is why the order of work matters. Trim the excerpt first, in an editor or in GarageBand, then convert the short clip. Converting a full song gives you a full-length M4R. Listen to the finished file before you rely on it, and remember that making the file does not install or select the tone on a phone; that step happens on the phone, for example through GarageBand. The M4R is a derivative made for one job; the M4A stays your listening copy.

Choosing several M4A files queues them: each converts after the one before and downloads as an M4R of its own, with no ZIP.

### Other ways to convert M4A to M4R

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i input.m4a -f ipod -b:a 192k -c:a aac output.m4r`. It re-encodes the audio. The -ss and -t options set where to start and how long to write if you need only a short excerpt.
- **NCH Switch:** press Add File(s), set the destination through Save to Folder, Output Folder or Browse, pick M4R in the Output Format drop-down and press Convert. NCH lists Windows PC, Mac OS X and Android.
- **GarageBand (iPhone):** import the audio from Files, drag it to the far left of the Tracks view and trim it, then open My Songs, tap Share and choose Ringtone. Apple limits ringtones to 30 seconds, and protected or undownloaded songs are dimmed and unavailable.

### Problems with M4A files

- **Audacity cannot import the file**: install its optional FFmpeg library first. Audacity also cannot import DRM-protected recordings through that route.
- **The page refuses the file with a FairPlay message**: protected M4P purchases cannot be converted here.
- **"FFmpeg failed with exit code"**: the file may hold no audio track.
- **Importing many recordings into one Audacity window replaces the project tags**: Audacity keeps the last file's tags.
- **The M4R is far longer than a ringtone**: the page has no trim control and converts the whole recording. Trim the clip before converting.
- **A song in GarageBand is dimmed**: it is protected or has not been downloaded to the iPhone yet.

guide.title: About M4A files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

The M4A extension marks MPEG-4 files containing audio only, which Apple adopted for music files without protection. Its media type is audio/mp4, and most M4A files contain AAC audio, which is defined in MPEG-4 Part 3, ISO/IEC 14496-3. Inside there is normally AAC or lossless Apple Lossless (ALAC) audio, along with optional metadata tags and cover art.

AAC is lossy and was built to beat MP3 for sound quality at a given bitrate. Sample rates from 8 up to 96 kHz are supported, and bitrates reach 512 kbps. Apple used AAC for songs sold through iTunes, so M4A turns up in music from iTunes and Apple Music, in podcasts and in iPhone voice memos.

AAC audio in an MP4 container plays in every major browser, and Android handles AAC in .m4a files across all its versions.

### Programs that play or import M4A

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Audacity: needs its optional FFmpeg library installed before it can import M4A, and it does not take protected files.
- ffplay: the player that comes with FFmpeg.

**Windows, Mac, Linux and Mobile**

- VLC: opens M4A on the desktop and, as VLC for Android, on phones, with decoding limited by what the container holds.

**Windows**

- Windows Media Player: opens M4A files.

**Mac**

- Apple Music: opens M4A files, including music from iTunes and Apple Music.

**Web**

- Firefox and Chrome: play supported audio directly, and the codec inside still matters.

**Mobile**

- mpv for Android: plays it.

### M4A and MP3 compared

- **Standards**: the name MP3 abbreviates MPEG-1 Audio Layer III. Two ISO/IEC documents cover it: 11172-3 from 1993, and 13818-3, which extended it, from 1995. Development began in the late 1980s at Fraunhofer IIS, with other MPEG audio group members involved.
- **Media types**: audio/mp4 for M4A and audio/mpeg for MP3.
- **Compression**: both are lossy. The MP3 method models human hearing and discards sound that listeners are unlikely to notice. Roughly one eleventh of the data of the same CD audio is what a 128 kbit/s MP3 needs.
- **Bitrates**: MPEG-1 MP3 runs at 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz with bitrates from 32 up to 320 kbps, and the MPEG-2 and MPEG-2.5 modes add lower bitrates and sample rates. AAC goes up to 512 kbps and from 8 to 96 kHz.
- **Tags**: an M4A stores metadata tags and cover art. In an MP3, song titles and other tags sit in separate ID3 structures within the file.
- **Licensing**: the patent licensing program for MP3 came to an end on 23 April 2017.
- **Lossless option**: an M4A can hold ALAC audio, which keeps the sound exactly. An MP3 is always lossy.
- **Support**: every major browser plays MP3, and it plays on nearly every device.

In this page, FFmpeg on your device reads the M4A, leaves out video streams and encodes the audio as MP3 with LAME. The conversion asks for 192 kbit/s. Below 32 kHz MP3 cannot reach that rate, so LAME tops out at 160 kbit/s for 16 to 24 kHz audio and 64 kbit/s for 8 to 12 kHz audio. The sample rate is not changed, and the page sets no size limit.

### Other ways to convert M4A to MP3

- **Apple Music (Mac):** choose Music > Settings, open the Files tab, click Import Settings and set Import Using to MP3 Encoder. Select the songs, then choose File > Convert > Create MP3 Version. Converting between lossy formats loses some quality, and protected AAC purchases cannot be converted.
- **iTunes (Windows):** go to Edit > Preferences > General > Import Settings and pick MP3 Encoder from the Import Using list. Choose the songs, then pick File > Convert > Create MP3 Version. Only iTunes Plus purchases convert.
- **FFmpeg (terminal, any platform):** `ffmpeg -i input.m4a -acodec libmp3lame -b:a 192k -vn output.mp3` writes the MP3.

### Problems with M4A files

- **Audacity can't open the file**: its optional FFmpeg library has to be installed before M4A can be imported, and DRM-protected recordings cannot be imported that way.
- **Tags get replaced**: bringing several recordings into one Audacity window swaps the project tags for those of the last file.
- **A song bought from iTunes won't convert**: older purchases use Protected AAC, and Apple Music and iTunes convert iTunes Plus songs only.
- **You need the best copy**: converting to MP3 adds a second lossy step. Keep the M4A, which may hold ALAC audio kept exactly.
- **You need WAV instead**: use the [M4A to WAV converter](/m4a-to-wav/).

guide.title: About M4A files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

An M4A file is an audio-only file in the MPEG-4 container. Apple adopted the .m4a extension for unprotected music files, and the sound inside is usually AAC, the codec defined in MPEG-4 Part 3 (ISO/IEC 14496-3). An M4A can also hold Apple Lossless (ALAC). Its media type is audio/mp4.

AAC is a lossy codec that aims at better sound than MP3 for a given bitrate. Its sample rates span 8 to 96 kHz and its bitrates reach 512 kbps, and iTunes sold its songs as AAC. You meet M4A files as music from iTunes and Apple Music, as podcasts and as iPhone voice memos. Both Android and every major browser play AAC in this container, so an M4A rarely needs converting just to be heard.

### Programs that open M4A files

**Windows and Linux**

- VLC media player: plays M4A.

**Windows**

- Windows Media Player: plays M4A.

**Mac**

- Apple Music: plays M4A.

**Web**

- Chrome and Firefox: play AAC in MP4 and M4A files. Firefox can depend on the codecs your system has.

**Mobile**

- Android: every version handles AAC audio in .m4a files, and VLC for Android and mpv for Android decode whatever codec the file holds.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Audacity: imports M4A, along with MP4, AC3 and WMA files, once you install its optional FFmpeg library. It can't import files that are DRM-protected to work only in particular software.
- ffplay: the player that comes with FFmpeg. Its decoders must be part of your FFmpeg build.

### M4A and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .m4a is registered as audio/mp4. MP4 files use .mp4 or .m4v, and the MP4 media types are video/mp4 and audio/mp4.
- **Container**: both are built from nested boxes, the structure MPEG-4 Part 14 (ISO/IEC 14496-14) describes, so an M4A is an MPEG-4 file kept for audio. MP4 first appeared in 2003. The container uses the ISO Base Media File Format, itself a descendant of Apple's QuickTime format. What QuickTime calls atoms, the MP4 family calls boxes.
- **Codecs**: an M4A holds AAC or Apple Lossless. An MP4 most often pairs H.264 video with AAC audio, but AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus can ride in it too.
- **Picture**: an M4A is sound only. An MP4 can have video, subtitles and chapters, but this page doesn't create any.
- **Tags**: M4A holds metadata tags and cover art.
- **Reach**: every major browser plays MP4.

In this conversion the container hardly changes and the sound does. The converter decodes your audio and writes it again as AAC at 96 kbps. If the destination only checks the name, the FFmpeg method below keeps your original audio untouched.

### Other ways to convert M4A to MP4

- **FFmpeg:** in a terminal, `ffmpeg -i input.m4a -c copy output.mp4` rewraps the file. The `-c copy` option selects stream copy, which the FFmpeg manual describes as copying the stream without decoding or encoding it, so the original AAC or ALAC data goes into the new file as it is.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** with the FFmpeg library installed, choose File > Export Audio, pick M4A (AAC) Files (FFmpeg) and give the file the .mp4 extension, which Audacity permits. The same list of permitted extensions also names .m4r for ringtones and .3gp for mobile phones. This encodes the sound again. M4A (AAC) is a lossy format. Audacity's installer doesn't include the FFmpeg library, so install it separately before the format shows in the list.

### Problems with M4A files

- **Audacity won't open the file**: install the optional FFmpeg library first. A copy-protected recording still won't import.
- **Tags run together in Audacity**: importing several recordings into one project replaces the project's tags with the last file's tags. Give each file its own window so its tags survive.
- **The file plays with no sound or won't play**: a player that supports the container may still lack the decoder for what's inside. Try VLC.
- **An M4A with cover art fails to convert**: in our test runs, M4A files with an embedded PNG or JPEG cover ended in an FFmpeg error. Remove the cover image in a tag editor and try again.
- **The page says it produced something else**: the converter checks that its result is an MP4 and stops with a message naming the format it got instead when it isn't. Try the file again or use a different browser.

guide.title: About M4A and OGG
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

M4A is the extension for MPEG-4 files that hold only audio, and Apple adopted it for unprotected music files. The audio inside is mostly AAC, specified in MPEG-4 Part 3 (ISO/IEC 14496-3). It is a lossy codec built to beat MP3 at a given bitrate. Apple used AAC for songs sold through iTunes. AAC handles sample rates from 8 to 96 kHz and bitrates up to 512 kbps, so one M4A can differ a lot from another in size and detail.

The media type for M4A is audio/mp4. Listening is easy: browsers play AAC in MP4 and Android plays .m4a on every version. It is less convenient when a game engine, an open-source editor or a system asks for Ogg, which is why people convert.

### Programs that open M4A files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity opens an M4A only through the optional FFmpeg library, and protected files cannot be imported.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay, the player from FFmpeg, plays M4A through the demuxer that FFmpeg includes for it.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome both play M4A themselves, with AAC support that may rest on the system's codecs.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is a free media player that decodes what is inside the container, and mpv for Android, the port the mpv project links to, plays it too.

### M4A and OGG compared

Ogg is an open container kept by Xiph.Org. Compressed sound and video streams can share one file, and each stream's compression is set by its codec. Its framing carries timestamps and error detection, and streams are read and written in sequence.

- **Extensions:** .m4a; .ogg, with .oga as the broader audio extension.
- **Media types:** audio/mp4 for M4A; audio/ogg for an audio-only Ogg stream, registered by the IETF in September 2008.
- **Codecs:** usually AAC in M4A; Vorbis in this page's OGG.

A file name can mislead, since RFC 5334 treats .ogg Vorbis, general .oga audio and .ogv video as different things. A player needs the codec inside as well as Ogg support. Damaged pages are detected, yet missing encoded audio is not rebuilt.

On the desktop, Audacity imports Ogg Vorbis directly, and VLC plays Ogg containers and decodes Vorbis audio on Windows, Mac and Linux. That makes the OGG a practical choice when the file is headed for an editor that has no FFmpeg library installed.

This page runs libvorbis at quality 5 and drops any video track. You download your file's name with .ogg at the end, and the M4A itself is left alone. Title, artist and album tags are copied to the OGG. A low-bitrate AAC file does not gain detail by becoming Vorbis, so convert when the destination needs Ogg and not to improve the sound.

A game or playback library may ask for Ogg Vorbis because that is the decoder it ships, and that can justify the conversion even when M4A plays well elsewhere. If the receiving program accepts the AAC directly, re-encoding is unnecessary.

### Other ways to convert M4A to OGG

- **Audacity:** import the M4A, which needs the optional FFmpeg library, then open File > Export Audio and pick the format from the dropdown. Ctrl+Shift+E opens the same dialog. Some formats offer options such as quality or encoding, and Ogg Vorbis has its own export options page.
- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i memo.m4a -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 memo.ogg` encodes Vorbis at quality 5. libvorbis must be enabled when FFmpeg is built, and the quality range runs from -1.0 to 10.0.

### Problems with M4A files

**Audacity refuses to import:** it needs its optional FFmpeg library before it can import M4A.

**A protected recording will not open:** DRM-protected recordings cannot be imported through Audacity's documented FFmpeg route.

**The tags are wrong after a batch import:** bringing several recordings into one Audacity window leaves the project with the tags of the last file.

**A player stays silent or refuses:** playback needs the matching decoder as well as the container, and a browser may depend on the system's AAC support. Try Firefox, Chrome or VLC for Android.

**A later export sounds worse:** each lossy conversion adds loss. Return to the best source before making each new format, because AAC is already lossy.

guide.title: Understanding M4A to WMA
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

Files ending in .m4a are audio-only MPEG-4, a form Apple took up for unprotected music. AAC, defined in MPEG-4 Part 3, is what most of them hold, though some carry lossless Apple Lossless (ALAC). AAC is a lossy design meant to beat MP3 at a given bitrate, with support for sample rates between 8 and 96 kHz and bitrates reaching 512 kbps. iTunes songs were sold as AAC. All the major browsers play AAC inside MP4, Android plays .m4a on every release, and the media type is audio/mp4.

### Programs that open M4A files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity needs its optional FFmpeg library before it opens M4A, and protected files are excluded. ffplay, the player that comes with FFmpeg, opens it from the command line, using FFmpeg's decoders.
- **Web:** Chrome and Firefox play AAC in MP4, though Firefox can depend on system codecs.
- **Mobile:** VLC and mpv for Android handle it, depending on the media inside.

### M4A and WMA compared

Microsoft developed WMA as a family of audio codecs kept in the ASF container. Its standard version is lossy, a Lossless variant also exists, and the format is proprietary. It served Windows media libraries and older portable music players, and Windows Media Player, VLC media player and foobar2000 open it.

This page decodes the M4A and writes WMA with the wmav2 encoder at 192 kbps. The video stream is dropped, and the rest of the choices are left to FFmpeg's defaults. AAC to WMA is a lossy-to-lossy step, so there is no quality gain.

### Other ways to convert M4A to WMA

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i song.m4a -vn song.wma` drops any video stream and writes a WMA.
- **WavePad for Windows:** open the M4A, choose File > Save As and select WMA. WMA saving is offered only in the Windows version.

### Problems with M4A files

The FFmpeg library route cannot import DRM-protected recordings. If you import several recordings into one project window, the last file's tags replace the project tags. M4A import in that program depends on the optional library being installed, and a file that library cannot decode will not open.

guide.title: About M4B files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4B file?

An M4B is an audiobook file in the MPEG-4 family. Apple documents .m4b as an AAC audiobook extension and lists audio/x-m4b as its media type in its archived iOS media documentation. FFmpeg recognizes it through the same MOV and MPEG-4 container reader it uses for other MP4-style files.

What sets an audiobook apart from a song is structure. The MOV and MPEG-4 family supports chapter metadata, which players handle separately from the audio samples, so an audiobook app can jump between chapters. M4B is used for audiobooks distributed without DRM, as well as in Apple-oriented listening workflows. You come across one when a DRM-free audiobook is sold or shared as a single long file, or when an app such as BookPlayer on an iPhone imports it. FFmpeg's documentation notes that Audible AAX files are encrypted M4B files, which tells you that an .m4b extension alone doesn't mean the audio is free of protection.

### Programs that open M4B files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FFmpeg: reads an unencrypted M4B through its MOV and MPEG-4 demuxer.
- ffplay: plays media through the FFmpeg libraries.

**Mobile**

- BookPlayer: an iPhone audiobook player with M4B import and chapter navigation, intended for DRM-free audiobooks. It also plays M4A and MP3, changes playback speed, has a sleep timer and shows the progress of your books.

### M4B and MP3 compared

- **Container**: an M4B is an MPEG-4 file made for audiobooks. An MP3 is a stream of MPEG-1 Audio Layer III frames, first standardized in 1993 as ISO/IEC 11172-3, then extended in 1995 by ISO/IEC 13818-3.
- **Sound**: M4B holds AAC. MP3 is a different lossy codec, so converting means decoding and encoding again. Its psychoacoustic model throws away sound that most listeners are unlikely to notice.
- **Origin**: Fraunhofer IIS developed MP3 from the late 1980s; other members of the MPEG audio group took part too. Patent licensing for MP3 ended on 23 April 2017.
- **Structure**: M4B can carry chapter metadata. An MP3 stores titles and other tags in separate ID3 structures inside the file.
- **Compatibility**: every major browser plays MP3, and its registered media type is audio/mpeg.
- **Size**: The MP3 format spans 320 kbps down to 32 kbps with 32, 44.1 and 48 kHz as the sample rates. At 128 kbit/s, an MP3 comes to about one eleventh of the same audio's size on a CD.

FFmpeg, running in your browser, is given `-acodec libmp3lame -b:a 192k -vn`: LAME asked for 192 kbit/s, with any video stream dropped. It sets no sample rate or channel count and passes no stream or tag mapping, so FFmpeg's defaults apply. A long book takes the time your device needs, because no timeout or size cap is built in. The first run also loads the FFmpeg engine, so it starts a little slower than later files.

### Other ways to convert M4B to MP3

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i book.m4b -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k -vn book.mp3`. The libmp3lame encoder wraps LAME. The -vn option disables automatic selection of any video stream, and the page's own command uses the same options.

### Problems with M4B files

- **A purchased book won't play or convert**: BookPlayer is designed for DRM-free audiobooks, so protected purchases fall outside its stated scope, and this page does not remove protection either. Use files you can already play.
- **Chapter buttons are gone in an FFmpeg-based app**: FFmpeg's MOV reader parses chapters only for seekable input, so a non-seekable stream may show none.
- **Chapter markers clash with a tagging program**: Nero-style chapter markers can conflict with some tagging applications. FFmpeg normally writes both Nero chapters and a QuickTime chapter track, and documents an option that writes only the QuickTime track.
- **An Audible AAX book won't convert**: FFmpeg's documentation describes AAX files as encrypted M4B files that can be decrypted with a 4-byte activation secret. This page has no such option and doesn't remove protection.
- **The page says FFmpeg failed with an exit code**: this can happen, for example, when a file has no audio track.
- **The file is damaged or cut short**: FFmpeg usually logs an error and writes what it could read, which leaves the MP3 shorter than the book. Get a fresh copy of the M4B if the end is missing.

guide.title: About M4P and MP3
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4P file?

M4P is the ending Apple used for MPEG-4 audio that carries its FairPlay copy protection. Apple's archived media-format documentation identifies .m4p with protected AAC audio and gives its media type as audio/x-m4p. Songs from the early iTunes Store were sold this way. The container is MPEG-4 and the audio is AAC, but the copy protection restricts playback to authorized Apple software or devices.

Today the format mostly turns up in older iTunes Store purchases and in music libraries on Apple devices. That is why an M4P plays in Apple Music, iTunes, an iPhone, iPad or Mac that is authorized for the purchase, and in little else. Apple allows up to five authorized computers at a time for an Apple Account. Apple also says older purchased songs can remain in a Protected AAC format that prevents them from being converted in the Music app.

### Programs that open M4P files

- **Windows and Mac:** Apple Music, where Apple documents authorizing a computer for your Apple Account purchases, and iTunes, which the format reference also names for playback.
- **Mobile:** iPhone and iPad are named for playing authorized purchases.

You can only authorize a computer you have access to. Apple says you can't authorize one using another computer or an iPhone or iPad, and a sixth computer can't be added until you deauthorize one.

### M4P and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .m4p and audio/x-m4p; .mp3 for MP3.
- **Container and codec**: an M4P is an MPEG-4 container with AAC audio. MP3 is its own format, standardized as ISO/IEC 11172-3.
- **Copy protection**: M4P carries FairPlay DRM. MP3 has none.
- **Compression**: both are lossy.
- **Tags**: MP3 keeps song details in ID3 tags.
- **Playback**: MP3 plays on nearly every device, while a protected M4P plays only where it is authorized.
- **Status**: M4P is a legacy format, used for older iTunes Store purchases and for music libraries on Apple devices.

The page does not decrypt anything. If the file is FairPlay-protected, the page stops and shows a refusal message. Otherwise the FFmpeg build in your browser reads the audio and writes an MP3 with the LAME encoder, requesting 192 kbps. The picture stream, if any, is dropped. The page sets neither a size limit nor a timeout, so how long a long song takes depends on your device. The file stays on your machine, and the original M4P is left as it was.

The page does not decrypt Apple's protection, so a purchased song that is still protected can't be converted here, even though you own it. Pick this page for M4P files that are not protected. If you are not sure which kind you have, drop it in and the page tells you. Several files can be queued together; each gets its own MP3, named after the original.

### Other ways to convert M4P to MP3

- **Apple Music on a Mac:** open Music > Settings > Files > Import Settings, choose MP3 Encoder from the Import Using menu and click OK. Then select the song and choose File > Convert > Create MP3 Version, and the MP3 appears next to the original in your library. Apple says older purchased songs in Protected AAC can't be converted this way.

### Problems with M4P files

- **A message says the file is copy-protected**: the song is FairPlay audio, and this page cannot convert it. That is the refusal, not a fault.
- **Apple Music cannot convert the song**: Apple says older purchases that remain in Protected AAC can't be converted.
- **The M4P won't play on a new computer**: the computer needs authorizing for your Apple Account first, and only five can be authorized at once.
- **Authorization isn't working**: it must be done on the computer being authorized, not from another device.
- **A new computer can't be authorized**: while all five authorization slots are occupied, no further computer can be authorized.
- **You own the song but cannot convert it**: ownership and decryption are separate. The remaining option is to play the song in authorized Apple software.
- **The song plays on an Apple device but nowhere else**: that is the protection at work. Playback is limited to authorized Apple software or devices, and this page can't lift it.
- **The MP3 sounds different**: it has been compressed again as lossy MP3. Keep the original when possible.

guide.title: Understanding M4R for MP3 output
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4R file?

The M4R ending marks an iPhone ringtone. The contents are ordinary AAC in an MPEG-4 wrapper; only the ending sets it apart for iTunes and the iPhone. It sits in the MPEG-4 family, which keeps the container structure separate from the encoding of the tracks inside it. MediaInfo files the .m4r extension with the MPEG-4 formats, and NCH's WavePad manual calls M4R the ringtone type for iPhone. Like other MPEG-4 files, an M4R can carry track metadata beside the encoded sound. Audacity's documentation shows the other direction: its AAC export accepts .m4r as the filename of an MP4 ringtone.

Most people meet an M4R when they make a custom ringtone. Apple's GarageBand workflow on iPhone limits a ringtone to 30 seconds and offers to shorten a longer sound before it finishes. A dimmed source song in that workflow can mean it hasn't been downloaded to the phone.

### Programs that open M4R files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** MediaInfo shows the container and stream properties, and its format registry includes .m4r. It is not an audio player.
- **Windows:** WavePad reads and writes .m4r according to NCH's documentation, though it can't decode copy-protected input. NCH lists it on Windows but not on Mac, and links M4R output to the encoder options it shares with AAC and M4A.
- **Windows, Mac and mobile:** Switch, NCH's converter, accepts M4R input on Windows, Mac and Android, but excludes copy-protected files.
- **Mobile:** GarageBand for iPhone creates and installs custom ringtones from eligible audio.

### M4R and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .m4r for ringtones; .mp3 for MP3, whose registered media type is audio/mpeg.
- **Standard**: The name MP3 abbreviates MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, which became ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993. Fraunhofer IIS and other MPEG audio group members built it, starting in the late 1980s.
- **Compression**: MP3 is lossy. It uses a model of human hearing to drop sound listeners are unlikely to notice. A 128 kbit/s MP3 occupies about one eleventh of the space that the same sound needs on a CD.
- **Audio coding**: an M4R holds AAC audio in an MPEG-4 container. AAC is a perceptual audio coding family standardized through MPEG, placed in MPEG-4 Part 3, and it is lossy. It was designed to sound better than MP3 at the same bitrate.
- **Sample rates and bitrates**: AAC covers sampling from 8 up to 96 kHz, with bitrates reaching 512 kbps. MP3 bitrates run from 32 to 320 kbps.
- **Tags**: titles and similar tags in an MP3 sit in ID3 structures kept apart from the audio.
- **Playback**: every major browser plays MP3. Patent licensing for the format ended on April 23, 2017.

Here, FFmpeg in your browser uses the LAME encoder and asks it for 192 kbit/s. Audio sampled under 32 kHz ends up with a smaller bitrate, since the page leaves the sample rate alone. Any video is dropped. The command passes no track options, so FFmpeg's defaults pick the stream and copy the input's title, artist and similar tags to the MP3.

MP3 keeps song titles and similar tags in ID3 structures, while the M4R keeps track metadata the MPEG-4 way. If a tag matters, check it in the MP3 and add it in a tag editor. A batch of ringtones is handled in sequence, and each MP3 is saved separately without a ZIP.

### Other ways to convert M4R to MP3

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i personal-tone.m4r -vn -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k personal-alert.mp3`. The `-vn` drops video, `libmp3lame` is FFmpeg's wrapper for the LAME encoder, and `-b:a` sets the audio bitrate in bits per second.

### Problems with M4R files

- **WavePad or Switch won't open it**: copy-protected input isn't decoded, so M4R support doesn't mean they can remove protection.
- **A ringtone is cut to 30 seconds**: if an export exceeds 30 seconds, GarageBand offers to shorten it before completing the ringtone.
- **A source song is dimmed in GarageBand**: it may be unavailable because it hasn't been downloaded to the iPhone.
- **A player says the file is unsupported**: open the file in MediaInfo, which inspects container and stream properties, to see what its tracks hold. Then convert it here to get an MP3.
- **This page reports "FFmpeg failed with exit code N"**: the file may have no audio track. Get the original ringtone again.

guide.title: Understanding M4R to WAV
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4R file?

M4R is the file extension for iPhone ringtones. It is MPEG-4 audio with AAC sound, renamed to .m4r so that iTunes and the iPhone use it as a ringtone. An MPEG-4 file keeps its container structure apart from the encodings of its tracks, and it can store track metadata next to the encoded samples. Apple's GarageBand export limits a ringtone to 30 seconds.

### Programs that open M4R files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** MediaInfo inspects the container and stream properties, though it does not play audio, and its format registry includes .m4r.
- **Windows and Mac:** Switch accepts M4R input, and copy-protected files are excluded.
- **Windows:** WavePad lists .m4r as readable and writable here but not on Mac.
- **Mobile:** GarageBand for iPhone can make a custom ringtone from eligible audio and install it. Switch lists Android M4R input support.

Audacity's AAC export accepts .m4r as an MP4 ringtone filename.

### M4R and WAV compared

WAV is an audio container developed by Microsoft and IBM and based on RIFF. It usually holds uncompressed PCM, so files are large but exact, and it has a 4 GB file size limit. It suits recording, editing and professional sound production, and it often serves as a source format before compression. You can open it in Audacity, VLC, Windows Media Player or a web browser.

The page decodes the M4R and writes pcm_s16le, 16-bit little-endian PCM, with no video stream. Nothing is trimmed, so the WAV runs as long as the ringtone does. AAC detail that was lost stays lost.

### Other ways to convert M4R to WAV

- **WavePad for Windows:** open the M4R, choose File > Save As, select WAV and review the encoding.
- **Switch:** add the M4R, pick WAV as the Output Format, look over Encoder Options and press Convert.
- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i tone.m4r -vn tone.wav` writes a WAV and skips any video stream.

### Problems with M4R files

WavePad does not decode copy-protected input, so its M4R support does not cover protected tones. In GarageBand, a dimmed song is one not yet downloaded to the iPhone. When a ringtone runs over the limit, GarageBand proposes a shorter cut before it finishes the export.

faqs.answer: Not exactly. The video is re-encoded, not copied, and the page passes no quality setting, so some detail from the original can soften.

faqs.question: Can I convert an iTunes video?

faqs.question: Is M4V different from MP4?

faqs.question: Can I choose the audio track?
faqs.answer: No. There is no picker, and nothing maps streams by hand, so the streams that land in the AVI are the ones FFmpeg picks by default.

guide.title: Understanding M4V to AVI
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4V file?

M4V is Apple's video format, a close sibling of MP4 used for videos in iTunes and the Apple TV app and for phone and tablet video. It typically carries H.264 video with AAC audio in an MPEG-4 container. HandBrake treats its .m4v and .mp4 outputs as the same MPEG-4 container. Apple's iTunes Store sold some files with FairPlay DRM protection. FFmpeg's MOV/MP4 demuxer lists .m4v among the extensions it handles. The MPEG-4 family stores timed audio and video tracks and metadata in boxes, and playback depends on the encodings inside.

### Programs that open M4V files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC handles MPEG-4 containers with the usual MPEG-4 video and AAC audio codecs. FFmpeg lists M4V input explicitly, though processing also needs the relevant decoders.
- **Mac:** On Apple devices, QuickTime Player and the Apple TV app play M4V.

### M4V and AVI compared

AVI is a container introduced by Microsoft in 1992, based on RIFF. It interleaves video and audio and can hold many codecs, so the extension alone says nothing about quality. Modern features are poorly supported, which makes it a legacy format, yet you will still meet it in old Windows video, capture files and archives. VLC media player, Windows Media Player and QuickTime Player open AVI.

The page writes MPEG-4 Part 2 video, tagged xvid and without B-frames, plus MP3 sound at 96 kbps. Output is deinterlaced where needed. A frame over 1920 pixels on its long side is scaled down, a rate over 30 fps is thinned, and both sides are rounded to even numbers. Nothing is scaled up.

### Other ways to convert M4V to AVI

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i recording.m4v recording.avi` writes an AVI from the command line.
- **Prism for Windows:** add the M4V, set the Output Format to AVI, review Encoder Options and press Convert.

### Problems with M4V files

An unsupported codec can stop playback even when a player recognizes the container. Renaming the suffix cannot fix a damaged file or an unsupported encoding. A recording whose writing ended before the required metadata was finished may not open at all. If you need a different file than M4V provides, convert a copy and keep the original.

guide.title: Understanding M4V for MOV output
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4V file?

M4V is a label for an MPEG-4 container file. HandBrake treats the .m4v and .mp4 files it writes as one container, and it chooses the M4V ending for some jobs that combine chapters, subtitles and AC3 passthrough. In FFmpeg's source, the reader for MOV and MP4 files names .m4v among the endings it accepts. Inside, the MPEG-4 family keeps audio and video as separate tracks and stores metadata in boxes, so what plays depends on how each track was encoded.

You meet M4V files as exports from video software, as phone and tablet video, and as films or shows in iTunes and the Apple TV app. The ending doesn't reveal the codecs, which is why one M4V plays everywhere and another opens only in certain apps. Playback hangs on the encodings inside, so the first thing to learn about a stubborn file is its codecs, not its extension.

### Programs that open M4V files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg, the command-line tool, reads .m4v input explicitly in its MOV/MP4 reader. VLC media player supports MPEG-4 containers plus common MPEG-4 video and AAC audio.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player opens M4V files and can export a movie as a MOV.

The MPEG-4 container family stores audio and video tracks, and M4V is one of its files.

### M4V and MOV compared

- **Names**: .m4v for M4V, and .mov or .qt for MOV, whose media type is video/quicktime.
- **Origin**: Apple created MOV as the QuickTime format in 1991 and shipped it for Windows in 1994. It later served as the basis of the MPEG-4 file format, yet MOV and MP4 stay separate and can't be swapped freely.
- **Structure**: a QuickTime file is assembled from objects named atoms, and software may skip any atom it can't read. The MPEG-4 family uses the same idea under the name boxes.
- **Contents**: H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG video, with AAC or uncompressed PCM sound.
- **Reach**: browser support for MOV is patchy, and even Apple has largely moved to MP4. Mac screen recordings arrive as MOV files.

Here the video isn't copied across. FFmpeg in your browser rewrites it as H.264, using the ultrafast preset at CRF 32, and rewrites the sound as AAC at 96 kbps. The index goes at the front of the MOV so playback can start early. Anything over 1920 px on either side is scaled down, and frame rates beyond 30 fps are capped. Both sides are trimmed to even values, which costs an odd-sized picture one pixel, and interlaced frames get deinterlaced before encoding. Because it re-encodes, the MOV is a second generation of a lossy video. A fast preset trades compression for speed, so the file may be larger than a slow, careful encode would give. Your M4V is untouched; the result comes back as a separate file.

### Other ways to convert M4V to MOV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i family-film.m4v -c:v libx264 -crf 21 -c:a aac -b:a 160k family-review.mov`. A lower CRF keeps more quality than this page does.

### Problems with M4V files

- **It won't play**: a codec the player lacks stops playback, even if the app knows the container. Try another player such as VLC.
- **Renaming didn't help**: a different suffix can't repair damage or add support for an unsupported encoding. Convert it instead.
- **It stops partway**: a normal MOV or MP4-family recording can be unreadable if writing ended early, and an interrupted export gives the same result. Export it again from the source project if you still have it.
- **The MOV is shorter than the M4V**: a damaged or cut-short M4V usually still produces a file: the MOV holds whatever the page managed to read and is shorter. Compare the lengths before deleting the original.
- **The MOV is bigger than expected**: the fast preset favors speed over compression, so a heavy source can stay heavy. Run FFmpeg yourself with a higher CRF number if you need a smaller file, and expect some loss of detail.
- **The MOV won't play in a web page**: browser support for MOV is limited, so check the result in a desktop player before you embed it.
- **It came from the iTunes Store**: such files may carry FairPlay DRM, which this page does not remove.

guide.title: About M4V files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4V file?

An M4V is a video file in the MPEG-4 container family. It is associated with Apple's video workflows, but the extension does not prove who made the file. Both of HandBrake's output suffixes, .m4v and .mp4, hold the same container. MP4 itself, MPEG-4 Part 14, sits on the ISO Base Media File Format, an outgrowth of Apple's QuickTime, and video files in this family carry either .mp4 or .m4v.

A container organizes timed tracks. The picture and the soundtrack are separate tracks, each with its own encoding that a player must understand, and playback depends on those encodings. The family stores timed media tracks and metadata in boxes. Turning an M4V into an MP3 makes sense when you only need the sound, because the MP3 holds no picture. The MP3 is a fresh lossy encode of the soundtrack, not a copy of the original audio.

Videos bought from the iTunes Store can carry FairPlay DRM. Use a recording you have the right to process, and keep the original M4V in case you ever need the video again.

The MP3 format, formally MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, was developed at Fraunhofer IIS from the late 1980s and became ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993. Being lossy, it keeps what a model of human hearing says will be noticed and drops the rest. Every major browser plays MP3, and audio/mpeg is its registered media type. That is the usual reason for this conversion: not to improve the sound, but to get a file that plays almost everywhere.

### Programs that open M4V files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg reads .m4v through its MOV/MP4 demuxer, and the matching decoders must be present as well. VLC media player handles MPEG-4 containers along with common MPEG-4 video and AAC audio.

### M4V and MP3 compared

- **What they hold**: an M4V holds a picture track and a soundtrack. An MP3 holds compressed sound only.
- **Compression**: MP3 is lossy; it trades some sound information for a smaller file. Re-encoding a soundtrack as MP3 is a lossy step, not a rename.
- **Metadata**: tags such as song titles live in separate ID3 structures within an MP3.
- **Bitrates**: an MP3 can be as slow as 32 kbps or as fast as 320 kbps, using a 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz sample rate.
- **Reach**: MP3 plays on nearly every device, and its patent licensing program ended in April 2017.
- **Media types**: video/mp4 and audio/mp4 for the MP4 family, audio/mpeg for MP3.

Here the picture is dropped and the soundtrack is encoded with the LAME encoder at a constant-bitrate setting that the page fixes; you cannot change it. An MP3 cannot reach that rate for audio sampled below 32 kHz, so a soundtrack sampled lower than that gets a lower bitrate. No track is chosen by you: FFmpeg's defaults pick the streams. A video without any sound cannot supply material for the encoder, so the page reports an error instead of writing an empty file. The download takes the M4V's name with an .mp3 ending, and the original video file is not changed.

The new MP3 cannot improve the original recording. Saving an edited MP3 as a new MP3 adds one more lossy pass, so keep the M4V in case you need the original sound again.

### Other ways to convert M4V to MP3

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i input.m4v -vn -b:a 128k -c:a libmp3lame soundtrack.mp3`. The `-vn` option leaves out the picture, and The name libmp3lame refers to the LAME encoder inside FFmpeg. Decoding the input also requires the relevant decoders.

### Problems with M4V files

- **The conversion fails at once**: check that the video has an audio stream. A video with no audio track gives an error that begins "FFmpeg failed with exit code".
- **Unsupported codec**: a recognized container can still hold a codec the player lacks.
- **A new extension does not help**: renaming cannot repair damage or add support for an encoding.
- **Recording cut short**: a normal MPEG-4 family recording may be unreadable if writing ends before the required metadata is finished.
- **Very long files**: processing time depends on your device, and the page sets no length limit. Keep the M4V until you have played the downloaded MP3 to the end.

guide.title: About M4V files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4V file?

Apple developed M4V as a video format that sits very close to MP4. Both use the MPEG-4 container for video, audio and other tracks, and an everyday M4V holds H.264 video with AAC sound. FFmpeg's MP4 reader names .m4v among its endings, and HandBrake counts its M4V and MP4 outputs as one container.

You meet M4V in the iTunes and Apple TV world and in video made for phones and tablets. HandBrake picks the M4V ending for some combinations of chapters, AC3 passthrough or subtitles. The MOV and MP4 family supports timed media tracks and metadata stored in boxes, and how a file plays depends on the encodings of its tracks.

Files from the iTunes Store may be protected with FairPlay, Apple's copy protection. HandBrake's documentation lists MP4 and M4V as common file types for video from phones, tablets and cameras.

Most people convert an M4V so that a player, a site or an editing program accepts it. MP4 with H.264 and AAC is the combination that plays on nearly every device, and MP4 is the container that nearly every player expects.

### Programs that open M4V files

- **Mac, Windows and Linux:** VLC media player supports MPEG-4 containers and common MPEG-4 video and AAC audio. FFmpeg's MOV/MP4 reader lists .m4v input explicitly, and processing also requires the relevant decoders.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player and the Apple TV app open M4V.

### M4V and MP4 compared

- **Extensions**: .m4v and .mp4, with video/mp4 as the media type of an MP4.
- **Container**: both use the MPEG-4 file structure. MP4 is defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14 and can hold video, audio, subtitles and metadata. M4V is Apple's variant.
- **Codecs**: the usual contents are H.264 video and AAC audio. MP4 may also hold H.265 or AV1 video. An unsupported codec can prevent playback even when the application recognizes the container.
- **Protection**: an M4V can carry FairPlay DRM.
- **Metadata**: the MOV and MP4 family keeps metadata in boxes, and FFmpeg's reader treats .m4v as part of that family.
- **Support**: MP4 plays on nearly every device.

This page does not repack the streams. It decodes your video and encodes it again with H.264 video and AAC audio. The result is a new encode, not a bit-for-bit copy. If you want the original quality in a new container, copy the streams with FFmpeg on your computer.

### Other ways to convert M4V to MP4

- **FFmpeg (command line):** type `ffmpeg -i library.m4v -c copy library-remux.mp4`. FFmpeg's manual describes stream copy as copying packets without decoding or encoding them, and warns it may fail if the target container needs information the source lacks. Without `-map`, FFmpeg picks one video, one audio and one subtitle stream, so extra tracks are left out. In a test with a sample M4V, this command wrote an MP4.
- **HandBrake (Windows, Mac, Linux):** pick Open Source, then either keep the default Fast 1080p30 preset or choose another, give the output a destination under To, and select Start. HandBrake's docs list M4V among common video file types it reads. It re-encodes the video, so check the size, frame rate and codec in the result. HandBrake itself chooses the .m4v ending for some outputs, since it treats M4V and MP4 as one container.
- **VLC:** open Media > Convert/Save, use Add to select the M4V, fill in the Destination file, pick a profile like Video - H.264 + MP3 (MP4), then click Start. That profile's audio codec is MP3, not AAC.

### Problems with M4V files

- **The video will not play outside Apple apps**: the file may be a FairPlay-protected purchase, or the player may lack the codec inside it.
- **An FFmpeg exit-code message appears**: the page prints "FFmpeg failed with exit code" when the file could not be processed. Play it in VLC to see whether it opens at all.
- **The MP4 looks softer**: the video is re-encoded at CRF 32 with the ultrafast preset. Use HandBrake or the FFmpeg copy command when quality matters.
- **The MP4 has a smaller picture or fewer frames than expected**: 1920 pixels is the cap on the longer side, and footage faster than 30 fps loses frames.
- **A recording from a camera or phone will not open**: a normal MOV/MP4-family recording may be unreadable if writing ended before the required metadata was finished.

guide.title: About MAC and PNG
guide.markdown:
### What is a MAC file?

A .mac file can hold an image in the legacy MacPaint format, the picture format of the drawing program released with the original Apple Macintosh in 1984. MacPaint pictures are black and white on a fixed canvas of 576 by 720 pixels, and the data is normally run-length encoded, although a file with the compression turned off can still conform to the format. The data fork alone does not carry all the classic Mac file identification information, so a copy without a MacBinary or BinHex wrapper may not be recognized as a picture. Today the format turns up in legacy Macintosh graphics and retro computing archives.

### Programs that open MAC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Deark is a free extractor whose raster formats include MacPaint, and Netpbm's macptopbm is a command-line reader that writes PBM.
- **Mac:** GraphicConverter lists MacPaint import and export in its vendor manual.

### MAC and PNG compared

- **Colors**: MacPaint is black and white. A PNG can hold full color but here carries the same two tones.
- **Canvas**: MacPaint has a fixed canvas, and its writers crop oversized input.
- **Compression**: both formats are lossless.

The page runs ImageMagick compiled to WebAssembly on the main thread and reads the file as one image. Nothing is uploaded. The result is a PNG of the monochrome bitmap, written at the full size of the canvas, so there are no colors to lose.

### Other ways to convert MAC to PNG

- **Netpbm:** `macptopbm old_drawing.mac > drawing.pbm; pnmtopng drawing.pbm > drawing.png` converts in two steps through PBM. If the picture comes out shifted, the file may have a 128-byte prefix, and macptopbm has an `-extraskip` option for it.
- **Deark:** `deark -m macpaint old_drawing.mac` selects the MacPaint module, which is needed because not every MacPaint file can be autodetected. Deark converts pictures to formats such as PNG.

### Problems with MAC files

- **The picture is shifted**: a 128-byte Finder prefix was probably added in transfer. Try macptopbm with `-extraskip`.
- **The file will not open on classic Mac OS**: the data fork needs a MacBinary or BinHex wrapper to be identified.
- **Oversized art is cropped**: the fixed canvas cannot hold a larger picture.
