guide.title: About MJPEG and MP4
guide.markdown:
### What is an MJPEG file?

Motion JPEG is a way of coding video: each frame is compressed as an ordinary JPEG picture and the frames follow one another, with no prediction between them. It is therefore an encoding and not a container. AVI files carry it under the MJPG FourCC, following a profile that OpenDML documented in 1996 and 1997, and QuickTime can hold it as well. Cameras and capture hardware commonly record it, and editors sometimes work in it before exporting something lighter for delivery.

### Programs that open MJPEG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player lists MJPEG A/B decoding, and FFmpeg reads raw MJPEG.

### MJPEG and MP4 compared

- **Compression**: MJPEG compresses every frame on its own, so size follows the encoded images. H.264 also exploits similarity between frames.
- **Container**: MJPEG is an encoding that sits in AVI, QuickTime or a raw stream, and MP4 is a container.
- **Editing**: because every frame stands alone, editors can cut at any frame, while H.264 is made for delivery.
- **Reach**: every major browser plays MP4.

Conversion happens in your browser with FFmpeg, and nothing is uploaded. libx264 does the work, set to ultrafast with CRF 32 and the zerolatency tune. A picture above 1920 pixels on either side is scaled down, and 30 frames a second is the ceiling. Interlaced frames are cleaned up on the way, and audio, if there is any, becomes AAC at 96 kbps. After converting, play the MP4 and check its length and speed against the original recording, since the page does not preview the result for you.

### Other ways to convert MJPEG to MP4

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i camera.mjpeg -c:v libx264 -an camera_view.mp4` encodes H.264 and drops audio from the command.
- **FFmpeg with a chosen pixel format:** `ffmpeg -i clip.mjpeg -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:v libx264 clip_player.mp4` also sets the pixel format to yuv420p.

### Problems with MJPEG files

- **The file will not parse**: raw MJPEG and multipart JPEG are different formats, and a wrong assumption can stop FFmpeg.
- **A saved frame is not a valid JPEG**: an extracted frame can lack a Huffman table that a standalone decoder needs.
- **The result has no sound**: a raw MJPEG stream normally carries none.

guide.title: Understanding MKV and AVI
guide.markdown:
### What is an MKV file?

An MKV file is a Matroska video. Matroska is an open container format whose structure is written in EBML, itself a binary relative of XML, and it grew out of the earlier MCF project. One MKV can hold several picture, sound and subtitle streams together with chapter marks and descriptive tags.

Matroska fixes neither the codec nor the quality. What sits inside is the author's choice, so two MKV files can call for very different decoders and look very different on the same player.

You find MKV files in video collections, Blu-ray rips and downloads with several audio languages or subtitle tracks. WebM is a subset of Matroska, and IANA registers video/matroska for Matroska video.

### Programs that open MKV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv plays MKV with selectable audio and subtitle streams. ffplay, which ships with FFmpeg, reads the container through FFmpeg's Matroska demuxer and plays the video and audio inside.
- **Windows:** Windows Media Player opens MKV only with codecs added.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android plays whatever its decoders support, which depends on the streams in the file, and VLC for iOS plays most movie formats stored on the device or on the network.

### MKV and AVI compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mkv and video/matroska; .avi and video/x-msvideo, one commonly used label.
- **Structure**: Matroska is built on EBML and holds many streams, chapters and tags. AVI is a RIFF file with a header for dimensions and frame rate and another chunk for the media.
- **Codecs**: Matroska takes almost any codec. AVI names its streams with FOURCC codes, and its video can be stored raw or compressed, with or without loss, so the .avi ending says nothing about quality.
- **Size limits**: the original AVI format has size restrictions that differ from those of the later OpenDML extension.
- **Modern features**: AVI has limited support for them.

This conversion picks the codecs for you. The MKV is decoded and its video and sound are encoded again, which adds another lossy pass to both. Video becomes MPEG-4 Part 2 carrying an Xvid tag and no B-frames, and sound becomes 96 kbps MP3. Any frame larger than 1920 pixels in either direction is reduced, a frame rate above 30 fps is lowered to 30 by dropping frames, though the running time stays the same, and 1 pixel is cut from any odd width or height.

You cannot choose a stream here. If the MKV holds several audio tracks, the one FFmpeg selects by default is the one you get.

### Other ways to convert MKV to AVI

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i feature.mkv -c:v mpeg4 -c:a libmp3lame feature.avi`. FFmpeg's format list shows Matroska and AVI as both readable and writable. Add explicit `-map` options when you need a particular audio language.
- **Avidemux:** open the MKV with the Open button, set AVI in the Output Format section on the left, choose the video and audio encoders, then Save. Its output-format table lists AVI with MPEG-4 ASP video among many codecs, and calls MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 in AVI highly problematic.
- **Prism for Windows:** choose Add File(s), select AVI in Output Format, check Encoder Options, choose Save to Folder and press Convert. Prism lists MKV as an input only when the Matroska DirectShow filter is installed.

### Problems with MKV files

- **Wrong language or subtitles in your player**: you picked the wrong stream. The same MKV can hold several, so switch tracks in a player such as mpv.
- **Seeking is slow or jumps**: Matroska keeps its seek index (the cues) apart from the media, so a file with that index missing or damaged is harder to skip around in.
- **The file opens but shows nothing or has no sound**: the container was recognized but a codec inside it was not. Try another player, such as VLC.
- **The file is cut short or damaged**: the AVI is generally still produced, only shorter, and it stops at the point where FFmpeg could no longer read. Copy or download the MKV again if you need all of it.
- **The file is very large**: the page sets no size limit; a long film mostly means a longer wait on your device.

guide.title: About MKV and GIF
guide.markdown:
### What is an MKV file?

The .mkv extension marks a Matroska video file. Matroska uses EBML, a binary structure derived from XML, as its base, and it developed out of the older MCF project as a container for audio and video. An MKV may contain multiple video, audio and subtitle streams alongside chapters and descriptive tags, which the format includes by design. IANA registers video/matroska as the media type, and WebM is a subset of Matroska.

The container does not prescribe one compression method or a fixed level of quality, so two MKV files can differ completely inside. People use MKV for high-quality video collections, Blu-ray rips and videos with several audio and subtitle tracks. A clip from such a file makes a decent GIF only when it is short.

### Programs that open MKV files

- **Linux, Mac and Windows:** mpv offers desktop playback where you can select the audio and subtitle tracks.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay relies on FFmpeg's Matroska demuxer.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player is among the programs that open MKV.
- **Mobile:** Android and iOS both have a VLC app, and playback hinges on what is inside the container.

Plex also reads MKV, and Windows Media Player needs extra codecs for it.

### MKV and GIF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mkv uses video/matroska, and .gif uses image/gif.
- **Content**: an MKV holds video, audio and subtitle streams with any codec. A GIF holds only pictures, with a palette of at most 256 colors per image, compressed losslessly with LZW.
- **Sound**: GIF has no soundtrack, so a GIF made here is silent.
- **Transparency**: a GIF can designate one palette color fully transparent but offers no partial levels, and video frames have no need of them.
- **Frame timing**: CompuServe introduced GIF in 1987. GIF89a, dated July 1990, added the extensions for frame timing, with each delay set in hundredths of a second. A GIF can hold many images, and those delays are how GIF animation works.
- **Support**: every major browser displays GIF. License fees for LZW were first charged by Unisys in 1994; the patent expired in the US in 2003 and in Europe and Japan in 2004.

This page makes the conversion in two FFmpeg passes that share the same filter chain, so the palette matches the frames it is applied to. That chain deinterlaces frames flagged as interlaced, samples the video at 15 frames per second and fits the picture inside a 480 px box, keeping its shape and never enlarging a smaller video. Both dimensions are rounded down to even numbers. The first pass analyzes the whole video and writes a single palette. The second pass writes the GIF with that palette, set to loop forever. No audio is written.

### Other ways to convert MKV to GIF

- **FFmpeg (command line):** build a palette with `ffmpeg -i input.mkv -vf palettegen palette.png`, then write the GIF with `ffmpeg -i input.mkv -i palette.png -lavfi paletteuse output.gif`. The palettegen filter generates one palette for a whole video stream, and paletteuse then maps the frames to it, which is the approach this page takes. These commands keep the original size and frame rate, so the GIF differs from one made here.
- **Kdenlive (Windows, Mac, Linux):** put the MKV on the timeline and open File > Render from the menu bar. Pick GIF High Quality from the Generic presets, choose Full Project or Selected Zone and select Render to File. Full Project is the default and renders from the start of the first clip to the end of the last. Selected Zone renders only the part of the project you marked, so it lets you choose the section you want.

Both routes write a GIF without sound. Check the result at its normal size, since palette reduction shows most in gradients.

### Problems with MKV files

- **Wrong audio or subtitle language**: choosing the wrong audio or subtitle stream can give the wrong language. mpv provides track selection controls.
- **Seeking is slow or fails**: cues are defined apart from the media clusters in Matroska, and a file whose cues are missing or damaged can be harder to seek in.
- **The container opens but the video doesn't**: a player that understands the container may still lack a decoder for the codec inside.

guide.title: About MKV files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MKV file?

Matroska is the container behind the .mkv extension. Its structure is EBML, a binary format derived from XML, and the format developed from the earlier MCF project. A single Matroska file may carry numerous picture, sound and subtitle streams, plus chapters and descriptive tags in its design. The container requires neither a particular codec nor a quality level, so two MKV files can hold quite different video inside. IANA registers video/matroska for it.

You come across MKV files as video collections, as videos with several audio and subtitle tracks, and as Blu-ray rips. WebM is a subset of Matroska. People ask for this conversion because the movie plays fine but an editor or an Apple workflow wants a .mov. Both formats are containers rather than codecs, so the copy this page makes keeps the same video and sound and changes only the wrapper.

### Programs that open MKV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- ffplay: FFmpeg's player, which reads Matroska.
- mpv: a desktop player with controls for switching audio and subtitle tracks.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android and VLC for iOS: free apps that play most movie formats from local storage or the network.

### MKV and MOV compared

MOV is Apple's QuickTime file format. QuickTime arrived in 1991 and reached Windows in 1994, and its files end in .mov or .qt. Inside are objects called atoms, which software may skip if it doesn't know them. The codecs a MOV holds include H.264, ProRes and Motion JPEG for video and AAC or uncompressed PCM for sound. Mac screen captures of video land in this format.

- **Owner**: Matroska is an open container. MOV is Apple's QuickTime format.
- **Streams**: MKV carries several video, audio and subtitle streams. MOV can hold H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG video and AAC or PCM audio.
- **Relatives**: QuickTime underlies the MPEG-4 file format, but a MOV file and an MP4 file are different things and can't stand in for each other.
- **Browser use**: MOV is only partly supported there, and Apple mostly uses MP4 itself now.
- **Media types**: video/matroska and video/quicktime.
- **Extensions**: .mkv for Matroska; .mov or .qt for QuickTime.
- **Metadata**: chapters and descriptive tags are part of Matroska's design, while a MOV keeps its data in atoms.

This page doesn't re-encode. It runs FFmpeg with `-c copy` in your browser, which copies the video and audio streams into a MOV wrapper. Size and frame rate stay as the source had them, so the cap of 1920 px and 30 fps that other video conversions use is not applied. Because the codecs are copied as they are, they must be ones MOV can hold. The page maps no streams itself, so FFmpeg's defaults decide which ones to copy.

### Other ways to convert MKV to MOV

- **FFmpeg, copy:** run `ffmpeg -i input.mkv -c copy output.mov`. This is the same stream copy as the page. The `-c` option takes the special value copy, which means the stream is not re-encoded.
- **FFmpeg, re-encode:** run `ffmpeg -i input.mkv -c:v libx264 -c:a aac output.mov` when the copy stops or the editor wants H.264 and AAC. FFmpeg transcodes every stream unless you ask for `-c copy`, so this takes longer than a copy. In a local run it converted a VP9 and Opus source into a MOV holding H.264 and AAC.

### Problems with MKV files

- **Wrong language on playback**: an MKV can hold several audio and subtitle streams, and choosing the wrong one gives the wrong language. mpv has track selection controls, and FFmpeg's `-map` option chooses streams on your computer.
- **Seeking is slow or broken**: missing or damaged cues can make seeking harder. Matroska defines cues separately from the media clusters.
- **It plays in one app but not another**: recognizing the container doesn't mean every embedded codec can be decoded by the chosen player.
- **The MOV copy stops with an error**: MOV may not accept a stream's codec, and a copy can't change it. Use the re-encode method above.
- **The editor still refuses the MOV**: QuickTime containers may use codecs that the destination editor lacks. A new filename ending can't transcode the video or add a missing decoder, so re-encode to a codec the editor supports.

guide.title: About MKV files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MKV file?

Matroska, the format behind .mkv, is a container built on EBML, a binary relative of XML. It grew out of an earlier project named MCF. One file can hold several video, audio and subtitle streams, along with chapters and descriptive tags. The container does not prescribe a compression method, so an MKV's quality depends on the codecs inside. IANA registers video/matroska for it.

Because the container only wraps other streams, two MKV files of the same length can differ widely in size and in what a player needs to decode them.

You meet MKV in high-quality video collections and Blu-ray rips, mostly because one file can carry multiple audio languages and subtitle tracks.

### Programs that open MKV files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- mpv is a desktop player with selectable audio and subtitle streams.
- FFplay ships with FFmpeg and plays MKV files.
- VLC media player is a general-purpose desktop option.
- Plex, and Windows Media Player once codecs are installed, are also listed as ways to open it.

**Mobile**

- On phones, the free VLC for Android and the VLC for iOS player both handle the format, though decoding depends on the media inside the container.

### MKV and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mkv with video/matroska; .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **What they are**: MKV is a container for any mix of streams. MP3 is both a codec and a file format, MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, standardized in 1993.
- **Compression**: MP3 discards sound that a model of hearing says listeners won't miss. The audio in an MKV may be lossy or lossless.
- **Tracks**: MKV holds many. An MP3 holds one stream of sound.
- **Metadata**: chapters and tags live inside an MKV, whereas an MP3 stores song titles and the rest in separate ID3 structures.
- **Size**: set beside the same audio on a CD, a 128 kbit/s MP3 takes about one eleventh of the space, and a 192 kbit/s one about one seventh.
- **Bitrate range**: bitrates span 32 to 320 kbps in MP3, and its sample rates are 32, 44.1 and 48 kHz.
- **Origins of MP3**: Fraunhofer IIS started MP3 work in the late 1980s, joined by other MPEG audio group members. ISO/IEC 13818-3 extended ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1995, and licensing of its patents stopped on 23 April 2017.
- **Bitrate mode**: an MP3 can use a constant or a variable bitrate.
- **Typical use**: MKV serves video libraries and rips. MP3 serves music libraries, podcasts and audio for portable players.
- **Players**: Nearly every device is meant to play MP3, and each major browser does. An MKV needs a capable video player.

The command behind this page asks the LAME encoder for 192 kbit/s with the video disabled, so one MP3 holds the soundtrack FFmpeg selects. MP3 cannot reach that rate from sound sampled below 32 kHz, and the sample rate is left unchanged, so such a source gives a lower-rate file.

### Other ways to convert MKV to MP3

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i recording.mkv -map 0:a:0 -b:a 192k -c:a libmp3lame -vn soundtrack.mp3`. The `-map` option gives manual control of which stream is used, `-vn` turns video off.
- **MKVToolNix:** run `mkvextract recording.mkv tracks 1:audio.mp3`, where 1 is a track ID from `mkvmerge --identify`. The tool writes the stream as it is stored, so this gives a playable MP3 only when the track is already MP3.

### Problems with MKV files

- **The wrong language plays**: the file has several audio streams. mpv lets you switch tracks, and FFmpeg's `-map` chooses one when converting.
- **Seeking is slow**: missing or damaged cues make jumping through the file harder, because Matroska defines cues apart from the media clusters.
- **It plays but won't convert**: the container is recognized, yet a codec inside may not decode in the chosen program.
- **An error and no MP3**: the MKV may have no audio track. Check it in VLC first.
- **A command that errors**: FFmpeg's `-map` must name a stream the file really has, and an MKV without audio leaves nothing to map.
- **A second lossy pass**: re-exporting an edited MP3 as MP3 puts the audio through lossy encoding twice, so hold on to the first MP3 as the master.

guide.title: About MKV files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MKV file?

The Matroska format (MKV) rests on EBML, a binary layout descended from XML, and developed out of the older MCF project. Inside one file you can find many video, audio and subtitle tracks, plus chapter marks and tags. Its media type, registered with IANA, is video/matroska.

Matroska prescribes no compression method and no fixed quality level, so two .mkv files may hold unrelated codecs and behave differently on the same device.

### Programs that open MKV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay plays it through FFmpeg's Matroska demuxer, and mpv offers audio and subtitle stream selection.
- **Mobile:** VLC, in its Android and iOS versions, plays most movie formats.

### MKV and TS compared

A TS file holds an MPEG transport stream, defined as a system format in ISO/IEC 13818-1. It interleaves separately coded video and sound, with timestamps that coordinate decoder buffering, and can bundle several programs. Broadcast distribution is an important use. The usual extension is .ts and the media type is video/mp2t. An MKV can carry several streams plus chapters and tags.

The page decodes the MKV and encodes it afresh: H.264 with the ultrafast preset, zero-latency tuning and CRF 30, plus AAC sound at 96 kbps, wrapped as an MPEG transport stream. A deinterlace filter runs, frames above 1920 pixels on the longer side are shrunk, 30 fps is the most it keeps, and widths and heights round down to even values.

### Other ways to convert MKV to TS

- **FFmpeg, new encode:** run `ffmpeg -i movie.mkv -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -f mpegts movie.ts` to make an H.264 and AAC transport stream.
- **FFmpeg, stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i movie.mkv -map 0:v:0 -map 0:a:0 -c copy -f mpegts movie.ts` to keep the first video and the first audio untouched. Their codecs must fit TS.
- **tsMuxer:** run `tsMuxeR movie.mkv` to list the tracks, write the ones you want into a .meta file with lines such as `V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC, movie.mkv, track=1`, then run `tsMuxeR project.meta movie.ts`.

### Problems with MKV files

- **Wrong language**: an MKV can hold several audio or subtitle streams, and a player such as mpv lets you choose the right one.
- **Seeking is slow or jumpy**: cues sit apart from the media clusters in Matroska, so when they are missing or damaged, finding a position gets harder.
- **A player opens it but shows nothing**: knowing the container says nothing about the codecs, and your player may lack the one inside.

### What is an MKV file?

MKV is the Matroska container. Its structure is EBML, a binary encoding modeled on XML, and the format descends from an earlier project called MCF. A single file may carry multiple picture, sound and caption streams. Matroska's design covers chapter marks and descriptive tags as well, and WebM is a subset of it. Matroska itself sets no compression method or quality level, so how an MKV sounds depends entirely on the codecs inside it. IANA registers video/matroska as its media type.

An MKV can carry several soundtracks, such as an original-language mix and a commentary. That matters here: the WAV holds exactly one of them. None of the container's structure survives in the output, which is a plain sound file with no picture and no chapter list.

### Programs that open MKV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** the mpv player lets you pick the audio stream while MKV plays. The FFmpeg project's ffplay opens MKV as well, because FFmpeg includes a Matroska demuxer, though playback still needs decoders for the codecs inside the file.
- **Mobile:** the Android and iOS editions of VLC play MKV files stored on the phone. Whether a given file decodes depends on the codecs inside, not on the MKV wrapper.

### MKV and WAV compared

WAV is a RIFF-based wrapper for sound, specified by Microsoft and IBM in August 1991. Linear PCM is the usual payload, though compressed encodings can appear, and Broadcast WAVE adds production metadata. The Library of Congress names WAVE as a recommended format for audio collections.

This page decodes the soundtrack and writes signed 16-bit little-endian PCM with the video removed. FFmpeg's default stream selection decides which audio stream is used, since no -map option is given. Neither a sample rate nor a channel count is requested. Only the audio comes across, as PCM, and the title tag is normally carried along.

Expect a file many times the size of a compressed soundtrack. A WAV made from a lossy soundtrack is larger but not better, since decoding does not bring back what the encoder discarded. The 16-bit limit also trims any higher-precision source. For archival work, keep the MKV; the page never changes it, and the WAV is a separate download.

The result opens almost anywhere. Audacity imports most WAV recordings, PCM variants included, so you can start editing at once. Firefox can play a WAV straight from disk, and the Android edition's supported audio list includes it. A WAV keeps its tags in INFO chunks or in Broadcast WAVE extensions, and the two hold different information, so a field one editor shows may be absent in another.

### Other ways to convert MKV to WAV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i movie.mkv -map 0:a:0 -vn -c:a pcm_s16le sound.wav`. The -map option names the audio stream, so you decide which language or commentary track you get; 0:a:0 is the first audio stream of the first input, and 0:a:1 the second. The -vn option drops the video, and -c:a sets the audio codec. FFmpeg's format list includes Matroska and WAV, and it lists 16-bit little-endian PCM among the audio codecs.
- **mpv:** run `mpv movie.mkv --vid=no --oac=pcm_s16le --o=sound.wav`. The --o option switches mpv into encoding mode, and --vid=no leaves the picture out.

### Problems with MKV files

**Wrong language in the WAV.** The audio stream you extract decides the language. Use mpv to see which tracks the file holds, then pick one with FFmpeg.

**Seeking is slow or broken.** Seeking relies on cues, which Matroska stores apart from the media clusters. If they are missing or damaged, jumping around the file gets harder.

**A player opens the file but stays silent.** Matroska only wraps the streams. Recognizing the wrapper is not the same as decoding what is inside, so a player can open the file and still have no decoder for the audio codec. Try desktop FFmpeg or VLC, which cope with many codecs, and compare the result with the stream list shown by mpv.

**An enormous result is coming.** A long film can pass a gigabyte once it is PCM. Past the size limit of the original RIFF header, a very large recording needs the RF64 variant.

guide.title: Understanding MKV for WebM output
guide.markdown:
### What is an MKV file?

MKV is Matroska, a container for audio and video built on EBML, a binary format derived from XML. Its roots lie in a previous project, MCF. A single file can hold multiple video, audio and subtitle streams, and the design includes chapters and tags that describe the content. IANA lists video/matroska as its media type. MKV turns up in high-quality video collections and Blu-ray rips.

Matroska doesn't prescribe a compression method or a quality level. Two MKV files with the same ending can hold very different video and sound, so an MKV that plays in one app can fail in another that understands the container but lacks a decoder for what is inside. A file with several audio and subtitle streams can also start in the wrong language until you choose another track.

### Programs that open MKV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv offers desktop playback with a choice of audio and subtitle streams. ffplay comes with FFmpeg and its Matroska demuxer.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android costs nothing, and its decoding depends on the media in the container. VLC for iOS can play most video formats, taken from local storage or from network sources.
- **Media servers:** Plex plays MKV libraries, and Windows Media Player opens MKV only with extra codecs installed.

Desktop players differ in how much they decode, so if one refuses a file, try another before you decide it is damaged.

### MKV and WebM compared

- **Relationship**: the WebM Project backs an open format for delivering media on the web, and its container is based on Matroska.
- **Codecs**: VP8 or VP9 for the picture, Vorbis or Opus for the sound. An MKV can hold far more.
- **Media types**: video/webm for video, audio/webm for sound only.
- **Typical uses**: MKV for video collections and rips; WebM for web video and browser screen recordings.
- **Terms**: the project releases the format technology royalty-free.
- **Playback**: browsers care about the codecs inside, not the .webm suffix. Safari 14.1 on macOS began playing WebM files that use VP8 or VP9 plus Vorbis.

Nothing is copied from the MKV here. FFmpeg in your browser rebuilds the video as VP8 with libvpx at CRF 40 in realtime mode and 4:2:0 color (yuv420p), and the sound as Vorbis at 64 kbps. These settings favor speed over compression, so expect lost detail and a bigger file than a slow encode would give. The frame keeps its size and speed, capped at 1920 px along the longer side and 30 frames per second. Both sides are trimmed to even values, so an odd-sized picture loses one pixel, and interlaced footage is deinterlaced first. Because the page doesn't map streams itself, FFmpeg's own defaults choose which video and audio tracks reach the WebM. The MKV itself isn't modified.

Keep the MKV when chapters, extra tracks or attachments matter. The WebM is a narrower copy meant for playback on the web, and it can't bring back anything the re-encode discarded.

### Other ways to convert MKV to WebM

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i lecture-archive.mkv -c:v libvpx-vp9 -crf 31 -c:a libopus lecture-browser.webm` for VP9 video and Opus audio. Here -c:v libvpx-vp9 picks VP9, -crf 31 sets the quality level and -c:a libopus picks the audio encoder.

### Problems with MKV files

- **No sound or the wrong language**: the player may have picked another audio or subtitle stream. mpv lets you switch tracks.
- **Seeking is slow or jumps**: missing or damaged cues make it harder to move around the file. Matroska stores cues apart from the media clusters, and a WebM with no cue index has the same trouble.
- **It opens but won't play**: recognizing the container doesn't mean the player can decode every codec inside. Try VLC.
- **The WebM looks softer than the MKV**: the encode favors speed, so fine detail and busy scenes lose the most. Use FFmpeg locally with a lower CRF number if quality matters more than speed.
- **A track is missing after conversion**: no stream-mapping options are passed, so play the WebM before you delete the MKV.
- **The WebM is shorter than the MKV**: with a damaged or cut-short MKV the conversion typically carries on and saves only the readable part, so check the running time before you delete anything.

guide.title: About MKV and WMV
guide.markdown:
### What is an MKV file?

The Matroska container is written in EBML, a binary relative of XML, and traces back to the MCF project. Several video, audio and subtitle streams fit in one file, next to chapter markers and tags. It leaves the codec and the quality up to whoever made the file, and its registered media type is video/matroska. Films, fan releases and screen recordings are common sources of MKV files.

### Programs that open MKV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv lets you switch between the audio and subtitle streams while an MKV plays, and ffplay opens the file too.
- **Mobile:** on a phone, MKV plays in VLC for Android or VLC for iOS, depending on the streams inside.

### MKV and WMV compared

- **Container**: MKV is Matroska, built on EBML, and a WMV is an ASF container.
- **Streams**: an MKV can carry many audio and subtitle streams, while an ASF holds audio, video and other streams.
- **Codecs**: Windows Media Video versions 7, 8 and 9 appear in a WMV, whereas an MKV can wrap any codec.

FFmpeg works inside your browser tab, and the .wmv ending makes FFmpeg choose MS-MPEG4 version 3 video at about 200 kbit/s and Windows Media Audio version 2. The page also limits pictures to 1920 pixels on the long side and the rate to 30 frames a second, and it deinterlaces flagged frames. Without a track picker, FFmpeg decides which audio lands in the file. Play the WMV afterwards and check the language, the length and the picture.

### Other ways to convert MKV to WMV

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i film.mkv film.wmv` takes the Windows Media codecs from the .wmv ending.
- **FFmpeg with chosen streams:** `ffmpeg -i multilingual.mkv -map 0:0 -map 0:1 delivery.wmv` uses `-map` to name the video and audio streams that go into the WMV. Change the second index to pick another audio track when the MKV has several.
- **Prism for Windows:** add the MKV through Add File(s), set the Output Format to WMV, then click Convert. Prism lists MKV as an input when the Matroska DirectShow filter is installed.

### Problems with MKV files

- **Wrong language**: the page has no track picker, so choose the track with `-map` in FFmpeg.
- **Seeking is slow in the MKV**: missing or damaged cues make seeking harder, and they are stored apart from the media.
- **A stream cannot be decoded**: recognizing the Matroska container does not ensure that a player or converter can decode every codec inside it.

guide.title: Understanding MOV to FLV
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

Apple's QuickTime movie format, MOV, appeared in 1991 and reached Windows in 1994. QuickTime files are made of atoms, and programs may skip any atom they do not recognize. Inside, video may be H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG, and audio AAC or uncompressed PCM. QuickTime was the starting point for the MPEG-4 file format, though the two are not interchangeable. Mac screen recordings are saved as MOV, and its media type is video/quicktime. Few browsers handle it well, and Apple now favors MP4 in its own tools.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay handles MOV through FFmpeg's demuxer, and mpv plays it on the desktop.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MOV when the necessary decoder is available.
- **Mobile:** Phones can use VLC, on Android or iOS, though decoding depends on the media inside.

### MOV and FLV compared

Macromedia, and Adobe afterwards, built FLV to serve video through Flash Player. Streaming was the aim, and the typical contents are H.263 or H.264 picture with MP3 or AAC sound. With Flash at end of life it is now a legacy format for older web video and archived Flash content. VLC media player, mpv and Adobe Media Encoder can open it.

This page encodes H.264 with a fast preset and AAC at 96 kbps, wrapped as FLV. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced. Any side beyond 1920 pixels gets scaled down, and a rate beyond 30 fps is thinned by dropping frames, which leaves the length unchanged. Smaller or lower-rate video is left alone.

### Other ways to convert MOV to FLV

- **Prism for Windows:** add the MOV, set FLV as the Output Format, glance at the Encoder Options and click Convert.
- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i take.mov -c:a aac -f flv -c:v libx264 take.flv` writes H.264 and AAC into FLV.

### Problems with MOV files

Codecs inside a QuickTime container may be missing from the editor you are moving to. A rename does not transcode the video or add the absent decoder, so a file that will not open under another extension still needs a real conversion.

guide.title: Understanding MOV and HEVC
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

Apple's QuickTime format stores media as tracks inside one container. A MOV can hold several kinds of compressed picture and sound, so two files that both end in .mov may need different decoders. A camera recording and an editing export are examples.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** to inspect the source clip first, mpv gives a choice of audio and subtitle streams, and ffplay opens MOV.
- **Windows and Mac:** Premiere imports a MOV once it has the decoder for the clip's codec.
- **Mobile:** MOV opens in VLC for Android and VLC for iOS once their decoders cover the codec inside.

### MOV and HEVC compared

MOV is a wrapper; HEVC, also called H.265, is a video codec. A MOV can already hold HEVC. The .hevc output holds pictures alone: no audio track, no container.

Here the video is always re-encoded. FFmpeg decodes the first video stream of the MOV, shrinks a picture whose long side tops 1920 pixels and holds the rate to 30 fps. Your browser's HEVC encoder produces the new pictures, and FFmpeg writes them as an Annex B stream. A new encode can lose detail. Copying an existing HEVC track avoids that, and the FFmpeg extraction method below does it.

### Other ways to convert MOV to HEVC

- **FFmpeg encoding:** `ffmpeg -i camera.mov -an -c:v libx265 encoded.hevc` creates new HEVC pictures: `-an` leaves out the audio and `-c:v libx265` selects the x265 encoder. The result is a new lossy encode.
- **FFmpeg extraction:** if the MOV already contains HEVC, `ffmpeg -i camera.mov -c:v copy -an extracted.hevc` copies the video stream without re-encoding it, which works only when that stream is already HEVC. `-an` again leaves out the audio.

### Problems with MOV files

**A decoder is missing:** a MOV may hold a codec that the destination editor lacks, so check the codec inside rather than the ending.

**Renaming is not converting:** a new filename ending leaves the video as it was and installs no decoder.

**A broken save:** a MOV whose write was cut off can be unusable, although fragmented output recovers in a different way.

guide.title: Understanding MOV for M4A output
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

A MOV is a movie in the QuickTime format, which Apple released in 1991 and which reached Windows in 1994. The files end in .mov or .qt and carry the media type video/quicktime. Inside, a QuickTime file is a set of objects called atoms, and a program can pass over any atom it doesn't understand. The video might be H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG, and the sound might be AAC or uncompressed PCM. Screen recordings made on a Mac are saved as MOV, and iPhones record to it too; editors on macOS and professional pipelines use it as well.

The ending describes packaging, not quality or codecs, so one MOV can need decoders that another doesn't. QuickTime also fathered the MPEG-4 file format, though MOV and MP4 remain different and aren't interchangeable. Browsers support MOV only partly, and Apple now mostly uses MP4 itself. For this conversion what matters is the sound: a movie with no audio track can't give you a listenable file.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay relies on FFmpeg's QuickTime demuxer plus the right decoders for the streams in the file. mpv gives desktop playback where the audio and subtitle tracks are yours to pick.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MOV when a decoder for its contents is available.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player plays the movie.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android plays what its codecs cover, free of charge. VLC for iOS opens most movie formats from local and network storage.

### MOV and M4A compared

- **What it holds**: The M4A ending marks MPEG-4 files with audio and nothing else. Apple adopted it for music files without copy protection.
- **Codec**: almost every M4A holds AAC audio, a codec specified in MPEG-4 Part 3. AAC is lossy, and it was designed to beat MP3 at the same bitrate.
- **Range**: AAC supports 8 to 96 kHz sampling and up to 512 kbps. Songs sold through iTunes used it.
- **Reach**: all major browsers play AAC inside an MP4 container, and Android plays it in .m4a files on every release. Firefox may depend on system codecs for AAC.
- **Media type**: audio/mp4, against video/quicktime for the MOV.
- **Tracks**: the M4A carries one kind of track. Everything else in the movie, including any subtitles or extra video, stays in the MOV.

Here the soundtrack is not copied across. FFmpeg in your browser discards the video and turns the audio into AAC at 192 kbps, so the M4A is a new lossy generation of the sound, even if the MOV already held AAC. No stream-mapping options are passed, which means FFmpeg's defaults choose the audio track when a movie has several. A movie with no audio fails with the error "FFmpeg failed with exit code" and then the code itself. Files in a queue run one at a time, each saved separately. AAC is lossy and the sound is encoded again, so avoid converting the same recording back and forth. The page sets no limit on size or run time, and the MOV itself is never changed.

### Other ways to convert MOV to M4A

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i interview-camera.mov -vn -c:a aac -b:a 192k interview-listening.m4a`. The movie needs a valid audio stream.

### Problems with MOV files

- **The sound plays but the movie will not in a browser**: MOV support in browsers is partial, whereas every major browser plays AAC held in an MP4 container, which makes the M4A the safer file for a web page.
- **Your editor rejects it**: a QuickTime movie may use codecs the target editor doesn't have. Convert to a format it supports.
- **Renaming didn't help**: a new filename ending neither transcodes the video nor installs a missing decoder.
- **It broke after a crash**: a write cut short may leave an ordinary MOV unusable, though fragmented output recovers in a different way.
- **You need the picture too**: the M4A holds sound only, so keep the MOV if slides, gestures or on-screen text carry information the listener would miss.
- **The M4A is shorter than the movie**: a MOV that is damaged or cut short can still yield an M4A, but only for the stretch that could be read. Listen to the end before you delete the original.

guide.title: Understanding MOV and M4V
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

A MOV packages media using Apple's QuickTime structure. It can hold video, sound and other tracks, with different codecs permitted inside. A professional camera export and a small shared clip need not have similar sizes or decoding requirements just because both end in .mov.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows and Mac:** Premiere Pro can import MOV when it has the decoder the clip needs.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay, with the right decoders built in, and mpv both play MOV.
- **Mobile:** On Android and iOS, the VLC apps handle MOV, depending on the media it contains.

### MOV and M4V compared

M4V is an extension for MPEG-4 container files. HandBrake's documentation says an M4V and an MP4 differ only in the extension. FFmpeg also has a separate raw MPEG-4 video muxer named m4v, which is not what this page makes.

The page runs one FFmpeg command: x264 at CRF 30 with the ultrafast preset, AAC at 96 kbps, and faststart. Both the video and the audio are encoded again, and nothing is copied from the MOV. A larger or faster clip comes out with a smaller frame or fewer frames per second than it went in, so keep the MOV when you need the full frame for editing.

A frame already under the cap is left unchanged. A test run showed the file written with the ipod muxer and an M4V brand.

### Other ways to convert MOV to M4V

- **FFmpeg explicit MP4:** `ffmpeg -i edit.mov -f mp4 -c:a aac -c:v libx264 movie.m4v` names the MP4 wrapper outright and encodes H.264 and AAC.
- **FFmpeg repackaging:** `ffmpeg -i edit.mov -c copy -f mp4 repacked.m4v` copies the streams without re-encoding, which works when the MP4 muxer accepts their codecs.

### Problems with MOV files

**No decoder in the editor:** QuickTime containers can use codecs that a destination editor does not have, and an M4V ending does not change that.

**A new ending is not a conversion:** swapping .mov for .m4v changes the name only.

**A cut-off save:** a regular MOV that stopped mid-write may not play at all, whereas fragmented output recovers in its own way.

guide.title: About MOV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

QuickTime, Apple's movie format, dates to 1991, with a Windows release in 1994. Its files end in .mov or .qt and have the media type video/quicktime. Internally they consist of atoms, and software can skip the ones it does not recognize.

A MOV may hold ProRes, H.264 or Motion JPEG pictures, and its sound can be AAC or uncompressed PCM, so MOV files are a common source of Motion JPEG footage.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay and mpv, which offers selectable audio and subtitle streams.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MOV.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android and VLC for iOS.

### MOV and MJPEG compared

Motion JPEG treats a video as a series of separate JPEG pictures, one per frame. It is an encoding, not a container, so it travels in a wrapper such as AVI, where it is commonly identified by the MJPG FourCC, or in QuickTime. Because frames do not depend on each other, file size follows the pictures themselves, and production teams often edit in it before delivering in another encoding.

FFmpeg in your browser re-encodes the clip with its Motion JPEG encoder set to -q:v 8, adds 16-bit PCM audio and writes an AVI wrapper. Larger frames shrink to 1920 pixels, 30 fps is the maximum rate, a deinterlace filter runs and both dimensions come out even numbers.

### Other ways to convert MOV to MJPEG

- **FFmpeg to AVI:** run `ffmpeg -i take.mov -c:a pcm_s16le -c:v mjpeg -q:v 8 take.avi`.
- **FFmpeg raw stream:** run `ffmpeg -i take.mov -an -c:v mjpeg -q:v 5 -f mjpeg take.mjpeg` to write pictures only, with no audio.
- **FFmpeg to MOV:** run `ffmpeg -i take.mov -c:v mjpeg -q:v 3 -c:a pcm_s16le take_mjpeg.mov` to keep the QuickTime wrapper around Motion JPEG pictures.

### Problems with MOV files

- **An editor rejects it**: a QuickTime container may use a codec your editor lacks, and changing the file ending does not add the decoder or transcode the video.
- **The file will not play after a crash**: a MOV in its standard layout may be unusable after the write stops midway, while fragmented output behaves differently.

### What is a MOV file?

QuickTime, Apple's media technology, launched in 1991 and came to Windows in 1994. MOV is its file format. Matroska is a container built on EBML. It stores several video and audio streams in one file, along with chapters and tags, and it prescribes no single codec. guide.title: About MOV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

MOV comes from Apple's QuickTime, first released in 1991, with a Windows version in 1994. The file endings are .mov and .qt, and the media type reads video/quicktime. Inside, a MOV is a container made of objects called atoms. Software can pass over atoms it doesn't know, so the format could grow without breaking older players.

Video inside can be H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG; audio can be AAC or uncompressed PCM. It stores video, audio, text and timecode tracks. That range is why a player can handle the container yet lack a decoder for what is inside.

You meet MOV files in iPhone recordings and in Mac screen recordings, and in video editing on macOS. The MPEG-4 file format grew from QuickTime, but MOV and MP4 remain separate formats that are not interchangeable. Browser support for MOV is limited, and Apple itself now generally uses MP4.

### Programs that open MOV files

**Windows, Mac, Linux and Mobile**

- VLC: its input formats include MOV, MP4 and 3GP. VLC for Android and VLC for iOS are free mobile apps, and the contents of the file decide what they can decode.

**Mac, Windows and Linux**

- mpv: desktop playback with selectable audio tracks.
- ffplay: FFmpeg's own player, which plays MOV.

**Mac and Windows**

- Adobe Premiere: imports the container when the needed decoder is available.

**Mac**

- QuickTime Player: Apple's own player for MOV files.
- Final Cut Pro: Apple's editing program, which works with MOV files.

**Web and Windows**

- Microsoft Clipchamp: accepts MOV among its video containers and exports MP4.

### MOV and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mov or .qt with video/quicktime; .mp4 or .m4v with video/mp4.

guide.title: About MOV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

MOV files are what QuickTime, Apple's media framework, writes. The format dates to 1991, and a Windows version arrived in 1994. Names end in .mov or .qt, and the registered media type is video/quicktime.

Inside, a MOV is assembled from objects called atoms. Software that meets an atom it does not recognize can skip it. The MPEG-4 file format started from QuickTime, though MOV and MP4 remain separate formats and neither substitutes for the other.

A MOV is only a container. Picture data may be H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG; sound may be AAC or plain PCM. The extension never tells you which, so two .mov files can hold very different streams.

iPhone recordings and Mac screen recordings are the MOV files most people meet. Apple itself now generally uses MP4, and browser support for MOV is limited. Tracks for video, audio, text and timecode can sit together in a MOV, which professional video workflows use.

### Programs that open MOV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- ffplay plays MOV, because FFmpeg includes the format's demuxer.
- Desktop users get mpv, a player that lets you pick between audio streams.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Premiere from Adobe takes in MOV as long as it has the decoder the contents need.

**Mobile:**

- Android users can run VLC for Android, a free mobile media player.
- Most movie formats open in VLC for iOS, which reaches local and network media.

### MOV and MPEG compared

- **Origin**: MOV is Apple's QuickTime container. MPEG-2 grew out of compressed television delivery, and DVDs adopted it afterward.
- **Structure**: a MOV is a tree of atoms. In MPEG systems, coded picture, sound and data travel as streams, each elementary stream standing for a single coded component.
- **Video codecs**: MOV commonly holds H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG. This page writes MPEG-2 video.
- **Audio**: AAC or PCM in a MOV, MP2 in the file produced here.
- **Typical use**: MOV for video editing on a Mac and for iPhone footage. MPEG files serve Video CDs, DVD video and older video downloads.
- **Packaging**: packetized elementary streams divide each coded component into packets. A file with the MPEG ending can hold a system stream or bare video. Sound and picture multiplexed into one file still keep separate codecs, so a player decodes both.
- **Extensions**: the endings .mpeg and .mpg both serve MPEG video, whose media type per the Library of Congress is video/mpeg.
- **Media type**: video/quicktime for MOV, with .mov or .qt as the extension.

The page does the conversion in your browser through FFmpeg. It decodes the MOV and writes new MPEG-2 video using a fixed quality scale of 6, then encodes MP2 sound at 96 kbps. Frames marked interlaced are deinterlaced, large pictures are cut down to fit 1920 pixels, and the rate stops at 30 frames per second. No DVD or VCD preset is applied.

You can add several MOV files. They run in the order added, and each MPEG arrives as its own file, not inside an archive. The page applies no size limit, and the time a long clip needs depends on your device. The original MOV is never altered, and nothing is uploaded.

There is no per-file quality or bitrate choice, because the MPEG settings are fixed. The methods below use FFmpeg presets instead.

### Other ways to convert MOV to MPEG

- **FFmpeg, PAL DVD preset:** run `ffmpeg -i interview.mov -target pal-dvd interview.mpeg`. The documentation says the -target option accepts vcd, svcd, dvd, dv and dv50, and allows a pal-, ntsc- or film- prefix on the type. All the format options (bitrate, codecs, buffer sizes) are then set automatically.
- **FFmpeg, preset without sound:** run `ffmpeg -i interview.mov -an -target pal-dvd silent.mpeg`. The -an option disables audio recording, so the result has only video.
- **FFmpeg, NTSC DVD clip:** run `ffmpeg -i interview.mov -target ntsc-dvd -t 30 first-30-seconds.mpeg`. As an output option, -t stops writing after the duration you give, here 30 seconds.

### Problems with MOV files

- **Codec missing in the editor**: QuickTime files can use codecs that the program you open them in does not include.
- **A renamed file**: editing the file name leaves the video as it was and adds no decoder.
- **An interrupted write**: a cut-short write can leave an ordinary MOV unusable, and fragmented output recovers in another way.

guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

Files ending in .mov are QuickTime movies. The Library of Congress dates the format to 1991 on Apple's side and to 1994 for Windows. Files can use the .qt extension too, and the media type is video/quicktime.

MOV is organized as a tree of atoms, and software is free to pass over ones it does not understand. MOV and MP4 share a root, because QuickTime served as the starting point of the MPEG-4 file format, yet each is its own format.

What the movie contains is a separate question. Video could be H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG, and sound could be AAC or uncompressed PCM. The extension never tells you which.

You will find MOV files on a Mac, because screen recordings are saved in that format, and on iPhones. Browser support is limited and Apple now generally uses MP4 for its own work.

### Programs that open MOV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- mpv is a desktop player; you can switch between the audio and subtitle streams in a file.
- ffplay reads the container because FFmpeg includes its demuxer.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Premiere takes MOV files when it has the decoder for their codec.

**Mobile:**

- Android devices can use VLC for Android, a free player.
- VLC for iOS opens local and network media in most movie formats.

### MOV and MPG compared

- **Container versus family**: MOV is one specific container. MPG is an extension for MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 video and audio in an MPEG program stream.
- **Disc heritage**: the MPEG program stream was the standard for VCD and DVD video, while MOV is used for editing on a Mac and for iPhone recordings.
- **Number of tracks**: a MOV can hold video, audio, text and timecode tracks, whereas the MPG written here carries MPEG-2 video and MP2 sound.
- **Streams**: inside an MPEG file each coded component, such as the picture or the sound, travels as its own elementary stream.
- **Compression**: MPG is lossy, so converting a MOV into it means decoding the picture and compressing it again.
- **Audio**: a MOV may carry AAC or PCM. The MPG written here has MP2.
- **Uses**: MPG appears in Video CDs, DVD video, older downloads and broadcast capture.
- **Media type**: video/quicktime is MOV's registered type, and for MPEG video the Library of Congress gives video/mpeg.

This page decodes the MOV and builds a new MPG with FFmpeg inside your browser. The MPEG-2 picture is encoded with a fixed quality scale of 6, and the MP2 soundtrack runs at 96 kbps. Anything over 1920 pixels on its longer side is reduced, interlaced frames pass through a deinterlacing filter, and no more than 30 frames play each second. No DVD or VCD preset is used, so the result is a general MPEG-2 file, not a disc image.

Clips run in the order you add them, with a separate MPG saved for each. Everything runs in the tab, so nothing is uploaded, and how long a clip takes depends on your device. The page sets no limit on size, and your original MOV stays untouched.

Because these values are fixed, the page has neither a quality field nor a bitrate field. The presets below are the way to get a different set of options.

### Other ways to convert MOV to MPG

- **FFmpeg, VCD preset:** run `ffmpeg -i presentation.mov -target ntsc-vcd presentation.mpg`. FFmpeg's documentation gives `-target vcd` with a .mpg output as an example, and says all the codec and bitrate options are then set automatically.
- **FFmpeg, SVCD preset:** type `ffmpeg -i presentation.mov -target pal-svcd slides.mpg`. The type may be vcd, svcd, dvd, dv or dv50, with an optional pal-, ntsc- or film- prefix.
- **FFmpeg, film DVD preset:** use `ffmpeg -i presentation.mov -target film-dvd feature.mpg`. The film- prefix selects the film standard from the same list.

### Problems with MOV files

- **Missing codec in the destination**: a QuickTime file may use codecs that your editor lacks.
- **Only the name changed**: a new ending neither transcodes the video nor adds the decoder.
- **Unplayable after a crash**: an interrupted write can leave a regular MOV unusable, and fragmented output recovers differently.
- **Premiere or another editor will not take the MOV**: the editor may lack the decoder for what is inside, which is a different problem from the extension.

### MOV and MXF compared

MXF stands for Material Exchange Format, standardized through SMPTE documents. It wraps media essence with descriptive and structural metadata for professional acquisition, exchange and preservation, and operational patterns define how packages and essence are laid out. Files end in .mxf and use the media type application/mxf. The video inside can use various encodings, so the name alone fixes no image quality, and some layouts refer to essence kept outside the file.

The conversion decodes the MOV and writes fresh MPEG-2 video: 2,000 kbps, 4:2:2, forced to 25 fps, with frames shrunk when they pass 1920 pixels. The sound is 48 kHz stereo PCM. A deinterlace filter is in the command, and profile options are not.

- **The codec is missing**: the destination editor may lack a codec that the QuickTime file uses, and changing the file ending installs nothing.
- **The movie will not open after a crash**: a failed save may ruin a regular MOV, while fragmented output is affected differently.

faqs.answer: The WAV is 16-bit PCM, which is uncompressed, but it holds the MOV's sound as FFmpeg decoded it. It cannot restore detail that was already thrown away. If the MOV's sound was compressed, say as AAC, the WAV holds that decoded result.

faqs.question: Why is the WAV so large?
faqs.answer: WAV usually holds uncompressed PCM, so its size grows with the length of the recording, and WAV files have a 4 GB limit. The MOV's own sound is often compressed.

faqs.question: What if my MOV has more than one audio track?
faqs.answer: The page does not let you pick a track. FFmpeg's default choice decides which one you get. If you need a particular microphone or language, extract it with an FFmpeg `-map` option on your computer.

faqs.question: Why did my MOV fail to convert?
faqs.answer: A MOV that lacks audio makes FFmpeg stop, and the message reads "FFmpeg failed with exit code" and then a figure.

faqs.question: Can I extract the audio from a batch of MOV clips?
faqs.answer: Yes. Select the clips together and each is processed in turn, saving a WAV named after its MOV. Nothing is zipped, so you get one file per clip.

faqs.question: Can I set the WAV's sample rate or channel count?
faqs.answer: Not here. The page hands FFmpeg no sample rate and no channel count, so there is nothing for you to choose. If you need an exact format, the VLC method in the guide sets one.

faqs.question: Does my MOV get uploaded?
faqs.answer: No. Everything happens inside your browser tab, so the video never leaves your device. The only thing saved is the finished WAV.

faqs.question: Can I get an MP3 instead of a WAV?
faqs.answer: Yes. The site has a [MOV to MP3 converter](/mov-to-mp3/). Choose WAV when you plan to edit the sound.

guide.title: About MOV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

QuickTime's container is the MOV. It stores video, audio, text and timecode tracks side by side, and it served as the basis for the MPEG-4 file format. iPhones record in it, Mac editing programs export it, and production workflows use it for codecs such as ProRes. The ending tells you about the container, not the codec inside it.

For a WAV, only the sound track matters. A MOV is a multi-track container, so it can hold more than one audio track. It can also hold none, as in a silent animation or a screen recording made with the microphone off.

A QuickTime container can use codecs missing from the editor you send it to. Renaming a file never transcodes it or installs a missing decoder. A regular MOV may also be unusable after an interrupted write.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Linux, Mac and Windows:** ffplay ships with FFmpeg and plays MOV. VLC media player opens MOV too, while mpv adds desktop playback in which you choose the audio and subtitle streams.
- **Windows and Mac:** Premiere, Adobe's editor, imports MOV, provided the decoder it needs is present.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player is Apple's own player, and Final Cut Pro is Apple's editor.
- **Mobile:** Android and iOS users can play MOV in VLC, as far as the media inside the container allows.

### MOV and WAV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mov for the movie container; .wav for audio, labeled audio/wav or audio/x-wav.
- **What they hold**: MOV is a multi-track movie container. WAV is a RIFF-based sound wrapper documented by Microsoft and IBM in 1991, and it normally holds uncompressed PCM. Compressed encodings can appear in a WAV too.
- **Compression**: the audio inside a MOV may be compressed. The WAV made here is 16-bit PCM, so it is not.
- **Size**: a WAV is large because it is uncompressed, and it is capped at 4 GB.
- **Video**: a WAV has none, so the picture of the MOV is not carried over.
- **Variants**: Broadcast WAVE adds metadata for production and preservation work, while RF64 replaces the original RIFF size fields for very large recordings.
- **Metadata**: INFO chunks and Broadcast WAVE extensions each hold different details, so support varies.
- **Archiving**: WAVE is the Library of Congress's recommendation for digital audio collections.

Here the video is discarded and the audio is written as 16-bit PCM. Sample rate and channel count are not options on this page. Hold on to the MOV if the picture or its timing may matter later, since the WAV is a separate copy.

### Other ways to convert MOV to WAV

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i interview.mov -vn -c:a pcm_s16le interview-audio.wav`. The -vn option stops any video stream from being selected. In a test with a sample MOV this wrote a WAV. For a MOV with more than one audio stream, a `-map` option picks the one you want.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** Audacity's manual says FFmpeg is needed to import audio from most video files, and that on Mac only it can import unprotected MOV files without it. Bring in the MOV, go to File > Export Audio, select WAV under Save as type, and either leave the Signed 16-bit PCM encoding as it is or choose a different one.
- **VLC:** choose Media > Convert/Save, add the MOV, set the profile to Audio - CD, give the destination a .wav name and click Start. That profile writes 16-bit PCM, stereo, at 44,100 Hz.

### Problems with MOV files

- **An FFmpeg exit-code error appears**: a MOV without a sound track is one cause. Open it in a player first, to confirm that there is audio before you try again.
- **The WAV has the wrong audio**: with several tracks in the MOV you receive just one. Extract the right one with FFmpeg `-map`.
- **The WAV is large**: WAV is uncompressed, so its size follows the length of the sound and it stops at 4 GB.
- **The MOV will not play in your editor**: the editor may lack the codec inside it. Renaming the file does not install the codec.
- **A recording made on a phone will not open**: if the recording stopped before it was finished, a regular MOV may be unusable.

guide.title: About MOV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

Apple created the QuickTime file format behind MOV in 1991 and brought it to Windows in 1994. A MOV is built from atoms, and a reader may skip each atom it has no use for. It organizes media tracks, including video, sound and timing, and files use the .mov or .qt ending. A screen recording made on a Mac is saved as a MOV.

Typical contents are H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG video together with AAC or uncompressed PCM audio. The extension alone does not tell you how a file will play. QuickTime containers may use codecs the destination editor does not have, and renaming a file does not convert the video or supply a decoder it lacks.

After an interrupted write a standard MOV may not be playable at all, whereas fragmented output recovers differently. If a MOV from a camera or phone refuses to open, it may need repair before any converter can read it.

### Programs that open MOV files

**Mac, Linux and Windows**

- mpv: a desktop player where the audio and subtitle stream can be picked.
- ffplay: the MOV demuxer ships with FFmpeg.

**Windows & Mac**

- Adobe Premiere: opens the container once a decoder for the contents is installed.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android: free, and the codecs inside the file settle whether it works.
- VideoLAN's VLC for iOS: a player for most movie formats, with local and network media access.

A program that opens the container may still fail on the video inside, so test the file in the player you plan to use.

### MOV and WebM compared

- **Origin**: MOV is Apple's QuickTime container. WebM is an open format from the WebM Project, based on Matroska and intended for web delivery.
- **Codecs**: WebM video is VP8 or VP9, and its audio is Vorbis or Opus. A MOV can hold many codecs, including H.264 and ProRes.
- **Terms**: royalty-free terms cover the format technology the WebM Project provides.
- **Media types**: video/webm for video, audio/webm for audio-only files, and video/quicktime for a MOV.
- **Seeking**: a missing cue index can make seeking in a WebM less efficient, because the player has less direct location information.
- **Playback**: a browser cares about the real codecs inside, not the file ending.
- **Safari**: older Safari behavior should not be generalized to current releases. On macOS, Safari plays WebM holding VP8 or VP9 video with Vorbis sound.

On this page the choices are fixed: VP8 video at a constant-quality value of 40 in real-time mode, yuv420p pixels and Vorbis sound at 64 kbps. That favors a quick result. A source whose longer edge is at most 1920 px and whose rate is at most 30 fps keeps both. A smaller or slower source is not enlarged or accelerated. The download takes the name of your MOV with a .webm ending, and the original file is not changed.

### Other ways to convert MOV to WebM

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run ffmpeg -i quicktime.mov -c:a libopus -c:v libvpx-vp9 web-copy.webm. It needs libvpx-vp9 and libopus support, and uses a different codec combination from this page.
- **OpenShot (Windows, Mac, Linux):** add the MOV to the project, open File > Export Video, go to Advanced, set Video Format to webm and export. Codecs and bitrates are chosen on that tab too.

The desktop options let you pick the codecs, which this page does not. Before you publish a WebM, play it in the browsers your visitors use, since the codecs inside decide whether it plays.

### Problems with MOV files

- **The editor lacks the codec**: a MOV may use a codec the destination editor does not have. Convert it to a format the editor reads instead of renaming it.
- **A renamed file fails**: a changed ending touches neither the video nor the decoders on your system.
- **The file will not open after a crash**: an ordinary MOV can be left unplayable by an interrupted write, and a fragmented one recovers differently.
- **The WebM will not play on one device**: browser playback depends on the actual video and audio codecs, so check which codecs that device decodes.
- **The WebM is not identical to the MOV**: video and sound are encoded again with VP8 and Vorbis rather than copied, so the result is a new lossy version of the same picture and sound.
- **Seeking is slow in the WebM**: the cause may be the cue index, which the player uses to jump.

faqs.question: Will my old Windows player open the WMV?

faqs.question: Is WMV just ASF?
faqs.answer: In practice, yes: .wmv names Windows Media content in an ASF container, a design meant for synchronized media and delivery over networks. This page writes that container with MS-MPEG4 v3 video rather than Windows Media Video.

faqs.question: Why not rename the MOV to WMV?

guide.title: Understanding MOV for WMV output
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

The MOV is the QuickTime movie format, introduced by Apple in 1991 and available on Windows since 1994. Files use the .mov or .qt ending, and video/quicktime is the registered media type. A file is organized in objects called atoms, which a program may skip when it doesn't recognize them. Inside you might find H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG pictures paired with AAC or PCM sound.

iPhones record to MOV, macOS editors and professional pipelines use it, and Mac screen recordings arrive as MOV files. MPEG-4's file format was built on QuickTime, but the two aren't the same and can't stand in for each other. Browsers handle MOV poorly, and Apple itself now leans on MP4. A MOV says how its contents are packaged but not which codecs they use, so a file that edits smoothly in one program can be refused by another.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay depends on FFmpeg's demuxer for the format and needs decoders for the actual streams. mpv is a desktop player with a track menu for audio and subtitles.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MOV only when it has a matching decoder.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is free, with codec support deciding what plays. VLC for iOS reads most movie formats, local or network.

### MOV and WMV compared

- **Container**: WMV files are ASF containers that carry Windows Media content. ASF suits synchronized media that has to travel over a network, and it holds audio and video streams.
- **Delivery**: streams can come from a local disk or an HTTP server.
- **Compression**: WMV can use Windows Media Video 7, 8 or 9.
- **Media type**: the Library of Congress notes video/x-ms-wmv as commonly used, with no IANA registration.
- **Players**: VLC supports the ASF and WMV container and handles the 1, 2 and 9 generations of Windows Media Video. In FFmpeg's own list, the Windows Media Video 9 decoder is marked as not completely working, so support varies by player.

When a fixed hardware player or a legacy program asks for WMV, find out which codecs, maximum size and frame rate it accepts before converting. A new container can meet a delivery rule, but it can't make every movie run on every device. Keep the original MOV, since it may hold better quality than the copy.

The page re-encodes the video with FFmpeg in your browser and writes a WMV with FFmpeg's defaults for that container: MS-MPEG4 v3 video, which differs from Windows Media Video, plus WMA v2 sound at 128 kbit/s. Video keeps FFmpeg's default of 200 kbit/s, which leaves a busy scene looking soft. The frame is shrunk when it exceeds 1920 px on either side, the rate is held to 30 fps, and an odd-sized picture loses one pixel. Deinterlacing happens before encoding. Knowing the container isn't the same as having the video decoder, so an old player that opens some WMV files may still reject yours. Your MOV is not modified.

### Other ways to convert MOV to WMV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i presentation-source.mov -b:v 1800k presentation-legacy.wmv`. FFmpeg guesses the WMV format from the ending and uses the -b:v option to set a higher video bitrate than this page does.

### Problems with MOV files

- **Your editor can't read it**: a QuickTime file can use codecs the destination editor never installed. Export a format it does handle.
- **Renaming didn't help**: swapping the ending doesn't transcode the video or add a missing decoder.
- **It stopped working after a crash**: an ordinary MOV may be unusable once writing was interrupted, whereas fragmented output has its own recovery behavior.
- **The WMV looks soft**: the page sets no video bitrate, so the default applies. A tool where you choose the bitrate, such as the FFmpeg line above, gives you control.
- **The player reads the file but shows nothing**: a program can parse the ASF wrapper without owning the decoder for what it holds, so a compatible reader is no promise of codec support.
- **The WMV won't play on the old device**: picture quality depends on the codec and compression settings, not the .wmv ending, so a legacy player can still refuse the result. Check what it supports.

guide.title: MP2 to MP3: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP2 file?

An MP2 file holds MPEG Audio Layer II, a lossy format with perceptual coding, defined in ISO/IEC 11172-3 and completed in 1992. ISO/IEC 13818-3 extends Layer II for MPEG-2. Its decoding complexity is low, and it is the predecessor of MP3, which is Layer III. You meet Layer II in digital radio, on DVD-Video soundtracks, in broadcast television and in Video CD production. The Library of Congress lists audio/mpeg as the media type for MP2 files.

An .mp2 audio file is not MPEG-2 video. People convert MP2 to MP3 for players, music libraries and apps that expect MP3.

### Programs that open MP2 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg decodes and encodes MP2, ffplay plays it as well, and Audacity imports MP2 files natively.

### MP2 and MP3 compared

Both are lossy, so converting decodes Layer II and encodes Layer III, which adds a second round of loss. The MP3 here is made with LAME, which is asked for 192 kb/s. MP3, developed with major contributions from the Fraunhofer Society, grew into the most widely used format for music downloads. It supports constant or variable bitrate and ID3 tags, and it plays on nearly every device. The download is named after your MP2 with the .mp3 extension. A higher bitrate cannot recover sound the MP2 already left out. Editing the MP3 and exporting another MP3 adds a third lossy stage, so do your editing on the MP2 or a lossless copy.

### Other ways to convert MP2 to MP3

- **FFmpeg (command line):** enter `ffmpeg -i input.mp2 -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k output.mp3`.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** bring the MP2 in with File > Import > Audio, then open File > Export Audio and select MP3.

### Problems with MP2 files

- **Mistaken for video**: Layer II is an audio coding, so a file that carries a picture is the wrong source here.
- **Lost detail**: lossy MP2 coding omits sound information, and decoding cannot recover what was discarded.
- **Surround needs speakers**: multichannel playback needs a suitable multichannel speaker arrangement.
- **A player offers no MP2 support**: convert the file to MP3.

guide.title: About MP3 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

The letters MP3 come from MPEG-1 Audio Layer III. A 1993 standard, ISO/IEC 11172-3, defined it, and ISO/IEC 13818-3 broadened it in 1995. Fraunhofer IIS and MPEG audio colleagues built it starting in the late 1980s. Browsers all play it, and its media type is audio/mpeg.

Compression in MP3 is lossy: a hearing model picks out sound people are unlikely to miss and throws it away, so the file cannot be turned back into the original samples. Bitrate choices span 32 to 320 kbps at 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz. A 128 kbps file is about an eleventh of the CD size of the same audio. Titles and other tags live in ID3 blocks embedded in the file.

When an MP3 feeds another lossy format, the new encoder works from decoded audio that already reflects the first compression step. An edit followed by another MP3 export stacks a second lossy stage in just that way. A converted file cannot be better than the MP3 it came from, so treat the MP3 as the final source for listening and the converted file as a copy made for compatibility.

### Programs that open MP3 files

**Mac, Windows and Linux**

- Audacity: opens an MP3 as an editable project.
- ffplay: FFmpeg includes the MP3 demuxer.

**Web**

- Firefox: plays supported media by itself, though AAC and H.264 may rely on codecs from the system.
- Chrome: handles supported web audio and MP4 combinations, with the inner codec still deciding the outcome.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android: a free player on the phone, with the file's own contents deciding what it can decode.
- mpv for Android: a port listed by the mpv project.

Audacity can report an import error on a malformed MP3 that another player plays without trouble.

### MP3 and AAC compared

- **Family**: MP3 is MPEG Layer III. AAC is Advanced Audio Coding, a perceptual audio coding family standardized through MPEG. MPEG-2 specifies AAC in Part 7, and MPEG-4 places it in Part 3.
- **Wrappers**: MP4, QuickTime and other containers can carry AAC. A bare .aac file usually holds ADTS frames. The registered media type is audio/aac.
- **Profiles**: AAC includes LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2.
- **Use**: streaming and delivery to listeners are where AAC is found.
- **Compatibility**: a decoder for MPEG-2 AAC may not understand the MPEG-4 variants.

Encoding here goes through FFmpeg's built-in AAC encoder at 192 kbps, and the .aac output starts with ADTS frames. That is useful when an app asks for AAC. It is not a repair for a noisy recording or a low-quality download. If you still have a lossless master or the original, encode AAC from that instead.

The raw stream is the part people trip over. An .aac file carries ADTS frames one after another, with no MP4 wrapper. A player such as VLC reads it, while software that expects an M4A may not.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to AAC

- **FFmpeg (command line):** the command ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -vn -b:a 192k -c:a aac converted.aac does it. This is another lossy encode, and the bitrate cannot restore source information. For an MP4-based file, name the output with .m4a.
- **Audacity:** load the MP3 and export through File > Export Audio as M4A (AAC) Files. The optional FFmpeg library is required, and you get an M4A, not a raw AAC stream.

If you need the AAC inside an MP4-style wrapper, pick the Audacity route or name the FFmpeg output .m4a.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **Audacity refuses the file**: a malformed MP3 can fail there while another player copes. Try a clean copy from the source.
- **Tags change after combining files in Audacity**: with several imports in a single project, the newest file's tags can overwrite earlier ones.
- **Quality drops after converting**: each lossy encode removes more. Start from the original recording when you can.
- **The AAC will not play in a music app**: the app may want M4A. Renaming the extension to .m4a keeps the ADTS frames and adds no MP4 wrapper, so use one of the routes above for a real M4A.
- **The new file is not smaller**: 192 kbps is fixed here, so a low-bitrate MP3 can grow.
- **Cover art is gone**: it sits in a video stream, which the page leaves out. Add it again in your music app.
- **A decoder complains about the AAC**: the decoder may only know the older MPEG-2 form, so try another player.
