guide.title: MP3 to AIFF: formats and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 is short for MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, a standard that ISO published in 1993 and widened two years later. The work was led at Fraunhofer IIS, beginning in the late 1980s. Because it is lossy, an encoder throws away what a hearing model rates as least audible. At 128 kbit/s, the space an MP3 needs is roughly one eleventh of what the same audio takes on a CD. Bitrates range from 32 to 320 kbps.

ID3 structures kept apart from the audio hold the song title and other tags. MP3 is common in music libraries, downloads and podcasts. The media type is audio/mpeg, every major browser plays it, and the MP3 patent licensing programme ended on 23 April 2017.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports MP3 into an editable project, and ffplay, part of FFmpeg, can play it from a terminal.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP3 directly.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android and mpv for Android.

An AIFF opens in Audacity, which handles most AIFF files and every PCM variant, and Adobe Audition opens uncompressed AIFF as well.

### MP3 and AIFF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mp3 is audio/mpeg. .aiff is audio/aiff or audio/x-aiff.
- **Compression**: MP3 is lossy. AIFF often carries uncompressed linear PCM, and the AIFF-C variant extends the family to compressed audio.
- **Size**: a compressed version of a recording takes less storage than uncompressed PCM.
- **Metadata**: MP3 uses ID3 tags. AIFF can carry named chunks for author, copyright and annotations.
- **Origin**: Apple developed AIFF as an audio wrapper derived from the IFF family from Electronic Arts. Apple's version 1.3 specification is dated 4 January 1989.
- **Use**: masters and intermediate recordings are where professional audio users rely on AIFF.
- **Bit depth**: this page writes signed 16-bit big-endian samples.

Inside your browser, FFmpeg built as WebAssembly decodes the MP3 and writes the AIFF, as `ffmpeg -y -nostdin -i input.mp3 -acodec pcm_s16be -vn output.aiff`. The `-vn` option turns off video, and an MP3's embedded cover picture counts as a video stream, so the picture is not copied. The page sets no quality option. The AIFF is a decoded copy, so it carries every flaw of the MP3 and is much larger. Several MP3s run one after another, and each is saved as its own file named after the MP3 with an .aiff ending. Nothing is uploaded.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to AIFF

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i voice.mp3 -c:a pcm_s16be voice.aiff`. The encoder name asks for signed 16-bit big-endian PCM.
- **Apple Music (Mac):** open Music > Settings > Files > Import Settings and pick AIFF in the Import Using menu. Select the songs, then use File > Convert > Create AIFF Version. Apple says the song takes up much more space but sounds the same.
- **iTunes (Windows):** choose Edit > Preferences > General > Import Settings and set Import Using to AIFF Encoder. Select the songs, open the File menu, choose Convert and then Create AIFF Version. Apple limits conversion of store purchases to iTunes Plus songs.

Apple Music and iTunes add the converted copy next to the original in your library. Converting a compressed file to an uncompressed one does not restore lost quality, so none of these methods improves the sound. FFmpeg suits scripts and a folder of files, while the Apple apps suit a music library.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **A damaged MP3 may not import**: Audacity can report an import error for a malformed MP3 even when another player can play it. Try re-downloading the file.
- **Tags get replaced when you combine files**: a single Audacity project that receives several imports may overwrite earlier metadata with the tags of the last file. Check the title and artist before you export.
- **A second lossy pass costs quality**: if you edit an MP3 and export another MP3, a second lossy encoding stage is added. Export to AIFF instead if you plan to keep editing.
- **The cover picture does not carry over**: this page drops the embedded picture, so add the artwork again in your editor.
- **It does not sound better**: detail was already lost when the MP3 was encoded. Look for a lossless original if you need a master.

guide.title: About MP3 and AMR
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file

Short for MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III, MP3 is a lossy format that MPEG standardized under ISO/IEC 11172-3 with substantial help from the Fraunhofer Society, and it became the normal choice for music downloads, podcasts and portable players. It can be encoded at a constant or a variable bitrate, keeps song titles and other tags in ID3 structures, and has the media type audio/mpeg.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows and Mac:** Audacity edits it as an imported project.
- **Windows:** Windows Media Player for listening.
- **Linux:** ffplay, the FFmpeg player.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play it straight from a page.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android and the Android port of mpv.

Apple Music and VLC media player also play MP3.

### MP3 and AMR compared

- **Purpose**: MP3 carries music. AMR is a speech codec standardized by 3GPP for mobile phone networks, optimized for voice.
- **Rate**: AMR narrowband spans 4.75 to 12.2 kbps at 8 kHz in 20-millisecond frames.
- **Origin**: AMR expands to Adaptive Multi-Rate and was standardized by ETSI for GSM speech, and 3GPP adopted it for third-generation cellular systems.
- **Storage**: RFC 4867 defines storage files as well as RTP transport, and the media type for narrowband AMR is audio/AMR.
- **Use**: AMR is used for voice recordings and voice messages on phones.

On this page the command asks FFmpeg for the libopencore_amrnb encoder at 8,000 Hz, mono, 12.2 kbps. That encoder is missing from this page's FFmpeg build, so no AMR file is written. Use the methods below on your own machine.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to AMR

- **FFmpeg with an external AMR-NB encoder:** `ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -codec:a libopencore_amrnb -b:a 12.2k -ar 8000 -ac 1 voice.amr`.
- **SoX with AMR-NB writing support:** `sox song.mp3 -t amr-nb -C 7 -c 1 -r 8000 voice.amr`.
- **Switch Sound File Converter:** use the Add button or File > Add to load the MP3, choose AMR in the Output Format field and click Convert.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **Import errors**: Audacity can refuse a malformed MP3 that another player still plays.
- **Tags replaced**: when you combine imports in a single Audacity project, tags from the latest file can replace earlier metadata.
- **Two lossy stages**: exporting another lossy file after editing an MP3 compresses the audio a second time, so keep the original.

guide.title: About MP3 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 is short for MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III. MPEG standardized this lossy audio format as ISO/IEC 11172-3, and the Fraunhofer Society contributed heavily. For downloadable music it is the most common choice.

Lossy compression means some sound is discarded to save space. The bitrate may be constant or variable, titles and artists sit in ID3 tags, and the file plays on nearly every device. Music libraries, podcasts and portable players all use it.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity turns an MP3 into an editable project. ffplay can play it if the FFmpeg build you installed includes the decoder.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play supported audio directly.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android plays it, and so does mpv for Android.

### MP3 and AU compared

An AU file opens with the four bytes .snd, then a header recording the encoding, sample rate and channel count. Multibyte values are big-endian. The specification defines linear PCM, mu-law, A-law, floating point and ADPCM, so one .au file can differ from the next, and Sun's format is a legacy one used for Unix and Java system sounds.

FFmpeg decodes the MP3, drops any video and writes signed 16-bit big-endian PCM at 44,100 Hz in two channels. Nothing is compressed afterward, so quality is exactly what the MP3 had and the file grows a great deal. Before you convert, confirm the receiving program accepts this AU encoding. Afterward, play the AU once to check the length and that both channels carry sound.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to AU

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i audio.mp3 -c:a pcm_s16be -ar 44100 -ac 2 -f au audio.au`.
- **SoX:** run `sox audio.mp3 -r 44100 -c 2 -b 16 -e signed-integer -B audio.au`.
- **Switch Sound File Converter on Windows:** use Add to load the MP3, set Output Format to AU and press Convert.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **An import fails**: Audacity may report an error on a damaged MP3 that a different player still plays.
- **Tags change after combining files**: bringing several MP3s into one Audacity project can swap earlier metadata for the newest file's tags.
- **A re-saved MP3 sounds worse**: exporting a new MP3 after editing one adds another lossy stage, so stay in PCM until the end.

### What is an MP3 file?

MP3, formally MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, came out of Fraunhofer IIS and was standardized as ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993. It saves space by discarding what a hearing model says most listeners would not notice. Sampling can happen at 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz, with the bitrate set between 32 and 320 kbps; tags such as titles live in separate ID3 blocks. Every major browser plays MP3, which makes it the usual way to share a recording and a poor one to edit.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** an MP3 imported into Audacity becomes a project you can edit, and ffplay plays one.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP3 directly, so nothing needs installing just to listen.
- **Mobile:** the Android port of mpv and VLC for Android handle MP3.

### MP3 and CAF compared

- **Compression**: MP3 is lossy, and a CAF written here holds uncompressed PCM.
- **Container**: CAF uses 64-bit offsets, so it can hold recordings larger than older containers allow.
- **Metadata**: MP3 keeps titles in separate ID3 blocks, while CAF has its own information chunks for descriptive text.
- **Channels**: CAF supports multiple channels with optional layout information.

Everything runs locally with FFmpeg and nothing is uploaded. FFmpeg decodes the MP3 and writes 16-bit little-endian stereo PCM at 44.1 kHz into the CAF. Those settings are fixed, so a mono or 48 kHz MP3 still comes out as two channels at 44.1 kHz. Decoding cannot restore sound the MP3 already discarded; the CAF only stops any further loss while you edit. Open the CAF in your editor afterwards and listen to the start and the end.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to CAF

- **FFmpeg PCM:** `ffmpeg -i listening.mp3 -c:a pcm_s16le -ar 44100 -ac 2 -f caf editing.caf` names the PCM encoder, the sample rate, the channel count and the CAF container, the same recipe this page runs.
- **Apple afconvert:** `afconvert -f caff -d LEI16@44100 -c 2 listening.mp3 editing.caf` is the tool built into macOS. The `-f caff` option selects CAF and `-d LEI16@44100` selects 16-bit little-endian samples at 44.1 kHz.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **Re-exporting as MP3 costs quality**: every export is another lossy pass, so keep the CAF as the working copy.
- **A damaged file will not import**: Audacity may refuse a broken MP3 that another player still handles.
- **Tags can be overwritten**: bring several files into one Audacity project and the newest file's tags may replace the earlier ones.

guide.title: About MP3 and CDDA
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 is MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, defined in ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993. It omits sound that listeners are unlikely to hear, and its bitrates run from 32 to 320 kbps. ID3 tags carry the title and artist inside the same file, and it is the usual way to share a recording on the web.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** an imported MP3 becomes an editable project in Audacity, while ffplay handles playback.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP3 directly.
- **Mobile:** a phone can play MP3 with either VLC for Android or the mpv port.

### MP3 and CDDA compared

- **Compression**: MP3 is lossy, while the result here is raw samples.
- **Header**: MP3 has frames and ID3 tags. The raw file has no header, so nothing in it states the rate or channel count.
- **Apple's .cdda**: on macOS the ending names AIFF-C audio, and a suffix alone cannot prove what is inside a file.

Nothing leaves your device, because FFmpeg runs inside the tab. The MP3 is decoded and the signed samples are written as a raw stream, always as two channels. The rate and sample format are fixed, so any player must be told them, and the output is not the AIFF-C file Apple software expects. Nothing is compressed, which is why the file is larger than the MP3. Open it as raw audio in an editor and listen before you rely on it.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to CDDA

- **FFmpeg raw PCM:** `ffmpeg -i track.mp3 -ar 44100 -ac 2 -c:a pcm_s16le -f s16le samples.cdda` writes headerless samples, the same layout this page writes.
- **FFmpeg WAV and Python wave extraction:** Convert to WAV with FFmpeg first (`ffmpeg -i track.mp3 -ac 2 -ar 44100 -c:a pcm_s16le prepared.wav`), then use Python's `wave` module to read the frames with `readframes` and write them out with no header. A short script can check the channels, sample width and rate with `getnchannels`, `getsampwidth` and `getframerate` before writing.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **A broken MP3 is rejected**: a malformed file can trigger an import error in Audacity even when other players cope.
- **Metadata follows the last import**: when several MP3s share one Audacity project, the latest file's tags can displace the earlier ones.
- **Going back to MP3 loses more**: encoding the raw samples again as MP3 is a new lossy step.

guide.title: About MP3 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 began as MPEG-1 Audio Layer III and became a standard in 1993 as ISO/IEC 11172-3. Its development took place at Fraunhofer IIS, which worked on it from the late 1980s. Patent licensing ended on 23 April 2017. The media type is audio/mpeg.

The format is lossy. A model of human hearing decides which sounds listeners are unlikely to notice, and those are discarded. Decoding an MP3 produces audio samples, but it does not undo those decisions, so the loss stays part of the signal handed to the next encoder.

Song titles and other tags live in separate ID3 structures inside the file. Available bitrates range between 32 and 320 kbps. Take 128 kbps: that file comes to around one eleventh of the same audio on a CD. A request for FLAC can mean different things: a program may need that format as input, or someone may want an archival master, and a FLAC made from an MP3 is not one.

### Programs that open MP3 files

**Windows, Linux and Mac**

- Audacity: imports MP3 into an editable project, which suits trimming and fixing a track.
- ffplay: FFmpeg's own player, which plays MP3 through FFmpeg's MP3 demuxer from the command line.

**Web**

- Chrome and Firefox: both play MP3 directly, which makes a browser a quick way to confirm the file is readable.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android: a free player, and its decoding follows from what the file contains.
- mpv for Android: the Android port that the mpv project itself links to.

If you import many tracks into one Audacity project, the last file's tags can replace what came before.

### MP3 and FLAC compared

- **Compression**: MP3 is lossy. FLAC squeezes integer PCM audio down while keeping every sample intact.
- **Standard**: FLAC's specification is open, and its reference implementation is open source. The format description was published as RFC 9639 in December 2024.
- **Range**: from one through eight channels, and each sample can be stored at a depth between four and 32 bits, which covers everything from low-resolution speech to studio masters.
- **Metadata**: seek points, pictures and Vorbis comments can all be stored in FLAC, and the media type is audio/flac.
- **Integrity**: a damaged frame can fail its checksum, but lossless encoding does not prevent storage corruption.
- **Size**: a FLAC can be far larger than an MP3 of the same song.
- **Re-saving**: a FLAC can be saved again without further loss, while exporting another MP3 adds a second lossy stage.

The page decodes the MP3 and writes its samples through FFmpeg's FLAC encoder, so the numbers are exact but the music is the MP3's music. It sets no compression level or bit depth.

FLAC suits a working copy. If you plan to trim or otherwise edit the track in several rounds, saving each round as FLAC avoids stacking another lossy encode on the MP3. When the edits are done, export to whatever format the destination needs.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to FLAC

- **Audacity:** load the MP3, choose File > Export Audio, select FLAC from Format, review channels, sample rate, bit depth and level, then export. The level changes packing efficiency, not quality.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -vn -c:a flac decoded.flac. It decodes the MP3 and stores the samples losslessly, and the FLAC does not become a lossless original recording.

Both give the same kind of result: a bigger file with the MP3's sound. Pick Audacity if you want to fix the track first, and FFmpeg if you have many files and a terminal.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **An import error**: a badly formed MP3 can be refused by Audacity yet play elsewhere. Try a clean copy.
- **No quality gain**: the samples the MP3 threw away stay gone. FLAC only stores what the MP3 decodes to.
- **Editing adds loss**: editing an MP3 and exporting another MP3 introduces a second lossy encoding stage. Exporting FLAC avoids adding one.
- **Tags change on import**: several files in one Audacity project can leave you with the latest file's tags in place of earlier metadata.
- **A player rejects the FLAC**: native Android handling of FLAC is documented for mono or stereo and favors 16-bit samples. Try another player.

guide.title: About MP3 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 stands for MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, a lossy codec. Development began at Fraunhofer IIS in the late 1980s alongside other members of the MPEG audio group. It was first standardized in 1993 as ISO/IEC 11172-3, with an extension in 1995 as ISO/IEC 13818-3. Its encoder follows a model of human hearing and throws away sound a listener probably won't notice. Set against a CD, an MP3 at 128 kbit/s is roughly an eleventh of the size for the same audio.

Titles and further tags live in separate ID3 structures within the file. The allowed bitrates go from 32 to 320 kbps, with sampling rates of 32, 44.1 and 48 kHz. On 23 April 2017 the MP3 patent licensing program ended. You come across MP3 in music libraries and downloads, in podcasts and on portable players, and every major browser plays it. Its registered media type is audio/mpeg.

### Programs that open MP3 files

**Windows and Linux**

- VLC media player: can play MP3 files.

**Windows**

- Windows Media Player: plays MP3.

**Mac**

- Apple Music: plays MP3.

**Web**

- Chrome and Firefox: play MP3 directly.

**Mobile**

- Android: VLC for Android plays MP3, and mpv for Android does too.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Audacity: turns MP3 audio into an editable project, and exports M4A after you install its optional FFmpeg library.
- ffplay: the player that comes with FFmpeg.

### MP3 and M4A compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mp3 uses audio/mpeg. .m4a uses audio/mp4.
- **Container**: an MP3 is a stream of audio frames. M4A wraps its audio in the MPEG-4 container, the one MP4 files use.
- **Codec**: MP3 is always lossy. An M4A usually holds AAC, which is also lossy, or lossless Apple Lossless. AAC covers sample rates of 8 to 96 kHz and bitrates reaching 512 kbps, a wider range than MP3's 32 to 320 kbps.
- **Quality for size**: AAC aims for better sound than MP3 at an equal bitrate.
- **Tags**: MP3 stores them in ID3 structures. M4A has metadata tags and cover art in the MPEG-4 container.
- **Editing**: M4A import in Audacity depends on the optional FFmpeg library, and a DRM-protected recording will not load. The converter here writes a fresh AAC encode, which has no DRM.
- **Reach**: every major browser plays MP3, and every Android version handles AAC audio in .m4a files.

The converter decodes the MP3 and writes AAC into an M4A, with a 192 kbps setting and video streams left out. The new file has the MP3's audio plus one more generation of loss. If your MP3 was 128 kbps, the swap can cost space and buys nothing audible; do it because an app or device asks for M4A, not for the sound.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to M4A

- **Audacity:** after opening the MP3, File > Export Audio leads to a Format menu, where M4A (AAC) Files (FFmpeg) is the entry to choose. FFmpeg's library isn't bundled with Audacity, so you add it yourself first. M4A (AAC) is a lossy format.
- **FFmpeg:** in a terminal, `ffmpeg -i source-track.mp3 -b:a 192k -c:a aac listening-copy.m4a` encodes AAC at the bitrate you give it. The `-c:a aac` option selects FFmpeg's native AAC encoder, and `-b:a` sets the audio bitrate. Because the MP3 is already lossy, this adds a second lossy encoding.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **A damaged MP3 won't import**: Audacity may refuse a malformed file with an import error, although some other player still plays it. Play it to the end elsewhere, then get another copy.
- **Tags replaced in Audacity**: importing several MP3 files into one project can replace earlier metadata with the tags of the latest file. Open every file in a separate project window to hold on to its tags.
- **Editing and re-exporting adds loss**: an MP3 edited and saved as MP3 is encoded a second time. Cut from a lossless source when you have one.
- **The cover picture is gone**: the converter treats embedded cover art as a video stream and drops video streams. Add the picture again in your music app.
- **A very long MP3 takes a while**: there is no size limit or timeout, and your own device does the encoding, so the time follows its speed.

guide.title: Understanding MP3 for M4R output
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

The MP3 name comes from MPEG-1 Audio Layer III. ISO/IEC 11172-3 standardized it in 1993; the 1995 extension is ISO/IEC 13818-3. Fraunhofer IIS began the work in the late 1980s with other MPEG audio group members. Being lossy, it discards sound that a listener is unlikely to miss.

An MP3 runs from 32 up to 320 kbps, sampled at 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz. ID3 structures inside the file hold the title and other tags apart from the audio. Its media type is audio/mpeg, and all the major browsers play it. The program that licensed MP3 patents ended on 23 April 2017.

MP3 files turn up in podcasts, downloaded music and on portable players. The MP3 you start from is usually a whole song, while a ringtone is a short passage of it, so most of the work in making a ringtone is choosing the part you want to hear when the phone rings.

### Programs that open MP3 files

**Linux, Mac and Windows**

- Audacity: opens an MP3 as an editable project, which is where you can trim a song.
- ffplay: plays MP3 through FFmpeg's decoders.
- VLC plays MP3 files.

**Windows**

- Windows Media Player plays MP3 files.

**Web**

- Firefox plays supported media directly.
- Chrome handles supported web audio.

**Mobile**

- Android: VLC for Android is a free player for phones, and mpv for Android is the mpv project's port.

### MP3 and M4R compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mp3 with audio/mpeg; .m4r for iPhone ringtones.
- **What is inside**: an M4R holds AAC-encoded sound in an MPEG-4 file. MPEG-4 separates the container structure from the encoding its tracks carry.
- **Compression**: both are lossy, so the M4R is a second generation of the sound. MP3 leaves out the sound a hearing model predicts listeners would not notice.
- **Bitrate**: an MP3 at 128 kbit/s takes about one eleventh of the room the same audio uses on a CD. The M4R from this page is AAC at 192 kbps, whatever bitrate the MP3 had.
- **Purpose**: the .m4r ending is what iTunes and the iPhone treat as a ringtone, and the format is used for iPhone ringtones and alert tones.
- **Metadata**: MPEG-4-family files can carry track metadata in addition to the samples. MP3 keeps its tags in ID3 structures.

On this page the MP3 is decoded and encoded again as AAC at 192 kbps and written into an MPEG-4 audio container, with the video, if any, left out. The whole song is converted, and no trimming is done. A full track therefore gives a full-length file. The title and artist tags of the MP3 are copied into the M4R. The download takes its name from your MP3 and ends in .m4r, and the original is left as it was.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to M4R

- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** import the MP3 with File > Import > Audio, then choose File > Export Audio. Install the optional FFmpeg library, then pick the M4A (AAC) (FFmpeg) choice from the format list, type a file name that ends in .m4r, such as rhythms.m4r, and press Export. The export dialog also sets the channels and sample rate and lets you export the entire project or only the current selection, so you can cut the song down first.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i cue.mp3 -c:a aac -f ipod cue.m4r`. FFmpeg's format list includes MP3, and its ipod muxer writes an MPEG-4 audio file like MOV or MP4 but limited to audio streams. The command does not trim the audio or put it on a phone, and when no bitrate is given FFmpeg falls back on its own default.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **Audacity reports an import error**: A damaged MP3 can stop Audacity from opening it, yet still play in another player. Try the file in VLC, or get a fresh copy.
- **Tags change after several imports**: bringing several files into one Audacity project can overwrite the earlier metadata with that of the latest file.
- **Quality drops after editing**: every MP3 you export after editing adds a second lossy encoding pass. Keep the original MP3 so you can pick another passage later.
- **A renamed file won't work**: changing .mp3 to .m4r leaves MP3 data inside, because only the label changes.

guide.title: About MP3 and MP2
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 comes out of Fraunhofer IIS, whose engineers worked with the wider MPEG audio group on it during the late 1980s. Two ISO standards cover it: 11172-3 from 1993 and 13818-3 from 1995. The allowed bitrate runs from 32 kbps at the low end to 320 kbps at the top, and the sampling rate is 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz. Music libraries, podcasts and portable players rely on it, and browsers all play it.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Linux:** Audacity brings MP3 audio into an editable project.
- **Mac:** ffplay, the FFmpeg player.
- **Windows:** Windows Media Player, or ffplay from the FFmpeg tools.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome decode MP3 inside the browser.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android and mpv for Android.

Audacity runs on Windows and Mac too. Apple Music and VLC media player also open MP3.

### MP3 and MP2 compared

- **Family**: both are MPEG audio. MP2 is Layer II of MPEG-1 Audio, finalized in 1992, and is specified by ISO/IEC 11172-3. It is the predecessor of MP3 Layer III.
- **Where used**: MP2 appears in digital radio and television broadcasting, DVD-Video soundtracks and Video CD production.
- **Media type**: the Library of Congress lists audio/mpeg for MP2 files.
- **Complexity**: MP2 has low decoding complexity.
- **Loss**: MP2 uses perceptual lossy coding, so decoding cannot recover the sound information it omitted. ISO/IEC 13818-3 later extended Layer II for MPEG-2.
- **Programs**: VLC media player, Audacity and foobar2000 open MP2, and FFmpeg's audio codec list includes MP2 decoding and encoding.

Here FFmpeg uses its mp2 encoder in your browser at 192 kbps, without video. The page passes no sample rate, channel count, stream mapping or tag option.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to MP2

- **FFmpeg, native encoder:** `ffmpeg -i track.mp3 -c:a mp2 -b:a 192k track.mp2`.
- **FFmpeg with libtwolame:** `ffmpeg -i track.mp3 -c:a libtwolame -b:a 192k track.mp2`. The libtwolame encoder is a TwoLAME wrapper, a separate implementation of MP2.
- **Audacity:** open the MP3, then pick File > Export Audio and select MP2 as the Format, set a bit rate from 16 to 384 kbps (the default is 160) and press Export.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **A failed import**: a damaged MP3 can make Audacity complain even when another player still opens it.
- **Overwritten metadata**: tags from the most recently imported file may replace earlier tags in a shared Audacity project.
- **Generation loss**: editing an MP3 and exporting a second lossy file adds another lossy encoding stage, so hold on to the original.

guide.title: Understanding MP3 and OGA
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 uses MPEG Audio Layer III perceptual coding. It is common in downloaded music and spoken recordings because its lossy compression reduces storage. Earlier encoding losses remain part of the decoded sound; putting it into another file cannot reconstruct the original samples. Its metadata is stored separately from the sound, so tags travel as their own data.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity brings an MP3 into an editable project, and ffplay plays one.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome can play MP3 straight from a page, though the codec inside the file still counts.
- **Mobile:** MP3 opens in VLC for Android and in mpv for Android.

### MP3 and OGA compared

OGA names general audio in the Ogg container, not one codec. RFC 5334 keeps .ogg for Vorbis-only Ogg and gives .oga to the broader case, so a receiving application still has to decode whatever audio is inside. The same RFC gives .oga as the default extension for the audio/ogg media type.

This page runs FFmpeg with libvorbis at quality 5 and writes Ogg. The title and artist tags are copied as Vorbis comments, and any embedded cover picture is left behind. The result is a second lossy encoding with a quality-based variable bitrate, not a promised file size. The page never uses FLAC, though Ogg can carry that codec.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to OGA

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 -f ogg song.oga` explicitly requests Ogg and Vorbis.
- **Audacity:** import the MP3 into a project and choose Ogg Vorbis as the Format in the File > Export Audio dialog. Its quality slider runs from 0 to 10.

### Problems with MP3 files

**The import errors out:** Audacity may refuse a damaged MP3 file even when a different player handles it.

**Tags get overwritten:** if you load more than one file into a single project, Audacity can replace the earlier tags with those of the newest file.

**A second lossy pass:** editing an MP3 and then saving another MP3 puts the sound through a second lossy encode, so keep the original.

guide.title: Understanding MP3 and Opus
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 is MPEG Audio Layer III, a lossy audio format standardized by MPEG (ISO/IEC 11172-3) and developed with the Fraunhofer Society as a major contributor. It became the most common format for downloadable music. It stores a compact approximation of the sound, and once the encoder has discarded detail, decoding the MP3 cannot bring it back.

You will find MP3s across music collections, podcasts and portable-player audio. Opus is newer. It is an open codec developed for speech and music, including interactive communication, and the IETF standardized its original definition as RFC 6716 in September 2012.

Opus combines SILK technology from Skype with CELT from Xiph.Org, and its coding modes trade signal detail for a compact representation. A .opus file commonly keeps the sound in an Ogg stream, specified by RFC 7845. Its media type is audio/ogg, with a codec parameter naming Opus.

People convert MP3 to Opus when a service, chat app or player asks for Opus. A conversion from MP3 is still a second lossy generation, so the result can be no better than the MP3. Whether the file comes out smaller depends on the MP3's own bitrate: a low-bitrate MP3 can grow.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity opens MP3 files among its built-in formats, so the MP3 becomes a project for cutting, fades and effects.
- **Windows, Mac, Linux, iOS and Android:** VLC plays most multimedia files, MP3 included, without codec packs.
- **Windows:** Windows Media Player opens MP3 files.
- **Mac:** Apple Music opens MP3 files.
- **Web:** any web browser plays MP3.

### MP3 and Opus compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mp3 and audio/mpeg; .opus and audio/ogg with the opus parameter.
- **Wrapper**: MP3 is its own stream format. Opus usually lives in an Ogg file, which supports descriptive metadata and seeking.
- **Compression**: both are lossy. Opus trades signal detail for a compact representation.
- **Sample rate**: Ogg Opus times playback on a 48 kHz basis, a separate matter from the recording's own sample rate.

The page's settings are fixed: a libopus target of 128 kbps and compression level 4, run by FFmpeg inside your browser. The encoded file carries only the audio: any cover picture is left out. Because both formats are lossy, bit counts don't compare directly: a 128 kbps Opus file and a 128 kbps MP3 are not equivalent. In a test, a 44.1 kHz MP3 came out as an Opus file reported at 48 kHz.

Two Opus details matter if a player misbehaves. Reading Vorbis in Ogg does not guarantee reading Opus: Ogg gives Opus its own headers. And ignoring the pre-skip value can leave stray samples at the start; Ogg Opus defines how readers apply it. The MP3 you chose stays untouched, as the download is a new file; picking several makes the page work through them in sequence, each ending as a separate .opus.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to Opus

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i podcast.mp3 -c:a libopus -b:a 128k podcast.opus`. The page's own command also sets compression level 4 and drops any picture stream.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** import the MP3, choose File > Export Audio and select Opus (OggOpus) Files (FFmpeg) in the Format list. The same dialog sets channels, sample rate, bit rate and quality, unlike this page.
- **Switch for Windows:** add the MP3 files and choose Opus in Output Format. Check Encoder Options and the destination, then click Convert. The vendor's table lists Opus output for Windows and Mac but not Android.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **A malformed MP3 gives an import error**: Audacity may report one even when another player can play the file.
- **Tags change when imports are combined**: Audacity can overwrite earlier metadata with the newest file's tags when several imports share one project.
- **A second lossy pass**: each time an edited MP3 is saved as MP3 again, another lossy encoding stage is added, and this conversion adds one too. It sounds no better than the MP3, because low-bitrate artifacts stay. Go back to a lossless master.
- **Artwork vanished**: embedded cover art isn't copied, so re-add it in an editor.
- **A long file takes a while**: the encoder is single-threaded WebAssembly on your device, so how long it takes depends on the length of the audio and your device.

guide.title: Understanding MP3 for WebM output
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3, or MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, became a standard in 1993 as ISO/IEC 11172-3 and was extended in 1995 by ISO/IEC 13818-3. Fraunhofer IIS developed it from the late 1980s together with other people in the MPEG audio group. The format is lossy; it applies a model of hearing to drop sounds that listeners probably won't notice. At 128 kbit/s, an MP3 takes up roughly one eleventh of the space the same recording needs on a CD.

Supported bitrates run from 32 to 320 kbps, with sampling at 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz. Titles and other tags live in ID3 structures stored apart from the audio inside the file. Patent licensing for MP3 ended on April 23, 2017. Every major browser plays it, and audio/mpeg is its media type. Because the discarded sound can't be recovered, each new lossy encode removes a little more.

The file is most often a song, a podcast episode or a voice note. Because MP3 is not one of the codecs WebM allows, a request for WebM is really a request for a different audio package.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports MP3 audio into an editable project. ffplay uses FFmpeg's demuxer.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly. Chrome plays supported web audio, though the internal codec still matters.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is free, and codec support decides what plays. mpv for Android plays it too.

### MP3 and WebM compared

- **Purpose**: WebM comes from the WebM Project, which promotes an open format for the web. The container is built on Matroska.
- **Codecs**: VP8 or VP9 for video, Vorbis or Opus for sound. MP3 is not on that list, so the sound has to be encoded again.
- **Media types**: video/webm, and audio/webm for a file with no picture.
- **Typical uses**: WebM is used for video on the web, screen captures made in browsers and short animated clips, and the main browsers support it. MP3 serves songs, podcast episodes and voice notes.
- **Terms**: the project offers the format technology royalty-free.
- **Playback**: browsers look at the codecs inside, not the .webm ending. Safari gained support for VP8 or VP9 WebM with Vorbis in version 14.1 on macOS.

On this page, FFmpeg in your browser turns the sound of your MP3 into Vorbis at 64 kbps. Both formats are lossy, so the WebM is a second lossy generation, and you should keep the MP3 if quality matters. The original isn't changed, and the result is a separate download. Nothing in the page limits size or run time. Vorbis is one of the two audio codecs WebM defines, the other being Opus, so the output stays within the format's own choices. If you need Opus, run FFmpeg yourself with the command below. Play the WebM in the player you plan to use before you delete anything.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to WebM

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i spoken-note.mp3 -vn -c:a libopus -b:a 64k spoken-note-opus.webm` to write Opus instead of Vorbis. The -vn option turns off video, so an attached cover picture is left out.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **Import error**: a malformed MP3 can trigger an import error in an editor even though another player handles it.
- **Lost tags in an editor**: bringing several files into a single Audacity project can overwrite earlier tags with those of the last file.
- **Quality drops on re-export**: editing an MP3 and exporting a new MP3 adds a second lossy encoding stage. Export from the original source when you can.
- **A tag looks wrong**: titles and other tags sit in ID3 structures inside the MP3, so an editor that reads them differently can show different text. Check them in the player you will use.
- **Seeking is sluggish**: a missing cue index gives the player less direct location information, so jumping around in a WebM can be slower.
- **An old browser balks**: what an early Safari did says little about current releases, so try the WebM in the very browser you need.
- **Playback depends on the codec**: a player that recognizes the file may still lack the decoder, so try another one. VLC and mpv are free choices on Android.

guide.title: About MP3 and WMA files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

Layer III of MPEG-1 Audio, known as MP3, was standardized in 1993 as ISO/IEC 11172-3 and widened by ISO/IEC 13818-3 two years later. The format is lossy, using a model of human hearing to discard sound listeners are unlikely to notice. Fraunhofer IIS led its development from the late 1980s, working with other members of the MPEG audio group.
The media type is audio/mpeg, and every major browser plays MP3. Choose from 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz sampling, with bitrates from 32 to 320 kbps. ID3 structures inside the file hold titles and other tags. At 128 kbps the file is around one eleventh of the CD's size for the same audio. The patent licensing program ended in 2017.
Because the compression is lossy, an MP3 has already lost information that no converter can bring back. That matters when you move music into another compressed format such as WMA. Before you convert a library, check that the destination really needs WMA, because it may already play MP3. A new extension does not make a better copy of the performance, and the MP3s are worth keeping for any later migration.
### Programs that open MP3 files
**Windows**
- Audacity: brings an MP3 into an editable project.
**Mac**
- FFplay: FFmpeg's own player, which plays MP3 files through FFmpeg's libraries.
**Web**
- Firefox and Chrome: play MP3 directly.
**Mobile**
- VLC for Android and mpv for Android: both play MP3.
### MP3 and WMA compared
- **Extensions**: .mp3 with the media type audio/mpeg; .wma, commonly audio/x-ms-wma.
- **Codec family**: MP3 is MPEG Audio Layer III. WMA is Microsoft's family, with standard, Professional, Lossless and Voice variants.
- **Container**: MP3 is a stream of audio frames with ID3 tags. WMA audio files use Microsoft's ASF container, and the .wma extension marks audio-only ASF content.
- **Compression**: both are lossy by default. WMA Lossless exists, but this page does not use it.
- **Bitrate**: MP3 runs from 32 to 320 kbps. WMA 9 supports variable bit rate encoding. This page writes WMA at 192 kbps.
- **Tags**: an MP3 keeps its tags as ID3, and FFmpeg copies the title and artist across.
- **Where it plays**: all major browsers play MP3; WMA is aimed at delivery workflows and occasionally intermediate storage.
The change that matters here is the codec. FFmpeg decodes the MP3 and encodes the sound with its WMA version 2 encoder at 192 kbps, then writes an ASF file with a .wma name. Any video stream is ignored.
Output size is not guaranteed to fall. A low-bitrate MP3 can become a larger file at 192 kbps WMA, because size follows duration and bitrate more than the extension. Compare the two files before you replace anything. VLC lists ASF/WMA input, so it can help you check the finished file.
A WMA made from an MP3 is a copy of a copy. If you have the original recording, convert from that. If you only have the MP3, keep it too, because it is the better source for any later conversion.
### Other ways to convert MP3 to WMA
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i input.mp3 -b:a 192k -c:a wmav2 output.wma`. This writes lossy WMA, not WMA Lossless.
- **Audacity:** with the MP3 open, use File > Export Audio and pick WMA (version2) Files (FFmpeg) as the format. Audacity needs the separate FFmpeg library installed, and the export options offer Mono, Stereo or Custom mapping.
- **NCH Switch:** use Add File(s), choose the output location from Save to Folder, Output Folder or Browse, select WMA from Output Format and press Convert.
### Problems with MP3 files
- **Importing many files into one Audacity project replaces earlier tags**: the project keeps tags from the latest file.
- **The WMA sounds rough**: the MP3 was already compressed. Convert from an original recording.
- **Editing then exporting MP3 again adds another lossy stage**: export to a lossless format while you work.
- **Tags are missing or wrong**: FFmpeg copies the MP3's global tags into the WMA where it has fields for them, so a tag blank in the MP3 stays blank. Edit them in your music library afterward.

- **Audacity refuses the file**: a damaged MP3 can be rejected on import although a different player copes with it.

guide.title: About MP4 and 3GP files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

ISO/IEC 14496-14 defines the MP4 container, which stores video, audio, subtitles and metadata as tracks. H.264 video with AAC audio is the most common combination, but the extension does not name a codec. Two MP4 files can behave differently on the same device, because one may carry a combination an old phone accepts and another a codec it does not.

A container that opens is no proof of decoding: a player or editor can accept an MP4 and still show no picture or no sound, so look at the codecs inside before you blame the file.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows**

- mpv: a desktop player with audio and subtitle stream switching.

**Mac**

- FFplay: the player that ships with FFmpeg, which plays MP4 through FFmpeg's MP4 demuxer.

**Web**

- Firefox: shows supported media itself; whether AAC and H.264 play can hinge on system codecs.
- Chrome: plays the audio and video combinations in MP4 that it supports.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android and iOS: plays local and network files in most movie formats.

### MP4 and 3GP compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mp4 with video/mp4; .3gp with video/3gpp, or audio/3gpp for sound only.
- **Container family**: 3GP is a specialization of the ISO base media file format from the 3GPP mobile standards, and MP4 is built on the same family. A file-type box names a 3GP profile.
- **Purpose**: 3GP supports mobile messaging, download and streaming. MP4 targets general use.
- **Video codec**: MP4 usually holds H.264. The 3GP standard registers H.263, MPEG-4 Visual, AVC and HEVC. This page writes H.263.
- **Audio codec**: a 3GP can hold AMR variants or AAC. This page writes AAC.
- **Contents**: video, speech, other sound and timed text can all live together in a 3GP presentation, while a sound-only 3GP has no video track to recover.
- **Parsing**: parsers that follow the specification may skip boxes or codecs it does not cover, and the extension never says which permitted codec a 3GP recording holds.

What changes in this conversion is the quality, not just the wrapper. FFmpeg corrects the source's pixel aspect ratio, scales the video to fit inside 352 by 288 and pads the rest of the frame, so a widescreen video gets borders instead of being stretched. The video is H.263 at 12 frames per second and 200 kbps. The sound is AAC at 24 kbps, 8 kHz and one channel.

Those are big reductions from a typical modern MP4: fine detail softens, motion looks choppier and stereo is lost. The settings belong to this page rather than to every 3GP the standard allows. A particular phone may want a different resolution or audio type, so test on the real device before sending a batch.

If a service or an old handset tells you which resolution and codec it wants, trust that over these defaults and use a desktop tool where you can set them. Convert a short clip first and play it on the actual phone before you prepare a whole batch.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to 3GP

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v h263 -s 352x288 -r 12 -c:a aac output.3gp`. The `-s` option forces the size and can distort a widescreen picture.
- **NCH Prism:** choose Add File(s), choose where the file goes (Save to Folder, Output Folder or Browse), set Output Format to 3GP and click Convert.
- **MP4Box:** run `MP4Box -add input.mp4 -new output.3gp`. A .3gp name switches on 3GPP rewriting, and some tracks may be removed. It repackages and does not transcode.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **The player opens the MP4 but shows no picture or no sound**: container support does not guarantee a decoder for the codec inside. Play it in a player that has the decoder.
- **An audio editor finds nothing to import**: an MP4 with no audio has no audio track to hand over.
- **A cut-short recording will not play**: a recording that stopped early can leave an unfinished MP4, since packet metadata normally stays together in one place. A damaged MP4 may still convert here, to a shorter 3GP.
- **One phone plays the MP4 and another does not**: the extension does not name the codecs, and devices accept different combinations.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 debuted in 2003 as MPEG-4 Part 14, which carries the number ISO/IEC 14496-14. The ISO Base Media File Format supplies the layout, taking over the box-in-box design that Apple's QuickTime atoms pioneered.

Think of MP4 as packaging and not as a codec. The common contents are H.264 pictures with AAC sound, but AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus fit too. Video files take .mp4 or .m4v, and MPEG-4 files with sound only often take .m4a. Registered media types: video/mp4 and audio/mp4.

All major browsers play MP4. On Android, HEVC video inside it works from version 5.0.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Desktop playback in mpv comes with selectable audio streams.
- Playing MP4 through ffplay works because FFmpeg has the demuxer.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Importing MP4 into Adobe Premiere succeeds when the decoder for its contents is available.

**Web:**

- Firefox plays supported media directly, although AAC and H.264 can depend on codecs in the system.
- Chrome plays the MP4 pairings it supports, and the inner codec stays decisive.

**Mobile:**

- Free to use, VLC for Android decodes according to what the container holds.
- A mobile player for most movie formats is VLC for iOS, which also reaches network media.

### MP4 and AAC compared

- **Kind of thing**: MP4 is a container, and AAC is a codec, and MPEG covers it in Part 7 of the MPEG-2 standard as well as in Part 3 of MPEG-4.
- **Contents**: an MP4 can carry pictures and sound. A .aac file is a single stream of audio.
- **Wrapper**: a standalone .aac file commonly carries ADTS framing, while AAC inside an MP4 sits in boxes.
- **Quality goal**: As a lossy codec, AAC aims at better sound than MP3 for an equal bitrate.
- **Use**: Streaming audio and end-user delivery are typical uses, and its media type is audio/aac.
- **Profiles**: they include LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2.
- **Range**: Sample rates in AAC span 8 to 96 kHz, and bitrates reach 512 kbps.
- **M4A**: Unprotected music files from Apple took the .m4a extension, and most contain AAC audio.

This page decodes the MP4 in your browser with FFmpeg and discards the video. The sound goes through FFmpeg's AAC encoder at 192 kbps and is saved as a .aac file. The page has no bitrate field, no trimming and no tag editing, and it does not copy the original stream.

Add several MP4 files and they run in sequence, each producing a separate .aac. An MP4 without sound has nothing to extract. If FFmpeg gives up on a file, you see a message that begins "FFmpeg failed with exit code". Nothing is uploaded, no size limit applies, and the original MP4 stays as it was.

Because AAC is already compressed, encoding it again is a second pass of lossy compression. The copy method below avoids that when the audio in your MP4 is AAC.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to AAC

- **FFmpeg, re-encode:** run `ffmpeg -i recording.mp4 -vn -c:a aac -b:a 192k recording.aac`. With -vn the video is omitted, while -b:a fixes the audio bitrate.
- **FFmpeg, copy the stream:** type `ffmpeg -i interview.mp4 -vn -c:a copy -f adts extracted.aac`. Nothing is re-encoded, so it fits an MP4 whose sound is already AAC, and the adts muxer accepts a single AAC stream.
- **FFmpeg, choose an audio track:** use `ffmpeg -i lecture.mp4 -map 0:a:1 -c:a aac -b:a 192k second-track.aac`. In the specifier 0:a:1, the 0 is the first input and a:1 is the audio stream with index 1, counted from zero; the command fails when the file has fewer audio streams.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No decoder for the contents**: a container that is supported does not guarantee a decoder for the sound or picture in it.
- **No audio track**: an audio editor has nothing to import from an MP4 that carries no sound.
- **Unfinished recording**: an ordinary MP4 holds its packet metadata in one place, so a write that was cut off can leave an unplayable file.
- **Variant mismatch**: software built for MPEG-2 AAC may fail on MPEG-4 AAC variants.
- **Renamed ending**: changing .aac to .m4a does not swap ADTS framing for an MP4 wrapper.

guide.title: MP4 background and AIFF conversion
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is specified by Part 14 of MPEG-4, also numbered ISO/IEC 14496-14, and the first edition appeared in 2003. It is built on the ISO Base Media File Format, which grew out of Apple's QuickTime, and it is made of nested boxes. MP4 is a container: it commonly holds H.264 video with AAC audio, and it can also carry AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus. Video usually carries .mp4 or .m4v, while MPEG-4 files with sound alone commonly end in .m4a. Registered media types for it are video/mp4 and audio/mp4, and the big browsers can play it.

A screen recording, a phone clip or a downloaded video usually arrives as MP4. People convert it to AIFF to pull the sound out for an audio editor or a Mac workflow that wants uncompressed audio.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay can play MP4, and mpv plays it on desktop systems.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere takes MP4 in as an import when a suitable decoder exists.
- **Web:** Firefox plays MP4 media it supports, and Chrome handles supported MP4 audio and video pairings.
- **Mobile:** VLC apps for Android and iOS play MP4 on a phone.

### MP4 and AIFF compared

MP4 is a container for timed media, not a single audio codec, so its sound may be AAC or something else. The Audio Interchange File Format is an Apple audio wrapper descended from Electronic Arts' IFF family. It often carries uncompressed linear PCM samples, and AIFF-C extends it to compressed audio. Named chunks can hold author, copyright and annotations. Professional audio users choose AIFF for masters, and Audacity and Adobe Audition open it. Apple published version 1.3 of the AIFF specification on 4 January 1989, and the usual media types are audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff.

The page runs FFmpeg in your browser with `-acodec pcm_s16be -vn`: the video is dropped and the sound is written as signed 16-bit big-endian PCM. Decoding the sound to PCM doesn't restore detail removed when the MP4 was made.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to AIFF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i interview.mp4 -vn interview.aiff`. As an output option, `-vn` turns off video, so only the sound is written to the AIFF.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No sound to extract**: if the MP4 holds only picture, there is nothing to write into the AIFF.
- **A cut-off file will not play**: an interrupted MP4 recording can be unplayable because its packet index is kept as a single block.
- **No decoder for the contents**: understanding the MP4 wrapper is not enough if the player has no decoder for the codec used inside.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14, a container format defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14. It can hold video, audio, subtitles, chapters and metadata, and combining H.264 video with AAC audio is typical.

Typical uses are streaming, phone footage, camera recordings and sharing clips. It plays on nearly every device.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay opens it provided the FFmpeg build in use includes the decoders, and mpv adds selectable audio and subtitle streams.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports it when the decoder is available.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play supported combinations directly.
- **Mobile:** VLC on Android and on iOS plays it.

### MP4 and AMR compared

AMR is built for speech. Narrowband AMR offers eight modes between 4.75 and 12.2 kbps, samples at 8 kHz and works in 20-millisecond frames. RFC 4867 (April 2007) specifies storage files and RTP transport. AMR-WB samples at 16 kHz, so narrowband output cannot match its range.

ETSI standardized AMR for GSM, and 3GPP adopted it for third-generation cellular systems, and that background explains its use in phone voice recordings and messages. Files are very small because only speech is kept. Playback support depends on the program, so test the AMR in the program that will use it.

This page does not make AMR files. Its command names the libopencore_amrnb encoder, and the browser's FFmpeg build lacks it, so the run ends in an error and no AMR is produced. Before converting elsewhere, check that the MP4 has an audio track, because a video-only file has nothing to extract. Afterward, play the AMR to confirm the speech came through.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to AMR

- **Switch Sound File Converter on Windows:** press Add, pick the MP4, choose AMR as Output Format, then press Convert.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No audio to extract**: an MP4 without an audio track cannot supply sound to an audio converter.
- **The video plays but the sound is silent**: container support does not guarantee a decoder exists for the sound inside.
- **A download stops partway**: normal MP4 files keep packet metadata together, so an interrupted write can leave an unfinished file unplayable.

guide.title: About MP4 and ASF
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4, short for MPEG-4 Part 14 (ISO/IEC 14496-14), appeared in 2003. It descends from Apple's QuickTime by way of the ISO Base Media File Format, and its content sits in nested boxes. H.264 video paired with AAC sound is the usual payload, though other codecs fit as well. The .mp4 and .m4v endings mark video, and .m4a usually marks audio only.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv lets you pick audio and subtitle streams while playing, and ffplay plays it too.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere takes in MP4 files provided the right decoder exists.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP4 directly, though support for AAC and H.264 may depend on codecs the system provides.
- **Mobile:** phones have VLC for iOS as well as VLC for Android.

### MP4 and ASF compared

- **Container**: MP4 is ISO/IEC 14496-14, while ASF is Microsoft's proprietary wrapper, whose specification is public.
- **Streams**: an ASF is not limited to sound and pictures, since stills and other kinds of stream can ride along, and WMA and WMV are its subtypes.
- **Metadata**: ASF header objects can carry titles, authorship and copyright data, and its registered MIME type is application/vnd.ms-asf.
- **Reach**: every major browser plays MP4, whereas the .asf ending names a wrapper and does not say which decoders a player needs.

Nothing leaves your device, because FFmpeg does the encoding inside the tab. The video is written by the wmv2 encoder at 500 kbps and the audio by wmav2 at 96 kbps. A picture taller or wider than 1920 pixels shrinks to fit, and anything above 30 frames a second is thinned out. Play the ASF afterwards in a player that lists ASF, such as VLC, and check the picture and the sound.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to ASF

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i presentation.mp4 -f asf presentation.asf` selects the ASF muxer and leaves the codecs to FFmpeg.
- **FFmpeg with a video bitrate:** `ffmpeg -i presentation.mp4 -b:v 1400k -f asf presentation.asf` sets the video bitrate with `-b:v`, which gives you control the page does not offer.
- **Prism for Windows:** add the MP4 through Add File(s), select ASF as the Output Format and click Convert. Prism lists MP4 as an input when an mp4 filter is installed.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **Missing picture or sound**: the player supports MP4 but lacks a decoder for the codec inside, since container support alone does not guarantee one.
- **Interrupted recordings**: a normal MP4 keeps its packet metadata together, so a write that stopped early can leave a file no player opens.

guide.title: Understanding MP4 for AV1 output
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

The MP4 container, defined by ISO/IEC 14496-14, stores video, audio, subtitles and metadata together, and its extension does not name the video codec: one MP4 may use H.264, another H.265 or AV1. A phone recording with speech is a typical example, with the picture and the microphone track stored together. It plays on nearly every device, and chapters can travel inside it.

### Programs that open MP4 files

For AV1 output, open the MP4 in:

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay and mpv play MP4 files.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere takes in MP4 when it can decode what is inside.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP4 in the browser.
- **Mobile:** On phones, use VLC for Android or VLC for iOS.

Opening the container is not enough, since a decoder must also exist for the video inside.

### MP4 and AV1 compared

- **Kind**: MP4 is a container. AV1 is a codec from the Alliance for Open Media that can sit inside MP4, MKV or WebM.
- **Efficiency**: AV1 compresses better than H.264 and VP9.
- **This page's output**: a bare stream of AV1 data in an IVF wrapper, with no audio.

FFmpeg first decodes your MP4 to an intermediate copy, deinterlacing it, scaling anything over 1920 pixels on the long side down and dropping frames above 30 per second. Your browser's AV1 encoder then compresses that copy, and FFmpeg writes the stream out as a .av1 file. The encoder is the browser's, so whether it works depends on your device.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to AV1

- **FFmpeg with SVT-AV1:** run `ffmpeg -i camera.mp4 -an -c:v libsvtav1 -crf 35 -preset 8 -f ivf camera.av1`. `-an` leaves the sound out, `-crf` sets the quality, and a higher preset number encodes faster at lower quality.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **The MP4 won't convert**: a recording interrupted while it was being written can leave an unfinished, unplayable file. Re-export it.
- **It plays in one program but not another**: the container does not guarantee a decoder, so an MP4 with an unusual video codec needs software that carries it.
- **The MP4 has sound you need**: the sound stays in the MP4, since a .av1 stream cannot hold it.

guide.title: About MP4 and AVCHD
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

A media container standardized as MPEG-4 Part 14 (ISO/IEC 14496-14) and published in 2003, MP4 bundles video, audio, subtitles and metadata. The common contents are H.264 video and AAC audio, and phones, cameras and streaming sites produce it. Browsers all play it.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Mac:** QuickTime Player opens it.
- **Windows:** Adobe Premiere imports it once a decoder for the contents is present, and Windows Media Player plays it.
- **Linux:** mpv lets you pick audio and subtitle streams.
- **Web:** Chrome and Firefox play it directly.
- **Mobile:** VLC has apps for Android and iOS.

mpv and ffplay also run on Windows and Mac, and VLC media player plays MP4 too.

### MP4 and AVCHD compared

- **Origin**: AVCHD was introduced by Sony and Panasonic for HD camcorders. It packages its streams as MPEG-2 Transport Stream in MTS or M2TS files.
- **Video**: its standard compression is MPEG-4 AVC/H.264, with 8-bit samples and 4:2:0 chroma, in interlaced and progressive HD modes.
- **Audio**: Dolby Digital AC-3 or uncompressed Linear PCM.
- **Media**: it records to memory cards, built-in storage or small 8 cm DVDs.

On this page, FFmpeg re-encodes the video with libx264 at CRF 30 and the audio as AAC at 96 kbps into an MPEG transport stream. The picture keeps its size when the longer side is 1920 px or less, extra frames are discarded to stay at or below 30 fps, and each width and height is rounded down to an even number.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to AVCHD

- **FFmpeg, H.264 and AC-3:** `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -f mpegts -mpegts_m2ts_mode 1 -c:a ac3 -c:v libx264 clip.m2ts`.
- **FFmpeg, remux:** `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -c copy -mpegts_m2ts_mode 1 -f mpegts clip.m2ts`, which copies the streams and suits an MP4 whose codecs already fit AVCHD.
- **tsMuxer:** write a meta file whose first line is `MUXOPT --avchd`, then a `V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC, clip.mp4, track=1` line and an `A_AC3, clip.mp4, track=2` line, setting track to each stream's number in the MP4. Run `tsMuxeR project.meta avchd-output`.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **A decoder may be missing**: a container that a program accepts can still hold video or sound it has no decoder for.
- **No sound to extract**: an audio editor gets nothing from an MP4 that has no audio.
- **Interrupted recordings**: the packet metadata of a normal MP4 stays together, so if writing stopped early the file may not play.

guide.title: About MP4 and DivX
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is formally MPEG-4 Part 14, or ISO/IEC 14496-14, and dates from 2003. Under the hood it follows the ISO Base Media File Format; that standard comes out of Apple's QuickTime format, and stores its data in nested boxes (QuickTime's word was atoms).

The file wraps streams instead of fixing one codec. H.264 with AAC is the common combination, though AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus can sit inside too. Both .mp4 and .m4v mark video. Registered media types: video/mp4 and audio/mp4. On Android, HEVC video inside an MP4 plays from version 5.0 on.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv plays MP4 on the desktop.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MP4.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP4 directly.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android plays MP4, and so does VLC for iOS.

### MP4 and DivX compared

- **Container**: MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14. DivX is a brand of video codec and container software from DivX, Inc., and its files are usually AVI.
- **Video**: MP4 commonly carries H.264, H.265 or AV1. Early DivX versions were MPEG-4 Part 2 video, and later versions added H.264. This page writes MPEG-4 Part 2 video.
- **Audio**: this page writes MP3 at 96 kbps.
- **Extras**: Menus and chapter points come from DivX authoring, and a DivX movie can hold more than one audio track. This page adds no menu.
- **Devices**: DivX certification profiles distinguish what a device can play, and advanced menus, chapters and tracks depend on the receiving device's profile.

The .divx extension is one of the formats DivX Player lists. The converter names your download with that extension.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to DivX

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i source_movie.mp4 -c:v mpeg4 -vtag DIVX -c:a libmp3lame legacy_movie.avi`. The video is MPEG-4 with the DIVX tag, as in the converter above, and the audio is MP3.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **A player shows no picture or no sound**: a player that opens the container also needs a decoder for what each stream holds.
- **A cut-off recording won't play**: a normal MP4 stores its packet metadata in one place, so an early stop can leave the file unplayable.

guide.title: MP4 to F4V: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

An MP4 file follows MPEG-4 Part 14, written ISO/IEC 14496-14, which appeared in 2003. It builds on the ISO Base Media File Format, whose nested boxes come from QuickTime. Most files hold H.264 video and AAC audio, though AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus can be inside as well. Video uses the endings .mp4 and .m4v, and every major browser plays it.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay plays MP4 files whose streams the installed FFmpeg build can decode, and mpv offers audio-track switching.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MP4 when a suitable decoder is present.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play supported MP4 files directly.
- **Mobile:** VLC on Android and on iOS.

### MP4 and F4V compared

F4V, an Adobe format, borrows its layout from the MPEG-4 container. That makes it a wrapper rather than a codec, so the streams inside matter more than the ending. Flash Player support has ended and no current browser plays Flash, which leaves F4V for archives and older Flash projects.

FFmpeg, compiled to WebAssembly, deinterlaces the video, encodes it as H.264 and writes AAC audio at 96 kbps. Footage whose long edge exceeds 1920 px is downscaled, and a rate above 30 fps is brought down by dropping frames; smaller values stay. Each side is then made even, which costs an odd side one pixel. Files are processed one at a time, and the MP4 you chose is not modified.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to F4V

- **FFmpeg, re-encoding:** run `ffmpeg -i lesson.mp4 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -f f4v lesson.f4v` to write H.264 video and AAC audio into an F4V.
- **FFmpeg, stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i compatible.mp4 -c copy -f f4v compatible.f4v` to copy the streams without re-encoding. Use it when the MP4 already holds H.264 video and AAC audio.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **Sound or picture missing:** the file ending says nothing about which decoders a player has. Try another player, such as mpv.
- **A recording that stopped early:** MP4 gathers the index of its packets in one place, so a write cut short may leave an unplayable file.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

Defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14, MP4 packs video, audio, subtitles and metadata into a single file. H.264 video with AAC audio is common, yet the .mp4 ending doesn't guarantee any codec. People meet MP4 as streamed video, phone and camera clips, and files passed around.

Only the sound counts for this conversion. A lecture, a concert recording or an interview may need to enter an audio workflow without its pictures. The video's resolution says nothing about the quality of its audio. A clip can look sharp and carry a heavily compressed soundtrack, and a screen recording can carry none at all.

The audio codec decides what FLAC is worth here. AAC is lossy: it drops detail and can't take it back. Turning the track into FLAC stores the decoded result as it is, and from then on nothing more is lost. It does not bring back the original studio signal.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac, Linux:** ffplay, FFmpeg's player, has the MP4 demuxer. mpv plays desktop media with a choice of audio and subtitle tracks.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere can import an MP4 once the matching decoder is present.
- **Web:** Firefox opens the MP4 files it supports without help, though AAC and H.264 can lean on your system's codecs. Chrome opens only some MP4 combinations, so the codec inside decides.
- **Mobile:** The free VLC for Android decodes the codecs your MP4 holds, within what it supports. On an iPhone or iPad, VLC for iOS opens local and network media.

A container that opens doesn't guarantee a decoder for the sound inside it.

### MP4 and FLAC compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mp4, usually video/mp4; .flac and audio/flac.
- **Content**: MP4 holds video, audio, subtitles and metadata. FLAC holds audio only.
- **Compression**: the AAC inside most MP4 files is lossy. FLAC is lossless.
- **Channels**: FLAC handles one to eight of them.
- **Metadata**: FLAC carries Vorbis comments, embedded pictures and seek points.
- **Standard**: FLAC is described in RFC 9639, published in December 2024.

The page runs FFmpeg with `-acodec flac -vn`, which decodes the sound, writes FLAC and skips every video stream. Nothing in that command picks a track, and it leaves the sample rate and channel count unset, so FFmpeg's defaults apply. If the MP4 has several audio tracks, listen to the FLAC to confirm you got the one you wanted.

FLAC is larger than the AAC it came from, because it keeps every decoded sample. In a test with a one-second sample MP4, the FLAC was several times the size of the MP4. A longer file or a different audio setting changes the numbers.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to FLAC

- **FFmpeg (command line):** type `ffmpeg -i concert.mp4 -vn -c:a flac concert.flac`. `-vn` disables video. If a movie has several languages, `-map 0:a:1` selects the second audio stream.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** after adding the optional FFmpeg library, bring the MP4 in using File > Import > Audio, then pick FLAC under File > Export Audio. The FLAC export dialog lets you choose the channel layout, the sample rate, a bit depth of 16 or 24 and a level from 0 to 8.
- **VLC (command line):** On VideoLAN's wiki, `-I dummy` keeps VLC's window from opening, `--sout "#transcode{acodec=flac}:std{mux=raw,dst=yourAudio.flac}"` writes the FLAC, and `vlc://quit` closes it. The wiki's example input is an .mp4 file.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No audio track**: a screen recording made without a microphone has nothing to extract. Play the MP4 first. With no sound to extract, the conversion shows an FFmpeg exit code.
- **An unsupported codec**: a valid container can hold a codec your tools can't decode. Try another player or get another copy rather than renaming the file.
- **The wrong language came out**: no track is selected by the page, so use FFmpeg with its own `-map` option.
- **The title or artist is missing**: FFmpeg copies the MP4's global tags to the FLAC where it has fields for them, but it can't add a tag the MP4 never had. Check the tags in a tag editor and fill in what is missing.
- **An interrupted recording won't open**: a recording that stopped before it was finished can leave the file unplayable. Record or download it again.
- **The FLAC is much larger than the AAC**: FLAC is lossless and keeps every decoded sample, while AAC discards detail.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

Think of an MP4 as a box with compartments for picture, sound and descriptive data. Nothing in the .mp4 name reveals which codec fills each compartment, which is why a decoder must handle the compression and not merely the wrapper. H.264 video with AAC sound is the usual content, though other codecs are possible.

Every major browser can play MP4, and phones and cameras commonly produce it. Its data sits in nested boxes, and a normal file keeps its index together, which is why a recording that was interrupted before it finished can be hard to open.

Before converting, work out what the next system needs. A request that only says "Flash video" can mean H.264 and AAC, or the older Sorenson and VP6 pairings, and they are not interchangeable. If you are not sure the destination really needs FLV, ask for its list of accepted codecs first, and keep the MP4 in case the legacy copy cannot use something in it.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay plays MP4 through FFmpeg's demuxer, and mpv does desktop playback with selectable audio streams.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP4 files whose codecs they support.
- **Mobile:** on phones, VLC for Android and for iOS opens videos saved on the device.

### MP4 and FLV compared

- **Origin**: FLV is Flash Video, a binary container tied to Macromedia's Flash video delivery. Adobe ended Flash Player support on December 31, 2020, so treat FLV as legacy media.
- **Streams**: an FLV tops out at a single video plus a single audio track, whereas an MP4 can carry many.
- **Codecs**: FLV can carry Sorenson or On2 VP6 video, and audio such as MP3, PCM or ADPCM. This page writes H.264 and AAC instead, and a player needs the decoder for whatever codecs an FLV holds.
- **Extension**: the .flv extension does not identify a unique video codec.
- **Playback**: media software such as VLC can still read FLV without Flash Player.

Picture and sound are both encoded again. The video uses H.264 (ultrafast preset, CRF 32) and the audio uses AAC at 96 kbps. Footage whose long side exceeds 1920 px is shrunk, and a frame rate above 30 per second is trimmed by discarding frames, so the running time is untouched. Sizes are rounded to even numbers too. Footage flagged interlaced is deinterlaced beforehand. This is a fresh encode, not a stream copy, so quality and file size can change.

No stream mapping is given, so FFmpeg picks the streams by its own defaults.

The download carries the MP4's name with an .flv ending, and the original file is left as it was. You can pick several MP4s; each runs in turn and becomes its own FLV, and no ZIP is made. All of it happens inside your browser, where FFmpeg runs as WebAssembly in a worker, so the video is not uploaded.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to FLV

- **FFmpeg (re-encode):** `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -f flv -codec:v libx264 -codec:a aac output.flv` selects H.264 and AAC and names the FLV muxer with -f.
- **FFmpeg (stream copy):** `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c copy -f flv output.flv` skips encoding and copies the streams. An FLV has room for one video stream and one audio stream, nothing more.
- **FFmpeg (keyframe index):** `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -codec:v libx264 -codec:a aac -flvflags add_keyframe_index output.flv` adds a keyframe index that helps seeking, particularly for HTTP pseudo streaming.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **An old player opens the container but shows no picture**: the container may be understood while the codec inside is not. Compare the player's accepted codecs with H.264 and AAC.
- **Alternate audio is missing**: an FLV keeps one audio stream, so a workflow that needs several alternative audio tracks cannot keep them in the FLV. Return to the original MP4.
- **An unfinished MP4**: an MP4 normally keeps its packet index together, so a write that was interrupted may leave a file that will not play. Cut-short input often still converts, giving a shorter result, so compare the running time.
- **Not a Flash Player file**: you do not need Flash Player for an FLV. Use any player with FLV support.
- **Keep the MP4**: making an FLV for one old workflow should not make it the only surviving copy.
