guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 follows MPEG-4 Part 14, numbered ISO/IEC 14496-14 and first issued in 2003. An MP4 is a container: it wraps video, audio and other tracks instead of setting how they are compressed. Its foundation, the ISO Base Media File Format, descends from Apple's QuickTime; everything is stored in nested boxes, called atoms in QuickTime.

The usual contents are H.264 video with AAC audio, though AV1, VP9 and HEVC video, and MP3 or Opus audio, fit too. The extensions are .mp4 and .m4v for video, with .m4a common for sound alone. Every major browser plays MP4. Unisys started charging license fees for GIF's LZW coding in 1994. The American patent lapsed in 2003; those in Europe and Japan followed a year later.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly, but AAC and H.264 availability can follow system codecs. Chrome plays the MP4 combinations it supports, though the codec inside still decides.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay plays MP4. mpv, a desktop player, lets you pick the audio and subtitle tracks to play.
- **Windows and Mac:** when a suitable decoder is installed, Adobe Premiere accepts MP4 files.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is a free player, and VLC for iOS handles most video formats. Android can play HEVC in MP4 from version 5.0.

### MP4 and GIF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mp4, or .m4v for some video files, with video/mp4; .gif with image/gif.
- **What's inside**: an MP4 holds video and audio tracks. A GIF is a series of palette images, each followed by a pause measured in hundredths of a second.
- **Color**: no frame in a GIF can use more than 256 colors.
- **Compression**: an MP4 keeps whatever its codec produced, such as H.264. A GIF squeezes every image separately and losslessly with LZW.
- **Transparency**: a GIF can mark a single palette color as fully clear; there is no partial transparency.
- **Sound**: an MP4 can carry audio. A GIF cannot.
- **History**: CompuServe released GIF in 1987. With GIF89a in July 1990 came transparency, timing between frames and application data.

What this converter does: it deinterlaces interlaced video, samples 15 frames per second, and scales the picture to fit within 480 pixels on its longer side, keeping both sides even. A single palette is then built from the clip, every frame is mapped to it, and the GIF is set to loop forever. The audio is left behind.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to GIF

- **Adobe Photoshop:** use File > Import > Video Frames to Layers, make a frame animation from the layers in Window > Timeline, then export through File > Export > Save for Web (Legacy) as a GIF set to loop Forever. A long video may not import in full.
- **Microsoft Clipchamp:** put the video in a project, press Export at the top right and select GIF. The option is offered only for videos of 15 seconds or less.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.gif`. A GIF frame delay can't be under a hundredth of a second, and the output loops forever unless `-loop` says otherwise. This page runs FFmpeg too, with a palette built from your clip.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **It won't play**: an MP4 may hold video or sound your player has no decoder for. Try another player, such as mpv.
- **"FFmpeg failed with exit code N" appears**: the conversion didn't finish. Try another copy of the video.
- **A cut-short video gives a short GIF**: a damaged or truncated video can still convert, and the GIF then holds what FFmpeg managed to read.
- **The colors look coarse**: no frame can use more than 256 colors, so the palette built from your video can't keep every shade.
- **The GIF holds the whole video**: there is no trim step, so cut the clip to the moment you want before converting.
- **A long video takes ages**: everything runs on your device with no time limit, so a long clip needs more patience.
- **The motion looks choppy**: the GIF samples 15 frames per second, so fast action moves in visible steps.
- **The GIF is smaller than the video**: scaling stops at 480 pixels on the longer side, and a smaller video isn't scaled up.
- **Your video is a .mov**: use the [MOV to GIF converter](/mov-to-gif/).

faqs.question: Does the HEVC keep my video's frame rate?
faqs.answer: Up to 30 fps, yes. A slower source keeps its own rate, and the rate is written into the stream, which has no timestamps of its own. A faster source drops frames to reach 30 fps.

faqs.question: Is my video uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. The video is decoded by FFmpeg inside your browser tab and encoded by your device's own HEVC encoder, so it never leaves your device.

guide.title: About MP4 and HEVC files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 follows ISO/IEC 14496-14 and keeps video, audio, subtitles and metadata in separate tracks. The video inside may be H.264, H.265 or another codec, and the sound is usually a separate track. Container support alone does not mean a player has a decoder for what is inside, and an MP4 whose writing was interrupted can be left unplayable.

An MP4 file plays on nearly every device, which makes it the usual source for a video you want to re-encode. The extension names the wrapper and never the codec, so an MP4 can already hold H.265 without any sign of it in its name.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows**

- FFplay: ships with FFmpeg and plays MP4 through FFmpeg's MP4 demuxer.

**Mac**

- Adobe Premiere: can import MP4 once the decoder it needs is available.

**Linux**

- mpv: a desktop player that lets you switch audio and subtitle streams.

**Web**

- Firefox: opens MP4 files directly; AAC and H.264 may need system codecs.
- Chrome: plays MP4 files whose audio and video combination it supports.

**Mobile**

- VLC on Android and iOS: a free mobile player for most movie files, local or networked; the codec inside the file decides whether decoding works.

### MP4 and HEVC compared

- **Layer**: MP4 is a container. HEVC is a video codec, so an MP4 may already hold HEVC.
- **Audio**: an MP4 can carry sound. The .hevc file made here carries none.
- **Structure**: a raw stream has no track organization and no timestamps.
- **Profiles**: HEVC profiles set different feature combinations, including higher bit depths and full-resolution chroma. A decoder must support the stream's profile and level.
- **Support**: Apple introduced HEVC media support with iOS 11 and macOS High Sierra 10.13, and older Apple devices may be limited by the video's resolution or frame rate.

HEVC is a video codec, also named H.265 and MPEG-H Part 2. ISO/IEC and ITU-T standardized it jointly and first published it in 2013 for storage, television, streaming and video calls.

What changes in this conversion is the whole video, in three steps. FFmpeg first decodes the MP4, deinterlaces frames marked interlaced, shrinks anything above 1920 pixels or 30 fps, and passes a constant-rate copy to your browser. The browser's own HEVC encoder then re-encodes it. FFmpeg finally writes the encoded video as an Annex B .hevc stream and records the frame rate in it, because a raw stream has no timestamps.

Because the encoder belongs to your browser, the result depends on your device. A browser without an HEVC encoder stops with a message and no file is made. The video always goes through a fresh encode, so it is lossy, and the new extension is not a sign of a lossless copy.

Pick this conversion when a tool asks for an elementary H.265 stream, for example a pipeline that adds its own container later. If you want a smaller movie that still has sound, use an exporter that writes HEVC into an MP4 instead.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to HEVC

- **FFmpeg with libx265 (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -an -c:v libx265 -f hevc output.hevc`. It writes raw video without audio, and `-an` leaves the sound out.
- **x265 (standalone):** run `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -an -pix_fmt yuv420p intermediate.y4m`, then `x265 intermediate.y4m output.hevc`. x265 reads raw YUV or Y4M, not MP4, so the intermediate file needs disk space.
- **MP4Box:** run `MP4Box -info input.mp4` to find the HEVC track, then `MP4Box -raw 1:output=output.hevc input.mp4`, replacing 1 with that track number. This only works when the MP4 already contains HEVC, and it copies rather than encodes.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **A player says it cannot decode the video**: opening the container does not mean the player has the decoder for the codec inside. Try a player with that decoder.
- **An audio tool reports nothing to import**: this MP4 has no sound track, so there is no audio to give it.
- **The file stops partway or will not play**: an interrupted write leaves an unfinished MP4, because its packet metadata is kept together. This page usually still converts such a file, to a shorter output.
- **You only want the H.265 already inside**: extract it with MP4Box instead of encoding again.

guide.title: MP4 to M2TS: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

Phone clips, camera footage and downloaded web video usually arrive as MP4, which is MPEG-4 Part 14. It is standardized as ISO/IEC 14496-14 and dates from 2003. The file is a tree of boxes, the idea QuickTime calls atoms. Video takes .mp4 or .m4v, audio-only files often take .m4a, and the media types video/mp4 and audio/mp4 cover it.

### Programs that open MP4 files

To play the source MP4 before copying it:

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay uses FFmpeg's libraries and mpv switches between audio streams.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere reads an MP4 when a decoder is available for its contents.
- **Web:** Firefox plays MP4 and may lean on codecs supplied by the operating system for AAC and H.264, while Chrome handles the combinations it supports.
- **Mobile:** VLC on iOS and Android.

### MP4 and M2TS compared

M2TS packages video, audio and further streams for Blu-ray BDAV and AVCHD. It adapts the MPEG-2 transport stream and does not prescribe one video codec. Every source packet wraps a 188-byte transport packet and adds four bytes. Blu-ray permits MPEG-2, AVC and VC-1 pictures in it. Sony and Panasonic announced AVCHD in 2006.

FFmpeg runs in your browser and copies the streams from the MP4 without re-encoding. The picture therefore keeps its size and frame rate, and the 1920 px and 30 fps cap that other video pages apply is not in play. Each file downloads on its own, and the MP4 itself is not altered.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to M2TS

- **FFmpeg, stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i concert.mp4 -c copy -mpegts_m2ts_mode 1 concert.m2ts`. The `-mpegts_m2ts_mode 1` option enables M2TS mode.
- **FFmpeg, re-encoding:** run `ffmpeg -i delivery.mp4 -c:v libx264 -c:a ac3 -mpegts_m2ts_mode 1 delivery.m2ts` to write new H.264 video and AC-3 audio instead of copying.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **A missing decoder:** a player can accept the MP4 and still lack the decoder for what it holds, which gives a blank picture or silence. Try another player.
- **An unfinished file:** MP4 keeps its packet index together, so a recording cut off while writing may produce a file no player can open.

guide.title: Understanding MP4 to M4A
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is the container defined in MPEG-4 Part 14 (ISO/IEC 14496-14), which first appeared in 2003. The format rests on the ISO Base Media File Format, a descendant of Apple's QuickTime; data sits in nested boxes, which QuickTime calls atoms. MP4 is a container, not a codec. Typical contents are H.264 video and AAC audio, though a file may also hold AV1, VP9, MP3 or Opus. Video files carry the .mp4 or .m4v extension, and IANA registers video/mp4 and audio/mp4 as its media types.

For this conversion the important point is that the sound is one stream among others. An MP4 can have no audio stream at all, and a container that opens in a player still needs a decoder for each stream inside it.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv lets you choose the audio stream while an MP4 plays, and the FFmpeg project's ffplay opens the format as well.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere Pro imports MP4 for editing.
- **Web:** Firefox plays MP4 directly, although AAC and H.264 playback follows the codecs your system provides. Chrome plays supported MP4 combinations, so the codec inside the file is what counts.
- **Mobile:** Both VLC for Android, a free app, and VLC for iOS open MP4 files, and playback hinges on the streams inside the container.

### MP4 and M4A compared

Audio-only MPEG-4 files carry the M4A extension, which Apple took up for music files without copy protection. Most of them contain AAC, defined in MPEG-4 Part 3 (ISO/IEC 14496-3). As a lossy codec, AAC aimed for better sound than MP3 at equal bitrate, and it covers bitrates as high as 512 kbps at sample rates between 8 and 96 kHz. The media type for M4A is audio/mp4. The two extensions share a container design; what differs is what the file holds.

This page runs FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly inside your browser, with the command `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -acodec aac -b:a 192k -vn output.m4a`. The `-vn` flag leaves out the video. Audio is decoded and then re-encoded to AAC at 192 kbps, including when the MP4's own track is already AAC. No `-map` option is passed, so FFmpeg's default stream selection chooses the audio track, and the page has no control for picking another.

Re-encoding lossy audio never brings back detail the MP4 track was missing, so hold on to the MP4 if the original sound may matter later. Queue several MP4s and each is converted in turn, producing one M4A apiece.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to M4A

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i recording.mp4 -c:a aac -vn -b:a 192k interview-audio.m4a` makes the same AAC encode as this page. When the MP4's audio is already AAC, `ffmpeg -i recording.mp4 -vn -c:a copy interview-audio.m4a` copies the stream without re-encoding it. Stream copy can fail when the target container lacks information it needs.
- **Audacity:** after installing Audacity's optional FFmpeg library, import the MP4 through File > Import > Audio, then choose File > Export Audio and pick M4A (AAC) Files (FFmpeg) from the Format menu. The AAC bitrate you set is not always honored: for stereo, settings of 196 kbps or less export at 196 to 198 kbps, so check the result.
- **mpv:** run `mpv recording.mp4 --vid=no --oac=aac --oacopts=b=192000 --o=interview-audio.m4a`. The `--o` option turns on mpv's encoding mode and names the output file, whose format follows the file name unless you set `--of`. `--vid=no` disables video.

### Problems with MP4 files

**No sound to extract.** An MP4 without an audio track cannot give an audio editor or this page anything to work with. Play the file with the volume up before converting.

**The file will not play.** Opening the container is one thing; decoding the video or sound inside it takes a decoder of its own. Normal MP4 files keep their packet information together, so an interrupted write, such as a camera losing power, can leave an unfinished file that will not play. Try another copy of the recording.

**The wrong language or commentary.** A file with several audio tracks gets FFmpeg's default pick here. Run FFmpeg on your computer with the `-map` option to choose the track yourself.

guide.title: Understanding MP4 and M4R
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

ISO/IEC 14496-14 (MPEG-4 Part 14), published in 2003, defines the MP4 container. It holds separate tracks for video, audio, subtitles and metadata rather than being a codec itself. Most files pair H.264 pictures with AAC sound, and other codecs such as AV1, VP9, MP3 or Opus are allowed. The file is made of nested boxes, the idea QuickTime calls atoms. Registered media types: video/mp4 and audio/mp4. A container is a wrapper: it organizes the tracks, and codecs such as H.264 and AAC compress what each track holds.

The MP4 design is derived from the ISO Base Media File Format, which counts Apple's QuickTime among its ancestors. QuickTime came first, and the MPEG-4 file format took it as its basis. Files with pictures usually end in .mp4 or .m4v; audio-only MPEG-4 is commonly saved as .m4a.

You meet MP4 as phone and camera recordings, downloaded clips and almost every video on the web, since every major browser plays it. For a ringtone only one track matters: the audio. An MP4 with a picture but no sound has nothing to give an audio editor.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- ffplay, the player that ships with FFmpeg, includes the MP4 demuxer.
- mpv is a desktop player where you choose the audio and subtitle stream.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Premiere imports MP4 files into a project.

**Web:**

- Firefox opens MP4 files directly in a tab.
- Chrome opens MP4 files directly too.

**Mobile:**

- VLC, a free media player, has versions for Android and for iOS that open most movie formats.

### MP4 and M4R compared

- **Extensions**: .mp4 and .m4r. An M4R carries AAC sound in an MPEG-4 file, and the ending is what makes iTunes and the iPhone offer it as a ringtone.
- **Content**: an MP4 holds picture and sound. An M4R holds sound only.
- **Container**: both are MPEG-4 family containers.
- **Pictures**: the conversion disables video output, so no picture track reaches the M4R.
- **Compression**: both usually hold lossy codecs. The MP4's own audio is often already AAC, so this conversion encodes lossy sound a second time.

The conversion runs FFmpeg inside your browser tab and writes the audio as AAC at 192 kbps in an iPod-style MPEG-4 file, with the video dropped. It does not cut anything, so the M4R is as long as the soundtrack. Putting the ringtone on a phone is a separate step.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to M4R

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -b:a 192k -c:a aac -vn -f ipod tone.m4r`. The flags choose AAC at 192 kbps, drop the video and name the container, which FFmpeg's format documentation describes as MPEG-4 audio limited to audio streams.
- **GarageBand for iPhone:** first extract a sound file, for example `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -vn sound.wav`. In GarageBand tap the Loops Browser button, then Files, then Browse items from the Files app, and drag the file all the way to the left in Tracks view. Tap Share, then Ringtone, name it and tap Export.
- **WavePad (Windows):** extract a WAV the same way, open it in WavePad and save the result as M4R. NCH's format table lists WAV among the formats WavePad opens and M4R among those it saves on Windows, and not on Mac.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No audio comes out**: the MP4 has no sound track. Play the original first. A silent screen recording has no sound to pull out, and the page then reports a failed conversion.
- **The video won't play anywhere**: container support doesn't guarantee a decoder for the video inside. Try a different player.
- **The file stops partway or won't open**: a recording that was cut off while being written may not play at all. Capture or download it again.
- **The ringtone is too long**: Apple says ringtones can be up to 30 seconds, and GarageBand offers to shorten a longer one. This page does not trim, so cut the sound first or let GarageBand do it.
- **The audio isn't AAC**: an MP4 can hold MP3 or Opus sound instead. That makes no difference here, because the converter encodes the sound as AAC whatever the MP4 held.
- **A phone won't play the video**: Android supports HEVC video inside MP4 files starting with version 5.0.

guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

The MP4 format, MPEG-4 Part 14 (ISO/IEC 14496-14), appeared in 2003 as a container. A container is a wrapper that holds tracks and says nothing about how they are compressed: an MP4 can carry H.264, H.265 or AV1 video next to AAC, MP3 or Opus sound, with subtitles and chapters beside them. Inside, the file is a tree of boxes, which QuickTime calls atoms. That standard descends via the ISO Base Media File Format from Apple's QuickTime.

Almost everything you record or download as video is an MP4: phone clips, camera footage, saved web video. Every major browser plays it, and its registered media types are video/mp4 and audio/mp4. Android has played HEVC video in MP4 files since version 5.0. Because it is a container, whether a given MP4 plays depends on the codecs inside as much as on the .mp4 ending.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- mpv plays MP4 on the desktop and lets you choose the audio and subtitle stream.
- ffplay, the player included with FFmpeg, reads the MP4 format.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Premiere imports MP4 into editing projects.

**Web:**

- Chrome and Firefox play MP4 directly in the page.

**Mobile:**

- VLC plays MP4 on Android phones and tablets, and its iOS version handles most movie formats on iPhone and iPad.

### MP4 and M4V compared

- **Extensions**: .mp4 and .m4v. MDN lists both as extensions for video MPEG-4 files, and notes that audio-only MPEG-4 files often use .m4a.
- **Maker**: MP4 is an ISO standard. M4V is Apple's name for a very close relative, found in iTunes and on Apple TV.
- **Container**: HandBrake's documentation calls the two the exact same file apart from the extension.
- **Copy protection**: iTunes Store M4V files can be protected with FairPlay. An MP4 made here carries no such protection.
- **Codecs**: usually H.264 video with AAC audio in both.

Nothing is re-encoded here. FFmpeg lifts the existing video and audio streams out and sets them in a fresh MPEG-4 file with the .m4v ending, and the picture keeps the MP4's frame size and rate. The 1920 px and 30 fps limits that other video pages apply don't apply here, because the streams are copied instead of re-encoded. Since no compression is repeated, no quality is lost, and the job is mostly rewriting the container. The page puts no cap on size; a long file only takes your device longer, and you can choose several MP4 files at once. The M4V plays only where the player supports the codecs inside, just as the MP4 did.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to M4V

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i source.mp4 -c copy -f mp4 output.m4v`. The -c copy option is FFmpeg's stream copy, which passes the video and audio through without re-encoding, and -f mp4 sets the output container to MP4 under the .m4v name.
- **Rename a copy:** The HandBrake page calls the two the same file with a different extension, so you can copy the file and change .mp4 to .m4v. It adds that QuickTime and QuickTime-based apps can't play an MP4 with AC3 pass-through, subtitles or chapters enabled unless the ending is .m4v, which is a reason to rename a copy for those players.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **The video shows nothing or the sound is missing**: the container opens, yet a decoder for something inside is missing. Container support alone doesn't guarantee a decoder for the video or sound in it, so try another player.
- **The codecs inside suit one device and not another**: a new ending doesn't change what a player can decode. This page copies the codecs unchanged, so re-encode the video in another program if a device refuses them.
- **The picture plays but the sound doesn't, or the reverse**: an MP4 holds separate tracks, and a player may have a decoder for only one of them. The M4V behaves the way the MP4 did, because both tracks are copied as they are.
- **Renaming didn't fix it**: changing the ending can't repair a damaged file or an unsupported encoding.
- **The file is cut short or won't open**: an MP4 normally keeps its index data together, so a recording stopped mid-write may stay unplayable. Capture or download it again.

guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14 (ISO/IEC 14496-14), a container for video, audio and metadata. H.264 video with AAC audio is the pairing you will meet most. MP4 turns up as online video and streams, as phone and camera recordings, and as files passed between people.

Because MP4 is a container, the codec inside decides what a player needs.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay plays MP4, and mpv plays it on the desktop.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MP4 once the decoder it needs is present.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly, and Chrome plays supported MP4 combinations.
- **Mobile:** VLC on Android (VLC for Android) and on iPhone (VLC for iOS) both play MP4, and decoding depends on the media inside.

### MP4 and MJPEG compared

Motion JPEG codes a video as a succession of individually JPEG-coded images, with no compression between frames, so its files usually come out larger than H.264. It is a video encoding rather than a container: AVI files commonly mark it with the MJPG FourCC, and QuickTime is another wrapper. This page stores the Motion JPEG in an AVI wrapper, turns the sound into 16-bit PCM and limits the picture to 1920 px on the longer side and the frame rate to 30 fps. Frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced first. MJPEG turns up in webcams and IP cameras, video editing and digital cameras' video modes. The OpenDML extension to AVI defines a profile for storing MJPEG, and production workflows may edit MJPEG and then use another encoding for delivery.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to MJPEG

- **FFmpeg (command line):** enter `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v mjpeg -q:v 5 output.avi`. It applies none of this page's size or frame-rate limits.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No decoder for what is inside**: a container can be supported while the decoder for its video or sound is missing.
- **An unfinished file will not play**: an MP4 interrupted while being written can be unplayable, since its packet metadata is stored together.
- **No audio track to extract**: audio editors need an audio track, and an MP4 without one has none to give.

faqs.question: Can I just rename my .mp4 file to .mkv?

faqs.answer: No. The conversion happens on your device through FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly: it reads the MP4 and writes the MKV there. Your original file isn't changed.

guide.title: About MP4 and MKV
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

An MP4 file is a container, defined as MPEG-4 Part 14 in ISO/IEC 14496-14 and first published in 2003. It can carry video, audio, subtitles and metadata together, and H.264 video paired with AAC audio is the most common combination. MP4 can also hold codecs such as AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus, so the .mp4 ending names the wrapper, not the compression inside it. Because it is only a wrapper, an MP4 can be healthy and still refuse to play on a device that lacks the decoder for the video inside.

MP4 follows the ISO Base Media File Format, itself derived from QuickTime, and its content sits in nested boxes (QuickTime called them atoms). The .mp4 and .m4v extensions mark video, .m4a often marks audio-only MPEG-4, and the media types video/mp4 and audio/mp4 are registered for the format. Every major browser plays MP4, and Android plays HEVC video in MP4 files from version 5.0.

You meet MP4 in online video and streaming, in phone and camera recordings, and in files shared between people. That is also why people want to move one into Matroska. They want several audio or subtitle tracks, chapters, or a format their media server prefers.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Linux, Mac and Windows:** ffplay plays an MP4 once the matching decoders are in your FFmpeg build.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv plays MP4 files and lets you choose which audio and subtitle streams play.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player opens MP4 files.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere brings in an MP4 only if it has a decoder for the codec the file holds.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player opens MP4 files.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly, and AAC and H.264 availability can depend on the codecs in your system.
- **Web:** Chrome plays the MP4 files whose codecs it supports.
- **Mobile:** Android and iOS both get their own VLC app, which plays an MP4 whose codecs it supports.

### MP4 and MKV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mp4 for MP4; .mkv for Matroska video, registered as video/matroska.
- **Design**: MP4 is an ISO standard container. Matroska is an open container format. It grew out of the MCF project and is built on EBML, a binary markup derived from XML. WebM is a subset of Matroska.
- **Tracks**: MP4 can carry subtitles and chapters. Matroska files can include several video, audio and subtitle streams, with chapters and descriptive tags built into the design. In a player such as mpv, choosing the wrong audio or subtitle stream gives the wrong language, and the player lets you switch.
- **Codecs**: neither container fixes a codec or a quality level. The codec decides how the picture looks, and a container swap leaves it as it was.
- **Reach**: MP4 plays on nearly every device. MKV plays in VLC, mpv and Plex, so check that the player you plan to use accepts it before you convert a whole library.

This page copies the streams (`-c copy` in FFmpeg). They are not decoded and compressed a second time, so the picture keeps its size and frame rate. What you gain is the new container. What you do not get is a codec change.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to MKV

- **FFmpeg (command line):** copy the streams across with `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c copy output.mkv`. This is the same copy this page performs. By default FFmpeg picks one stream of each kind, so add explicit stream mapping when you need a particular track set.
- **HandBrake (Windows, Mac, Linux):** choose Open Source and select the MP4, then pick a Matroska preset such as H.264 MKV 1080p30, set the Save As destination and select Start. The presets set their own encoders, so the video is encoded again, which suits a file whose codec has to change too.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **A codec your player lacks**: a container can open fine while the video inside can't be decoded. Converting to MKV does not change that, because the codec is copied.
- **An unfinished MP4**: normal MP4 files keep their packet metadata together, so an interrupted recording or download can leave a file that never plays. Record or download it again before you convert.

guide.title: About MP4 and MP2 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

An MP4 keeps a video's picture and sound as separate tracks inside one wrapper. Standards bodies call the wrapper MPEG-4 Part 14, numbered 14496-14 by ISO and IEC, and it appeared in 2003. Apple's QuickTime is the ancestor, with the ISO Base Media File Format in between, and the file itself is a tree of nested boxes (QuickTime's term is atoms).

MP4 is a container, so the extension says nothing about how the contents were compressed. The common contents are H.264 pictures and AAC sound, though AV1, VP9, MP3 or Opus can sit inside too. Video files take .mp4 or .m4v, audio-only MPEG-4 files frequently take .m4a, and the media types on record are video/mp4 and audio/mp4. You come across MP4 in online video, phone and camera recordings, and clips people share. For this pair, the converter takes the soundtrack and writes it again as MP2.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows, plus Mac**

- Premiere, from Adobe, will import an MP4 provided the decoder for its contents is present.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- ffplay plays MP4 through FFmpeg's MP4 demuxer.
- mpv is a desktop player that offers a choice of audio and subtitle tracks while an MP4 plays.

**Web**

- Firefox plays MP4 in the page, but whether AAC and H.264 work can hinge on codecs the system supplies.
- Chrome plays supported web audio and MP4 combinations, and the codec inside still matters.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android is a free mobile player, and its decoding follows whatever codecs the MP4 holds; VLC for iOS opens most movie formats, whether stored on the phone or reached over a network.

### MP4 and MP2 compared

- **Names and types**: .mp4 goes with video/mp4 and audio/mp4, while .mp2 goes with audio/mpeg.
- **What a file holds**: a single MP4 may combine video, audio, subtitles and chapters, while an MP2 file holds audio only.
- **Compression**: MP2 is MPEG-1 Audio Layer II, specified in ISO/IEC 11172-3 and finalized in 1992. It is lossy and perceptual, it needs little decoding work, and it came before MP3, which is Layer III. ISO/IEC 13818-3 extends Layer II for MPEG-2.
- **Where it is used**: digital radio and television broadcasting, Video CD production and DVD-Video soundtracks.
- **The name trap**: the MP2 produced here is MPEG audio Layer II, and it is unrelated to MPEG-2 video files.

Here the picture is left out and the sound is encoded again. FFmpeg writes MPEG-1 Layer II at 192 kbps, whatever codec the MP4's audio used. MP2's lossy coding omits sound information that decoding cannot recover, so the conversion cannot bring back detail the MP4's audio did not have.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to MP2

- **FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -vn -c:a mp2 -b:a 192k soundtrack.mp2`. The `-vn` option disables video, and FFmpeg's documentation lists MP2 among the audio codecs it can encode. This is the same single encode the page runs.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** Audacity imports MP4 audio only with its optional FFmpeg library installed. Import the file, choose File > Export Audio and select MP2 in the Format list. The bit rate runs from 16 to 384 kbps, with 160 kbps as the default.
- **TwoLAME with FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -c:a pcm_s16le -vn extracted.wav`, then `twolame -b 192 extracted.wav soundtrack.mp2`. It takes two steps because TwoLAME reads sound files through libsndfile, and `-b` sets the total bitrate in kbps.

Audacity suits you when you want a bitrate other than 192 kbps. The TwoLAME route uses a dedicated Layer II encoder, at the cost of a large intermediate WAV file, since WAV usually holds uncompressed audio.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No sound to extract**: an MP4 without audio cannot give an audio editor a track, and this page fails with an FFmpeg exit-code error. Play the video and listen for sound first.
- **No decoder for what is inside**: a player that accepts the MP4 wrapper may still lack a decoder for the video or sound it carries. Identify the codecs before blaming the player.
- **The file stops partway**: ordinary MP4 files store their packet metadata in one place, which means a recording or download cut short can leave something unplayable. Record or fetch it once more.
- **The MP4 holds several audio tracks**: some players let you choose a track, and mpv shows the audio streams a file has. Check which track you want before converting.

guide.title: Understanding MP4 and MPEG
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is the everyday name for MPEG-4 Part 14, ISO/IEC 14496-14, whose first edition dates from 2003. It packages timed video, audio and extra streams such as subtitles. Apple's QuickTime heritage underlies it, standardized as the ISO Base Media File Format, and the file stores everything in nested boxes, which QuickTime calls atoms. Among them is the index telling a player where each video, audio or subtitle sample sits, which is why one file can carry several streams side by side.

The container says nothing about the codec: a phone clip and a downloaded film can both be .mp4 yet hold different video and sound. The typical contents are H.264 video and AAC sound; AV1, VP9, MP3 or Opus may appear instead.

You meet MP4 files everywhere. Phones and cameras record them, streaming sites serve them and people share them as files, and every major browser plays them. The usual endings are .mp4 or .m4v for video and .m4a for audio-only MPEG-4, with video/mp4 and audio/mp4 as the registered media types.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv plays MP4 and lets you pick among its audio and subtitle streams. FFmpeg's bundled player, ffplay, contains the MP4 demuxer but still needs decoders for what the file holds.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere can import MP4 once the required decoder is present.
- **Web:** Firefox plays MP4 directly, but AAC and H.264 playback can hinge on the system's codecs. Chrome handles the MP4 codec combinations it supports.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is a free player; what plays depends on the codecs in the file. VLC for iOS handles most movie formats from the device or the network.

### MP4 and MPEG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mp4 and video/mp4; .mpeg or .mpg and video/mpeg. The Library of Congress records video/mpeg for MPEG video.
- **Codecs**: the MPEG file this page writes holds MPEG-2 video with MP2 audio, an older pair than what most MP4 files use.
- **History**: MPEG-2 began as a coding for compressed television and was later taken up for DVDs. MPEG systems treat every coded picture, sound or data component as an elementary stream, which packetized elementary streams then cut into packets.
- **Frame rate and size**: the page limits output to 30 fps and a 1920 pixel long edge, and trims an odd width or height by 1 pixel.
- **Quality**: the video targets a set quality level, not a file size, and the audio is set at 96 kbps.

The word MPEG confuses people, because MP4 already belongs to the MPEG family. A .mpeg file uses the older MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 coding that TV delivery and DVDs relied on. The MPEG file here is plain video, without DVD menus or chapters. Nothing on the page lets you choose a track. With several audio tracks in the MP4, whichever FFmpeg selects by default ends up in the MPEG. The original MP4 stays untouched, since you download a new copy.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to MPEG

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i recording.mp4 -c:v mpeg2video -c:a mp2 legacy.mpeg`. FFmpeg's format and codec tables list MP4, MPEG-2 video and MP2. This page's own command also sets a quality level, a 96 kbps audio bitrate, scaling and a frame-rate cap, so the bare command gives a different file.
- **Prism for Windows:** add the MP4 with Add File(s), choose MPEG or MPG under Output Format, then set the Save to Folder path and hit Convert, reviewing Encoder Options first if you wish. Prism lists MP4 as an input only when an mp4 filter is installed, and its output list includes .mpeg and .mpg.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **It plays on one device and not another**: a device may take the container but lack a decoder for what it carries. Check the codec, not the extension, and open the file in VLC to see what it holds.
- **The file won't play at all**: if recording stopped abruptly, the MP4 may be unfinished and refuse to play, since its packet metadata is kept together. Record or download it again.
- **Newer codecs fail on older software**: Android plays HEVC video in MP4 files only from version 5.0.
- **The MP4 is cut short or damaged**: the MPEG usually still gets written, only shorter, stopping where FFmpeg could no longer read.

guide.title: About MP4 and MPEG-2 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

Think of MP4 as a standardized box that holds compressed video, audio and other data without saying how any of it was compressed. The name on the standard is MPEG-4 Part 14, dating from 2003, and its roots lie in Apple's QuickTime, reached through the ISO Base Media File Format.

Typical contents are H.264 pictures with AAC sound, and the wrapper is just as happy to carry AV1, VP9, MP3 or Opus. A video file is named .mp4 or .m4v, with video/mp4 and audio/mp4 as the recorded media types. Online video and streaming, phone and camera recordings, and shared clips all use MP4, and every major browser plays it. A converter that targets MPEG-2 has to decode whatever codec the box holds, then encode the pictures again.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows and macOS**

- Adobe's Premiere imports an MP4 once the decoder for its contents is available.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- mpv is a desktop player where an MP4's audio and subtitle tracks can be chosen during playback.
- ffplay, from the FFmpeg project, reads MP4 with FFmpeg's demuxer.

**Web**

- Firefox plays MP4 in the page, with AAC and H.264 sometimes depending on system codecs.
- Chrome handles supported MP4 combinations, but the codec inside still decides.

**Mobile**

- On phones, VLC for Android and VLC for iOS open video stored on the device, decoding whatever codecs the file contains.

### MP4 and MPEG-2 compared

- **Names and types**: MP4 uses video/mp4. MPEG-2 video is registered as video/mpeg.
- **Role**: MP4 is a container for many codecs. MPEG-2 is a picture coding, defined in ISO/IEC 13818-2 and ITU-T H.262.
- **Compression**: MPEG-2 combines block transforms with prediction between frames, so not every frame stands alone. It was developed for compressed television and later adopted for DVDs, and it supports interlaced video.
- **Streams**: audio and pictures can be assembled into a program stream, and a transport stream can combine several programs.

The codec is what changes here, and nothing is copied across: the picture is decoded from whatever the MP4 holds and encoded again. FFmpeg re-encodes the video as MPEG-2 at a fixed quality level (6) and the sound as MP2 at 96 kbps. A frame wider or taller than 1920 pixels is scaled down to fit, a rate above 30 fps is reduced to 30 by dropping frames, and both sides are made even. The deinterlacing filter runs on frames the file marks as interlaced. MPEG-2 compression can reduce detail, so the encoder settings affect how the result looks.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to MPEG-2

- **FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `ffmpeg -i source.mp4 -c:a mp2 -c:v mpeg2video converted.mpg` to name the video and audio encoders yourself. FFmpeg's documentation lists MP2 audio and MPEG-2 video among the codecs it supports. Add any bitrate, size or frame rate your destination requires.
- **FFmpeg DVD target (Windows, Mac, Linux):** the command is `ffmpeg -i source.mp4 -target pal-dvd dvd-ready.mpg`. FFmpeg's documentation says a target type may be prefixed with pal-, ntsc- or film-, so choose the standard for your region. This sets DVD-style encoder and muxer options for the file; it does not author menus or burn a disc.

Use the DVD target when the file is headed for a disc and the plain command when you want only a codec change.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **Playback fails**: container support does not mean a decoder exists for its contents. Find out which codecs the file holds, then use a player that has them.
- **The MP4 ends abruptly**: a regular MP4 gathers its packet metadata in one spot, so a download or recording halted early may leave a file that refuses to play. Obtain it again.
- **A 4K or 60 fps MP4**: this page caps the longer side at 1920 pixels and the rate at 30 fps, and it drops frames rather than slowing the video. Run FFmpeg yourself if the destination needs more.
- **Moving edges show combing**: only frames the file marks as interlaced get the deinterlacing filter. Footage that is interlaced but not marked passes through, so deinterlace it in an editor first.
- **The MP4 has no audio track**: the conversion still runs, and the MPEG-2 file has pictures only. Add sound in an editor if the destination needs it.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

In an MP4, the picture, the sound and the descriptive data each get their own track inside one container. Codecs are chosen separately from the container. The familiar pairing is H.264 picture with AAC sound, but other encodings can sit inside, so whether a file plays on older equipment depends on the streams within it as well as the wrapper.

Every major browser plays MP4, and it is a common format for phone and camera recordings and online video. Its structure is a set of nested boxes, and normal files keep their packet index together, so a recording interrupted before it is finished can be hard to play.

A request for MPG often signals a legacy playback or authoring requirement. Get the receiving system's actual specifications first: the MPEG version, picture dimensions, frame rate and supported sound. A file named .mpg does not certify that all of those have been met.

This matters most when a device manual mentions DVD. A movie file accepted by an editing program is not a finished disc, because disc authoring adds navigation and a directory structure around compliant streams. Keep the MP4 while you decide whether you need a playable file, an intermediate for authoring or a real disc.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay plays an MP4 locally, and mpv is a desktop player for the same files.
- **Web:** Chrome and Firefox can play an MP4 in a tab when they support its codecs.
- **Mobile:** you can open local files in VLC on Android or iOS.

### MP4 and MPG compared

- **Container family**: MPG is the usual extension for an MPEG program stream carrying MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 picture and sound. MP4 belongs to the MPEG-4 family. Both wrap encoded media, but they support different combinations.
- **History**: MPG was the standard extension for VCD and DVD video.
- **Suffixes**: both .mpeg and .mpg label MPEG video, and neither tells you whether the video inside is MPEG-1 or MPEG-2.
- **Streams**: some MPEG files are system streams and others are raw video, so a tool has to identify the structure before choosing a demuxer.

Here the picture is encoded as MPEG-2 and the soundtrack as MP2 at 96 kbps. Nothing from the MP4 is copied across: the video gets a new lossy pass. A long edge beyond 1920 px is scaled down, a rate above 30 frames per second is cut by dropping frames so the clip keeps its length, and widths and heights end up even. Anything flagged as interlaced gets a deinterlacing pass before encoding.

These are general conversion settings. They do not match a PAL or NTSC DVD profile, so do not treat the result as universally disc-compliant. No -map option is used; FFmpeg decides which streams go in. Your MP4 stays untouched; what you save is a new file ending in .mpg.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to MPG

- **FFmpeg (DVD target):** `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -target ntsc-dvd output.mpg` sets the codecs, bitrates and buffer sizes for NTSC DVD. Use pal-dvd for PAL. The file still needs disc authoring if you want a navigable DVD.
- **FFmpeg (VCD target):** `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -target pal-vcd output.mpg` applies the Video CD settings instead, for gear that expects them.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **A player rejects the MPG**: compare its streams with the device manual. The extension does not settle bitrate, dimensions, scan type or accepted audio. A standard-definition MPEG device may refuse a larger MPEG-2 file that a desktop player handles.
- **It won't act as a DVD**: burning one MPG as data is not the same as building a DVD-Video layout with navigation and supporting files.
- **Lost detail**: a lossy MPEG encode cannot keep every detail of the picture, and a large frame may also be resized.
- **Decoder missing**: playback needs a decoder for the sound as well as the picture, and sharing a container does not make their codecs interchangeable.
- **Unfinished MP4**: a recording stopped mid-write may be unplayable. The output from a cut-short input can end early, so check its length.

For an equipment handoff, ask for a short sample known to play on that device and compare its specifications with your export. That beats matching a suffix.

### What is an MP4 file?

Formally MPEG-4 Part 14 (ISO/IEC 14496-14), MP4 dates from 2003. Apple's QuickTime format was the ancestor of the ISO Base Media File Format that MP4 builds on, and the data sits in nested boxes.

As a container, MP4 doesn't fix one codec. H.264 video and AAC audio make the typical combination; the container can also carry streams such as Opus, MP3, VP9 or AV1.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows and Linux:** ffplay uses FFmpeg's MP4 demuxer and needs the matching decoders to play.
- **Windows:** Premiere on Windows takes MP4 files when the right decoder is installed.
- **Mac and Linux:** mpv plays MP4 and lets you select audio and subtitle streams during playback.

### MP4 and MTS compared

- **Extensions**: .mp4 and .mts.
- **Container**: MP4 is a box-based file. MTS is an MPEG transport stream, the extension for video from AVCHD camcorders.
- **Codecs**: H.264 video can sit in either wrapper, while AVCHD audio is Dolby Digital or linear PCM. The wrapper and the compressed video are independent layers, so streams can move across unchanged.
- **Structure**: camcorder MTS clips normally sit in an AVCHD recording structure, which a single converted clip lacks.

The page runs FFmpeg with `-c copy`, so video and audio aren't re-encoded and the picture keeps its frame size and rate. The MTS can still end up larger than the original.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to MTS

- **FFmpeg, copying streams:** `ffmpeg -i event-delivery.mp4 -c copy event-transport.mts`. FFmpeg's documentation says stream copy doesn't re-encode, and that the output format is guessed from the file extension. Read the log for streams that were dropped.
- **FFmpeg, encoding the video again:** `ffmpeg -i editor-source.mp4 -c:v libx264 -c:a copy editor-transport.mts` encodes the video with libx264 and copies the audio. Your FFmpeg needs that encoder.
- **Prism (Windows):** add the MP4 with Add File(s), pick a Save to Folder, select MTS under Output Format, open Encoder Options to change settings, and press Convert. NCH's product page lists MP4 as an input and MTS as an output.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **The MP4 won't play**: a recognized container says nothing about the codecs inside it, which need their own decoders. Try mpv or ffplay.
- **An unfinished recording**: because an MP4 gathers its packet metadata in one structure, a write that stopped early may leave a file that won't play. FFmpeg may still convert what it can read, giving a shorter MTS.
- **Sound missing from the MTS**: FFmpeg can leave out a stream the transport stream can't hold, or carry it as a data stream, and reports no error. Play the MTS before deleting the MP4.

guide.title: About MP4 and MXF
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

Defined by ISO/IEC 14496-14 (MPEG-4 Part 14) on top of Apple's QuickTime lineage, MP4 is a container. A single file can carry H.264 video with AAC audio, or other video and audio codecs, along with subtitles and chapters.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows:** mpv offers desktop playback, and Windows Media Player opens MP4 as well.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player is the built-in viewer, and Premiere imports MP4 given the right decoder.
- **Linux:** ffplay, the player that ships with FFmpeg.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome.
- **Mobile:** the VLC apps for Android and iOS.

VLC media player is listed for MP4 as well.

### MP4 and MXF compared

- **Standard**: MXF, the Material Exchange Format, is standardized through SMPTE documents (SMPTE 377M) for professional video and audio.
- **Contents**: it wraps media essence with descriptive or structural metadata, and the wrapper can carry different video encodings, so MXF alone does not define image quality.
- **Use**: professional acquisition, exchange and preservation workflows. Its operational patterns describe arrangements of packages and essence.
- **Extension and type**: the extension is .mxf and the media type is application/mxf.
- **Caution**: some arrangements reference essence stored outside the file.

This page runs FFmpeg in your browser and writes MPEG-2 video at 2000 kbps in 4:2:2, with 16-bit PCM audio at 48 kHz stereo, at a fixed 25 fps. The longer side is capped at 1920 px, and both sides end up even after rounding down.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to MXF

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -ar 48000 -b:v 2000k -c:a pcm_s16le -r 25 -c:v mpeg2video -ac 2 -pix_fmt yuv422p -f mxf clip.mxf`.
- **FFmpeg OP-Atom:** swap in the mxf_opatom muxer with `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -an -c:v mpeg2video -b:v 4M -f mxf_opatom clip.mxf`. The -an option drops the audio, so the file is video only.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **Unreadable contents**: an editor can import the MP4 container and still fail on the codec inside it.
- **Silent clips**: with no audio track in the MP4, an audio editor has nothing to import.
- **Unfinished files**: if a recording was cut off before it finished, the MP4 can be left incomplete and unplayable.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4, or MPEG-4 Part 14, is a container defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14. One file can carry video, audio, subtitles and metadata. The usual pairing is H.264 video with AAC audio, yet H.265 and AV1 video fit too. Phones and cameras record in it, and it plays on nearly every device.

Because MP4 is only the wrapper, the codec inside decides what a player has to decode. Container support alone does not guarantee that a decoder exists for the video or sound inside it, so a file can carry the right ending and still fail on a device that lacks the codec.

People take the sound out of an MP4 for many reasons. A lecture or a talk becomes an audio file for a commute. A video of a song becomes a track. OGG is a natural target when the audio is headed for a game or an open-source player, since game audio and open-source music are among its common uses.

The page keeps the sound and drops everything else. It does not ask you to pick a track or a bitrate, and the finished file is named after the MP4 with an .ogg ending.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Mac, Windows and Linux:** ffplay is bundled with FFmpeg and plays MP4. mpv is a desktop player where audio and subtitle streams can be selected, and VLC media player will open MP4 as well.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere can import MP4 when a suitable decoder is installed. QuickTime Player and Windows Media Player are also listed for opening MP4.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play supported media in a tab, as long as the codec inside is one they handle.
- **Mobile:** Phone users can try the Android or iOS versions of VLC, which open MP4 whenever they can decode the contents.

### MP4 and OGG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: MP4 files use .mp4 and video/mp4. Audio-only Ogg is labeled audio/ogg, while Ogg with video is labeled video/ogg. The .ogg ending is conventionally used for Vorbis audio, and .oga is the broader audio ending.
- **What they hold**: MP4 is a multi-track container for video, audio, subtitles and metadata. The OGG made here carries one thing, Vorbis audio.
- **Codecs**: Ogg is the container, and the codec determines how each stream is compressed. Vorbis is a lossy codec in an open, patent-free format.
- **Openness**: Ogg is maintained by Xiph.Org as a free format. MP4 is defined in an ISO standard.
- **Streaming**: Ogg can be read and written in sequence, a good fit for streaming. Timestamps and error detection are part of its framing.
- **Video**: gone. The picture of the MP4 does not carry over.
- **Support**: Firefox, Chrome, VLC and Audacity open OGG.

The OGG is a new compressed copy, so choose it because you need Ogg Vorbis, not because it improves the audio. The MP4 to MP3 converter on this site is the alternative for apps that expect MP3 audio.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to OGG

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i lecture.mp4 -vn -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 lecture-sound.ogg`. A `-map` option selects a particular stream when the MP4 has several.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** Audacity's manual says the optional FFmpeg library lets it import audio from most unprotected video files, and that on a Mac it can import MP4 without it. Import the MP4, choose File > Export Audio, pick Ogg Vorbis as the format and set its quality slider, which runs from 0 to 10 and defaults to 5.
- **VLC:** choose Media > Convert/Save, add the MP4, set the profile to Audio - Vorbis (OGG), enter a destination with an .ogg name and click Start. That profile has video turned off and writes 128 kbps stereo at 44,100 Hz, so it differs from the quality setting on this page.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **The page reports "FFmpeg failed with exit code"**: an MP4 with no audio is the likely reason. Audacity's manual notes that such a file cannot supply an audio track.
- **The OGG has the wrong language or track**: this page does not select tracks for you. Extract the needed track with FFmpeg `-map`.
- **An OGG will not play**: the container does not say which audio encoding it holds, so the player must handle that codec and Ogg itself. Try VLC or a current browser.
- **An MP4 will not play at all**: the codec inside may be one your player lacks. VLC carries many decoders of its own and is worth a try.
- **A site or player wants .oga or .ogv**: RFC 5334 treats .ogg, .oga and .ogv as different endings, so a tool that expects one may refuse another.
- **The file was cut off when the recording stopped**: normal MP4 files keep packet metadata in one place, which is why a write that stops early can leave a file that will not play.

guide.title: About MP4 and OGV
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is Part 14 of the MPEG-4 standard, ISO/IEC 14496-14, first published in 2003. QuickTime is where the design began and the ISO Base Media File Format carried it on, so the data is stored in nested boxes, which QuickTime calls atoms. As a container instead of a codec, MP4 is able to hold subtitles and chapters alongside the picture and sound. H.264 (AVC) video with AAC audio is the usual pairing, though AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus can also appear inside.

Phone and camera recordings, downloaded clips and web video often come as MP4, and every major browser plays it. The endings .mp4 and .m4v mark video, while .m4a is common for audio-only MPEG-4. The two registered media types are video/mp4 and audio/mp4. From version 5.0 onward, Android plays HEVC video held in MP4.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - mpv, an open desktop player, plays MP4 with selectable audio and subtitle streams.
  - ffplay, bundled with FFmpeg, includes the MP4 demuxer; playback also needs the matching decoders.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - Adobe Premiere imports MP4 when the necessary decoder is available.
- **Web:**
  - Firefox plays supported media directly; AAC and H.264 availability can depend on system codecs.
  - Chrome plays the web audio and MP4 pairings it supports, and which ones work depends on the codec within.
- **Mobile:**
  - On Android, VLC is free, and what it decodes depends on the media stored in the container. On iOS, VLC opens most movie formats and can connect to media on the device or the network.

### MP4 and OGV compared

- **Names and types**: .mp4 with video/mp4; .ogv with video/ogg.
- **Layout**: an MP4 is a tree of boxes. An Ogg stream starts with the bytes OggS.
- **Who looks after it**: MPEG and ISO for MP4; the Xiph.Org Foundation for Ogg.
- **Typical codecs**: H.264 and AAC in MP4. Theora video with Vorbis sound is one documented Ogg combination.
- **Where it plays**: every major browser plays MP4. Ogg video opens in VLC and Firefox, and FFmpeg can read Ogg streams.

Nothing is copied across unchanged. FFmpeg decodes the video and writes it out again, which makes the OGV a fresh encode. The page passes no codec settings for .ogv, so FFmpeg's defaults apply: Theora video with Vorbis audio, and the video rate stays at its 200 kbit/s default. Frames marked as interlaced are deinterlaced on the way. The picture is fitted inside 1920 pixels, frames above 30 per second are dropped to reach 30 (the clip keeps its length), and the final size is forced to even numbers, which turns a 1279 by 719 source into 1278 by 718.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to OGV

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v libtheora -c:a libvorbis output.ogv` names the codecs outright, Theora for the picture and Vorbis for the sound, and writes them into an Ogg file. FFmpeg has to be built with libtheora and libvorbis support. Unlike this page, the command leaves the size and frame rate alone, so a large source stays large.
- **VLC media player:** From a terminal, `vlc sample.mp4 --sout="#transcode{acodec=vorb,vcodec=theo}:std{access=file,mux=ogg,dst=sample_new.ogv}"` transcodes with VLC's own encoders and writes sample_new.ogv. VLC's manual explains that the container must change because Theora and Vorbis are not compatible with MP4, and it shows the chain with an .ogg name for the same payload; .ogv is the ending Xiph recommends for Ogg video.
- **ffmpeg2theora:** `ffmpeg2theora input.mp4 -o output.ogv` uses a converter made for Ogg Theora and Vorbis. Its man page says it converts any media file that ffmpeg can decode, and that `-o` sets the output name; leave it out and the file is named after the input with an .ogv ending.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **An MP4 opens but shows no picture**: support for the container alone does not promise that your player can decode the video or the sound stored in it. Try another player, or convert the file here.
- **An MP4 has no sound to extract**: a file without an audio track leaves nothing for an audio editor to take.
- **The file will not play at all**: an interrupted write can leave an unfinished MP4 unplayable, because a normal MP4 keeps its packet metadata together. Record or fetch the file once more.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is the MPEG-4 container, which can hold several kinds of track side by side. The extension does not say which codecs are inside, so one MP4 may carry H.264 and AAC while another has no sound at all. For pulling out audio, the thing that matters is whether a soundtrack exists.

An MP4 stores its index data in one place, so a recording that was interrupted midway may not play at all.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv plays MP4 on the desktop, and FFplay plays it.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports the container when the necessary decoder is available.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly and may rely on system codecs for AAC and H.264, and Chrome plays supported combinations where the internal codec still matters.
- **Mobile:** The VLC apps on Android and iPhone cost nothing; whether a file plays hinges on the streams inside.

### MP4 and Opus compared

- **Names**: .mp4; .opus, which commonly holds Opus audio in an Ogg stream as specified in RFC 7845.
- **Standards**: RFC 6716 from the IETF, dated September 2012, defines Opus, which merges Skype's SILK with Xiph.Org's CELT.
- **Contents**: MP4 carries picture and sound. Opus is lossy audio only, designed for speech and music.

The page drops the video and encodes the audio with libopus at 128 kbps. FFmpeg runs inside your browser, so the MP4 is not uploaded.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to Opus

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i talk.mp4 -vn -c:a libopus -b:a 96k talk.opus` to choose your own bitrate.
- **Audacity:** open the MP4, which needs the optional FFmpeg library, then choose File > Export Audio (Ctrl+Shift+E) and pick Opus.
- **opus-tools with FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i session.mp4 -vn session.wav`, then `opusenc --bitrate 64 session.wav session.opus`.

### Problems with MP4 files

Playing the container is not the same as decoding what it holds, so a player can open an MP4 yet lack the codec for its sound. A clip recorded without sound gives an editor no audio track to work with.

Reading Vorbis from Ogg is no proof that a program decodes Opus, since the Ogg mapping uses distinct Opus headers. If a player rejects the file, try another one before blaming the conversion.

Afterward, listen to the result at dialogue breaks and music transitions.

guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

Most phones and cameras save video as MP4, defined by MPEG-4 Part 14, ISO/IEC 14496-14, published in 2003. Boxes nest inside boxes, a layout inherited from QuickTime through the ISO Base Media File Format. A typical MP4 holds H.264 pictures and AAC sound, although VP9 and Opus can also appear. Files end in .mp4 or .m4v, and audio-only MPEG-4 files frequently use .m4a.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay, which comes with FFmpeg, opens an MP4, and mpv can choose among audio tracks.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere takes in an MP4 when it has the decoder for the contents.
- **Web:** Chrome and Firefox play the MP4 combinations they support.
- **Mobile:** the VLC apps for Android and iOS.

### MP4 and RM compared

RM is RealMedia. RealNetworks described it as a streaming container in an Internet-Draft dated March 1998, covering playback from local storage or over a network. A RealMedia file begins with a .RMF header and continues in tagged chunks with four-character identifiers. Separate headers describe the whole file and each stream. The draft is work in progress, so its version-specific structures are history, not a guarantee.

The command here is plain: FFmpeg reads the MP4 and writes an .rm file, with no codec options of its own. The page first tries a server route and then converts in your browser with FFmpeg. You still get a separate download for each file, and your original is untouched.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to RM

- **FFmpeg with RealVideo 1.0 and AC-3:** run `ffmpeg -i exhibit.mp4 -c:v rv10 -b:v 800k -c:a ac3 exhibit.rm`. The `-b:v` option sets the video bitrate.
- **FFmpeg, silent:** run `ffmpeg -i display.mp4 -an -c:v rv20 -b:v 800k display.rm` to leave out all sound and use RealVideo 2.0.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **Silent or black playback:** a player needs a decoder for every stream in the file, and the ending does not promise one. Try another player, such as mpv.
- **A cut-off recording:** MP4 stores its packet index in one place, so an interrupted write may leave a file nothing can play.
- **Nothing for an audio editor:** an MP4 with no audio track gives an editor nothing to import.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

ISO/IEC 14496-14, also called MPEG-4 Part 14, defines MP4 and dates from 2003. Apple's QuickTime is the distant ancestor, and the content is arranged as boxes inside boxes, a layout that passed through the ISO Base Media File Format.

An MP4 wraps streams and is not a compression method itself. H.264 video with AAC sound is the everyday payload, yet AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus can be carried too. The extensions are .mp4 or .m4v for video and frequently .m4a when only sound is inside, while the registered media types are video/mp4 and audio/mp4.

Major browsers all play MP4, and Android has handled HEVC video in it since version 5.0. Keep your MP4 as the master copy, because the page writes a new file and leaves the original alone.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- ffplay plays MP4, since the demuxer is included.
- The mpv player runs on the desktop and can switch between audio streams.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Premiere brings in MP4 only when a matching decoder is available.

**Web:**

- Firefox plays MP4 inside a web page, and for AAC and H.264 it may lean on codecs the operating system provides.
- Chrome opens the combinations it supports, so the streams inside the file still decide.

**Mobile:**

- Android owners can install VLC for Android, a free player.
- Local and network media open in VLC for iOS.

### MP4 and SWF compared

- **Origin**: SWF is tied to Macromedia and Adobe Flash and counts as a legacy multimedia format. Adobe acquired Macromedia in 2005.
- **Name**: SWF is also known as Small Web Format, and application/vnd.adobe.flash.movie is among its registered media types.
- **Contents**: SWF can combine vector graphics, animation and bitmap video, while an MP4 simply carries streams.
- **Interactivity**: interactive SWF content uses ActionScript as well as a timeline. A converted video cannot retain those interactions as executable controls.
- **Playback**: after its end-of-life block, Flash Player from Adobe stopped running Flash content. Ruffle emulates Flash in a browser through WebAssembly and has downloads for Windows, Mac and Linux. Lightspark is an incomplete Flash implementation for Windows and Linux.
- **External media**: an SWF may refer to media outside itself instead of holding every resource.
- **Today**: MP4 suits sharing, and SWF suits an old project that insists on it.

FFmpeg decodes the MP4 in your browser tab and writes a new SWF. Frames marked interlaced pass through a deinterlacer, a side longer than 1920 pixels is scaled down, odd dimensions are rounded to even numbers and the rate is capped at 30 frames per second. No codec is named in the command, so FFmpeg's defaults for SWF apply: Sorenson Spark (FLV1) video at FFmpeg's default of 200 kbit/s, and MP3 sound. FFmpeg's documentation says the SWF muxer accepts one audio stream, one video stream, or both.

Test the file in Ruffle before you depend on it, because Ruffle does not implement every Flash API and results can differ from the original Flash behavior.

Files convert one at a time, and each SWF downloads separately. No size limit applies, and the time a long video needs depends on your device. The work stays in the tab, so nothing is uploaded.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to SWF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 clip.swf`. The .swf output extension selects the SWF muxer, and FFmpeg picks the codecs.
- **FFmpeg, video only:** type `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -an silent.swf`. The -an option skips the audio stream, so the SWF has none.
- **FFmpeg, set the frame rate:** use `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -r 15 slower.swf`. As an output option, -r duplicates or drops frames to reach a constant rate.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **Missing decoder**: reading the container is not the same as having a decoder for the video or sound inside.
- **Interrupted write**: packet metadata in an ordinary MP4 stays in one place, so a file cut short can be unplayable.
- **SWF will not play**: Flash Player no longer runs the content, and Ruffle can show graphical or behavioral differences, depending on the ActionScript features a file uses.
- **Missing assets**: an SWF that refers to external media can fail to behave as intended when those resources are absent.
- **Controls missing**: ActionScript interactions are not carried over by a video conversion.

guide.title: Understanding MP4 and TS
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 stores timed media in a structured container. A file can hold different compressed audio and video codecs, so its suffix is not a complete description of playback requirements. It is common in camera exports and video sharing, where a self-contained movie is convenient.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP4 files in a page, though AAC and H.264 can rely on codecs from the system.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere takes MP4 in, provided the decoder for the clip is present.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** to look at the source MP4, ffplay and mpv read it, and mpv can switch between the audio and subtitle streams.
- **Mobile:** both VLC apps, for Android and for iOS, play MP4.

### MP4 and TS compared

TS is the MPEG transport stream, a system format from ISO/IEC 13818-1 that multiplexes separately coded video and sound. It splits them into 188-byte packets, can carry several programs, and does not set a picture codec. Its packets are built so that streams survive transmission errors, and it is used for digital television, HLS streaming segments and camcorder recordings.

This page uses copy mode, so the pictures are never decoded and rebuilt and the source keeps its size and frame rate. A transport stream also does not make a broadcast package. The receiver sets the codecs and profile it accepts, so test the finished .ts in the receiver that needs it.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to TS

- **FFmpeg copy:** `ffmpeg -i recording.mp4 -c copy transport.ts` repackages the streams with no new lossy encode, the same operation this page performs.
- **FFmpeg transcode:** `ffmpeg -i recording.mp4 -c:a aac -c:v libx264 -f mpegts recoded.ts` creates new streams when the receiver needs those codecs. This changes the media instead of merely its wrapper.

### Problems with MP4 files

**The decoder is missing:** an MP4 can be perfectly valid and still contain video or sound that your player has no decoder for.

**There is no audio:** an MP4 with no audio track cannot supply one to an audio editor.

**The file is unfinished:** if the write that created an MP4 was interrupted, the unfinished file can be unplayable.

guide.title: Understanding MP4 and VOB
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

Behind the .mp4 ending is MPEG-4 Part 14, written up as ISO/IEC 14496-14 and published in 2003. Video, audio, subtitles and metadata sit in separate tracks within nested boxes, a layout inherited from Apple's QuickTime and the ISO Base Media File Format. Contents vary: H.264 with AAC is the common pair, and VP9, AV1, MP3 or Opus are allowed as well.

You will have MP4s from phones, cameras, screen recorders and downloads, because every major browser plays them. It is registered as video/mp4 for video and audio/mp4 for audio, and video files use either .mp4 or .m4v. MP4 is used for streaming, for clips from phones and cameras, and for files you share. Container support on its own doesn't guarantee a player can decode what is inside.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- mpv switches between audio and subtitle streams while it plays an MP4.
- ffplay, FFmpeg's own viewer, plays the format.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Premiere imports MP4 files.

**Web:**

- Chrome and Firefox open MP4 directly.

**Mobile:**

- VLC runs on Android phones and tablets and also on iOS, where it handles most movie formats.

### MP4 and VOB compared

- **Extensions**: .mp4 and .vob. VOB stands for DVD Video Object.
- **Structure**: a VOB is closely related to an MPEG-2 program stream. On a disc, video, sound, subtitles and menu content all travel in VOB streams.
- **Codecs**: the MP4 usually holds H.264 and AAC. The output here is MPEG-2 video with MP2 audio at 96 kbps, which is why the conversion means a full re-encode.
- **Companion files**: a DVD also relies on IFO and BUP files, and the VOBs normally sit in a VIDEO_TS folder. One VOB from this page is therefore not a finished disc.
- **Players**: VLC and MPC-HC open VOB files, and Windows Media Player does with codecs installed.
- **File size**: VOB files are limited to 1 GB each.
- **Encryption**: VOBs on commercial discs may be encrypted with CSS. The VOB made here is plain.
- **Subtitles**: DVD subtitles can be bitmap images rather than text, which some players skip even when they decode MPEG-2.
- **Frame rate**: a source faster than 30 fps has frames dropped to fit, keeps its running time; a slower one keeps its own rate.
- **Interlacing**: frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced, one output frame for each; progressive frames pass through.

This is why a lone VOB suits a quick test or an editor that wants MPEG-2, and a disc needs more. FFmpeg, running in your browser, writes the stream in the DVD layout. Frame size and rate follow the MP4 within two ceilings: a 1920-pixel long edge and 30 fps. The page never enlarges a small frame, and sides are rounded down to even numbers. The page does not scale to a DVD standard size and makes no menus, so use FFmpeg's DVD target or a DVD authoring program when a player needs a real disc.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to VOB

- **FFmpeg DVD target (NTSC):** run `ffmpeg -i movie.mp4 -target ntsc-dvd dvd-video.vob`. FFmpeg's documentation says the target sets the format options, such as bitrate, codecs and buffer sizes, for you.
- **FFmpeg DVD target (PAL):** run `ffmpeg -i movie.mp4 -target pal-dvd dvd-video.vob`. FFmpeg accepts the pal-, ntsc- and film- prefixes in front of the target type to pick the corresponding standard.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No picture or no sound**: the container opened, but a decoder for the video or audio inside is missing. Container support alone doesn't promise a decoder, as Adobe's list of supported formats also shows.
- **The file stops or won't open**: a regular MP4 keeps its packet index in one place, so a recording interrupted while being written can be unplayable. Record or download it again.
- **A phone refuses the video**: Android's supported-formats list has HEVC in MP4 beginning with version 5.0. The codec inside decides, not the .mp4 ending.
- **The MP4 is very long**: the converter imposes no size limit or timeout, so a long clip keeps your device busy until it finishes. The picture and the sound are both re-encoded in your browser, so close other heavy tabs if the device struggles.
- **The picture is interlaced**: footage from camcorders and broadcast captures may be flagged as interlaced. The converter deinterlaces those frames, so no extra step is needed.

guide.title: MP4 to WMA: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is formally MPEG-4 Part 14, standardized as ISO/IEC 14496-14: one file can hold video, audio, subtitles and chapters. The usual video and audio inside is H.264 with AAC, though H.265 and AV1 video turn up as well. Phones and cameras record MP4, and it is a common choice for online video, streaming and sharing.

People pull WMA out of an MP4 to get a listening copy for a Windows media library or an older portable player.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay and mpv open an MP4 on the desktop.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports the container when it has the decoder.
- **Web:** Firefox plays MP4 directly, and Chrome plays supported combinations.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android and VLC for iOS both open MP4.

### MP4 and WMA compared

MP4 is a general container for video and audio. Windows Media Audio is a family of audio codecs from Microsoft, stored in the ASF container. The standard version is lossy, with Professional, Lossless and Voice variants, and the .wma ending marks audio-only ASF content without telling you which variant a file uses. The WMA made here is encoded by FFmpeg at 192 kb/s. WMA is used to deliver audio and sometimes for intermediate storage, and its common media type is audio/x-ms-wma.

The sound is decoded and encoded again, so the WMA cannot beat the MP4's audio. Converting to WMA also costs the picture.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to WMA

- **FFmpeg (command line):** enter `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -vn output.wma`. The `-vn` option drops the video.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** install the FFmpeg library and import the MP4. In File > Export Audio, the format to pick is WMA (version2) Files (FFmpeg).

### Problems with MP4 files

- **Nothing to extract**: with no audio in the MP4 there is nothing for an audio editor or this page to take.
- **Sound without a decoder**: a container a player reads successfully still needs a decoder for the sound inside.
- **A cut-off recording**: because packet metadata sits together in a normal MP4, a write interrupted midway may leave a file that will not open.

faqs.answer: FFmpeg runs on a single thread inside your browser, and every frame is decoded and encoded again. A long or large video takes the time your device needs.
