guide.title: About PPM and PNG files
guide.markdown:
### What is a PPM file?

PPM is Netpbm's portable pixmap, a format for color images. Each pixel has three samples, one each for red, green and blue, and the maximum sample value can be anything from 1 to 65535. The normal binary form starts with the signature P6, and the rarer plain-text form starts with P3. A raw PPM can also contain a sequence of images with no separators between them.

The appeal is simplicity: there is almost no metadata and no compression, so a program can write a PPM in a few lines. The price is size, since the files are large next to compressed pictures. IANA has not registered the conventional media type, image/x-portable-pixmap.

### Programs that open PPM files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads and writes PPM color images. Netpbm supplies the libnetpbm reader and tools for PPM processing.

### PPM and PNG compared

- **Compression**: PPM stores samples as they are. PNG compresses them losslessly with DEFLATE, which combines LZ77 with Huffman coding.
- **Metadata**: PPM carries almost none. PNG is built from chunks, and its third edition allows Exif metadata in an eXIf chunk.
- **Transparency**: a PPM stores no alpha channel, while PNG can add an optional one for per-pixel transparency.
- **Support**: PNG shows up in all major browsers and has no known patents that bear royalties.
- **Depth**: PPM sample values can run up to 65535, which is 16 bits. PNG supports 1 to 16 bits per sample.
- **Origin**: PNG was introduced as a patent-free replacement for GIF in the W3C Recommendation of October 1996. It is also described by RFC 2083 and ISO/IEC 15948:2004.
- **Structure**: PNG files open with a fixed signature, then chunks: IHDR (header), IDAT (pixels) and IEND (the end).
- **Image types**: PNG supports indexed, grayscale and truecolor images, so a PPM's red, green and blue samples fit its truecolor kind.
- **Edition**: the PNG specification's third edition was made a W3C Recommendation on 24 June 2025. Animated PNG is covered, and software unable to animate falls back to the default still image.
- **Everyday use**: macOS saves screenshots as PNG files by default, so PNG is a format most people already handle.
- **Newer features**: HDR support arrives in the third edition through the cICP chunk, and image/png is the registered media type, with image/apng for animated files.
- **Media types**: image/png for PNG; PPM's image/x-portable-pixmap is conventional only.

What this page does is read the PPM with ImageMagick, compiled to WebAssembly and running on your device, and write a PNG. It reads one picture per file and sets no compression or color options of its own. The page rejects a picture beyond roughly 537 megapixels. The sample depth of the output is not something you choose on this page. The download keeps the original's name with a .png ending, and the source file stays untouched.

### Other ways to convert PPM to PNG

- **Netpbm pnmtopng (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `pnmtopng render.ppm > render.png`. It is the format's own toolset. Netpbm's documentation says it scales the maxval automatically to 255 or 65535, so check technical images.
- **ImageMagick (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `magick render.ppm delivered.png`. ImageMagick's formats page lists PPM as readable and writable, and PNG as well.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the PPM, then choose File > Export As (Shift+Ctrl+E) and export it as a PNG. GIMP's PNM plug-in loads pnm, ppm, pgm, pbm, pfm and pam files.

The page uses ImageMagick, so the second method is the closest to what it does.

### Problems with PPM files

- **The file is huge**: PPM uses a redundant representation with little image metadata, so files are bulky next to compressed distribution formats.
- **A program reads only some PPM files**: some readers implement only one eight-bit image. Normalize complex input with pnmtopnm and reduce sample depth with pamdepth when necessary.
- **Colors look wrong**: a file labeled PPM now and then holds sRGB or linear values rather than the transfer function the format specifies. pnmgamma can reconcile the variants.
- **Only one picture comes out**: a raw PPM can contain a sequence of images without separators, but the page writes a single PNG per file. Split the sequence first if you need every picture.
- **The sample values run high**: a PPM's maximum sample value may be anywhere from 1 to 65535, so it can hold more than eight bits per sample.

guide.title: Understanding PPT and JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is a PPT file?

PPT is the binary presentation format used by PowerPoint 97 through Office 2003. It differs from the later XML-based PPTX. A presentation holds slides with text, graphics, transitions and animations, plus notes, handouts and comments.

### Programs that open PPT files

- **Web:** in a browser, PowerPoint for the web shows a PPT and needs a .pptx copy for editing, and Google Slides imports Microsoft PowerPoint files.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** for re-saving a PPT as PPTX, LibreOffice Impress opens .ppt and .pps from File > Open, and Apache OpenOffice Impress imports PPT and can save back in PowerPoint format.
- **Windows and Mac:** PowerPoint itself reads legacy 97-2003 presentations, though newer features may need PPTX.

### PPT and JPEG compared

A presentation keeps separate objects, notes and playback instructions. JPEG is a flat lossy image with no editable text, transitions or animation states.

The slide renderer on this site serves PPTX files: it draws each visible slide as SVG in a worker and saves a JPEG at 2x the slide's dimensions in points. Nothing sends a .ppt file there. To get a PPTX from a PPT, open the older file in PowerPoint or Impress and save a copy in the newer format.

Keep the presentation for editing, notes and media.

### Other ways to convert PPT to JPEG

- **PowerPoint on Windows:** select the slide, choose File > Save As, pick JPEG File Interchange Format as the type, click Save, and choose Just This One.
- **PowerPoint on Mac:** open the slide, use File > Export, choose JPEG, select Save Current Slide Only, set the width and height if you like, then Export.
- **Impress plus ImageMagick:** open the PPT in Impress and use File > Export as > Export as PDF. Then run `magick -density 150 slides.pdf slide.jpeg`, which writes one JPEG per PDF page. ImageMagick needs Ghostscript to read PDF.

### Problems with PPT files

**Features are lost:** saving newer presentation features into PPT can drop functions that the old format cannot store.

**The web editor wants PPTX:** PowerPoint for the web reads .ppt but requires a .pptx copy for editing.

**Office blocks the file:** an internet download may be blocked by Office security, which then says it cannot open the file.

guide.title: About PPT files
guide.markdown:
### What is a PPT file?

A PPT is a PowerPoint presentation in the binary format used from PowerPoint 97 through Office 2003. Newer versions of PowerPoint save .pptx instead, a different XML-based format, and PPT cannot hold every feature added since PowerPoint 2007. Inside, a deck is a stack of slides carrying text, graphics, transitions and animations, with notes, handouts and comments kept beside them. That is a lot more than a picture can hold, which is why exporting is a rendering job.

Its media type is application/vnd.ms-powerpoint. Saving newer presentation features into PPT can lose functionality that the older format cannot store.

This page cannot convert it. The page has only your browser's picture decoder and no presentation renderer, so a PPT ends in an error and nothing to download. The programs below can export the slides. Saving a .pptx copy first lets you use the [PPTX to PNG converter](/pptx-to-png/).

### Programs that open PPT files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- LibreOffice Impress opens .ppt and .pps through its File > Open command.
- Apache OpenOffice Impress imports legacy PPT presentations and can save in PowerPoint format.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Microsoft PowerPoint opens PowerPoint 97-2003 presentations; newer features may need PPTX.

**Mac:**

- Keynote opens PowerPoint presentations, .ppt included.

**Web:**

- PowerPoint for the web reads PPT, but you must save a copy as PPTX to edit it.
- Google Slides imports PowerPoint presentations into its browser editor.

### PPT and PNG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .ppt is application/vnd.ms-powerpoint. .png is image/png.
- **What they hold**: a PPT is a document of slides, notes and effects. A PNG is one still picture, so each exported slide is its own file.
- **Compression**: a PNG is always lossless, and DEFLATE, which is LZ77 plus Huffman coding, does the packing.
- **What is lost**: transitions, animations, notes and comments have no place in a picture, and text can no longer be edited.

The step that matters is the program that renders the PPT, since this page has none for the old binary format.

### Other ways to convert PPT to PNG

- **Microsoft PowerPoint (Windows, Mac):** on Windows, select the slide, open File > Save As, or Save a Copy when the file lives on OneDrive or SharePoint, pick PNG Portable Network Graphics Format as the type (the list also offers JPEG, GIF and SVG) and save; Microsoft says a slide saved this way is a picture you can use in other applications. Choose Just This One for the selected slide or All Slides for a separate image of each. On Mac, switch to Normal view, open the slide, choose File > Export, set the file format to PNG, select Save Current Slide Only, optionally enter a Width and Height, and click Export. The Mac steps cover the current slide only, and the Mac Export dialog also offers JPEG, TIFF and BMP; a message box then tells you where the image was saved.
- **LibreOffice Impress (Windows, Mac, Linux):** choose File > Open and select the PPT, then File > Export, pick PNG as the file type and click Save. PNG offers extra export options after you click Save.
- **Keynote (Mac):** open the PPT, choose File > Export To > Images, choose which slides to export and then an image format. Apple's page notes that a higher-quality image makes a larger file. Keynote remembers the slide range you set and applies it the next time you export that presentation.

### Problems with PPT files

- **The page shows an error**: the page has no way to read a PPT. Use PowerPoint, Impress or Keynote to export the slides.
- **Renaming to .pptx fails**: the extension does not change the contents. A real PPTX has to be saved by a program that opens the PPT.
- **The file will not open on Windows**: a deck downloaded from the internet may be blocked by Office security and report that it cannot be opened. Unblock it under Properties in File Explorer.
- **Newer features are missing**: saving into PPT lost anything the old format cannot store. Ask for the PPTX if one exists.
- **PowerPoint for the web will not let you edit it**: it reads .ppt but needs a .pptx copy for editing.
- **Only one slide needed**: pick Just This One in PowerPoint on Windows, or Save Current Slide Only on Mac.

### What is a PPTX file?

PPTX is a packaged PresentationML document. Its parts describe slides, relationships, themes and extras such as notes. A slide can combine editable text, diagrams, photographs and drawing objects instead of one finished picture.

JPEG suits a slide that must become a still image for a web page, a review sheet or a message. The export captures how the slide looks and drops the editable objects.

### Programs that open PPTX files

- **Windows:** PowerPoint opens and saves PPTX and can save slides as images, and LibreOffice Impress includes a PowerPoint XML filter.
- **Mac:** Apple Keynote, PowerPoint and LibreOffice Impress all open PPTX on a Mac.
- **Linux:** LibreOffice Impress and ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors open PPTX.
- **Web:** the web version of PowerPoint supports PPTX presentations.
- **Mobile:** Keynote for iPhone and the mobile PowerPoint app open PPTX.

### PPTX and JPEG compared

The page draws each slide with pptx-glimpse in your browser, at twice the slide's size in points, so a widescreen slide comes out at 1920 by 1080 pixels. Slides are saved as separate JPEG files named slide1, slide2 and so on, numbered as PowerPoint numbers them, hidden slides counted. Hidden slides, speaker notes and comments are left out.

Text is drawn with your device's fonts, so a font you lack falls back to another and lines can wrap differently. Elements the converter can't draw are left out, and the page tells you how many. At most 100 slides are saved. A package that inflates past 512 MB is refused, and drawing stops after 90 seconds. An older .ppt file or a password-protected deck must be saved as an unprotected .pptx first.

### Other ways to convert PPTX to JPEG

- **PowerPoint:** on Windows, open the deck, go to File > Save As, set the type to JPEG File Interchange Format and answer All Slides or Just This One when asked.
- **LibreOffice:** run `soffice --convert-to jpg deck.pptx`, and add `--outdir` with a folder name to choose where the JPEG goes.

### Problems with PPTX files

- **Text wraps differently**: install the deck's fonts, or export from PowerPoint.
- **A slide is missing**: it was hidden, or the deck has more slides than the page saves.
- **A video area is empty**: videos aren't played, so put a still frame on the slide before converting.
- **The page refuses the file**: save an older .ppt or protected deck as an unprotected .pptx.

guide.markdown:
### What is a PPTX file?

PPTX is PowerPoint's ordinary presentation document type. Since PowerPoint 2007 it has been a ZIP package of XML parts, standardized as Office Open XML (ECMA-376, ISO/IEC 29500), and PresentationML is the part of the standard that stores the slides. Each slide and its relationships occupy parts of their own, and notes and slide masters have XML parts too. Macro-enabled decks use .pptm instead.

Slide decks, training material and sales presentations are the usual PPTX files. A deck can also carry embedded media and charts, along with speaker notes and animations.

### Programs that open PPTX files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - LibreOffice Impress has a PowerPoint 2007-365 XML filter for import and export.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - Microsoft PowerPoint opens and saves PPTX, its native presentation type.
- **Mac and iPhone:**
  - Keynote opens a PowerPoint presentation dragged onto its icon on a Mac, and on an iPhone it opens .pptx and .ppt documents.
- **Linux:**
  - ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors is a desktop editor for Linux that opens PPTX.
- **Web:**
  - PowerPoint for the web supports PPTX presentations.
- **Mobile:**
  - The mobile PowerPoint app opens PPTX presentations.

### PPTX and JPG compared

- **Names and types**: .pptx with application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation; .jpg or .jpeg for the image.
- **Contents**: a PPTX is a package of slides, masters, notes and relationships. A JPG is one picture.
- **Compression**: JPG is lossy, a format designed for photographs, with adjustable quality.
- **Alpha and layers**: JPG has no alpha channel and cannot store layers.
- **Editing**: saving a slide as an image turns its objects into one flattened picture, so the text is no longer editable.

The page draws each slide as SVG with a renderer that runs in your browser, then encodes the picture as a JPG at double the slide's dimensions in points. Lettering is set in the fonts the slide names, with metric-compatible fallbacks, and uses fonts installed on your device. The page leaves out hidden slides, speaker notes and comments. Video, and a picture the slide only links to, are not drawn either, and the page counts what was left out. The renderer numbers slides from its own list, so a hidden slide is never drawn in place of a visible one.

A JPG is a single flat picture, so the conversion turns a slide into what it looks like on the screen and nothing else. Text that was editable is now pixels, and notes are left behind. Keep the PPTX as your source if you still need to edit the deck.

### Other ways to convert PPTX to JPG

- **PowerPoint for Windows:** Select a slide, then use File > Save As (Save a Copy if the presentation is on OneDrive or SharePoint), type a file name, open the Save as Type list and choose JPEG, then press Save. Pick Just This One to save the selected slide, or All Slides for the whole deck, in which case Microsoft's help page says every slide becomes its own file.
- **PowerPoint for Mac:** Open the slide in Normal view, choose File > Export, pick JPEG as the image format, choose Save Current Slide Only and optionally set the width and height, then click Export.
- **Keynote for Mac:** Keynote opens PowerPoint files with a .pptx or .ppt ending. Choose File > Export To > Images, choose the slides you want, select an image format and click Save, then choose a location from the Where menu and click Export. Higher image quality produces a larger file. If the deck uses fonts you do not have installed, Keynote shows a missing font notification so you can choose replacements.

### Problems with PPTX files

- **Fonts or line breaks differ**: a font that is not installed can change how a deck looks, which is why PowerPoint offers to embed eligible fonts. This page draws slides with the fonts on your device and fallbacks.
- **An old .ppt or protected file is refused**: only an unprotected .pptx works here.
- **Video or linked pictures are missing**: neither is drawn, so they are left out of the JPG.
- **Hidden slides do not appear**: slides marked hidden are skipped, but their numbers still count in the file names.
- **A long deck stops partway**: the drawing is stopped after 90 seconds.
- **Features disappear in an older format**: saving as an older presentation format can affect features that format does not have.

guide.title: About PPTX files
guide.markdown:
### What is a PPTX file?

A PPTX is the standard PowerPoint presentation file. It stores presentation content as PresentationML in an Office Open XML package, with individual slides and their relationships in separate package parts. Notes and slide masters have their own XML parts. Its media type is application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation, and macro-enabled presentations use .pptm instead.

A slide's appearance is assembled from layouts, themes, text, pictures and charts, so it isn't one picture. A deck can also carry notes, transitions, audio and video. Turning it into PNG images captures how each slide looks and leaves behind everything that behaves: the animations, the notes and the editable chart data.

That suits a picture for a document, a review thread or a web page. The recipient can't edit the text or replay a timed reveal from a PNG, so keep the deck for that.

A PNG per slide also keeps the layout fixed. Every recipient sees the same slide whatever fonts or PowerPoint version they have, which is why decks are often shared this way for reviews, handouts and web posts.

### Programs that open PPTX files

- **Windows and Mac:** Microsoft PowerPoint opens and saves PPTX natively.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** LibreOffice Impress reads PowerPoint 2007 to 365 files through an XML filter.
- **Mac:** Keynote opens a presentation dragged onto the Keynote icon.
- **Linux:** ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors opens PPTX in a desktop editor.
- **Web:** PowerPoint for the web supports PPTX presentations.
- **Mobile:** Phones open PPTX in the Microsoft mobile app. Keynote for iPhone opens .pptx and .ppt documents.

Missing fonts can change how a presentation displays, and PowerPoint can embed eligible fonts to prevent that.

### PPTX and PNG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .pptx, the Office Open XML presentation type; .png, image/png.
- **Content**: a PPTX holds slide objects and relationships. A PNG holds one flat picture of a slide.
- **Compression**: PNG is lossless, so the slide picture is exact at its pixel size.
- **Transparency**: PNG supports alpha transparency.
- **Editing**: a slide title becomes pixels, not a text box, and a chart becomes a picture.

This page draws each visible slide as SVG inside your browser using the pptx-glimpse library, then saves it as a PNG at twice the slide's size in points. No side of the picture goes beyond 4096 pixels. The files are named like name_slide3, using the slide's own number. A hidden slide keeps its number, so the sequence can skip one.

Hidden slides, speaker notes and comments stay out of the images. So do video and pictures a slide only links to, and the page reports how many items it skipped. The cap is 100 slides, the whole job is cut off at 90 seconds, and a package whose parts declare more than 512 MB inflated isn't read. Text uses the slide's own fonts through your device, with metric-compatible fallbacks, and text with no font gets the theme's body font.

The pixel size follows the slide size, so a deck set to a larger slide size gives larger PNGs, up to the 4096-pixel ceiling. A PNG has fixed pixels, so you can't enlarge one afterward without losing sharpness; set the size in the deck before converting.

### Other ways to convert PPTX to PNG

- **PowerPoint for Mac:** choose File > Export, set File Format to PNG, pick Save Every Slide or Save Current Slide Only, set the image size and export.
- **LibreOffice Impress:** open the deck, which Impress reads through its PowerPoint XML filter, then choose File > Export and select PNG as the file type. LibreOffice lets you set PNG compression and interlacing.
- **Keynote for Mac:** open the deck in Keynote by dragging it onto the Keynote icon, then choose File > Export To > Images. Select the slides, pick an image format and click Export.

### Problems with PPTX files

- **"Save it as an unprotected .pptx"**: the file is an old .ppt or has a password. Save a copy in PowerPoint without the password.
- **Missing logos**: a picture linked instead of embedded isn't drawn. Embed it in PowerPoint and convert again.
- **Fewer images than slides**: hidden slides are skipped, and only 100 slides become images. The page reports the count.
- **A font looks different**: install the font on this device or embed it in the deck.
- **The conversion stops early**: a very long or image-heavy deck can pass the 90-second limit. Split the deck into two files and convert each.
- **Notes or animations missing**: a PNG can't hold them. Export them from PowerPoint another way.

### What is a PSD file?

Adobe Photoshop saves its working documents as PSD. Inside are the layers, masks, adjustment layers and text that let a designer reopen and keep editing, in RGB or CMYK. Designers lean on it for mockups and retouching, and Adobe owns the specification.

Every file starts with the signature 8BPS, then come blocks for image resources, layer and mask data, and the merged image. Each side can be 30,000 pixels at most; PSB lifts that ceiling. Its registered media type is image/vnd.adobe.photoshop.

### Programs that open PSD files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick can read PSD, and so can GIMP. XnView MP also handles PSD, though business use needs a paid license.

### What is a PSD file?

Adobe Photoshop projects are stored as PSD files. Where a JPG stores a finished picture, a PSD stores the work behind it: layers, masks, adjustment layers, type and color data, so a design can be reopened and changed later. A designer can return to one headline or one retouching layer without rebuilding the image.

The data begins with the signature 8BPS, then a header, then separate sections for image resources, layers and masks, and pixels. Pixel data may be left uncompressed or packed with RLE or ZIP. A PSD tops out at 30,000 pixels on a side, and the related PSB format lifts that limit. Its registered media type is image/vnd.adobe.photoshop.

You meet PSD files when a designer, photographer or retoucher hands over a project. The PSD is the master; the JPG is the copy you place in a listing, send for approval or upload to a form that does not take PSD.

### Programs that open PSD files

- **Linux, Mac and Windows:** Command-line users can run ImageMagick, whose format list notes PSD support for alpha blending, adjustment layers and opacity masks. XnView MP lists PSD among the formats it opens, and company use needs a license. Adobe Photoshop and GIMP open PSD files too.
- **Mac:** Preview opens PSD files for a quick look.
- **Web:** Photopea works in the browser and uses PSD as its main document format; choose File > Open.

### PSD and JPG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .psd and image/vnd.adobe.photoshop; .jpg or .jpeg and image/jpeg.
- **Layers**: a PSD keeps layers and masks. A JPG cannot store layers.
- **Compression**: PSD pixel data is raw, RLE or ZIP. JPEG compression is lossy.
- **Transparency**: JPG carries no alpha channel, so see-through areas cannot be kept.
- **Bit depth**: a PSD can hold 1, 8, 16 or 32 bits per channel, and a JPG stores 8.
- **Quality**: programs usually offer a 0 to 100 slider for JPEG, but one program's 80 need not match another's.

The name JPEG is taken from the Joint Photographic Experts Group; ISO/IEC 10918-1 (1994) is its main standard. Most digital cameras and scanners write it directly, and all the major browsers can show it. A progressive mode exists too: a rough version shows up first, then refines while the rest downloads.

The result is one flat picture of the PSD, saved as a JPG. Individual layers are not written out, and the JPG cannot hand back editable text or masks. Use it as the copy you send for a listing, an email or an approval, and hold on to the PSD for changes. Your PSD itself is never altered, because the page gives you a separate new file named after it. Choose several PSDs together and they run one after another, each JPG is saved by itself.

### Other ways to convert PSD to JPG

- **GIMP:** load the PSD, then choose File > Export As. In GIMP's JPEG export dialog the Quality field runs from 0 to 100, and Advanced Options holds a progressive setting.
- **Photopea (web):** Photopea turns whatever you open into a PSD-based document, so open the file with File > Open, then use File > Export As > JPG. The result is a flat image, so look over text and effects before you send it on.
- **ImageMagick (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `magick input.psd output.jpg`. In a test with a two-layer PSD, this wrote one numbered JPG per layer, output-0.jpg and output-1.jpg, so check what came out.

### Problems with PSD files

- **The JPG looks different from Photoshop**: other programs have to interpret Photoshop-specific data, and opening a preview does not prove every feature was read the same way. Use the original PSD in Photoshop when an effect must match exactly.
- **The file is too large**: a document beyond the 30,000-pixel limit has to be saved as PSB. This page refuses anything past roughly 537 megapixels.
- **See-through areas are not in the JPG**: a JPG has no alpha channel. Use PNG when you need to keep transparency.
- **The JPG looks soft or blotchy**: the format throws detail away, and this page gives you no quality control. Export from GIMP when you need to choose the quality yourself.
- **Layers are missing from the result**: a flat image export does not keep layer and mask information. Go back to the PSD for any layer-level work.

### What is a PSD file?

A PSD is Adobe Photoshop's native document format. It stores an image together with what is needed to keep editing it: layers, masks, adjustment layers, text and color information. It is used for layered image editing, design mockups and photo retouching.

A PSD has five sections: a file header, color mode data, image resources, layer and mask information, and image data. The 8BPS signature starts every PSD, followed by a header that stores the version (1 for PSD, 2 for PSB), a channel count from 1 to 56 that includes alpha channels, a bit depth of 1, 8, 16 or 32 and one of eight color modes: bitmap, grayscale, indexed, RGB, CMYK, multichannel, duotone or Lab. Pixels are saved either raw or compressed with RLE or ZIP, and every value in the file is big-endian. PSD dimensions are limited to 30,000 pixels per side, and PSB, the Large Document Format, raises that to 300,000. The registered media type is image/vnd.adobe.photoshop.

Image resources hold non-pixel data such as pen tool paths, resolution information and an ICC profile, each in a block that starts with the signature 8BIM. The layer and mask section describes every layer's bounds, channels, blend mode, opacity and mask. The last section holds the merged, composite image, the flattened result of all layers.

### Programs that open PSD files

- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Photoshop is the native editor.
- **Windows and Mac:** Affinity Photo opens PSD files.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP opens PSD files for editing.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** From the command line, ImageMagick reads PSD images.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** XnView MP counts PSD among the formats it supports, but a company must buy a license to use it.
- **Mac:** Preview opens a PSD.
- **Web:** Photopea treats PSD as its native document format, and File > Open loads a file.

### PSD and PDF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .psd is image/vnd.adobe.photoshop. .pdf is application/pdf.
- **Purpose**: a PSD is a working file with editable layers. PDF packages a document from any application so it looks and prints the same on every system; its imaging model is taken from PostScript and is independent of device and resolution.
- **Origins**: PDF was created at Adobe. Camelot, John Warnock's 1991 project, turned into PDF by 1992.
- **Fonts**: to look the same everywhere, a PDF needs its fonts embedded. The PDF made here holds one picture, so it has no live text.
- **Contents**: a PDF can mix text, vector graphics and raster images, with links, bookmarks, form fields, annotations and media. A PDF may store its images with lossless compression like Flate, or with JPEG compression.
- **Standards**: PDF 1.7 became the ISO 32000-1 standard in 2008, and PDF 2.0 became ISO 32000-2 in 2017. Specialized subsets exist, such as PDF/A for archiving, PDF/X for printing and PDF/UA for accessibility.

This conversion makes a picture-only PDF. ImageMagick reads the PSD as one image, writes a PNG, and the PNG is embedded in a one-page PDF with no margin. One pixel becomes one PDF point, so the page takes the size of the image rather than A4 or Letter. The PDF comes from the layered PSD as a single picture rather than one item per layer. The PNG is embedded losslessly, with no JPEG compression added. Several PSD files give several separate PDFs, never one merged document.

### Other ways to convert PSD to PDF

- **ImageMagick (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `magick input.psd output.pdf`. ImageMagick lists both PSD, described as an Adobe Photoshop multispectral bitmap file, and PDF, the Portable Document Format, as formats it can read and write.
- **Photopea (web):** load the PSD through File > Open, choose File > Export As, pick PDF and save the file.

### Problems with PSD files

- **A document larger than the PSD limit**: it needs PSB or another suitable format.
- **Layers and masks are gone in a flat export**: a PSD includes layer and mask information that a simple flattened image export does not retain. Keep the PSD for editing.
- **The PSD opens, but looks different**: third-party readers must interpret Photoshop-specific data structures, so opening a preview does not establish full editing compatibility. Compare the result with the picture in Photoshop before you send it on.

Photoshop saves its work as PSD, and the format exists so a design stays editable: layers, masks, channels and other editing information stay together instead of being merged into one finished picture. Every PSD starts with the signature 8BPS in its header, which supports sample depths of 1, 8, 16 or 32 bits. Image resources and layer and mask information occupy separate sections, and the pixel data can be stored raw or compressed with RLE or ZIP. The registered media type is image/vnd.adobe.photoshop.

A PSD is limited to 30,000 pixels a side. A larger document uses PSB, which raises that limit. You meet PSD files as the source of a design, with layers, masks, adjustment layers and text that a designer can still change. Clients often receive the PSD when they only needed the picture, and a PNG is the lighter thing to open, share and upload.

### Programs that open PSD files

**Mac**

- Preview: opens PSD files.

**Web**

- Photopea: uses PSD as its main document format and opens files through File > Open.

An application that opens the extension doesn't promise to reproduce every Photoshop feature. Other programs have to interpret data structures specific to Photoshop, so compare masks, type and effects with the original before relying on one.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- ImageMagick: reads PSD images from the command line and writes PNG.
- XnView MP: lists PSD among its supported formats. Company use needs a license.
- GIMP: imports PSD for editing.

### PSD and PNG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .psd uses image/vnd.adobe.photoshop. .png uses image/png.
- **Layers**: a PSD holds layers and masks. The converter writes one picture into the PNG.
- **Compression**: a PSD stores pixels raw or with RLE or ZIP. A PNG always uses lossless DEFLATE, which is LZ77 plus Huffman coding.
- **Color depth**: a PSD allows 1, 8, 16 or 32 bits a sample. A PNG allows 1 to 16 bits a sample and an optional alpha channel for per-pixel transparency.
- **Who reads it**: every major browser displays PNG. PSD needs an editor or a viewer that knows Photoshop's structures.

PNG began as a patent-free successor to GIF. In October 1996 the W3C published it, the first format to get Recommendation status, and ISO later adopted it as ISO/IEC 15948:2004. A PNG begins with a set signature and then holds chunks: IHDR carries the header, IDAT holds the pixels, and IEND closes the file. The third edition of the specification became a W3C Recommendation on 24 June 2025. What this conversion changes is the structure: the layer stack stays behind, and one picture goes into the PNG. Because PNG compression is lossless, the PNG holds that picture as it was read.

### Other ways to convert PSD to PNG

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the PSD, then choose File > Export As (Shift+Ctrl+E) to save a copy outside the XCF format, and pick PNG. A PNG Export dialog then offers pixel format, compression level, interlacing and background-color options. Look at the imported picture first, since GIMP's reading of Photoshop features may differ.
- **Photopea (web):** open the PSD with File > Open, then choose File > Export As > PNG.

- **Only one picture arrives**: a single image is read out of the PSD. Use Photoshop or GIMP to export separate layers or artboards.

- **A viewer says it can't open the PSD**: many programs list PSD but read only part of it. Try GIMP or Photopea, or convert it here and open the PNG.

guide.title: About PSD files
guide.markdown:
### What is a PSD file?

PSD is the document format Photoshop uses to save its work. Unlike a flattened export, a PSD can hold layers, masks, adjustment layers, text and color data. Adobe's specification describes separate sections for the header, image resources, layer and mask information, and the final image data. The header begins with the signature 8BPS.

Depth per color channel in a PSD runs 1, 8, 16 or 32 bits, and one side can reach 30,000 pixels. PSB raises that limit. Pixels may be stored uncompressed or squeezed with RLE or ZIP.

This matters for PSD to SVG because a design that contains a logo isn't necessarily a vector logo. The outline in a PSD may be painted pixels, shape paths or both, and changing the file label doesn't recover paths that were never there. A PSD is mostly pixel data, and that is what the page turns into an SVG.

People search for PSD to SVG for several reasons: to put a design on a web page, to hand a logo to someone who asked for an SVG, or to feed a cutting machine. Only the first of those works with an embedded picture. For the others you need paths, which means redrawing the artwork or tracing it in a vector editor.

### Programs that open PSD files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads PSD images; `magick identify -list format` prints every format your install reads.
- **Mac, Windows and Linux:** XnView MP can open PSD, and company use requires a license.
- **Web:** Photopea works in PSD natively and loads files via File > Open.

Adobe Photoshop is the native editor. A preview in another program doesn't prove full editing compatibility.

### PSD and SVG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .psd for the source, .svg for the output.
- **Content**: a PSD holds layers, masks and pixels. An SVG describes shapes, text and effects in XML, and can embed pictures.
- **Scaling**: vector shapes in an SVG scale cleanly. An embedded picture keeps its pixels.
- **Layers**: PSD keeps them. This page reads one picture.
- **Fonts**: SVG text depends on the fonts available, but this output contains no live text.

On this page ImageMagick reads the PSD inside your browser. SVG isn't a format it writes directly, so the page writes a PNG and places it in an SVG file. The SVG's width and height are the picture's size in pixels, and the PNG sits inside it as base64 data. Nothing is traced. The result opens anywhere an SVG does, yet it behaves like an image, not like artwork you can reshape.

The page reads one picture from the PSD. A layered file gives you one picture, not an object per layer. It sets no quality value, and a picture of more than about 537 megapixels is refused because it is too big for the converter.

If you wanted to scale the picture, edit paths or send it to a cutting machine, an SVG made this way won't do that. If you only need the picture in an SVG-shaped file, it will.

The file carries the picture as base64 text, so it is larger than the PNG inside it. If the destination accepts PNG, the [PSD to PNG converter](/psd-to-png/) on this site gives the picture without the SVG wrapper.

### Other ways to convert PSD to SVG

- **Photopea (in a browser):** open the PSD through the Open dialog, then choose File > Export As and pick SVG. Photopea lists SVG among the formats it exports, next to PNG, JPG and PDF. It is a separate program, so the SVG it writes isn't the same file this page makes.

### Problems with PSD files

- **The edges look jagged when enlarged**: the SVG holds pixels. Redraw or trace the artwork in a vector editor if you need clean curves.
- **The layers are gone**: only one picture is read. Keep the PSD as the editable source.
- **The text can't be edited**: it is part of the picture.
- **The file is refused as too large**: that happens beyond about 537 megapixels. Shrink the picture in Photoshop first.
- **The SVG is larger than expected**: the PNG is stored inside it as base64 text, which takes more room than the PNG alone. Use the PSD to PNG converter if size matters.

guide.title: About PSD files
guide.markdown:
### What is a PSD file?

Adobe Photoshop saves its documents as PSD. The file starts with the 8BPS signature, and separate sections store the image resources and the layer and mask information. Sample depth can be 1, 8, 16 or 32 bits, and pixel data may be raw, RLE-coded or ZIP-compressed. Each side can reach 30,000 pixels, and the PSB variant lifts that cap.

### Programs that open PSD files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Open PSD in ImageMagick.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** XnView MP lists PSD among its formats, and a company needs a license.
- **Web:** Photopea, a web editor, treats PSD as its main document format and loads files via File > Open.

### PSD and WebP compared

- **Extensions**: .psd and .webp.
- **Layers**: layers and masks live in the PSD only; a flattened export loses them, and the WebP made here is a single picture.
- **Format**: WebP wraps VP8-based lossy data, or its own lossless method, in a RIFF container, and it can carry transparency, animation, color profiles and metadata.
- **Size**: a WebP is at most 16383 by 16383 pixels.

ImageMagick reads a single image from the PSD here and the WebP is written from it. No quality value is passed and a layer can't be chosen. Pictures past about 537 megapixels get a 'too large to convert here' refusal.

### Other ways to convert PSD to WebP

- **ImageMagick:** `magick campaign.psd campaign.webp`. ImageMagick's format list shows both PSD and WebP as readable and writable.
- **GIMP:** load the PSD, pick File > Export As and save it as WebP. Settings in its WebP dialog include Lossless, Image quality, Alpha quality and Save animation, plus metadata options; keep Save animation off for a still picture.

### Problems with PSD files

- **Layers and masks vanish**: a flat export doesn't retain them. Keep the PSD for editing.
- **A canvas past the limit**: a document over 30,000 pixels a side needs PSB, not PSD.

guide.title: About QT and MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is a QT file?

A .qt file is a QuickTime movie. Apple introduced the format in 1991, and a Windows version followed in 1994; it is the same format as ordinary MOV files, which use the .mov ending. The registered media type is video/quicktime. Inside, QuickTime is organized as atoms, and software that meets an unknown atom can skip over it.

Motion JPEG, ProRes and H.264 are all possible for the pictures, with AAC or uncompressed PCM for the sound. That variety is why the ending alone tells you little: a movie can use a codec the destination editor lacks. Screen recordings made on a Mac are written as MOV files. Browsers support MOV only to a limited degree, and Apple now generally uses MP4 itself, so that is the common reason to convert.

### Programs that open QT files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay, the player that ships with FFmpeg, plays QuickTime files through FFmpeg's MOV demuxer from the command line. mpv is a desktop player where you can also choose among the audio and subtitle streams during playback.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports this container when the necessary decoder is available.
- **Mobile:** on a phone, VLC for Android is a free player whose decoding follows from what the container holds, and VLC for iOS is an iPhone and iPad player covering most movie formats, from local or network sources.

### QT and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .qt or .mov with video/quicktime; .mp4 or .m4v with video/mp4.
- **Lineage**: MPEG-4's file format grew out of QuickTime, but MOV and MP4 are different formats and cannot stand in for each other. The MP4 file format is MPEG-4 Part 14, from 2003.
- **Structure**: MP4 is made of nested boxes, which is QuickTime's idea of atoms under another name.
- **Codecs**: H.264 with AAC is typical in an MP4, and AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus can live there too.
- **Reach**: every major browser plays MP4, whereas browser support for MOV is limited.

Wrapper and codecs both change. After decoding, FFmpeg encodes H.264 (ultrafast preset, CRF 32) and AAC at 96 kbps, and the MP4's index is placed up front. The picture is shrunk when its longer side tops 1920 pixels, 30 fps is the ceiling for frame rate, and both sides come out even. The deinterlacing filter is applied to frames the file marks as interlaced. Audio is always encoded again as AAC, even if the movie already used it. The page offers no quality or trim controls, and files are converted one after another; every MP4 is its own download and nothing is zipped.

### Other ways to convert QT to MP4

- **FFmpeg, full re-encode (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `ffmpeg -i legacy.qt -c:a aac -c:v libx264 quicktime-delivery.mp4`. It decodes and encodes again, so the source codecs must first be decodable.
- **FFmpeg, stream copy (Windows, Mac, Linux):** the command is `ffmpeg -i legacy.qt -c copy quicktime-remux.mp4`. It puts the streams into an MP4 untouched, which works only with streams the MP4 muxer can carry.
- **FFmpeg, first seconds only (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `ffmpeg -t 10 -i legacy.qt -c:v libx264 -c:a aac first-ten.mp4`. The `-t` option, given before `-i`, restricts how much input is read; this page has no trim control of its own.

A stream copy does not re-encode, so it keeps the original codecs. Re-encoding is the choice when the receiving program needs H.264 and AAC.

### Problems with QT files

- **An editor rejects the file**: a QuickTime container can use codecs that the destination editor does not have. Check the codec, because the ending settles nothing.
- **A renamed file fails**: altering the filename ending neither transcodes the video nor supplies the decoder it needs.
- **The file is damaged after an interrupted write**: regular MOV files may be unusable after an interrupted write, and fragmented output has a different recovery behavior. Copy or record the file again.
- **Combing on moving edges**: only frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced here, so footage that is interlaced but unflagged keeps its combing.
- **Frame size is smaller than expected**: a source whose longer side exceeds 1920 pixels is shrunk to fit. Keep the QT if you need the full size.

guide.title: RA to MP3: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is an RA file?

RealAudio is an audio format from RealNetworks, introduced in 1995 for streaming over the internet, and it carried online sound delivery from the mid-1990s onward. The .ra ending can identify audio delivered through RealMedia. The format is proprietary, with limited public technical documentation. The family spans several coding systems, so the extension alone doesn't tell you which codec a file uses. A RealAudio file can hold descriptive information such as a title or artist.

### Programs that open RA files

- **Windows:** RealPlayer, the free PC player, lists RA and RealAudio Lossless among its supported audio types.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg reads RealMedia through its demuxers, though it is a command-line converter and not a graphical player.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay, a portable player built on FFmpeg libraries.

### RA and MP3 compared

The MP3 format dates to the late 1980s work at Fraunhofer IIS with fellow MPEG audio group members, and ISO/IEC 11172-3 standardized it in 1993. A model of human hearing decides which sound it throws away. Every major browser plays MP3, and ID3 structures inside the file store titles and further tags. RealAudio is lossy already, so an MP3 made from it adds one more generation of loss.

On this page FFmpeg runs in your browser and encodes with libmp3lame, asking for 192 kbit/s and leaving video out. Below 32 kHz that rate is out of reach for MP3, so audio sampled low gets a lower bitrate.

### Other ways to convert RA to MP3

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i archive.ra -vn -b:a 192k -c:a libmp3lame listening.mp3`.
- **Switch Sound File Converter:** Switch converts from ra and to mp3. Click Add and choose the RA file, type mp3 into the Output Format field and click Convert.

### Problems with RA files

- **The file is just a link:** a .ram companion is a streaming metafile and is not interchangeable with the sound file itself. Look for the .ra it points to.
- **Some RA files play and others don't:** playback needs a decoder for the particular RealAudio variant, because the family includes several different coding systems.
- **Empty tags:** a RealAudio file only has a title or artist if one was stored in it, so otherwise the MP3 has nothing to copy.

guide.title: About RAF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a RAF file?

Fujifilm describes RAF as its original camera RAW format. On a camera like the X-T3, RAF data can be recorded uncompressed or with lossless compression, which is reversible. A RAF also carries an embedded JPEG preview, and RAW+JPEG recording saves a ready-to-use JPEG next to the RAW capture.

Fujifilm's RAW converter develops RAF data from X-series cameras, and it can apply a Film Simulation during development.

### Programs that open RAF files

- **Windows and Mac:** Fujifilm's development software is RAW FILE CONVERTER EX powered by SILKYPIX, which has a camera compatibility list to check.
- **Windows and Mac:** FUJIFILM X RAW STUDIO hands the RAW conversion to the image processor of a compatible camera that is connected.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick lists RAF among the camera RAW formats it reads.
- **Linux:** darktable recognizes RAF for import, and its camera support comes from the RawSpeed library.

### RAF and JPEG compared

- **Extensions**: .raf and .jpeg. The .jpg extension is the same format.
- **Data**: a RAF holds unprocessed sensor data in a proprietary Fujifilm format. A JPEG is a developed picture with lossy compression, 8 bits per channel and no transparency.
- **Quality**: a JPEG's quality is normally chosen on a scale from 0 to 100.

ImageMagick reads the RAF on this page and a JPEG is written. There is no quality value and no Film Simulation setting.

### Other ways to convert RAF to JPEG

- **RawTherapee:** in the Editor, click the hard disk icon at the bottom left of the preview, set the name, location and format in the dialog, then choose Save immediately or put the file in the processing queue.
- **darktable:** in the export module, choose file on disk as the target and the file format, set the quality and size, then press Export.
- **ImageMagick:** `magick mountain-capture.raf mountain-delivery.jpeg`. ImageMagick's format list shows RAF as readable.

### Problems with RAF files

guide.title: Understanding RAF and JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is a RAF file?

RAF is Fujifilm's original camera RAW format. Unprocessed sensor data and a small embedded JPEG preview make up the file, so it is raw material for developing a photo and not a finished picture. Cameras such as the X-T3 can record RAF either uncompressed or losslessly compressed.

Many Fujifilm cameras also offer RAW+JPEG recording, which saves a ready-to-use JPEG next to the RAF. If you shot that way, the JPEG already exists. A RAF is the file to convert when you want to develop the capture yourself, or when you shot RAW only. Fujifilm supplies its own RAW converter for X-series RAF data, and Film Simulation can be applied while the file is developed. The format is proprietary to Fujifilm, and photographers use it for editing before they convert to JPEG.

### Programs that open RAF files

- **Windows and Mac:** RAW FILE CONVERTER EX powered by SILKYPIX is Fujifilm's own RAW development software, so check its camera compatibility list. It develops RAF data recorded by X-series cameras and can apply Film Simulation during development. FUJIFILM X RAW STUDIO uses a connected compatible camera's image processor for the conversion.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick lists RAF as a readable camera RAW format.
- **Linux:** darktable recognizes RAF for import, with camera support from its RawSpeed library.

### RAF and JPG compared

- **Extensions and types**: .raf, and .jpg or .jpeg with image/jpeg.
- **What each is**: a RAF holds the sensor data and a preview. A JPG is a finished picture with the look chosen, in compressed pixels.
- **Compression**: a RAF's lossless option is reversible. JPEG discards data as it compresses: 8x8 pixel blocks go through a discrete cosine transform, and entropy coding comes last.
- **Color**: JPEG stores 8 bits per color channel.
- **Quality numbers**: programs usually offer a 0 to 100 quality scale, yet one number does not mean the same quality everywhere, so a JPG from another tool at the same setting may look different.
- **Loading**: progressive JPEGs exist too, where a coarse version of the image appears first and sharpens as more data loads.
- **Transparency and layers**: JPEG has no alpha channel and cannot store layers, so a JPG carries no editing history.
- **Support**: every major browser displays JPEG, and most digital cameras and scanners write it natively. Its US patents expired on 27 October 2006.

Your RAF is read in your browser by ImageMagick compiled to WebAssembly, which loads the first time you convert. ImageMagick reads camera RAW with its LibRaw decoder and then writes the JPG. The page passes no quality setting and has no development controls such as white balance or Film Simulation. Anything larger than about 537 megapixels is refused as too large to convert here. Your RAF itself stays untouched; what you save is a separate JPG.

### Other ways to convert RAF to JPG

- **FUJIFILM X RAW STUDIO:** on the camera, choose USB RAW CONVERSION under SET UP and connect it to the computer. In the software, pick the source image folder, which must be on the computer's drive, select the RAW files in Thumbnail View, adjust Conversion Settings and click Convert. The output is a JPEG or TIFF, saved in the same folder. The connected camera must be the model that took the photos.
- **darktable:** select the images, open export, choose file on disk as the target, pick JPEG for the format and run the export. Check the camera-support list first.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick photo.raf delivery.jpg`, which reads the RAF and writes the JPG.

### Problems with RAF files

- **The file won't open in an older program**: new camera models can require a converter update, and Fujifilm publishes the models it adds. A losslessly compressed RAF needs software that understands that variant.
- **"The RAW file is damaged"**: the decoder found a broken structure or couldn't decode the picture data. Copy the file from the card again.
- **The RAW data stops short**: the RAF is incomplete, as a copy interrupted part way would be.
- **Size refused**: the file declares a picture above roughly 537 megapixels, or the decoder would need more memory than it may use.
- **X RAW STUDIO won't start**: it requires a supported camera connection and doesn't convert with the computer's processor.

guide.title: Understanding RM and MP3
guide.markdown:
### What is an RM file?

RM identifies RealMedia, a container associated with RealNetworks' streaming ecosystem. A historical RealNetworks Internet-Draft describes its chunk-based structure and separate stream headers. It can carry more than one kind of encoded media, so a RealMedia filename is not itself a guarantee of an audible soundtrack. RealNetworks introduced it in 1997 for streaming audio and video over the internet, and it is now a legacy format.

### Programs that open RM files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay, the free playback utility from FFmpeg, plays RealMedia, and FFmpeg demuxes and muxes it, though each codec inside has its own support entry.

### RM and MP3 compared

RealMedia is a streaming container with tagged chunks and separate headers for the file and each stream. MP3 is an audio coding format.

This page runs FFmpeg with `-vn` and LAME asked for 192 kbit/s, a rate only a 32 kHz or higher source reaches, so any picture is discarded and the sound is encoded a second time. Detail lost to the original RealAudio compression does not come back. Which track is used, and the sample rate and channels, are left to FFmpeg's defaults.

Keep the RM if it has archival value beyond a listening copy, and compare the length of the MP3 with the original.

### Other ways to convert RM to MP3

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i archive.rm -vn -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k realmedia-audio.mp3` writes sound only, the same request this page makes. The `-vn` option drops the video, `-c:a libmp3lame` selects the LAME encoder, and `-b:a 192k` asks for 192 kbit/s.

### Problems with RM files

**A codec fails:** knowing a file is RealMedia says nothing about whether each codec in it can be decoded.

**The file is not recognized:** a damaged or missing initial .RMF header stops normal identification.

**The MP3 sounds no cleaner:** old compression artifacts are part of the decoded sound.

**The specification is old:** the RealMedia specification is a work in progress, so version-specific structures are no current universal guarantee.

**The soundtrack is missing:** check whether the RM holds audio at all, or only video.

guide.title: About RM and MP4
guide.markdown:
### What is an RM file?

RealNetworks described RealMedia as a streaming container in a March 1998 Internet-Draft. The format can be played from local storage or over a network. Its file format, RMFF, is built from tagged chunks with four-character identifiers, and a .RMF header marks a file as RealMedia. Separate headers describe the media as a whole and each stream inside it.

The container does not fix a codec. An RM file is a wrapper, and what it holds decides whether a given program can play it. Today it is a legacy format, met mostly as old streaming video and in media archives.

### Programs that open RM files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay is a free playback utility built on FFmpeg's libraries. FFmpeg itself lists RealMedia demuxing and muxing.

### RM and MP4 compared

- **Structure**: RM uses tagged chunks and stream headers. MP4 is the ISO/IEC 14496-14 file format, first published in 2003, a set of nested boxes in the ISO Base Media File Format that grew out of QuickTime.
- **Playback**: every major browser plays MP4, and its media type is video/mp4.
- **Contents**: MP4 commonly holds H.264 video with AAC audio, which is what this page writes.

The RM is decoded and then encoded from scratch, so the MP4 is a lossy copy of what the decoder produced. A picture bigger than 1920 px either way is scaled to fit, the frame rate cannot exceed 30 fps, and the audio is rewritten as AAC at 96 kbps. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced first.

### Other ways to convert RM to MP4

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i lecture.rm -c:v libx264 -c:a aac lecture.mp4`. The -c:v and -c:a options choose the video and audio encoders, and FFmpeg takes the output format from the .mp4 extension.

### Problems with RM files

- **No picture or no sound**: recognizing the container does not mean the codec inside can be decoded. Open the file in VLC media player or RealPlayer to see whether it plays at all.
- **The file isn't recognized**: a damaged or missing .RMF header at the start stops normal identification. Download the file again.

guide.title: About RMVB files
guide.markdown:
### What is an RMVB file?

RMVB stands for RealMedia Variable Bitrate. It belongs to the RealMedia family from RealNetworks, and the Library of Congress describes the .rmvb ending as variable-bitrate RealMedia video. RealVideo can be encoded toward an average bitrate or toward a constant visual quality, and the versions differ in efficiency: RealVideo 9 and 10 do not code the picture equally well. A RealMedia file can also carry descriptive information such as a title, an author and a copyright line. Its media type is application/vnd.rn-realmedia.

The format was popular for sharing movies in the early 2000s, so RMVB files turn up in old download collections and archived TV episodes. It is a proprietary RealNetworks format, and today it counts as a legacy one, with the older downloaded movies and media archives as its main remaining use. One thing that looks like an RMVB but is not one is the .ram file. It is a small reference file used in some RealMedia streaming setups, and it points to the video instead of holding it.

### Programs that open RMVB files

**Windows**

- RealPlayer HD: the vendor lists playback of RMVB videos, along with its Windows requirements.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FFmpeg: includes a RealMedia demuxer and codec-specific handling.
- ffplay: plays supported RealMedia streams through the FFmpeg libraries.

### RMVB and MP4 compared

- **Names and media types**: .rmvb is application/vnd.rn-realmedia. .mp4 is defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14.
- **Contents**: an RMVB carries RealVideo pictures. MP4 is a wrapper that can hold video made with several codecs, with H.264 and AAC the usual pairing. MP4 turns up in web video, streaming sites and files passed between people.
- **Bitrate**: an RMVB varies its bitrate through the movie. An MP4 holds whatever its encoder produced, constant or variable.
- **Extras**: MP4 can carry metadata alongside the streams.
- **Playback**: nearly every phone, TV and browser plays MP4. Playing one takes a reader for RealMedia and a RealVideo decoder.

The conversion itself: your browser runs FFmpeg, which reads the RealMedia file. Pictures larger than 1920 pixels are scaled down until they fit, anything above 30 frames per second is thinned out, with the running time unchanged, and widths and heights are trimmed to even values. Nothing leaves your device while this runs, and the RMVB itself is never altered. Each finished movie downloads as a new file with your RMVB's name and an .mp4 ending. Then x264 encodes H.264 video with its ultrafast preset at CRF 32, and FFmpeg's AAC encoder writes the sound at 96 kbps. Because the picture is compressed a second time, detail the RMVB had already lost stays lost.

### Other ways to convert RMVB to MP4

- **FFmpeg:** on the command line, `ffmpeg -i archive.rmvb -c:v libx264 -c:a aac archive.mp4` does the job by demuxing the RealMedia file and decoding its RealVideo. Here -i is the input file, and the two -c options pick the encoders for picture and sound. FFmpeg also has a special codec value, copy, that skips re-encoding, but copy would carry the RealVideo pictures over unchanged instead of making H.264, so name encoders as above.
- **VLC:** select Media > Convert/Save, click Add, choose the RMVB and click Open. VLC then shows a Convert window. Type a name for the destination file, pick a profile whose output is MP4 and click Start.

### Problems with RMVB files

- **It won't play on a phone or TV**: an RMVB needs a RealMedia reader and a RealVideo decoder, and many players lack them. Convert the file to MP4 here, or play it in RealPlayer HD.
- **The file is a .ram**: it only points to a stream. Find the actual .rmvb it names.
- **FFmpeg rejects the header**: FFmpeg turns down an invalid RealMedia header instead of guessing. If ffplay cannot open the file either, download it again.
- **A renamed file still fails**: changing .rmvb to .mp4 leaves the RealMedia data inside. Convert the file instead.
- **The download stopped early**: a cut-short or damaged RMVB usually still converts, and the MP4 is then shorter than the movie. Download the whole file again to get the full length.
- **The two halves of a movie are separate files**: converting never joins files. Join the MP4 files in a video editor.

guide.title: About SVG files
guide.markdown:
### What is an SVG file?

An SVG document describes artwork in XML. A curve stays a path, a label stays text, and a gradient keeps its stops. The file can also refer to a photograph or a font stored elsewhere, which is why a vector drawing and a self-contained illustration are different things, even when they look the same in a browser.

SVG suits diagrams, icons and illustrations that need to scale. Its document structure also allows CSS and browser behavior that a printed page doesn't reproduce.

Before converting, decide what the recipient needs. They may want the visible artwork, individual editable objects, or a native Illustrator production file. This page covers the first and part of the second. For the third, you need Illustrator.

A common case is a logo or icon that a designer, printer or sign maker asked for as an .ai file. If they only need to place the artwork in a layout, a PDF-compatible file is often enough. If they need to change colors, paths or layers, send the SVG as well.

### Programs that open SVG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Inkscape is a native SVG editor.
- **Windows, Mac, Linux and Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays SVG.
- **Web and Mobile:** Chrome draws SVG in the browser.
- **Mobile:** Safari renders SVG too.

CorelDRAW imports SVG files through File > Import. A browser preview shows how a drawing looks, not what a drawing application can edit.

### SVG and AI compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .svg, image/svg+xml; .ai, Adobe Illustrator artwork.
- **Format**: SVG is an open XML description. AI is Adobe Illustrator's native artwork format.
- **Content**: vector objects and pixel images can sit together in an AI document, along with Illustrator's editable effects, brushes, layers and transparency.
- **PDF compatibility**: saving from Illustrator with the PDF-compatible option adds a PDF version next to the Illustrator data.
- **History**: Illustrator 9 changed the AI format in 2000. Earlier files used PostScript.

An AI file is a PDF-compatible file, and this page makes that kind. It parses your SVG and draws it as vectors into a PDF page of the drawing's size, with jsPDF and svg2pdf.js. That page is sized from the SVG's width and height, with inches, centimeters and millimeters converted to points and one unit or pixel counting as one point. A side that is missing comes from the viewBox, and an SVG that gives no size at all gets a 300 by 150 page. Check the page dimensions before the file goes to print.

The file holds none of Illustrator's own editing data. A program that reads only the PDF part may not expose native Illustrator objects. An image embedded in the SVG stays a picture.

An SVG can link to pictures that live in other files, so embed what the artwork depends on. Text layout also depends on the fonts available, so a substituted font changes the drawing.

Keep the SVG as the editable source. If the recipient asks for a native Illustrator file, open the SVG in Illustrator and save an AI copy there.

### Other ways to convert SVG to AI

- **CorelDRAW:** choose File > Import, select the SVG and click Import. In the Import SVG dialog pick a scaling option (Automatic keeps the scale of the source file) and click OK, then click the page to place it. Next choose File > Export, pick Adobe Illustrator (AI) from the Save as type list, enter a name and click Export. CorelDRAW lists both SVG and AI among its file formats.

### Problems with SVG files

- **"This SVG file couldn't be read"**: the XML doesn't parse. Load the file in a browser or Inkscape and save a clean copy.
- **The page comes out the wrong size**: an SVG with no width, height or viewBox gets a 300 by 150 point page. Add a viewBox or explicit sizes before converting.
- **Text looks different**: when a font is substituted, the text changes shape. Convert text to outlines in your editor if the shapes must stay fixed.
- **A picture is soft when enlarged**: embedded pixel images in an SVG keep the resolution they started with.
- **The page size is wrong**: an SVG whose width and height are percentages has no absolute size, so the viewBox sets the page instead. Add an absolute width and height to the SVG.

guide.title: About SVG files
guide.markdown:
### What is an SVG file?

Instead of a color per pixel, an SVG describes its shapes in a structured XML document. Curves, text, clipping paths and gradients can be described independently of display size, which makes SVG a good fit for a logo that appears both in a small interface and on a large sign. Photographs embedded in an SVG remain raster images, even when the drawing around them is vector artwork.

SVG can also refer to outside resources and use features meant for a browser. Your browser paints the SVG as a flat image, so outside pictures, stylesheets and web fonts it points to are never fetched; just embedded data and fonts installed locally get drawn. Keep the SVG. The GIF can't replace it as the source for later changes to paths or lettering.

### Programs that open SVG files

- **Windows, Linux and Mac:** Inkscape edits SVG natively, and Mozilla Firefox displays it.
- **Web:** Chrome and Firefox open an SVG directly in their own window.
- **Mobile:** Safari and Chrome show an SVG as an ordinary picture.

For automated work, ImageMagick's format list marks SVG as readable and writable, with rendering through Inkscape, RSVG or its internal MSVG renderer. Different renderers may handle fonts or filters differently, so opening a file successfully is only the start of checking how it looks.

### SVG and GIF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .svg, image/svg+xml; .gif, image/gif.
- **Content**: SVG describes shapes and text. GIF is a grid of indexed colors.
- **Palette**: a GIF frame holds up to 256 colors, which suits flat artwork and strains gradients and photos.
- **Transparency**: GIF transparency is on or off. SVG edges can be partly transparent.
- **Scaling**: SVG scales without limit. A GIF has a fixed size.

Here your browser decodes the SVG and paints it at whatever size it reports. The page adds no scaling, size cap or viewBox handling. ImageMagick then writes the GIF. The conversion produces one still image, so nothing in the SVG that moves or runs is recorded. Compare the GIF with the SVG in a browser at the same size to see what the palette lost.

A larger GIF doesn't regain vector scalability, and enlarging one later shows pixel edges on diagonal strokes and small type. Decide the display size first, because the page adds no scaling of its own.

If the destination accepts SVG, keep the SVG. If it takes PNG, the SVG to PNG converter gives full color and soft edges.

GIF still has its place. It stores palette indexes compressed with LZW, and a frame can carry its own local color table, so a flat logo with few colors converts cleanly. A simple icon with solid fills and hard edges loses very little. A drawing with soft shadows, glows or gradients is where the 256-color palette shows, so preview the GIF at its real display size before you use it.

### Other ways to convert SVG to GIF

- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick artwork.svg artwork.gif`, the input-then-output form ImageMagick's docs show. The SVG renderer your installation uses affects the result, and the GIF is limited to 256 palette entries.
- **Inkscape and GIMP:** open the SVG in Inkscape and press Shift + Ctrl + E for the Export PNG Image dialog. Choose Page, Drawing, Selection or Custom as the area, enter the pixel size under Image Size, name the file and click Export. Then bring the PNG into GIMP and use File > Export As to write a GIF. In the GIF dialog the As animation option is disabled for a single layer, and GIMP's GIF export is limited to 256 colors.

### Problems with SVG files

- **A picture or font is missing**: a linked picture, an external stylesheet or a web font is never loaded. Embed the pictures in the SVG and install the fonts.
- **Fine strokes look rough**: the GIF is drawn at the SVG's own size with no scaling, so a thin line gets few pixels. Export a larger PNG from Inkscape and convert that.
- **The GIF doesn't move**: the page writes one still image, whatever the SVG does. Build the frames in an animation tool if you want a moving GIF.
- **Unexpected colors**: a gradient reduced once can't be restored by converting again. Start from the SVG.
- **A different font**: lettering falls back to another typeface when yours is missing. Convert text to paths.

guide.title: Understanding SVG and HTML
guide.markdown:
### What is an SVG file?

The name SVG stands for Scalable Vector Graphics, a W3C standard built on XML. A file lists the shapes, text and embedded pictures that make up a flat drawing. The W3C published version 1.0 as a Recommendation in 2001, and version 1.1 followed in 2003. The shapes are stored as instructions, which lets a renderer draw the same SVG at any size and keep its edges crisp.

Because the file is just text, any text editor opens it, and it can be searched, indexed and compressed; a gzip-compressed one ends in .svgz. Stylesheets and scripts can act on the drawing, which allows styling, scripting and animation, and the format includes clipping paths, masks and filter effects. Its media type is image/svg+xml, and every major browser displays it. On the web SVG typically carries logos, icons, illustrations, diagrams, charts and maps. You can show an SVG on its own or place it inside an HTML page.

### Programs that open SVG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Native SVG editing is what Inkscape does; Mozilla Firefox displays the format, and the list of programs that open it also names Adobe Illustrator and Figma.
- **Mobile:** Google Chrome and Safari display SVG, so a phone browser shows a drawing with no extra app.

### SVG and HTML compared

- **Extensions and types**: .svg with image/svg+xml, and .html with text/html.
- **What each is**: an SVG describes a drawing. HTML is the markup language used to describe web documents and applications, and the WHATWG maintains it as a Living Standard. Its early revisions developed at CERN and then the IETF during 1990 to 1995.
- **Roles**: HTML describes document meaning, CSS supplies presentation and JavaScript can add behavior.
- **Size**: an HTML document may point to other files instead of holding every asset inside itself. Here the drawing sits inside the page, so nothing else is needed.
- **Opening the result**: Firefox displays HTML files from your disk, and Visual Studio Code offers syntax highlighting, completion and formatting for editing them, with built-in analysis that covers only the open file.
- **Encoding**: HTML defines encoding declarations, and an incorrect character encoding can make a document's text render incorrectly. The page made here declares utf-8.
- **Uses**: HTML serves web pages, HTML email, and generated reports and tables.

Your SVG is turned into a web page in your browser. The converter copies the `<svg>` element and everything after it into a new HTML file, and drops the XML declaration, doctype and comments in front of it, which HTML doesn't allow there. The page has a doctype, `lang="en"`, a viewport tag and a title, which reads image. A short style block removes the page margins, centers the drawing in the window and lets it shrink to the window's width. The drawing stays vector. It is not converted to paragraphs, buttons or a rebuilt site layout. A file with no `<svg>` in it is refused with "This file has no SVG drawing in it."

### Other ways to convert SVG to HTML

- **Inline SVG in a text editor:** paste the entire SVG file into the body of an HTML document, as Mozilla documents for SVG in HTML. Keep the viewBox so the drawing scales. Save it with an .html ending and open it in a browser.
- **A CSS background:** give an element a size and set its background-image property to url("logo.svg"). Mozilla lists CSS background-image among the places browsers support SVG images.

### Problems with SVG files

- **A picture is missing**: pictures an SVG references by file name may vanish when those files are unavailable. Preserve the files with the SVG, or embed the pictures in it so the drawing carries everything it shows.
- **The text looks different**: the drawing's text relies on installed fonts, and a stand-in font can change how it looks.
- **An embedded photo looks soft when enlarged**: an SVG may contain pixel images, which keep their own resolution when scaled up; only the vector parts remain crisp.
- **Scripts and links don't work as an image**: an SVG drawn as an image has JavaScript disabled and can't load external resources, apart from data: URLs. A drawing placed inline in a page is not an image in that sense.

guide.title: Understanding SVG for ICO output
guide.markdown:
### What is an SVG file?

An SVG is a Scalable Vector Graphics file, an open W3C standard. Version 1.0 became a Recommendation in 2001 and 1.1 in 2003. Written in XML, it defines two-dimensional graphics through shapes, text and embedded images, which is why it can be scaled to any size and stay sharp.

An SVG is plain text, so any text editor opens it, and tools can search, index and compress the file. The .svgz extension marks an SVG compressed with gzip. Through CSS and JavaScript an SVG can be styled, scripted and animated, and clipping paths, masks and filter effects are supported. A browser can show it as a page of its own, or an HTML page can embed it. Every major browser displays SVG, and the registered media type is image/svg+xml.

Because shapes are stored as instructions rather than pixels, one SVG can serve a favicon, a poster and everything between. People use it for illustrations, diagrams, charts and maps, as well as logos and icons on the web.

You usually have an SVG because a logo or icon was drawn in a vector editor. The pixels only come into it when something, such as an icon file, needs a bitmap.

### Programs that open SVG files

- **Linux, Windows and Mac:** Mozilla Firefox displays SVG, and Inkscape does native SVG editing.
- **Web and Mobile:** Google Chrome displays SVG, and so does Safari.

### SVG and ICO compared

- **Names**: SVG files end in .svg (image/svg+xml), and ICO files end in .ico (image/vnd.microsoft.icon).
- **What is stored**: an SVG holds shapes, text and styling. An ICO holds bitmap images, and the entries can be PNG or bitmap. ICO files use little-endian byte ordering and may contain more than one image.
- **Sizes**: Windows Vista's icon guidance lists 256-by-256 images for high-DPI screens. Enlarged for such a display, a small icon may look soft, so the icon should hold a suitable larger image.
- **Uses**: The ICO format is Microsoft's, used for graphical interface icons, and it serves Windows application icons and website favicons.
- **Support**: Windows File Explorer, GIMP, IrfanView and any web browser open ICO. Firefox displays ICO pictures in browser content, and Chrome supports ICO images.
