guide.title: About TIFF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TIFF file?

TIFF is short for Tagged Image File Format, a design whose point is its tags. A file opens with a header, followed by one or more directories of tags, each directory with its own bitmap data; a directory and its bitmap form a subfile. That structure is how a TIFF holds a run of scanned pages. The tags define color, bit depth and compression, and Adobe keeps a registry of extensions. Some private tags, including color-profile extensions, mean nothing to certain readers.

Two endings, .tiff and .tif, point to this one format, which is registered as image/tiff. The Library of Congress describes the format as fully documented and free of external dependencies, and it is on the preferred list for photographs and other graphic images. TIFF/IT, TIFF/EP and GeoTIFF are subtypes that extend it, and camera Exif metadata shows up in TIFF/EP files. Aldus and Microsoft created TIFF; today Adobe controls the specification, having acquired Aldus's PageMaker program. It began in 1986 as a bilevel format. Version 6.0 was published in 1992, and TIFF 5.0 is still used for many uncompressed images.

### Programs that open TIFF files

**Windows, Linux and Mac**

- ImageMagick: handles TIFF in both directions, with settings for strips, tiles, byte order and compression.

**Mac**

- Preview: TIFF is among the file types offered under File > Export.

### TIFF and PNG compared

- **Names and types**: .tiff or .tif carry image/tiff; .png carries image/png.
- **Compression**: a TIFF can be stored raw, or use LZW, Group 4 (a CCITT scheme for black-and-white images) or JPEG. The LZW patent expired in 2003 in the U.S. and in 2004 in Europe and Japan. PNG compression is lossless.
- **Pages**: a TIFF can hold several images, handy for scanned sequences, but this page reads one picture from the file.
- **Color**: the Photometric Interpretation tag picks the color space. 8-bit grayscale and 24-bit RGB are widespread, though a few TIFF workflows exceed 8 bits per channel. PNG provides 8-bit and 16-bit channels.
- **Transparency**: only PNG offers an alpha channel here.
- **Size ceiling**: classic TIFF uses 32-bit offsets and stops near 4 GB, while BigTIFF uses 64-bit offsets.
- **Background**: TIFF is the older format, built around scanners and print. PNG followed in the mid-1990s as a GIF replacement without patent worries, and it became ISO/IEC 15948 and a W3C Recommendation.

The page decodes one picture with ImageMagick, running as WebAssembly inside your browser, and writes it as a PNG. It does not resize the picture or set a quality value, and the TIFF itself is never altered. If your TIFF is a multi-page scan or a print master, treat the PNG as a copy to share rather than a replacement.

### Other ways to convert TIFF to PNG

- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick 'master.tiff[0]' copy.png`. Put a different frame number in the brackets, counting from zero, to reach a later page. The quotes matter because Linux shells interpret brackets.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the TIFF, pick File > Export As, make the Name field end in .png and click Export.
- **Preview (Mac):** open the TIFF, pick File > Export, select PNG in the Format menu, then press Save. A batch works if you open the files in one Preview window and select them in the sidebar.

### Problems with TIFF files

- **Only the first page came out**: a TIFF can hold many images but this page reads only one. Use ImageMagick with a page number as shown, or software that exposes the whole sequence.
- **The picture is rejected as too large**: beyond about 537 megapixels the page refuses it. Lower the scan's resolution in an editor and retry.
- **A program reads it wrongly**: readers differ over private tags. Open the file in the software that created it and export a standard copy.
- **The file is near 4 GB**: classic TIFF can't grow past that because of its 32-bit offsets, which is what BigTIFF was made to fix.
- **The color profile is missing**: ICC profiles live in an extension tag that not every reader recognizes, so check the result in a second viewer before deleting the original.
- **A renamed file still fails**: changing .tiff to .png leaves TIFF data inside, so run an actual conversion.

guide.title: About TIFF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TIFF file?

The name TIFF stands for Tagged Image File Format, a raster wrapper first built by Aldus with Microsoft. The 6.0 revision appeared in 1992, and today the specification is under Adobe's control. Because a TIFF can use several compression methods and color representations, it serves scanners, print shops and photo archives, as well as document imaging and high-bit-depth preservation masters.

One TIFF file may hold a run of images, such as the pages of a scanned document. ImageMagick's format list describes extensive strip, tile, byte-order and compression tag controls for it. The endings .tif and .tiff both refer to the format, labeled image/tiff.

### Programs that open TIFF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- GIMP: opens image files for editing, and each export format keeps a different part of a project's properties.
- ImageMagick: reads TIFF and writes it, with compression, strip, tile and byte-order options.

**Mac**

- Preview: lists TIFF in the format menu under File > Export.

### TIFF and SVG compared

- **What they hold**: TIFF stores pixels. SVG describes shapes, paths and text, and can also embed a pixel image.
- **Scaling**: a TIFF is fixed at its pixel size. An SVG made of paths scales cleanly, but an SVG that only wraps a picture does not.
- **Pages**: one TIFF can carry many images. The SVG produced here carries one picture, held as pixels inside an image element.
- **Color**: TIFF supports high bit depth and CMYK. SVG is XML text styled with CSS, so you can open it in a text editor, and every major browser displays it.
- **Typical use**: TIFF belongs to scanning, print and archiving. SVG is the usual choice for site logos, icons, diagrams and maps.

Here is what happens to your file. ImageMagick, compiled to WebAssembly, reads the TIFF in your browser. SVG is not a format it writes, so it produces a PNG of the picture, and the converter then places that PNG inside an SVG as one image element at the same pixel size, with a matching viewBox. The PNG data is stored in the file as base64 text. This is not tracing: no outlines are found and no text is recognized. A multipage TIFF contributes one image only, and the rest of its pages are left out. Pictures beyond roughly 537 megapixels do not convert, and the page tells you the file is too big. The result fits a tool or web page that accepts only SVG files, and your original TIFF is left unchanged. Several TIFFs chosen at once go through one after another, and each SVG is saved under the TIFF's name. For paths you can edit, trace the picture instead.

### Other ways to convert TIFF to SVG

- **GIMP plus Inkscape:** in GIMP, choose File > Export As (Shift+Ctrl+E) to store the TIFF in a format other than XCF, and use PNG. The GIMP manual points to its Files section for details on each format. In Inkscape, import the PNG with File > Import, select it with the Selector tool and open Path > Trace Bitmap. Adjust the options, update the preview and apply the trace. The vector result sits exactly above your picture, so the original stays underneath until you move or delete it.
- **ImageMagick plus Potrace:** run `magick scan.tiff scan.bmp`, then `potrace -s scan.bmp -o scan-outline.svg`. Potrace reads PBM, PGM, PPM and BMP, converts other pixel values to black and white with a threshold, and -s selects the SVG output. Unless you give a resolution with -r, it assumes the input is 72 dpi, and -o names the file the output goes to. Multiple input files are only allowed for multi-page output backends, so trace one bitmap at a time. It does not list TIFF as input, and it traces black and white shapes, so this suits a clean symbol or line drawing better than a photograph.

### Problems with TIFF files

- **A viewer shows only the first page**: a TIFF may hold several images, so use software that shows the full sequence.
- **A program rejects the file**: not every reader understands each private tag, color-profile extensions among them.
- **The file is enormous**: the original TIFF layout counts offsets in 32 bits, so files top out near 4 GB, and BigTIFF widens those fields.

guide.title: About TIFF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TIFF file?

TIFF stands for Tagged Image File Format. Aldus first published it in 1986, and the Library of Congress records Microsoft as a co-developer. The 6.0 revision dates from 1992, and Adobe holds the specification today. A file begins with II for little-endian or MM for big-endian byte order, and the specification sets no limit on how many images a file may contain. Tags make TIFF flexible: a single file can mix compression methods and color representations and contain more than one image.

You find TIFF in scanners and archives, in professional photography and print workflows, and in fax and document imaging. High-bit-depth work and preservation master files are established uses. The registered media type is image/tiff, and both .tif and .tiff extensions are in use.

### Programs that open TIFF files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- GIMP: imports a TIFF as an editable image, and each export format carries over only some of a project's properties.
- ImageMagick: reads and writes TIFF, including its compression, strip, tile and byte-order settings.

**Mac**

- Preview: File > Export lists TIFF as one of its formats.

### TIFF and WebP compared

- **Compression**: TIFF supports many methods, lossless or lossy, and WebP has its own lossy and lossless modes.
- **Pages**: a TIFF can hold multiple images. WebP can hold the frames of an animation.
- **Color and depth**: TIFF can store CMYK images and high bit depth.
- **Origin**: Aldus and Microsoft developed TIFF. Google released WebP in 2010, built on the VP8 video codec for lossy images.
- **Reach**: current major browsers support WebP.

This page reads one picture through ImageMagick and writes it as a WebP. It passes no quality setting.

### Other ways to convert TIFF to WebP

- **cwebp:** run cwebp -q 80 scan.tiff -o article.webp. Google's command-line encoder takes TIFF input, and -q sets the quality from 0 to 100.
- **ImageMagick:** run magick scan.tiff scan.webp. ImageMagick needs its WebP delegate library for this.

### Problems with TIFF files

- **Colors differ between programs**: private tags, including some color-profile extensions, are not understood by every reader.
- **A file approaches the limit**: classic TIFF uses 32-bit offsets, capping files at about 4 GB, a limit BigTIFF removes by widening them.

guide.title: About TS files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TS file?

A TS file holds an MPEG-2 transport stream, a system format from the ISO/IEC 13818-1 standard. Instead of defining a picture codec, it interleaves video and sound that were coded separately, cut into 188-byte packets. Several programs with their own clocks can share one stream.

Broadcast distribution and error-prone transmission are the important uses, and HLS streaming segments and Blu-ray and camcorder recordings rely on it too. Timestamps in the stream coordinate presentation and decoder buffering. The usual extension is .ts, with video/mp2t as the registered media type.

### Programs that open TS files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg reads transport streams, and on the Mac you use it from the command line.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player lists TS as one of its input formats.
- **Mobile:** On a phone, VLC for Android lists TS input; decoding still depends on the media in the stream.

### TS and MKV compared

- **Extensions**: .ts and .mkv.
- **Purpose**: TS suits broadcasting and survives transmission errors. Matroska is an open container for any number of video, audio, picture and subtitle tracks, and chapters and tags belong to its design.
- **Codecs**: neither container prescribes a codec; Matroska doesn't fix a compression method or quality level.

On this page the video is rewritten as H.264 and the audio as AAC at 96 kb/s, with the picture held to 1920 px and 30 fps. IANA registers video/matroska as the media type for Matroska video.

### Other ways to convert TS to MKV

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i broadcast-segment.ts -c copy broadcast-segment.mkv` copies the streams without re-encoding.
- **HandBrakeCLI:** `HandBrakeCLI -i recorder-input.ts -o recorder-output.mkv -f av_mkv -e x264` encodes the video with x264 into Matroska. HandBrake lists TS among the sources it reads.
- **MKVToolNix:** `mkvmerge -o channel-archive.mkv channel-capture.ts`. mkvmerge reads MPEG transport streams.

### Problems with TS files

- **Several programs in one stream**: selecting the intended program matters.
- **The TS won't decode**: recognizing the wrapper doesn't settle which codec its audio or video needs.
- **Damaged timing or missing packets**: renaming the file won't fix them. FFmpeg usually logs the error and converts what it can read.

faqs.question: How do I convert TS to MP4?

faqs.question: How do I convert .ts to MP4 on my computer?
faqs.answer: Rewrap it with FFmpeg's stream copy, `-c copy`, with no re-encoding, or open the file in HandBrake or VLC and choose MP4. This page does the re-encode in the browser instead.

faqs.question: Is converting TS to MP4 lossless?
faqs.answer: On this page, no. The video is encoded again with x264 at CRF 32 and the audio as AAC at 96 kbps. The FFmpeg copy method on your computer doesn't re-encode, so it keeps the streams as they are when MP4 can hold them.

faqs.question: Will my 4K recording stay 4K?
faqs.answer: No. The picture is kept within 1920 px on the longer side and 30 fps. Dimensions are forced to even values, so a picture with an odd height comes out one pixel shorter.

faqs.question: Why does the MP4 start playing before it finishes loading?
faqs.answer: The page adds `+faststart`, which puts the index at the start of the file. Browsers can then begin playback early.

faqs.question: Which video and audio streams does the MP4 get?
faqs.answer: FFmpeg's defaults choose them, because the page maps no streams. The command has no `-map_metadata` option, so the input's global tags, such as the title, go into an output that has fields for them.

faqs.question: Why is the converted video softer than the broadcast?
faqs.answer: The encode is tuned for speed and size: ultrafast preset, CRF 32. That trades detail for a smaller file and a quicker run. Interlaced pictures also get a deinterlace filter.

faqs.question: Can I convert more than one TS recording?
faqs.answer: Yes, select them together. Each recording is processed in turn and saved as a separate MP4; they are not joined.

faqs.question: Does it work for a very long recording?
faqs.answer: Neither size nor running time is capped. A long recording keeps your device busy longer, and FFmpeg's single thread in the browser adds to the wait.

faqs.question: Why does the TS file not play in my browser?
faqs.answer: A transport stream is a system format for broadcast, and browsers play MP4 instead. Converting gives you the file they know.

guide.title: About TS files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TS file?

TS identifies an MPEG-2 transport stream, one of the system formats specified by ISO/IEC 13818-1. A transport stream doesn't define a picture codec. It multiplexes separately coded video and sound, and one stream can carry several programs with independent clocks. Its syntax uses timestamps to coordinate presentation and decoder buffering. Broadcast distribution and transmissions vulnerable to errors are important uses of TS. Besides television, TS is used for HLS segments in streaming and for footage from Blu-ray discs and camcorders, and its fixed 188-byte packets help streams survive transmission errors.

The usual extension is .ts and the registered media type is video/mp2t. You tend to meet it as a recording from a TV tuner, a stream or a capture, where the file is long and not tidy.

MP4 is the MPEG-4 Part 14 format, ISO/IEC 14496-14, first published in 2003. Typically it holds H.264 video and AAC audio, and all major browsers play it. That is the reason for the conversion: MP4 opens in places a .ts file doesn't. Because TS is a wrapper rather than a codec, the video inside may already be H.264. Even so, this page encodes it again, so the result is a new file with its own quality settings, not a copy of the original streams.

### Programs that open TS files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FFmpeg: reads transport streams.
- VLC media player: its input list includes TS.

**Mobile**

- Android: the VLC app lists TS among its inputs, and decoding depends on the stream's media.

### TS and MP4 compared

- **What it is**: TS is a system format for multiplexed streams and broadcast. MP4 is a file container built on the ISO Base Media File Format.
- **Codecs**: neither fixes the codec. An MP4 often has H.264 and AAC, and may use AV1, VP9, MP3 or Opus instead.
- **Programs**: one TS can carry several programs. An MP4 normally holds one movie.
- **Playback**: browsers play MP4; a .ts file needs a player that understands transport streams.
- **Timing**: a TS leans on timestamps for presentation and decoder buffering, which suits a broadcast that may lose packets. An MP4 is built for files you store and play back.
- **Extensions and types**: .ts and video/mp2t; .mp4 or .m4v and video/mp4.

This page encodes new video. In your browser, FFmpeg uses `libx264` (preset ultrafast, CRF 32, tune zerolatency) for video and AAC at 96 kbps for audio, adds `+faststart` so the MP4 can start before it has fully loaded, and applies a deinterlace filter (`yadif`). The longer side stays at or under 1920 px and the frame rate at or under 30 fps. Sides round down to even numbers, which costs an odd dimension one pixel. No `-map` is passed, so FFmpeg's defaults pick the streams.

### Other ways to convert TS to MP4

- **FFmpeg, copy:** run `ffmpeg -i input.ts -c copy output.mp4`. It doesn't re-encode, so the streams stay as they are, but MP4 must be able to hold them.
- **HandBrake:** choose Open Source, pick a preset, set the file name in Save As and the folder in To, then press Start. HandBrake's container page says it may switch an MP4 to the .m4v ending when AC3 pass-through, SRT subtitles or chapter markers are on, and a preference turns that off.
- **VLC:** under Media > Convert/Save, add the recording, select the Video - H.264 + MP3 (MP4) profile, name a destination and start. The profile's name says MP3 sound.

### Problems with TS files

- **It won't play in a browser**: browsers read MP4 rather than TS, so this is expected and not a fault in the file.
- **The codec isn't supported**: recognizing the TS wrapper doesn't settle which codec decodes its audio or video.
- **Glitches or jumps in the picture**: a TS is built to survive transmission errors, but lost packets can still leave flaws. The MP4 follows the stream as written, so it shows the same flaws. Try another copy of the recording.
- **The MP4 is smaller than the TS**: the picture is capped in size and frame rate, and CRF 32 compresses hard.
- **Fine detail looks worse**: the video is encoded again. Convert from the original TS each time.
- **A long recording is slow**: the conversion is single-threaded in your browser, so a longer file means a longer wait.

faqs.question: How do I convert TTF to PNG?

faqs.question: What is in the PNG?
faqs.answer: The font's name, then the capital letters, the small letters, the digits and a few punctuation marks. The image shows one pangram sentence five times over, growing from 16 to 64 pixels. It is drawn in black on white.

faqs.question: Can I type my own text or pick the size?
faqs.answer: No. The sample text, the five sizes and the black-on-white colors are fixed. For your own words, use Pillow in a short script or the Text tool in GIMP.

faqs.question: How wide is the PNG?
faqs.answer: The width follows the longest line plus a 40 pixel margin, and stays between 400 and 2400 pixels. The height follows the lines' sizes and spacing.

faqs.question: Where does the name at the top come from?
faqs.answer: From the font's own name table: the full name if it has one, otherwise the family name, cut to 64 characters. A font with no name shows "TTF font" instead.

faqs.question: Is the PNG an installable font?
faqs.answer: No. A PNG is a picture, so it has no glyph tables, metrics or outlines. Keep the TTF for installing the font.

faqs.question: Does it show every glyph in the font?
faqs.answer: No. It draws only the sample lines described above. It is a quick look at the typeface, not a full character map.

faqs.question: Can I get a texture atlas or a sprite sheet of the glyphs?
faqs.answer: Not from this page. It makes a single specimen image. A bitmap-font tool or a script that draws each glyph to its own cell is what an atlas needs.

faqs.question: Does it work with OTF fonts?
faqs.answer: This page takes TTF files. OpenType fonts have a separate OTF to PNG converter on the site.

guide.title: About TTF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TTF file?

A TTF file holds a TrueType font. Apple developed TrueType and licensed the technology to Microsoft, and System 7 shipped with it in May 1991. A TrueType font describes scalable character outlines, so letters stay smooth at any size. Its data is arranged in individually tagged tables, which can hold glyph mappings, outlines, metrics and naming information. The registered media type is font/ttf.

The naming table is how a program learns a font's name, and it is where a specimen takes its heading from. A font file with a broken table or a bad offset can fail to display at all.

### Programs that open TTF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FontForge: opens TrueType outlines for editing, including the tables.

**Windows**

- Windows Font Previewer: double-click the font to inspect it before installing.

**Mac**

- Font Book: installs and validates font files.

**Linux**

- GNOME Fonts: previews installed typefaces and installs downloaded .ttf files.

### TTF and PNG compared

- **What they store**: a TTF stores outlines, character mappings and metrics. A PNG stores a grid of pixels, losslessly compressed, with optional transparency.
- **Scaling**: a font scales to any size. A PNG stays at the pixel size it was drawn.
- **Text**: a font can set any words you type. A PNG shows only what was drawn into it, and it cannot be installed.
- **Use**: a TTF goes into an operating system or an app. A PNG goes into a web page, a slide, a document or a review thread, so people can see a typeface without installing it.

Here is how the specimen is made. ImageMagick, compiled to WebAssembly, loads the font in your browser and draws with FreeType. The top line is the font's name, taken from its name table (the full name, or the family name if there is no full name), cut to 64 characters, and a font with no usable name is labeled "TTF font". Below it come the capital letters, the small letters, and the digits with a few punctuation marks. Five more lines repeat one familiar test sentence, each at its own size of 16, 24, 32, 48 and 64 pixels. Everything is black on white inside a 40 pixel margin. The image is only as wide as the longest line needs, between 400 and 2400 pixels. You cannot change the text. It is a specimen, not the font's outlines and not a character map. The download is named after your file with a .png ending, and the TTF itself is not changed.

### Other ways to convert TTF to PNG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick display-face.ttf display-face-preview.png`. ImageMagick's TTF reader gives a preview image of the font.
- **Pillow (Python):** load the font with `ImageFont.truetype`, which loads a TrueType or OpenType font file at the pixel size you give. If the file is not at the given path, Pillow may search the standard font directories for your operating system, and it raises an OSError when the file cannot be read. Create a canvas with `Image.new`, draw your sample with `ImageDraw.text` and that font, then call `save` with a .png name. This takes a short script, but you choose the phrase, colors and size.
- **GIMP:** with the font available in the font selector, create an image, choose the Text tool, pick the font and size, type your sample and export with File > Export As, choosing PNG. The PNG holds pixels, not an editable text layer.

### Problems with TTF files

- **A font that never shows up**: a damaged font can fail to display. Font Book on a Mac can validate a font file.
- **Two copies conflict**: installing two copies of a font can create conflicts, and Font Book can resolve duplicates.
- **It is missing in an app**: a font missing from a third-party application may require that application's own troubleshooting.
- **The converter says it isn't a font**: FreeType could not read the file. Check that it opens in a font previewer.
- **The converter says it has no letters to draw**: the font has no glyphs for the sample lines, as can happen with an icon or symbol font. Draw your own sample with Pillow or GIMP.
- **You need the glyph outlines**: a PNG cannot give them. Open the TTF in FontForge.

guide.title: About TTF and SVG
guide.markdown:
### What is a TTF file?

Apple created TrueType and licensed it to Microsoft; its first appearance was in System 7, in May 1991. TrueType fonts describe scalable character outlines, and the font information is organized into individually tagged tables. Inside, a font can hold glyph mappings, outlines, metrics and names, and font/ttf is its registered media type.

A TTF is therefore more than a picture of its alphabet, even when a font and a picture can display the same letters on screen. People searching for TTF to SVG may want different results: one letter as a vector icon, a wordmark built from outlines, a specimen sheet, or a font defined in SVG. Decide which one you need before choosing a converter, because an image of sample letters cannot be installed as the original typeface.

### Programs that open TTF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FontForge loads TrueType files in its font editor, and it edits the outlines and tables.
- **Windows:** double-click a font to inspect it in Windows Font Previewer before installing.
- **Mac:** Font Book installs and validates font files.
- **Linux:** GNOME Fonts shows installed typefaces and can install a .ttf you downloaded.

### TTF and SVG compared

As an open W3C standard, SVG uses XML to describe flat pictures put together from shapes, text and embedded images. Browsers all display it, and its registered media type is image/svg+xml. As plain text, SVG opens in any text editor and can be searched, indexed and compressed. CSS and JavaScript work with it, so it can also be styled, scripted and animated. A normal SVG stores shapes as instructions, so it stays sharp at any size. An SVG ending alone does not tell you whether the file contains curves, live text that needs a font, or a pixel picture placed inside an SVG wrapper.

This page makes the third kind. It draws a specimen from the font you add: the font's name at the top, then uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits and punctuation, and a sample sentence at five sizes. The lettering is black on white in grayscale, and the picture grows wider to fit its longest line. The SVG wraps that picture and does not describe the characters as outline paths. It is suitable for viewing the typeface's appearance, but enlarging it cannot reveal additional vector detail.

Text in an SVG depends on available fonts, so a substituted font can change the drawing. A specimen picture avoids that, because the letters are already drawn. It cannot do what a font does, however. It carries no glyph mappings, metrics or naming tables, and no program can install it. Keep the TTF for installing the font, and use a font editor for individual glyph artwork.

### Other ways to convert TTF to SVG

- **FontForge graphical export:** open the TTF, open a glyph in its outline view, then choose File > Export and select SVG. The command is in the outline window, so export the characters you need one at a time. The result is glyph artwork and not an installable font.
- **FontForge Python:** import fontforge, then run `fontforge.open('font.ttf')['A'].export('A.svg')` to write the glyph A as an SVG. Run it in a FontForge-enabled Python environment. The glyph must exist in the font, and the destination folder must already exist.

### Problems with TTF files

**A damaged font fails to display:** a damaged font can fail to display. On a Mac, Font Book provides file validation.

**Two copies conflict:** a second copy of the same font can clash with the first, and Font Book is able to settle duplicates.

**The font is missing in another program:** if a font does not show up in a third-party program, that program's own troubleshooting may be needed.

**This converter reports an unreadable font:** the specimen needs the font to be readable and to have letters it can draw. A damaged file, or one renamed from another type, is reported as not being a font the converter can read. A font with no letters it can draw gets a separate message.

**You wanted a web font:** this page does not make one. The output is a picture of the font, so keep the TTF for any site that needs the typeface itself.

**You expected outlines:** the SVG from this page is a picture. Use FontForge or another font editor when you need editable curves instead of a sample.

guide.title: Understanding TXT and JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

TXT commonly identifies plain text: character data without a page-layout model or rich typographic instructions. The encoding determines how bytes become letters. A text editor supplies the font and display arrangement, so the same document can look different when opened with another editor or window width.

### Programs that open TXT files

- **Mac:** TextEdit creates, opens and saves plain text documents.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** to read the text before drawing it, Visual Studio Code and Vim both open plain text.

### TXT and JPEG compared

TXT records characters without layout, and the font and wrapping come from whatever opens it. JPEG records pixels with lossy compression. Rendering fixes the look of the text, including wrapping and font choice, and does not make it editable.

This page reads the file in the encoding it detects and draws it black on white in DejaVu Sans. It shows a limited number of lines, and a longer file stops with a note on the last line, so check the ending before sharing instructions or a transcript.

### Other ways to convert TXT to JPEG

- **ImageMagick:** `magick -background white -fill black -pointsize 20 -size 800x caption:@notes.txt notes.jpeg` wraps the file's text to 800 pixels. It needs an installed font, and some systems disable the `@file` form through a security policy. A trailing newline in the file adds a blank line.
- **GIMP:** choose Tools > Text, then pick the font from the list of installed fonts, and load the TXT with the folder icon in the Text Editor window and arrange it on the canvas. Export a .jpeg copy with File > Export As.
- **Inkscape plus GIMP:** type the text with the Text tool, set the font in Text > Text and Font, and export with File > Export PNG Image. Then open that PNG in GIMP and export a JPEG with File > Export As.

### Problems with TXT files

**Characters look wrong:** the wrong encoding can turn valid text into incorrect characters.

**Styling is gone:** a styled document loses its formatting once it is saved as TXT.

**No pictures or tables:** plain text cannot hold an image or table the way a word processor does.

guide.title: About TXT files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

Nothing but characters are held in a TXT file. There are no typographic commands in it, and it dictates no page layout, typeface or placement of pictures, so any editor on any operating system can read it. Its MIME label is text/plain, and the charset parameter tells a receiver how the bytes map to characters.

A styled document turns into plain text when it is saved as TXT, since TextEdit strips the styles and formatting when it converts rich text. What the characters look like is decided by whoever opens the file, not by the file.

### Programs that open TXT files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Visual Studio Code: a code editor that opens text files and lets you edit them.
- Vim: a text editor with Windows builds and documented Unix and macOS use.

**Mac**

- TextEdit: the Mac editor that works with plain text documents.

### TXT and JPG compared

- **What they store**: a TXT stores characters and line breaks. A JPG stores a grid of pixels, compressed with some loss, with an adjustable quality setting and no alpha transparency.
- **Look**: a TXT has no typeface of its own. A JPG fixes one, because the letters are already drawn into the picture.
- **Editing**: text in a TXT can be searched, copied and edited. Text in a JPG cannot be selected.
- **Support**: a TXT opens in any text editor, and a JPG is supported everywhere, so the picture is the safer choice when a destination takes only images.
- **Origin**: the Joint Photographic Experts Group defined JPG (ISO/IEC 10918-1) for photographs. The endings .jpg and .jpeg mean the same format.

Here is what the page does with your file. It decodes the bytes, drops terminal color codes and control characters, and turns each tab into spaces at stops every four characters. The text is then drawn on a canvas in your browser as dark text on white in DejaVu Sans. Lines that run long are folded at word breaks, and a single word wider than the page is cut. The picture is drawn at twice its size whenever it stays within 4,096 pixels a side, and the finished canvas is saved as a JPG at 0.85 quality. A text longer than one picture holds is cut, the last line of the picture says where, and the page shows the same notice. Your original TXT is not changed.

### Other ways to convert TXT to JPG

- **GIMP:** create an image and choose the Text tool. Turn on the editor window ("Use editor window") and load the TXT file with the folder icon in the text editor. Pick the font and size, drag a frame so the text fits, then use File > Export As and choose JPEG. GIMP puts the text on a new layer, and the size control offers several units. Check that no text runs off the canvas.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick -background white -fill black -pointsize 24 -size 800x caption:@notes.txt notes-card.jpg`. The caption: operator word-wraps long lines to the width you give with -size, and -font picks a typeface. The -pointsize option really controls the spacing between lines, newlines in the file act as paragraph separators, and -size is required so the wrapping has a width. A security policy can block reading text from a file.
- **Pillow (Python):** read the TXT with the right encoding, create a canvas with `Image.new` (its default color is black, so pass white), draw the lines with `ImageDraw.multiline_text` and a font, and call `save` with a .jpg name. Text containing newlines passed to `ImageDraw.text` is handed to `multiline_text`, and drawing changes the image in place. You decide the size, wrapping and page breaks.

### Problems with TXT files

- **Accented letters look odd**: a file read with the wrong encoding shows valid characters as the wrong ones. Re-save it as UTF-8.
- **Formatting disappeared**: a styled document saved as TXT loses its styling.
- **A table or image is missing**: plain text cannot preserve an image or table as a word processor would.
- **The text is very long**: a picture ends at 4,096 pixels, so a long log or manuscript is cut. Split the text into smaller files.
- **The converter reports an empty file**: a file with nothing but spaces and control characters leaves nothing to draw. Open it in an editor and check that the text is really there.

guide.title: About TXT and PDF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

A TXT file is plain text: characters and line endings, with no fonts, styles, tables or pictures. Its media type is text/plain, and a charset parameter says how the bytes stand for characters. Plain text carries no commands for typography and sets no page layout, which is why any editor on any system can open it and why the files stay small.

You find .txt files as notes, logs, readme files, exported data and the text of old documents. Because there is no layout, there is no page size either. That is the gap a PDF fills: it turns the same lines into fixed pages that print and look the same on every device.

Line endings differ by system, so a TXT may end its lines with CR LF, CR or LF. This page treats all three as a line break, along with NEL and the Unicode line and paragraph separators. It reads the encoding from a byte order mark when there is one: UTF-8 or UTF-16. Without one it tries UTF-8 and then Windows-1252.

### Programs that open TXT files

**Windows**

- Notepad: the format reference's first choice for plain text.

**Mac**

- TextEdit: handles plain text documents, including opening, editing and saving them.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Visual Studio Code: opens and edits text files in its editor.
- Vim: a text editor that runs on all three.

### TXT and PDF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .txt with text/plain, against .pdf with application/pdf.
- **Layout**: a TXT has none. A PDF is a set of fixed pages that look the same everywhere.
- **Fonts**: a TXT uses whatever font the viewer picks. A PDF embeds its fonts to keep its look.
- **Content**: a TXT holds text only. Beyond text, a PDF can carry vector graphics and images, along with links, bookmarks and forms.
- **Standards**: ISO adopted PDF 1.7 as ISO 32000-1 in 2008; PDF 2.0 followed as ISO 32000-2 in 2017.

This page sets your text on A4 portrait pages with 3/4 inch margins, in Courier at 10 pt with 12 pt between lines. That gives 61 lines to a page, each up to 81 characters, about what an 80-column printout holds. Nothing else is added.

Tabs stop at every fourth column, control characters and terminal escape sequences are dropped, and a line whose first letter is Hebrew or Arabic is set against the right margin, as an editor shows it. All-Windows-1252 text gets Courier; any other text gets DejaVu Sans, which has a wider range of letters but gives each its own width.

The PDF text is real text, not a picture of it, so a PDF reader can search and copy it.

### Other ways to convert TXT to PDF

- **TextEdit (Mac):** open the TXT, then choose File > Export as PDF. TextEdit lays the page out with its own settings, not a fixed grid of lines.
- **Adobe Acrobat:** use File > Create > PDF from File, change the file-type filter in the Open dialog so TXT files show, pick the file, press Open and save the result. The layout follows Acrobat's settings.

Use a word processor route when you want your own fonts, headers or page numbers.

### Problems with TXT files

- **Accents or symbols turn into odd characters**: the file was saved in a different encoding from the one it is read in. Re-save it as UTF-8.
- **A line is cut off in the PDF**: it is not cut. Lines longer than 81 characters wrap onto the next line, indented to match.
- **Text in Chinese, Japanese, Korean or emoji is refused**: the PDF font lacks those glyphs. Use TXT to PNG, which draws them.
- **The file is rejected as empty**: a file with only whitespace and control characters has nothing to set.
- **Tabs look narrow**: tabs stop every fourth column in the PDF, so a file written for eight-column tabs will look tighter than in your editor.
- **Columns drift**: the file has characters beyond Windows-1252, so the whole text was set in DejaVu Sans, where spaces do not line up columns. Remove those characters to get Courier.
- **A report keeps its page breaks only sometimes**: a form feed ends a page that has a line on it, but does nothing on a page with none.

guide.title: Understanding TXT and PNG
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

Nothing but plain text sits inside a TXT file: characters without fonts, styles or pictures, which is why every text editor on every operating system can read one. Its MIME label is text/plain. Plain text holds no typographic formatting commands and sets no page layout, font or placement of embedded images.

TXT is commonly used for notes and logs, configuration and readme files, and for exchanging text between programs. The bytes in a TXT file stand for characters through a character encoding, such as UTF-8, and the charset parameter tells a receiver which one. TextEdit on a Mac can convert rich text to TXT, and doing so removes the styles and formatting. A TXT file also can't keep an image or a table the way a word processor would.

### Programs that open TXT files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Visual Studio Code edits text files in its file-based editor, and Vim is another editor for plain text.
- **Windows:** Notepad is listed as able to open TXT.
- **Mac:** TextEdit opens, edits and saves plain text documents.
- **Web:** any web browser can open a text file.

### TXT and PNG compared

- **Extensions and types**: .txt with text/plain, and .png with image/png.
- **What each is**: a TXT file is characters. A PNG is a picture, so the words become pixels and can no longer be searched, selected or edited.
- **Compression**: PNG compression never loses data and uses DEFLATE.
- **Color**: a PNG can be indexed, grayscale or truecolor, with 1 to 16 bits per sample, plus an optional alpha channel for transparency.
- **History**: The aim behind PNG was a replacement for GIF free of patents. October 1996 saw it become the first format issued as a W3C Recommendation; ISO/IEC 15948 followed.
- **Structure**: a PNG file starts with a fixed signature and is then built from chunks, such as IHDR for the header, IDAT for image data and IEND to close the file.
- **Standard**: W3C made the third edition of the PNG specification a Recommendation on 24 June 2025.
- **Support**: every major browser displays PNG, and macOS saves screenshots as PNG files by default.

Your text is drawn in your browser, on a canvas. Letters are very dark gray on a white ground, set in DejaVu Sans: 16 pixels tall text, 24 pixels from one baseline to the next, and a 32 pixel margin around the block. A line breaks between words at 800 pixels, roughly 90 characters, and a word too long for one line is broken inside. Tabs stop every 4 characters. Control characters, terminal color codes among them, are stripped. The image is as wide as its longest line, and it is drawn at double size, which keeps zoomed-in text crisp, or smaller when the text is taller than 2048 pixels. A page holds at most 168 lines. Anything longer gets truncated; the image's final line says at which line it stopped, and the page displays a notice too.

DejaVu Sans covers Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew and Arabic. Other scripts fall back to your browser's own sans-serif font. The file is read as UTF-8, or UTF-16 when a byte order mark says so, and anything else is read as Windows-1252. Only the lines shown are measured, so a very long file is still drawn quickly. Select several TXT files and each is drawn into a PNG of its own, with your originals unchanged.

### Other ways to convert TXT to PNG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick text:notes.txt notes.png`. ImageMagick's text pages use a letter-size canvas of 612x792 pixels by default and don't wrap long lines, and too many lines give several pages and so several images.

### Problems with TXT files

- **Different systems, different looks**: plain text does not prescribe a page layout or a font, so the same TXT file can look different from one editor to the next.
- **Wrong characters**: choosing the wrong character encoding makes characters appear as others. Save the file as UTF-8 before converting.
- **Styling is gone**: saving a styled document as TXT discards its formatting, so the PNG has none either.
- **A table or picture is missing**: a text file holds no images or tables as a word processor document would.
- **Nothing to draw**: an empty file is refused with "This text file is empty: there's no text to draw."

guide.title: TXT files and SVG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

Plain text is what a TXT file holds: characters with no fonts, styles or images. Any text editor opens it, which is why it turns up as notes, logs, readme files and configuration. It has no page layout either, so turning it into a graphic means choosing a font, a width and margins.

The one thing a TXT file does carry is a character encoding such as UTF-8. A receiving program reads the bytes through that encoding, so the same file can show correct text in one program and wrong characters in another.

### Programs that open TXT files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Visual Studio Code opens and edits text files.
- Vim edits plain text.

**Mac:**

- TextEdit works on plain text files. Converting rich text to plain text there removes its styles and formatting.

### TXT and SVG compared

A TXT file is text/plain, with no layout of its own. An SVG is XML with the type image/svg+xml, and it can describe shapes, text and embedded pixel images.

This page uses the embedded picture. It draws your text on a canvas in DejaVu Sans, black on white, at 16 px on 24 px lines with 32 px margins, wrapped at 800 px, and wraps the resulting PNG in an SVG. The SVG holds no text and no paths, so its words cannot be selected or searched.

### Other ways to convert TXT to SVG

- **LibreOffice Draw:** click the page, choose Insert > File, select the TXT and click Insert, then click OK in the Insert Text dialog. Choose File > Export, select SVG as the file type and save. SVG shows no options dialog on export.
- **ImageMagick with Inkscape:** run `magick -size 800x -pointsize 16 caption:@note.txt note.png` to draw the text file as a PNG. Import the PNG into Inkscape with File > Import, choose the embed option and save the result as SVG. This also gives pixels, not text.

### Problems with TXT files

- **Strange characters**: the encoding was guessed wrongly. Save the file as UTF-8.
- **Formatting disappeared**: plain text never held any. A TXT file keeps no formatting from a styled document.
- **An image or table is missing**: a plain text file has no place to hold a picture or a table.

seo.howToHeading: How to convert video to GIF

faqs.question: How do I convert a video to a GIF?
faqs.answer: Pick an MP4 in the converter above. FFmpeg, running inside this browser tab, keeps 15 frames a second, shrinks the picture to 480 px at most, builds a 256-color palette from the clip and saves a looping GIF.

faqs.question: How do I turn a video into a GIF online for free?
faqs.answer: Use this page. It asks for no sign-up, and the clip isn't uploaded: the work happens on your own device, so the wait depends on your computer or phone.

faqs.question: How do I make a GIF from just part of a video?
faqs.answer: This page converts the whole file; its command has no start or end setting. Cut the moment you want first, then convert the shorter clip.

faqs.question: Which video formats can I use here?
faqs.answer: The file picker accepts .mp4. For MOV, WebM, AVI or MKV video, use the [MOV to GIF](/mov-to-gif/), [WebM to GIF](/webm-to-gif/), [AVI to GIF](/avi-to-gif/) or [MKV to GIF](/mkv-to-gif/) converter.

faqs.question: Is the GIF high quality?
faqs.answer: It suits short, small clips: 480 px on the longer side at most, 15 frames a second and 256 colors per image. Fine text, fast motion and soft gradients lose the most.

faqs.question: Can I change the GIF's size, speed or frame rate?
faqs.answer: Not here. Every GIF is made with the same settings. For other values, use FFmpeg or a video editor where you choose them yourself.

faqs.question: How long can the video be?
faqs.answer: No limit is set by the page itself. Every second adds 15 images to the GIF, so a few seconds make a handy file and a long clip makes a heavy one.

faqs.question: Does the GIF play on repeat?
faqs.answer: Yes. The conversion command sets the GIF to loop forever.

faqs.question: What happens to the sound?
faqs.answer: It is left out. The GIF holds pictures only, so the result is silent.

faqs.question: Does the converter work on a phone?
faqs.answer: The page runs in a phone browser like any other. How large a file a phone can convert depends on the device.

points: The GIF keeps 15 frames a second, whatever the video's frame rate.

guide.title: About video to GIF
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

The MPEG-4 Part 14 specification, ISO/IEC 14496-14, defines MP4 and dates from 2003. A typical MP4 holds H.264 video and AAC audio, yet containers of this kind take AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus too. The ISO Base Media File Format underlies MP4, and QuickTime is where that format came from. An MP4 consists of nested boxes, which QuickTime calls atoms.

Video uses the endings .mp4 or .m4v, while MPEG-4 files with audio alone often end in .m4a. The registered media types are video/mp4 and audio/mp4, and every major browser plays MP4. It turns up in online video, recordings from phones and cameras, and shared clips. Its properties include subtitles and chapters, and the usual video codecs are H.264, H.265 and AV1.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Mobile, Windows, Mac and Linux**

- VLC: plays MP4, MOV and 3GP among its input formats. On phones there are VLC for Android and VLC for iOS, and the container's contents decide what they can decode.

**Linux, Mac and Windows**

- mpv: plays on the desktop and lets you select among its audio and subtitle streams.
- ffplay: the FFmpeg project's own player, which comes with FFmpeg itself, alongside the ffmpeg tool.

**Windows and Mac**

- Adobe Premiere: imports the container if a suitable decoder is installed.

**Windows**

- Windows Media Player: opens MP4 files.

**Mac**

- QuickTime Player: can play MP4 files.

**Web**

- Firefox and Chrome: play supported MP4 directly. The codec inside still matters.

### MP4 and GIF compared

- **Origin**: CompuServe introduced GIF in 1987. GIF89a, from July 1990, introduced extensions covering transparency, timing between frames, comments and application data.
- **Color**: palettes in a GIF image are capped at 256 colors. Transparency designates a single palette entry as fully clear, and nothing is partly transparent.
- **Compression**: GIF uses lossless LZW coding for its images. Unisys started charging for LZW licenses in 1994. In the US the patent ran out in 2003; the European and Japanese ones followed in 2004.
- **Animation**: many images can be stored in one GIF, each with its own delay set in hundredths of a second.
- **Sound**: an MP4 can carry audio. The GIF made here holds pictures only.
- **Uses**: short looping animations, simple graphics, icons, reaction images and stickers suit GIF.
- **Editors**: GIMP can save a multi-layer image as an animated GIF that loops forever, cutting the colors to 256 at most.
- **Support**: All major browsers display GIF; the media type is image/gif.

Process here: on your device, FFmpeg scans the clip once to build a palette and then writes the GIF with it in a second pass. It keeps 15 frames a second and limits the longer side to 480 px, rounding both sides down to an even number. A smaller video is not scaled up. The command also deinterlaces frames marked as interlaced, and sets the GIF to loop forever. FFmpeg runs as WebAssembly in a worker in your browser, so nothing is uploaded. The page has no size or time limit of its own, and a long file simply takes as long as your device needs.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to GIF

- **Microsoft Clipchamp (Windows, web):** put the video in a project, click Export at the top right and pick GIF. Clipchamp offers the GIF export only for videos up to 15 seconds long and accepts MP4 among its containers.
- **FFmpeg (any platform):** the command `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.gif` writes a GIF. FFmpeg's GIF muxer loops forever by default, and a frame delay cannot be shorter than one hundredth of a second. This plain command skips the palette step this page uses.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **A player can't show the video**: opening MP4 files doesn't guarantee that a player can decode what is inside.
- **The GIF is too heavy to post**: shorten the clip before converting. Every second adds 15 images, so the file grows with its length.
- **The GIF looks grainy**: each GIF image is limited to 256 colors, which can alter smooth gradients.
- **Your file isn't an MP4**: the file picker takes .mp4 only, so a clip in another container needs its own converter.
- **Your video is another type**: try [MOV to GIF](/mov-to-gif/), or the WebM, AVI and MKV pages.

guide.title: About VOB files
guide.markdown:
### What is a VOB file?

DVD Video Object is what VOB stands for. Producers of DVDs keep a disc's video, sound and menus in VOB streams, which are closely related to MPEG-2 program-stream material. One file can hold up to 1 GB.

A DVD backup commonly places those files in a VIDEO_TS directory. DVD authoring also needs companion IFO and BUP files that tell a player how the pieces fit together. People meet VOB when they rip a DVD into files.

### Programs that open VOB files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- VLC: can open DVD-Video discs and MPEG program-stream files.
- HandBrake: accepts VOB files as well as VIDEO_TS disc folders, so long as nothing on the disc is protected.

### VOB and AVI compared

- **Container**: a VOB is an MPEG-2 program stream. An AVI is RIFF-based, was introduced by Microsoft in 1992 and can hold many codecs.
- **Streams**: a VOB can carry several audio streams. An AVI interleaves video and audio.
- **Position on a disc**: VOB files sit in the VIDEO_TS folder alongside IFO and BUP files. An AVI stands alone.
- **Players**: AVI files open in Windows Media Player, in VLC media player and in QuickTime Player.

The page hands the VOB to FFmpeg, which writes MPEG-4 for the picture and MP3 for the sound inside an AVI container.

### Other ways to convert VOB to AVI

- **Avidemux:** open the VOB with File > Open and let Avidemux index it. Choose MPEG-4 ASP (Xvid) video, MP3 (LAME) audio and the AVI output format, then use File > Save > Save Video. The program's own tutorial recommends two-pass encoding.
- **FFmpeg:** run ffmpeg -i segment.vob -c:a libmp3lame -c:v mpeg4 segment-copy.avi. FFmpeg's format list includes MPEG-PS input, and both streams are encoded afresh.

### Problems with VOB files

- **A protected disc**: a VOB may be encrypted with CSS. HandBrake does not process copy-protected DVD sources.
- **A loose file does not make a disc**: one VOB on its own does not replace the whole DVD structure that authoring needs.
- **A clip from the wrong title**: one disc can hold several titles, so picking the wrong one gives you the wrong footage in the AVI.

faqs.question: What is the MKV file called?

faqs.question: Why is my MKV only part of the movie?

faqs.question: Does the MKV keep the original resolution and frame rate?
faqs.answer: Small pictures and slow rates stay as they were. Oversized frames shrink, a source above the rate cap drops frames yet plays for the same time, and a side measuring an odd number of pixels is trimmed by one.

faqs.question: What happens to interlaced DVD video?
faqs.answer: The converter runs FFmpeg's yadif filter on frames flagged as interlaced, which smooths the comb-like lines on moving edges. Frames that are not flagged pass through untouched.

faqs.question: Why not just rename .vob to .mkv?
faqs.answer: A rename touches only the name, so the data inside is still a DVD program stream. Converting writes genuine Matroska, and the page tests the output to confirm it.

guide.title: Understanding VOB to MKV
guide.markdown:
### What is a VOB file?

The letters stand for DVD Video Object, the container that holds a disc's video, sound, subtitles and menus. It is closely related to the MPEG-2 program stream, and CSS encryption may be applied. Copies of a disc usually sit in a VIDEO_TS folder next to IFO and BUP companion files, and a lengthy title is divided among VOBs of up to 1 GB each.

### Programs that open VOB files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC can play discs in the DVD Video layout along with MPEG program streams. HandBrake accepts either a single VOB or an entire VIDEO_TS folder, so long as nothing on the source is protected.

### VOB and MKV compared

Matroska is a free, open container with space for as many video, audio, picture and subtitle tracks as you like, plus chapters and metadata. Nearly any codec fits, so the contents decide how it plays. It suits Blu-ray rips and films with many soundtracks, WebM is a subset of it, and a VOB by contrast follows the DVD-Video layout.

Here the MKV holds H.264 picture and AAC sound at 96 kbps, made with a fast preset. Interlaced frames are cleaned up by the yadif filter. A picture over 1920 pixels on the long side is scaled down, motion above 30 frames per second is thinned to 30, and both dimensions end up even. Nothing is scaled up and no rate is raised.

### Other ways to convert VOB to MKV

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i title.vob -c:v libx264 -c:a aac title.mkv` writes H.264 and AAC into Matroska. Add `-map` options when a disc has several soundtracks.
- **HandBrake:** use Open Source to pick the VOB or the whole VIDEO_TS folder, choose a title with the Title control if the source holds several clips, set the container to MKV and encode.
- **Prism for Windows:** add the VOB, choose MKV as the Output Format, review Encoder Options and press Convert.

### Problems with VOB files

- A short result tends to mean one numbered piece was converted, so run all of them.
- A disc often holds several titles, and the wrong choice gives the wrong clip.
- One VOB on its own cannot stand in for the full DVD structure that authoring needs.
- Some MPEG-2 players ignore the subtitle streams of a DVD.
- HandBrake does not defeat copy protection of any kind, so a protected disc has to be handled with other software.

faqs.question: Is interlaced DVD video fixed?

guide.title: VOB files and MOV output
guide.markdown:
### What is a VOB file?

VOB is the DVD Video Object. A DVD-Video disc keeps its video, sound, text overlays and menus inside VOB streams, which are based on the MPEG-2 program stream. A disc copy usually puts them in a VIDEO_TS folder next to companion IFO and BUP files, and a loose VOB does not replace that structure. A VOB file on a disc is limited to 1 GB, so a long film is split across several of them. People meet VOB files when ripping DVDs to files, and a disc can hold several titles, so choosing the wrong one gives the wrong clip.

### Programs that open VOB files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC media player reads DVD-Video media and MPEG program streams.
- HandBrake accepts VOB files as well as complete VIDEO_TS disc folders. Its input must be unprotected.

### VOB and MOV compared

A VOB is a DVD container with several audio and text-overlay streams, and some discs are encrypted with CSS. A MOV is Apple's QuickTime container, registered as video/quicktime, with the extension .mov or .qt. It holds video, audio, text and timecode tracks, and many codecs including H.264 and ProRes. The QuickTime format was the basis for the MPEG-4 file format, but MOV and MP4 are separate formats.

This page decodes the VOB and writes new H.264 video and AAC sound into a MOV, so it is not a copy of the DVD streams. Frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced. The picture may be 1920 px on its longer side at most, and the frame rate may be 30 fps at most.

### Other ways to convert VOB to MOV

- **FFmpeg, H.264 and AAC:** run `ffmpeg -i scene.vob -c:a aac -b:a 192k -c:v libx264 -crf 21 scene.mov` to re-encode both streams.
- **FFmpeg, stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i scene.vob -c copy scene-copy.mov`. Stream copy passes the packets through without decoding or encoding.
- **FFmpeg, ProRes:** run `ffmpeg -i scene.vob -c:v prores_ks scene-edit.mov` to encode the video as ProRes, one of the codecs a MOV can hold.

### Problems with VOB files

- **The clip is too short**: you chose one segment, or the wrong title on a disc with several.
- **No menus**: they are part of the DVD structure, which a loose VOB lacks.
- **Overlays missing**: a player that plays MPEG-2 video can still skip the DVD text overlays, which can be bitmap images rather than text.
- **A protected disc fails**: HandBrake does not process copy-protected DVD sources.

guide.title: Understanding VOB to MP3
guide.markdown:
### What is a VOB file?

VOB means DVD Video Object. Discs keep picture, audio, subtitles and menus inside these files, which are tied to MPEG-2 program streams. They are normally found in a VIDEO_TS folder beside IFO and BUP files. CSS may encrypt them, and with a limit of 1 GB per file, a long title runs across several VOBs.

### Programs that open VOB files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Either a lone VOB or a whole VIDEO_TS folder opens in HandBrake when the source has no protection. VLC plays DVD Video media as well as MPEG program streams.

### VOB and MP3 compared

A VOB bundles picture, sound and subtitles, and can carry several audio and subtitle streams. MP3 stores sound alone. Its full name is MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, and the ISO/IEC 11172-3 standard of 1993 grew out of work at Fraunhofer IIS and elsewhere in the MPEG audio group.

MP3 is lossy. A model of human hearing picks out sound that listeners are unlikely to notice, and that sound is thrown away. Song titles and other tags are stored apart, in ID3 structures, and every major browser plays MP3.

This page drops the video and encodes the soundtrack with the LAME encoder, asking for 192 kbps. Audio sampled under 32 kHz falls short of that rate and is written lower.

### Other ways to convert VOB to MP3

- **Switch:** add the VOB, set the Output Format to MP3, adjust Encoder Options if you like and press Convert. Switch lists VOB among its input formats.
- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i chapter.vob -vn -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k chapter.mp3` does the same job as this page. Add `-map` when you need a specific audio track.

### Problems with VOB files

- If the audio ends early, you probably converted a single numbered piece; run the rest too.
- A disc may hold more than one title, so check you chose the right one.
- A lone VOB lacks the wider DVD structure that authoring relies on.
- A player may handle the MPEG-2 video but skip DVD subtitle streams.
- Protected discs need other software, because HandBrake leaves copy protection alone.

faqs.question: Can I join all the VOB files of a DVD into one MP4?

faqs.question: Which VOB files should I convert from the VIDEO_TS folder?
faqs.answer: A disc can hold several titles, and menu content is stored in VOB streams too. Play the files in VLC to see which hold the movie, then convert those. Choosing the wrong title gives the wrong clip.

faqs.question: Do I need the IFO and BUP files?
faqs.answer: No. The page converts the VOB you choose and nothing beside it. The IFO and BUP files that sit with it in VIDEO_TS are used for DVD authoring, not for this conversion.

faqs.question: What happens to the DVD menus?
faqs.answer: The MP4 is a single video file with no menus or disc navigation, because a VOB holds only a piece of the disc's streams, not its structure. To pick a title or scene, choose the VOB that holds it before you convert.

faqs.question: Why does my VOB look striped when it plays?
faqs.answer: A DVD VOB is often interlaced, with every frame made of two fields. Frames flagged that way are deinterlaced during conversion, so motion in the MP4 should play without comb lines.

faqs.question: How large will the MP4 be?

guide.title: Understanding VOB for MP4 output
guide.markdown:
### What is a VOB file?

VOB stands for DVD Video Object. DVD producers store the video, sound, subtitles and menu content of a disc in VOB streams, and the data is closely related to MPEG-2 program-stream material. A VOB can carry several audio and subtitle streams, and it may be encrypted with CSS.

A DVD backup commonly puts the VOB files inside a folder named VIDEO_TS, next to IFO and BUP files that DVD authoring also needs. You meet VOB files on DVD-Video discs and when you rip a disc to files. A single VOB holds up to 1 GB, so a movie longer than that is spread over several, and a disc can hold several titles.

Because a VOB is MPEG-2 material built for a disc, it is awkward outside a player that understands DVDs. Converting the VOBs you want to keep to MP4 gives you ordinary video files that play on nearly every device.

### Programs that open VOB files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- VLC reads DVD Video media and MPEG program streams.
- HandBrake: opens VOB files and whole VIDEO_TS disc folders, as long as the source is unprotected. Its Title control picks which clip of a multi-clip source, such as a DVD, to use, and it does not defeat copy protection of any kind.

**Windows**

- MPC-HC opens VOB files.
- Windows Media Player opens a VOB when the right codecs are installed.

### VOB and MP4 compared

- **Extensions**: a VOB ends in .vob and sits in a VIDEO_TS folder. An MP4 ends in .mp4 and follows ISO/IEC 14496-14.
- **Format family**: a VOB is built on the MPEG-2 program stream, which FFmpeg's format list names as MPEG-PS, also known as VOB.
- **Streams**: a VOB can hold multiple audio and subtitle streams, and the MP4 container is built for several codecs plus subtitles and chapters.
- **Structure**: a VOB belongs to a set. The IFO and BUP files beside it support DVD authoring. An MP4 is one self-contained file.
- **Subtitles**: DVD subtitle streams can contain bitmap images rather than searchable text.
- **Support**: nearly every device and web browser accepts an MP4, whereas a VOB needs a DVD-aware or MPEG-capable player.
- **Quality**: the MP4 is built from the decoded VOB, so the picture goes through lossy compression a second time.

The VOB is decoded and re-encoded here, with H.264 for the picture and 96 kbps AAC for the sound, and the encoder favors speed over fine detail. Frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced, so motion does not comb. A frame up to 1920 px on the longer side keeps its size, apart from rounding each side down to an even number, and a larger frame is scaled down. Video above 30 fps has frames dropped. Several VOBs chosen together are converted one after another, each into its own MP4 named after its VOB. The VOB you choose is left untouched.

### Other ways to convert VOB to MP4

- **FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** use `ffmpeg -i clip.vob -c:v libx264 -c:a aac dvd-viewing.mp4`. FFmpeg's format list calls the MPEG program stream the format also known as VOB. The -i flag is the source file, and -c:v and -c:a pick the video and audio encoders, libx264 and aac. If you add nothing else, FFmpeg picks the streams on its own, so the output is not what this page makes.

### Problems with VOB files

- **Only part of the movie plays**: a VOB tops out at 1 GB, so a longer movie runs across several. Convert each one you want and play the MP4s in order.
- **Wrong clip**: a disc source may contain several titles, and choosing the wrong one produces the wrong clip. Check which VOBs belong to the title you want.
- **Copy-protected disc**: HandBrake does not process copy-protected DVD sources, and the format reference notes a VOB may be encrypted with CSS.
- **Menus do not play**: a loose VOB does not replace the full DVD structure, and an MP4 has no disc menus at all.
- **Subtitles missing in a player**: DVD subtitles can be bitmap images, and a player that handles MPEG-2 video may still ignore them.
- **Combing on moving edges**: DVD video is commonly interlaced. Converting here deinterlaces frames flagged that way.

guide.title: About WAV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

Sound stored in a WAV file sits inside a RIFF wrapper, so WAV names a container, not a single way of encoding audio. The August 1991 multimedia specification from Microsoft and IBM described it. Most WAV files contain linear PCM, the plain sampled form, but other encodings can ride in the same wrapper, which means two .wav files can differ a great deal inside. You will see audio/wav and audio/x-wav used as media types.

PCM is uncompressed, which makes WAV files big but exact. Broadcast WAVE is the variant that holds metadata used in production and in preservation, and the Library of Congress names WAVE among the formats it recommends for audio collections. Keeping a WAV master and making an AAC for listening is a common split. The usual filename ending is .wav.

### Programs that open WAV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Audacity: opens most WAV recordings, including PCM variants.
- ffplay: the player bundled with FFmpeg, which includes a WAV demuxer and plays WAV files from the command line.

**Mobile**

- Firefox for Android: plays WAV, which Mozilla lists among its supported Android audio types.
- VLC for Android: a free media player for Android phones and tablets, whose decoding follows from the media inside the container.
- mpv for Android: an Android port linked by the mpv project.

### WAV and AAC compared

- **Encoding**: WAV is a wrapper that usually holds uncompressed linear PCM. AAC is a perceptual, lossy codec, standardized as MPEG-2 Part 7 and MPEG-4 Part 3.
- **Packaging**: AAC can be carried in MP4, QuickTime or other wrappers. A freestanding .aac file normally uses ADTS framing and is labeled audio/aac.
- **Profiles**: AAC comes as LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2.
- **Quality**: linear PCM in a WAV is lossless. AAC discards detail in exchange for a compressed stream, and was standardized as the successor to MP3.
- **Use**: WAV suits recording and editing masters. AAC is used for streaming audio and end-user delivery.

On this page, FFmpeg runs inside your browser as WebAssembly and nothing is uploaded. It ignores any video, encodes the audio with its own AAC encoder at 192 kbps and writes an ADTS stream. No sample rate, channel count, trim or volume change is set by the command. A batch of WAV files is processed one by one, and each result is a separate .aac named after its WAV. Your original WAV stays unchanged. The codec is lossy, so converting the AAC back to WAV later will not restore the audio: encode from the original WAV, and avoid editing and re-encoding the AAC again and again.

The AAC comes out as a freestanding ADTS stream. FFmpeg's ADTS muxer accepts a single AAC stream, which is why the audio is written alone, and an app that wants an MP4 wrapper should be given the M4A converter's output instead.

### Other ways to convert WAV to AAC

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i session.wav -vn -c:a aac -b:a 192k session-listen.aac` on the command line. Here -vn drops video, -c:a aac selects FFmpeg's own AAC encoder and -b:a fixes the bitrate. Add a sample rate or channel option when a delivery spec calls for one.
- **Audacity with FFmpeg:** load the WAV, open File > Export Audio and pick Custom FFmpeg Export. In the format options choose a format and an AAC codec, which depends on how FFmpeg was built. This needs Audacity's optional FFmpeg library.
- **WavePad:** open the WAV and choose File > Save As, then pick AAC. NCH lists AAC writing for Windows and Mac. Because AAC is lossy, avoid repeated editing generations of the same file.

### Problems with WAV files

- **Import fails**: some recorders put proprietary compression into the WAV, a case where Audacity suggests installing its FFmpeg library.
- **A very large recording**: the original RIFF size fields top out near 4 GB, so recordings past them may need RF64, and a program built for the old layout may not handle such a file.
- **Tags are missing or odd**: tags kept in INFO chunks and in Broadcast WAVE extensions differ, so programs treat metadata differently.
- **One WAV opens and another does not**: WAV can wrap PCM or compressed audio, so programs differ in what they accept.

guide.title: Understanding WAV and AIFF
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

WAV (also written WAVE) stands for Waveform Audio File Format. Microsoft and IBM built it on the RIFF container and described it in a multimedia specification published in August 1991. The file wraps sound but does not fix one encoding, and linear PCM is the usual contents, which makes a WAV big and exact, though compressed audio can sit inside as well.

A program therefore needs a decoder that matches whatever the WAV holds. Files end in .wav, and audio/wav and audio/x-wav are the media types you will see. A Broadcast WAVE variant carries production and archiving metadata, and the US Library of Congress names WAVE as its recommended format for digital sound collections. The size fields in the original design limit a file to 4 GB; longer recordings may use RF64.

### Programs that open WAV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports most WAV recordings, including PCM variants, and ffplay, which ships with FFmpeg, plays a WAV through FFmpeg's WAV demuxer.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media itself, and Mozilla's list of audio types for Firefox on Android includes WAV.
- **Mobile:** The free VLC app on Android decodes according to what the file contains, while mpv on Android, a port linked by the mpv project, plays it too.

### WAV and AIFF compared

- **Extensions and types**: .wav with audio/wav, and .aiff or .aif with audio/aiff or audio/x-aiff.
- **Origins**: WAV came from Microsoft and IBM in 1991. Apple developed AIFF in 1988.
- **Container**: AIFF is derived from Electronic Arts' IFF family. WAV is derived from RIFF.
- **Sound**: both usually carry uncompressed linear PCM. AIFF-C extends the family to compressed audio.
- **Metadata**: AIFF can include named chunks for author, copyright and annotations.
- **Use**: professional audio users use AIFF for masters and intermediate recordings.
- **Opening the AIFF**: Audacity can import most AIFF files, and every PCM variant, without its optional FFmpeg library. Adobe Audition will open uncompressed AIFF too, along with the common compressed variants.
- **Specification**: Apple dated version 1.3 of the AIFF specification January 4, 1989.
- **Size**: WAV and AIFF files are limited to 4 GB, a general restriction and not an Audacity one. Many players are said to manage only files up to 2 GB.
- **CDs**: Audacity's manual says AIFF is suitable for burning an exported file to an audio CD.

Your WAV goes through FFmpeg in your browser, which writes the sound as 16-bit PCM in an AIFF file with the bytes in big-endian order. That is plain, uncompressed audio like the WAV's, so a 16-bit WAV keeps its samples. A WAV that holds 24-bit or floating-point audio is written at 16 bits. Only audio is written, since the command leaves out any video stream, and your original WAV is left as it was; the AIFF is a new file you download. Choose several WAVs and they convert one after another. If the conversion fails, the message names FFmpeg and gives its exit code.

### Other ways to convert WAV to AIFF

- **FFmpeg from a terminal:** run `ffmpeg -i session.wav -c:a pcm_s16be listening.aiff`.
- **Audacity:** load the WAV, open the Export Audio dialog, select the AIFF 16-bit PCM format (it has no options) and save. AIFF files are capped at 4 GB, a limit of the format itself.

### Problems with WAV files

- **It won't open**: the WAV may carry a proprietary compression from the recorder. Audacity recommends its FFmpeg library for importing such files.
- **A player opens one WAV and not another**: linear PCM or compressed audio can sit inside a WAV, so a program that plays one WAV can still refuse another.
- **The file is huge**: raw PCM needs more room than a delivery copy of the recording in compressed form.
- **A recording over 4 GB**: the original RIFF size fields can't describe it, and very large recordings may require RF64.
- **Tags look different afterward**: the INFO chunks of a WAV and the Broadcast WAVE extensions store different information, so programs treat metadata in different ways.
- **An author field looks misplaced**: Adobe Audition may show an AIFF author field as Dublin Core: Creator rather than as Author.
- **An AIFF-C won't play**: it needs a decoder for its particular encoding; knowing the family name does not guarantee support.

guide.title: WAV to AMR: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

A WAV does not name one audio encoding; it is a RIFF-based container for sound. Microsoft and IBM wrote the format down in a multimedia specification dated August 1991. Most files carry linear PCM, although a compressed encoding can sit inside as well. Expect the .wav ending, with audio/wav and audio/x-wav as the usual media-type labels. For production and preservation work there is the Broadcast WAVE extension, which adds metadata, and the Library of Congress recommends WAVE when building digital audio collections.

### Programs that open WAV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity brings in most WAV recordings, PCM variants included.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay, because FFmpeg has a demuxer for this format.
- **Web:** Firefox plays WAV directly in the browser.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android, a free media player.

### WAV and AMR compared

Adaptive Multi-Rate is what AMR stands for. ETSI standardized it to carry GSM speech, after which 3GPP chose it for third-generation cellular networks. In the narrowband codec, speech is sampled at 8 kHz and coded in 20-millisecond frames, with eight modes running from 4.75 up to 12.2 kbps. The separate AMR-WB codec samples at 16 kHz, so a narrowband recording cannot supply AMR-WB's wider frequency range. The two also keep different storage signatures. RFC 4867 covers storage files, and audio/AMR is the narrowband media type.

No AMR file comes out of this page. The FFmpeg command it runs requests the libopencore_amrnb encoder, the FFmpeg inside the browser lacks that encoder, and the attempt ends in an unknown encoder error.

### Other ways to convert WAV to AMR

- **Switch Sound File Converter:** select the WAV with Add, set the Output Format field to amr and press Convert. Its supported-formats list names wav as an input and amr as an output.

### Problems with WAV files

- **A WAV that won't open:** recorders sometimes put proprietary compression inside the WAV, and for importing those Audacity recommends its FFmpeg library.
- **Very large recordings:** the original RIFF size fields can fall short, and RF64 takes over.
- **Tags vary by program:** standard INFO chunks hold different information from Broadcast WAVE extensions.
