guide.title: About WAV and FLAC
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

WAV is a RIFF-based wrapper for sound, not one particular audio encoding. Microsoft and IBM documented the format in their August 1991 multimedia specification, and Broadcast WAVE later extended it with metadata for production and preservation. Linear PCM is the common payload, so files are large but exact, although compressed encodings can appear inside a WAV too. The usual filename ending is .wav, and audio/wav and audio/x-wav are common media-type labels.

Because it keeps every sample, WAV serves for recording, editing, studio work and uncompressed masters. The Library of Congress also lists WAVE as a recommended format for digital audio collections. The cost is storage: a WAV records every sample at a steady rate whether the sound is music, silence or room noise.

### Programs that open WAV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity brings in PCM WAV files of most kinds.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay, the player from FFmpeg, plays WAV through FFmpeg's demuxer.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly, and Mozilla lists WAV among the audio file types Firefox for Android supports.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android decodes whatever the file holds, and mpv for Android plays it too.

### WAV and FLAC compared

WAV names a container, while FLAC names a lossless codec. FLAC compresses integer PCM audio without discarding sample information. The specification is open, with an open-source reference implementation, and RFC 9639 standardized the format in December 2024.

- **Extensions and media types:** .wav with audio/wav; .flac with audio/flac.
- **Compression:** none for PCM WAV; lossless for FLAC.
- **Channels and depth:** FLAC supports one through eight channels and sample depths from four through 32 bits.
- **Metadata:** WAV uses INFO chunks or Broadcast WAVE extensions, which store different information. FLAC uses Vorbis comments, seek points and pictures.

Converting here runs FFmpeg's FLAC encoder on the WAV and drops any video stream. The page sets no quality option, because lossless output has none to set. Title, artist and album tags are copied across where FLAC has a field for them. The saved file keeps your WAV's name with .flac in place of .wav, and the WAV is not touched.

The FLAC can be smaller. How much smaller depends on the recording, and a dense or noisy one compresses less than a quiet one. Choose WAV when the next program in your chain reads only WAV, and FLAC when you want the same samples in a smaller file.

### Other ways to convert WAV to FLAC

- **Audacity:** open the recording, choose File > Export Audio, and pick FLAC in the format list. FLAC is one of the formats Audacity writes without its optional FFmpeg library. Audacity can also edit or mix the recording before it exports, which changes the signal the encoder receives.
- **The flac command-line tool:** run `flac recording.wav`. It reads WAVE input and writes the .flac file beside it. The tool supports linear PCM only, from 4 to 32 bits per sample, so it will not take a WAV with another encoding. Run `flac --test recording.flac` afterward to check the stream.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i recording.wav -c:a flac recording.flac`. This is the same encoder the page uses, and it leaves you free to add options.

### Problems with WAV files

**Audacity cannot import it:** a recorder can wrap proprietary compression in the WAV, and Audacity suggests its optional FFmpeg library for those files.

**A very long recording will not open:** the original WAV layout caps files at 4 GB, so long captures may use RF64 in place of the old RIFF size fields. Use software that understands the recorder's variant.

**Notes from the recorder look different:** a WAV keeps text details in INFO chunks or Broadcast WAVE extensions, so what survives depends on how the recorder wrote them. Inspect them in a tagger before relying on them.

**A player opens the file but plays nothing useful:** a .wav ending does not tell you what the samples are, so check which encoding the file holds before assuming a damaged file.

**A WAV made from a lossy file:** when the WAV was decoded from an MP3 or similar, the detail is already gone, and FLAC cannot bring back samples that were discarded earlier.

guide.title: About WAV and M4A
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

A WAV keeps its sound in the RIFF layout laid out by Microsoft and IBM in an August 1991 multimedia specification. The usual payload is linear PCM, which stores every sample, but compressed encodings can sit inside a WAV as well, so the ending alone does not say what the audio is. Studios and field recorders rely on WAV as a master that is made before any compression, and Broadcast WAVE adds production and preservation metadata on top.

Converting a finished WAV to M4A is a delivery step, not an editing step. A long interview or rehearsal becomes a small listening file, while the WAV stays in your archive for any later work.

### Programs that open WAV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity opens nearly every PCM WAV and lets you edit the waveform first.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay plays a WAV.
- **Web:** Firefox handles WAV directly, and so does its Android edition.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android relies on the codec inside the file, while mpv for Android must be built with the matching demuxer and decoder.

### WAV and M4A compared

The M4A ending marks an audio-only MPEG-4 file, a label Apple chose for its unprotected music. The sound inside is usually AAC, a lossy codec from MPEG-4 Part 3, though Apple Lossless (ALAC) can sit in the same kind of file. A PCM WAV is uncompressed, while AAC discards what listeners are least likely to miss. Apple used it for iTunes songs, and it was meant to beat MP3 at the same bitrate.

- **Extensions and media types:** .wav; .m4a with audio/mp4.
- **Compression:** none for PCM WAV; lossy for AAC.
- **Metadata:** the M4A can carry tags and cover art.
- **Editing:** a WAV passes through editors without another lossy encode, while each save as AAC re-encodes.

FFmpeg encodes the AAC here at 192 kbps and drops any video. The page applies no noise reduction and no loudness change, so a quiet or noisy recording stays quiet or noisy. Do any cleanup on the WAV master first, then make the M4A once. Title, artist and album tags are copied across. The saved file borrows your WAV's name with .m4a on the end, and queued WAVs each give their own M4A.

Converting the M4A back to WAV later expands the decoded audio without undoing what the AAC step discarded. If the WAV itself came from a lossy source, this adds another encoding stage on top. Apple Lossless is not written by this page; the FFmpeg route below can write it. Choose M4A for a small listening copy, and keep WAV for files that will pass through further editing.

### Other ways to convert WAV to M4A

- **Audacity:** load the WAV, then pick File > Export Audio and M4A (AAC) from the format dropdown. Audacity offers this output only through its optional FFmpeg library. The editor can also mix tracks or change project settings before it writes the file.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** `ffmpeg -i take.wav -c:a aac -b:a 192k take.m4a` is the same codec and bitrate the page uses, and you can change either.
- **FFmpeg, lossless:** `ffmpeg -i take.wav -c:a alac take.m4a` writes Apple Lossless instead. FFmpeg lists ALAC among the audio codecs it can encode, and the file stays an M4A.

### Problems with WAV files

**Audacity or another editor will not take it:** some recorders put proprietary compression inside the WAV, which Audacity handles better with its optional FFmpeg library. Play the sound in a player before you convert.

**A very long recording is cut or refused:** a classic WAV tops out at 4 GB, so a bigger capture needs RF64 where the old RIFF size fields fall short.

**The recorder's notes look different:** wording and fields written by one recorder may not match another's, because a WAV can use INFO chunks or Broadcast WAVE extensions. Look at the result in a tagger afterward.

**The WAV was ripped from compressed audio:** if the samples were produced by decoding earlier compressed audio, the detail is already thinned out, and encoding to AAC thins it a further time.

**Clipping or background noise is still there:** converting does not repair a recording. Fix it in an editor on the WAV, then convert.

guide.title: About WAV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

WAVE audio files, written .wav, use the RIFF chunk structure. Microsoft and IBM published the layout in a 1991 multimedia specification, and it describes a wrapper rather than a fixed encoding. Linear PCM is what you will usually find inside. Compressed audio is allowed too, so the extension alone cannot tell you what a given file holds. Common media types are audio/wav and audio/x-wav.

A variant called Broadcast WAVE carries extra metadata for production and preservation. The Library of Congress recommends the format for audio collections. As a source for a ringtone, a WAV is a good place to start because it usually holds uncompressed PCM, which makes files big but exact. The format record puts the original size limit at 4 GB.

### Programs that open WAV files

**Windows, Linux and Mac**

- ffplay: the player that ships with FFmpeg has a WAV demuxer, so it can play the WAV from the command line before you convert it.
- Audacity: reads the common WAV recordings, PCM variants included.

**Mobile**

- Android edition of VLC: plays media on phones and tablets, with decoding that depends on what the container holds.
- Firefox for Android: Mozilla lists WAV among the audio it plays directly.
- mpv for Android: a port the mpv project links to, which plays the WAV on a phone or tablet.

### WAV and M4R compared

- **Encoding**: WAV usually holds uncompressed linear PCM. M4R holds compressed audio, typically AAC.
- **Container**: an MPEG-4 file keeps its wrapper structure apart from whatever encoding the tracks use. MediaInfo classifies .m4r within its MPEG-4 container family, and these files can carry track metadata besides the samples.
- **Purpose**: WAV is a recording master, while NCH's WavePad manual calls M4R the iPhone's ringtone type.
- **Length**: Apple's GarageBand ringtone workflow limits the selected sound to 30 seconds, so a longer WAV has to be shortened elsewhere, because this page does not trim.
- **Support**: WavePad lists .m4r opening and saving on Windows, but not on Mac.

The conversion runs in your browser, where FFmpeg (WebAssembly) skips any video and converts the audio to AAC at 192 kbps. It writes the result with FFmpeg's iPod format, so the file is MPEG-4 audio that carries the .m4r name. The command leaves sample rate, channel count and length alone, so the ringtone runs as long as the WAV. The page does not install a ringtone either: you still have to add the M4R to the iPhone. Select a batch and every WAV is converted one at a time, each getting its own .m4r with the WAV's name. Your original WAV is not changed.

### Other ways to convert WAV to M4R

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i cue.wav -t 30 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -vn -f ipod cue-tone.m4r` on the command line. In this command -vn drops video, -c:a and -b:a choose the AAC encoder and its bitrate, and -f ipod writes the MPEG-4 container. This example cuts the audio at 30 seconds with `-t 30`. It makes the file and does not assign a ringtone.
- **WavePad on Windows:** open the WAV, then choose File > Save As and pick M4R. NCH lists M4R saving for Windows only.
- **GarageBand on iPhone:** create a recording project, then use Tracks > Loops Browser > Files > Browse items from Files to bring the WAV into Tracks and trim it. Back in My Songs, pick the project, then Share, Ringtone and Export. This builds and installs the ringtone on the phone, within the 30-second limit, and GarageBand offers to shorten a longer export. A dimmed song cannot be picked until it has been downloaded to the iPhone.

### Problems with WAV files

- **It will not import**: some recorders put proprietary compression inside a WAV. Audacity points to its FFmpeg library for those imports.
- **The file is too big for an old program**: recordings that outgrow the original RIFF size fields may be stored as RF64, which a program built for the older layout may not read.
- **A player balks at one file**: the same wrapper holds PCM or compressed audio, so one program can accept a file that another refuses.
- **Titles or tags are odd**: INFO chunks and Broadcast WAVE extensions carry different information, so metadata is handled unevenly.

guide.title: About WAV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

WAV, or WAVE, is a wrapper for sound built on RIFF, not one particular audio encoding. The format was set out by Microsoft and IBM in a multimedia specification dated August 1991. Linear PCM is the common payload, but compressed encodings can appear too, so the .wav ending alone doesn't tell you what is inside. The usual media-type labels are audio/wav and audio/x-wav. Broadcast WAVE extends the format with metadata for production and preservation, and the Library of Congress lists WAVE among its recommended formats for digital audio.

You come across WAV files from audio recorders, editing software and sound libraries: anywhere sound is kept untouched. The cost is size. An uncompressed recording takes far more space than a Vorbis copy of it, which is why many people look for a smaller file to send or store. The .wav ending also doesn't tell you whether a file holds plain PCM or something compressed.

### Programs that open WAV files

**Windows**

- Windows Media Player: opens WAV files.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Audacity: imports most WAV files, all PCM variants included.

**Web**

- Any web browser: plays a WAV with no extra software.

**Android, iOS, Linux, Mac and Windows**

- VLC media player: plays back WAV files.

### WAV and OGG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .wav uses audio/wav or audio/x-wav. .ogg uses audio/ogg for an audio-only stream.
- **Container**: WAV is a RIFF wrapper. Ogg is Xiph.Org's open container, which supports sequential reading and writing, so it suits streaming. Its framing includes timestamps and error detection.
- **Codec**: a WAV usually holds linear PCM. An OGG usually holds Vorbis, while .oga is the broader extension for audio in Ogg.
- **Size**: PCM is uncompressed. Vorbis is lossy and much smaller.
- **Metadata**: WAV keeps INFO chunks or Broadcast WAVE fields, which store different information.
- **Standards**: the IETF registered the Ogg media types in September 2008.

Ogg is Xiph.Org's open container for compressed multimedia streams. It can interleave sound and video, and the codec decides how each stream is compressed, which is why a bare .ogg ending doesn't name an encoding on its own.

This page decodes the WAV and writes Vorbis at quality 5 into an Ogg container. It is a quality setting, not a bitrate, so the size follows the sound. The command sets no bitrate, sample rate or channel count of its own, only the quality.

The practical split is simple. Keep a WAV for anything you will edit again, archive or hand to someone who mixes it. Make an OGG for a copy you will listen to, share or stream, where a small file matters more than the last bit of detail. Because Vorbis has already discarded sound, converting an OGG back to WAV gives you a large file with the same reduced content, not the original recording.

### Other ways to convert WAV to OGG

- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the WAV, choose File > Export Audio, pick Ogg Vorbis from the Format dropdown and choose a quality from 0 to 10. The default is 5.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i input.wav -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 output.ogg`. The quality scale runs from -1 to 10.
- **oggenc (command line):** run `oggenc -q 5 -o output.ogg input.wav`. The tool comes in Xiph's vorbis-tools and reads raw, Wave or AIFF audio.

### Problems with WAV files

- **Audacity won't import the recording**: a recorder may use proprietary compression inside the WAV. Audacity recommends installing its FFmpeg library for those.
- **A very large recording**: WAV files past the original RIFF size limit need RF64.
- **The WAV plays in one program but not another**: WAV is a wrapper, so a player needs the decoder for whatever encoding sits inside it. Convert it here or open it in Audacity to find out.
- **The OGG sounds worse than the WAV**: Vorbis is lossy. Keep the WAV, or re-run from the original recording rather than from another lossy copy.
- **A device rejects the OGG**: it may expect Opus or another codec. The extension doesn't identify one, and RFC 5334 keeps .ogg for Vorbis audio and gives general audio and video other extensions, .oga and .ogv.
- **A damaged OGG**: the container detects damaged pages but can't rebuild missing audio. Convert again from the WAV.

guide.title: WAV files and OPUS output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

The Waveform Audio File Format (WAV) wraps sound in RIFF chunks and was documented by Microsoft and IBM in 1991. It usually holds uncompressed linear PCM, so files are large but exact. Compressed encodings can appear inside too. Broadcast WAVE extends it with production metadata, and the Library of Congress also recommends WAV for digital audio collections. People use it for recording, editing and professional sound production.

### Programs that open WAV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Audacity brings in most WAV files, all PCM variants included.
- ffplay plays WAV, using the demuxer FFmpeg includes for it.

**Mobile:**

- Firefox for Android lists WAV among its supported audio types.
- VLC for Android is a free mobile media player.
- mpv for Android is the Android port linked by the mpv project.

### WAV and Opus compared

WAV is audio/wav or audio/x-wav and usually lossless, with a 4 GB file size limit. Opus is an open lossy codec from the IETF, defined in RFC 6716, which combines Skype's SILK and Xiph.Org's CELT. Ogg Opus supports descriptive metadata and seeking. Opus bitrates run from 6 to 510 kbit/s, it has low latency and it is royalty-free.

Here FFmpeg in your browser runs libopus on the WAV's sound with a 128 kbps target and compression level 4. Any picture stream is dropped. Nothing in the page lets you change the sample rate, channels or tags.

### Other ways to convert WAV to Opus

- **opusenc:** run `opusenc --bitrate 128 take.wav take.opus` from the opus-tools. It reads Wave input and writes Ogg Opus, with the bitrate in kbit/s.
- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i take.wav -c:a libopus -b:a 128k take.opus`. The libopus encoder is a wrapper that requires --enable-libopus.
- **Audacity:** choose File > Import > Audio and select the WAV. Then choose File > Export Audio, pick Opus as the format, name the file and export.

### Problems with WAV files

- **A recorder's WAV won't import**: it may use proprietary compression. Audacity recommends its FFmpeg library for such files.
- **Very large recordings**: they may need RF64 instead of the original size fields.
- **Tags differ**: INFO chunks and Broadcast WAVE store different information.

guide.title: Understanding WAV for WMA output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

WAV, or Waveform Audio File Format, is a RIFF-based wrapper for sound that Microsoft and IBM documented in their multimedia specification. Linear PCM is the usual payload, which makes files large but exact, though compressed encodings can appear too. Broadcast WAVE extends it with production metadata. Archives such as the Library of Congress recommend WAVE for collections. The usual media types are audio/wav and audio/x-wav.

### Programs that open WAV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity opens most WAV files, PCM variants among them, and ffplay plays them as well.
- **Web:** Firefox plays WAV directly, and so does Firefox for Android.
- **Mobile:** Phones can use mpv for Android or VLC for Android.

Audacity recommends its FFmpeg library when a recorder used proprietary compression inside the WAV.

### WAV and WMA compared

- **Container**: WAV is RIFF. WMA uses Microsoft's ASF container.
- **Compression**: WAV is usually uncompressed PCM. This page writes lossy WMA version 2.
- **Variants**: WMA has standard, Professional, Lossless and Voice codecs.
- **Size**: a WMA is usually much smaller than the WAV.
- **Media type**: WMA is commonly audio/x-ms-wma.

FFmpeg runs in your browser as WebAssembly and encodes the WAV with wmav2 at 192 kbps. The command sets no sample rate or channel layout.

### Other ways to convert WAV to WMA

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i rehearsal.wav -c:a wmav2 -b:a 192k rehearsal.wma`. This writes lossy WMA version 2.
- **Audacity:** open the WAV, then choose File > Export Audio and select WMA (version 2) Files (FFmpeg) from the format list. The FFmpeg library must be installed.

### Problems with WAV files

- **A very large recording**: past the 4 GB limit of RIFF's size fields it needs RF64, which not every tool reads.
- **A WAV that uses compression**: a recorder may have used proprietary compression inside the file, and Audacity needs its FFmpeg library to import it.
- **Metadata differs between WAVs**: the INFO chunks and the Broadcast WAVE extensions carry unlike information, so check which your file has.
- **The WAV is your only copy**: the WMA discards detail and cannot give the samples back, so keep the WAV.

guide.title: Understanding WebM to AVI
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebM file?

The WebM Project promotes WebM as an open media format for web delivery, built on the Matroska container. It carries VP8 or VP9 video next to Vorbis or Opus audio, and the project supplies its format technology royalty-free. Its media types are video/webm for video files and audio/webm for sound-only ones.

### Programs that open WebM files

- **Windows, Mac, Linux, Android and iOS:** VLC media player reads Matroska-family media. The Android app carries the desktop player's decoding, and the iOS app plays local media without conversion.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay plays WebM through FFmpeg's decoders.
- **Web:** Safari on macOS added WebM in version 14.1; it covers VP8 and VP9 video plus Vorbis audio.

### WebM and AVI compared

- **AVI**: Microsoft's RIFF-based container, dating from Windows 3.1 and a 1992 specification. Its video may be raw, lossless or lossy, so a .avi name reveals nothing about quality.
- **Video**: written by the FFmpeg `mpeg4` encoder and tagged xvid.
- **Audio**: MP3 at 96 kbps.
- **Frame size**: 1920 px is the ceiling for the longer side, and each side is trimmed to an even pixel count.
- **Frame rate**: 30 fps at most.
- **Interlacing**: frames marked as interlaced are deinterlaced.
- **Tags**: the command has no `-map` or `-map_metadata`, so FFmpeg's defaults choose the streams and copy global tags, for example title or artist, wherever the AVI has a field for them.
- **Privacy**: FFmpeg is compiled to WebAssembly and works in your browser, so the WebM is not uploaded. Several files run one after another, each downloading as its own AVI.

### Other ways to convert WebM to AVI

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i clip.webm clip.avi`. FFmpeg guesses the output format from the file extension.

### Problems with WebM files

- **Seeking is slow**: a missing cue index leaves the player with less direct location information.
- **It plays in one app only**: the streams inside, rather than the .webm name, determine playback, so a player such as VLC must support them.
- **An old Safari will not play it**: WebM playback arrived on macOS only with Safari 14.1, and only for VP8 or VP9 video with Vorbis sound.

guide.title: About WebM files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebM file?

WebM is an open media format that the WebM Project promotes for delivery over the web. The container is based on Matroska, and the streams inside are VP8, VP9 or AV1 video with Vorbis or Opus audio. The project offers its technology on royalty-free terms, and the major browsers support the format.

Video files carry the media type video/webm. A WebM holding nothing but sound is labeled audio/webm, so a .webm file is not always a video.

Typical sources are web video, the recordings that browser-based screen recorders save, and short animated clips.

### Programs that open WebM files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- The VLC media player reads Matroska-family media, though its codec support has to match the streams inside the WebM.
- FFplay ships with FFmpeg and plays WebM through FFmpeg's decoders, so which codecs work depends on how that copy was built.

**Web**

- Chrome, Firefox and Edge open WebM files directly.
- Safari 14.1 is where macOS gained WebM playback; the picture has to be VP8 or VP9 and the audio Vorbis.

**Mobile**

- Android and iPhone owners can use VLC for Android or VLC for iOS, which play local WebM files with VLC's own player rather than the system player.

### WebM and GIF compared

- **Names**: .webm goes with video/webm, and .gif with image/gif.
- **Kind of file**: WebM wraps video. CompuServe brought out GIF in 1987 as an image format that can store several images one after another.
- **Animation**: the GIF89a revision from July 1990 added the extensions for timing, comments, application data and transparency. Delays are counted in hundredths of a second, and a disposal setting decides how a later image sits on top of an earlier one.
- **Colors**: every GIF image picks its colors from a palette that tops out at 256 entries. WebM video has no such ceiling.
- **Compression**: GIF squeezes its images with LZW, which loses nothing. WebM depends on its video codecs.
- **Sound**: a WebM can carry Vorbis or Opus audio. The GIF this page writes holds one picture stream and no audio.
- **Transparency**: a single palette entry can be flagged as clear, and there is no partial opacity.
- **Repeat count**: a GIF keeps its repeat count in an application extension, and the file this page writes has it set to repeat forever.
- **Patents**: Unisys started asking for LZW license fees in 1994, and the last of those patents lapsed in 2004.
- **Support**: every major browser displays GIF.

For this pair the page writes 15 frames a second, shrinks anything above 480 px on its longer side, and sets the GIF to repeat. Frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced before they are scaled.

### Other ways to convert WebM to GIF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i input.webm output.gif`. FFmpeg takes the output format from the .gif ending, the same pattern its documentation shows with `ffmpeg -i input.avi output.mp4`. A plain command like this skips the frame-rate, size and palette steps this page applies.
- **Gifski with FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i input.webm frame%04d.png` to write one PNG per frame, then `gifski -o anim.gif frame*.png` to build the GIF. Gifski's documentation names `--width` and `--height` as the biggest levers for a smaller file, and `--quality` for lowering quality. Its site also shows `gifski --fps 10 --width 320 -o anim.gif video.mp4` for an MP4 source, where `--fps` sets the frame rate and a lower value gives a smaller file. On Windows, the frame pattern may need `%%04d`.

### Problems with WebM files

- **It plays in a browser but not in an editor**: playback depends on the video and audio codecs actually used, not on the .webm ending. Check which codecs the file really uses before blaming the container, then convert it here or open it in VLC.
- **Seeking is slow or jumpy**: without a cue index, a player gets less direct location information, so jumping to a point is less efficient. Re-saving the file in a video editor rebuilds it.
- **Safari won't play it**: releases before 14.1 predate WebM playback in Safari on macOS, so update the browser or use another one.
- **It holds only sound**: an audio-only WebM is labeled audio/webm and has no picture to show, so play it in VLC to check what is inside.

guide.title: Understanding WebM for MKV output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebM file?

WebM is a royalty-free web video format, defined as a subset of Matroska. A typical file holds VP8, VP9 or AV1 pictures with Vorbis or Opus sound. Because WebM is a restricted flavor of Matroska, the jump to MKV is a change of container rules more than of family. Matroska itself can hold chapters, tags and many video, audio and subtitle streams.

### Programs that open WebM files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay plays WebM through FFmpeg's decoders, and VLC reads Matroska-family media too.
- **Web:** Safari on macOS handles WebM that holds VP8 or VP9 video with Vorbis sound. Chrome and Firefox play it directly.
- **Mobile:** The VLC apps on Android and iOS open WebM straight from the device.

What actually decides playback is the codec inside, not the file extension.

### WebM and MKV compared

- **Codecs**: WebM allows a short list of video and audio codecs. MKV does not prescribe a codec.
- **Tracks**: MKV holds many audio and subtitle tracks, plus chapters.
- **Media types**: video/webm for WebM, video/matroska for MKV.
- **This page's output**: H.264 pictures with AAC sound at 96 kbps.

FFmpeg running in your browser decodes the WebM and writes fresh H.264 with libx264, using CRF 32 and the ultrafast preset. It deinterlaces, limits the long side to 1920 pixels, holds output to 30 fps and trims odd dimensions to the next even number down.

### Other ways to convert WebM to MKV

- **FFmpeg remux:** run `ffmpeg -i browser.webm -map 0 -c copy wrapped.mkv`. `-map 0` takes every stream from the input and `-c copy` copies them without re-encoding.

### Problems with WebM files

- **A second audio or language track is missing**: no -map option is set, so FFmpeg's defaults choose the streams. Remux with -map 0 to carry every track.
- **A fast clip looks different**: the page limits the frame rate, so a faster source loses frames.
- **A very sharp source softens**: the page re-encodes and may resize, so remux if you need the original streams.
- **Seeking is slow**: if the cue index is missing, the player has less to go on and seeks less efficiently.
- **The WebM has an odd width or height**: H.264 needs even dimensions, so the page trims it.

faqs.answer: Only if the video is larger than 1920 pixels on its longer side, in which case it is scaled down with the same aspect ratio. A width or height that is an odd number loses one pixel so both come out even.

faqs.question: What happens to the frame rate?
faqs.answer: A source at or below 30 fps keeps its own rate, because the page only limits the rate and never raises it. A faster source has frames dropped down to 30 fps and keeps its running time.

faqs.question: Does the audio survive?
faqs.answer: Yes, re-encoded as AAC at 96 kbps. With no audio or track controls on the page, a file that has several audio tracks lets FFmpeg's default choice decide which one is used.

faqs.question: Should I convert WebM to MOV or to MP4?
faqs.answer: MOV comes from Apple's QuickTime, and MP4 grew out of it, but they are separate formats. MOV has patchier browser support than MP4, and Apple's current apps mostly lean on MP4. Pick MOV when an editor or workflow specifically requests it.

faqs.question: Can I do more than one WebM in a single session?
faqs.answer: Yes. Add the whole set and the page encodes the clips one at a time, handing you one MOV per clip. Nothing is zipped and the clips are never joined.

faqs.question: How big a WebM can I use?
faqs.answer: The page sets no cap on size or duration. Encoding happens on your own device, so long or high-resolution clips depend on how powerful that machine is.

guide.title: Understanding WebM to MOV
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebM file?

Designed for delivery over the web, this open format comes from the WebM Project, and Matroska is the basis of its container. Typical streams are VP8 or VP9 for the picture and Vorbis or Opus for the sound, and the project offers the underlying technology royalty-free. The media type is video/webm for video and audio/webm when there is no picture. Browser screen recordings and short web clips are common places to meet one.

Whether a browser plays the file turns on the codecs it holds rather than the .webm suffix. That is why a file with a familiar extension can still be refused by a player or an editor that lacks the codec inside.

### Programs that open WebM files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player reads Matroska-family media, as long as its codecs cover the WebM streams. FFplay, part of FFmpeg, plays WebM too.
- **Mac:** Safari 14.1 brought WebM playback to macOS for VP8 or VP9 video with Vorbis audio.
- **Mobile:** On Android, VLC offers the decoding features of its desktop sibling, while on iOS it plays files stored on the device with its own player instead of the system one.

### WebM and MOV compared

MOV is the QuickTime movie format from Apple, launched in 1991 and ported to Windows in 1994. Files use .mov or .qt, and the media type is video/quicktime. Atoms are the building blocks of a QuickTime file, and a program may pass over any atom it does not recognize. QuickTime served as the starting point for MPEG-4, yet MOV and MP4 remain distinct formats and cannot be swapped freely. A MOV can wrap H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG pictures together with AAC or raw PCM sound. Screen recordings made on a Mac land in this format.

A WebAssembly build of FFmpeg does the work in your browser tab, writing a MOV that holds H.264 video and AAC audio at 96 kbps. The H.264 settings are the ultrafast preset and CRF 32, and the file's index is moved to the front, which FFmpeg calls faststart. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced. The longer side is capped at 1920 pixels, so bigger pictures are scaled down and both dimensions rounded to even numbers, and sources above 30 frames per second have frames dropped. Nothing in the command selects a particular audio or video stream, so FFmpeg's defaults decide, which matters for files holding several tracks. A damaged or cut-short WebM usually still converts, and the MOV then ends where FFmpeg could read no further.

This is a plain H.264 MOV, not a ProRes file. QuickTime containers may use codecs absent from the destination editor, so check what the receiving program accepts before you send the file. To look at the result, try mpv on the desktop, Adobe Premiere in an editing workflow, or the Android and iOS apps from the VLC project on a phone.

### Other ways to convert WebM to MOV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i capture.webm -c:v libx264 -c:a aac result.mov`. FFmpeg's format list includes both WebM and MOV, and it encodes H.264 through libx264 and AAC through its own encoder. Add options for the preset, size or frame rate if you want to set them.
- **mpv:** run `mpv capture.webm --ovc=libx264 --oac=aac --o=result.mov`. The `--o` option switches mpv into its encoding mode, and `--ovc` and `--oac` pick the video and audio codecs.

### Problems with WebM files

**The editor rejects the file.** Identify the video and audio codecs before blaming the container, since a decoder on your computer may open a file the operating system cannot preview. Renaming the file neither transcodes the video nor supplies a missing decoder.

**The MOV is not ProRes.** A ProRes-only workflow needs a ProRes encoder, and this page writes H.264 only.

**Older Safari notes are out of date.** Safari 14.1 is where WebM with VP8 or VP9 video and Vorbis audio arrived on macOS, so do not assume current releases behave like older ones.

**Seeking is slow or the file breaks.** A WebM without a cue index seeks less efficiently, since the player lacks a direct map of where things sit in the file. A regular MOV can also be unusable after an interrupted write, so let the conversion finish before closing the tab.

guide.title: About WebM and MP3 files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebM file?

Media for the web is what WebM is built for, and the WebM Project promotes it as an open format. It is based on Matroska and combines VP8 or VP9 video with Vorbis or Opus audio, with AV1 video also in use. The project provides the format's technology royalty-free. A WebM with video uses video/webm as its media type, and one that holds only sound uses audio/webm.

You usually meet WebM as a saved web video, a screen recording from a browser or a short animated clip. The sound is a separate stream inside the file, so a converter can take it out without touching the picture.

The files are made for delivery over the web. A missing cue index leaves a player with less direct location information, which makes seeking less efficient.

### Programs that open WebM files

**Windows, Mac, Linux, Android and iOS**

- VLC media player: reads Matroska-family media, provided its codecs match the streams in the file. The Android release carries over the desktop player's decoding features.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FFplay: plays WebM with FFmpeg's decoders.

**Mac**

- Safari: supports WebM from 14.1 onward, covering VP8, VP9 and Vorbis.

### WebM and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .webm with video/webm (audio/webm for sound only), against .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **Container**: WebM is a Matroska subset that holds video, audio and more. MP3 is a single audio stream.
- **Codecs**: WebM audio is Vorbis or Opus, while MP3 is MPEG-1 Audio Layer III from ISO/IEC 11172-3.
- **Openness**: the WebM Project licenses its technology royalty-free. The MP3 patent licensing program ended in April 2017.
- **Metadata**: ID3 data inside the MP3 is where titles and other tags live.
- **Support**: MP3 plays on nearly every device. Vorbis and Opus in a WebM depend on the player's codecs.
- **Typical use**: WebM fits web video, browser screen recordings and animated clips; MP3 fits music libraries, podcasts and portable players.

The page runs FFmpeg with its video output off and LAME set to 192 kbps, a rate LAME reaches only for audio sampled at 32 kHz or above. In a run on a sample WebM, FFmpeg decoded Vorbis audio and wrote it as a new MP3 stream. Both formats are lossy, so the audio goes through compression a second time, and detail the WebM already dropped does not return.

The output is named after the WebM, with .mp3 in place of .webm. A batch converts one file after another, and each MP3 is saved separately. Nothing caps size or running time, and FFmpeg works on one thread. The page gives you no bitrate, track or quality options.

### Other ways to convert WebM to MP3

- **FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** execute `ffmpeg -i input.webm -vn -c:a libmp3lame output.mp3`. -vn turns the video off.
- **Audacity with FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** Audacity can import the sound of most video files other than DRM-protected ones provided the optional FFmpeg library is installed. Then open the WebM, go to File > Export Audio and choose MP3 in the Format menu.

FFmpeg's b option sets a bitrate of your own, for example -b:a 192k, and Audacity's export dialog has MP3 options, so both desktop routes offer what this page does not.

### Problems with WebM files

- **An error or a silent result**: the WebM may have no audio track. Play it first to check.
- **Plays in one program but not another**: playback depends on the real video and audio codecs, not on the .webm ending.
- **The bitrate is lower than expected**: a WebM with 16 to 24 kHz audio gets at most 160 kbps from LAME, and one at 8 to 12 kHz gets 64 kbps.
- **The recording is cut short**: a damaged or truncated WebM often converts anyway, giving a shorter MP3.
- **Seeking is sluggish**: a WebM missing its cue index gives players less to seek with.
- **Older Safari will not play it**: releases before 14.1 on macOS lack WebM support.
- **A renamed file fails**: changing .webm to .mp3 leaves the Matroska data inside. Convert the file instead.
- **Titles are missing in the MP3**: FFmpeg carries the WebM's global tags, for example title and artist, into the MP3 when it has them. Add the rest with a tag editor.

faqs.question: Why do my browser recordings come out as .webm?

guide.title: Understanding WebM for WAV output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebM file?

The WebM Project describes WebM as an open media format meant for web delivery. It is built on Matroska; the video is VP8 or VP9, and the sound is Vorbis or Opus. The project supplies its format technology under royalty-free terms, and its container guidelines for streaming over HTTP are stricter than the Matroska specification itself. Audio tracks carry the codec IDs A_VORBIS or A_OPUS. A video WebM has the media type video/webm, and an audio-only one uses audio/webm. Its Uniform Type Identifier is org.webmproject.webm.

WebM is used for web video, browser screen recordings and animated clips. If the file you have is a meeting or a lecture where the sound matters more than the picture, that is the reason to pull out a WAV.

The .webm suffix alone doesn't say what is inside. Whether a browser can play a given file depends on the video and audio codecs it holds, not on the suffix.

### Programs that open WebM files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player reads Matroska-family media, which covers WebM.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay, the player that comes with FFmpeg, plays WebM input with FFmpeg's decoders.
- **Web:** Safari on macOS handles WebM files with VP8 or VP9 video and Vorbis sound from version 14.1.
- **Mobile:** Android and iOS each have a VLC app; the Android one reuses the desktop decoding, while the iOS one plays local files through VLC's own engine.

### WebM and WAV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .webm with video/webm or audio/webm; .wav with audio/wav or audio/x-wav.
- **Wrapper**: WebM is built on Matroska. WAV is a sound wrapper built on RIFF that can hold various encodings; Microsoft and IBM documented it in a multimedia specification from August 1991. A WAV starts with the marker RIFF, then WAVE and a fmt chunk that describes the encoding, and a data chunk holds the samples.
- **Compression**: WebM audio is lossy Opus or Vorbis. This page writes the WAV as linear PCM with 16 bits per sample, so each sample is stored in full. Linear PCM is a common WAV payload, though compressed encodings can appear in WAV too.
- **Video**: WebM can carry it. A WAV holds sound, so the video is dropped. Multichannel sound in a WAV relies on the WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE header that Windows 2000 introduced.
- **Size**: the WAV is larger than the compressed audio in the WebM. A single WAV also tops out near 4 GB, the point where RF64 is needed instead of the original RIFF size fields.
- **Metadata**: Tag handling in WAV varies: plain INFO chunks hold one set of fields and the Broadcast WAVE extensions another, aimed at production and preservation.
- **Archiving**: the Library of Congress names WAVE as the recommended format when libraries build digital audio collections, with the Broadcast WAVE variant WAVE_BWF_1 as the archival master format for reformatted mono and stereo analog recordings. The European Broadcasting Union adopted the format as the basis for Broadcast Wave. Its specifications are freely available and it needs no licensing or patents.

In short, the conversion decodes Opus or Vorbis into plain samples. That suits editing, and it doesn't improve the sound.

### Other ways to convert WebM to WAV

- **FFmpeg (command line):** `ffmpeg -i recording.webm -vn -c:a pcm_s16le speech.wav` does it. The `-vn` option disables video, and `-c:a pcm_s16le` selects the encoder for the audio, because a codec option placed before an output file chooses the encoder for that file. FFmpeg's documentation lists both WebM and PCM signed 16-bit little-endian among what it supports for encoding and decoding.

### Problems with WebM files

- **A player refuses the file**: a browser's ability to play a WebM comes down to the codecs it holds, and the suffix says little. Try VLC, or play it in a current browser.
- **Jumping to a time is sluggish**: a missing cue index can make seeking less efficient, since the player has fewer direct pointers to positions. The WebM guidelines say a demuxer disables seeking when a file has no keyframe Cues element.
- **An older Safari on a Mac won't play it**: Safari 14.1 is the release that added WebM playback on macOS, so don't assume an older release handles it.
- **A renamed file still fails**: changing the extension to .wav leaves WebM data inside. Convert the file instead.

guide.title: About WebP and ICO
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebP file?

WebP is an image format developed by Google and released as open source. Google announced it on 30 September 2010. Its lossy compression is based on VP8, the video codec Google released as open source in May 2010, and applies VP8's intra-frame coding to still images. The lossless variant takes another route, combining LZ77 matching, prefix codes and a color cache. A WebP file is a RIFF container.

Transparency and animation work in both lossy and lossless WebP, and the file can also store an ICC profile along with Exif and XMP metadata. An image can be at most 16,383 x 16,383 pixels. On average, Google says lossless WebP comes out about 26% smaller than PNG, and lossy WebP about 30% smaller than JPEG. WebP was documented in RFC 9649 in November 2024, which also registers the image/webp media type.

### Programs that open WebP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP handles WebP import and export natively as of version 2.10.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads WebP; inspect `magick identify -list format` for your installed build.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** XnView MP reads and writes WebP, and is free for private or educational use. A company needs a license.
- **Windows and Mac:** Photoshop reads and writes WebP without a plug-in from version 23.2.
- **Windows:** With Microsoft's WebP Image Extension installed, File Explorer and Photos can open WebP images.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome display WebP, though older versions may not animate it. Lossy WebP displays in Chrome 17+, Edge 18+, Firefox 65+ and Safari 14+.
- **Mobile:** Safari on iPhone and Chrome on Android display WebP. Android decodes WebP from version 4.0, and lossless or transparent WebP from 4.2.1.

### WebP and ICO compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .webp is image/webp. .ico is image/vnd.microsoft.icon.
- **Purpose**: WebP is a web image format. Microsoft designed ICO for icons in graphical interfaces, and the .ico extension is best known today from website favicons.
- **Several images**: an ICO file may contain more than one image. A WebP is one picture, or one animation.
- **Animation**: WebP can animate. The ICO written here holds one still image.
- **Transparency**: both formats support an alpha channel.
- **Size**: a WebP can be up to 16,383 px a side. ICO stores each side in one byte, so an image tops out at 256 px.
- **Byte order**: ICO files use little-endian byte ordering.

Windows Vista icon guidance includes 256-by-256 images for high-DPI displays, which is where the 256 px limit sits. On this page, the browser's own decoder reads the WebP and ImageMagick writes the ICO. Only one image goes in. A larger picture is fitted down to the limit, and one that is already smaller keeps its size. At 256 px the image is embedded in the ICO as PNG data. Metadata isn't copied.

### Other ways to convert WebP to ICO

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux):** open the WebP and choose File > Export As. Change the Name field's extension to .ico, or pick ICO under Select File Type, then export. The ICO dialog sets the color depth and offers a Compressed (PNG) checkbox.
- **Pillow (Python):** open the WebP with `Image.open` and call `save` with a .ico filename. Pass `sizes=[(16,16),(32,32),(48,48)]` to put several icon sizes in one file. The default is 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256 px, and any size bigger than the original or 256 is ignored. Pillow needs libwebp to read WebP.
- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i input.webp output.ico`. FFmpeg's documentation lists WebP among the image formats it decodes and ICO among the formats it reads and writes.

### Problems with WebP files

- **Older browsers and animation**: an old browser may show a still WebP yet be unable to play an animated one.
- **A WebP beyond 16,383 px**: WebP caps each side at 16,383 pixels, so a bigger image runs past the format's limit.
- **A tool can't read the WebP**: a given ImageMagick install might lack WebP decoding or encoding, so look in its format list.
- **The page says it can't open the file**: you see "This browser can't open ... files" when your browser has no WebP decoder, and "Image decode failed." for a file the browser can't read. Updating to a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari cures the first.

guide.title: About WebP files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebP file?

WebP is a Google-made image format, open source from the start. The announcement came on 30 September 2010. In lossy mode, WebP applies the intra-frame coding of VP8, a video codec that began at On2 Technologies and that Google released as open source in May 2010. The VP8 specification, RFC 6386, is built around On2's own reference decoder. A lossless mode with its own method followed, and both modes can carry transparency and animation. Inside, a WebP is a RIFF container. RFC 9649, published in November 2024, documents the format and registers its media type, image/webp.

You mostly meet WebP on the web. Google reports lossy WebP files about 30% smaller than JPEG on average, and lossless WebP files about 26% smaller than PNG. Animated WebP turns up too: WhatsApp's animated stickers, for example, are WebP files.

### Programs that open WebP files

- **Windows:** File Explorer and Photos open WebP once Microsoft's WebP Image Extension is installed.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP reads and writes WebP natively, since version 2.10. ImageMagick reads WebP, and its format list shows whether your installation can.
- **Web and mobile:** Google Chrome displays WebP.
- **Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays WebP, and so does Microsoft Edge.
- **Mac and mobile:** Safari shows WebP from macOS Big Sur and iOS 14.
- **Mobile:** On Android, WebP displays from version 4.0, with lossless and transparent files supported from 4.2.1.

Adobe Photoshop handles WebP files natively as well, starting with version 23.2.

### WebP and JPG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .webp and image/webp; .jpg or .jpeg and image/jpeg.
- **Compression**: lossy WebP codes the picture as a VP8 key frame, and lossless WebP uses LZ77, prefix codes and a color cache. Baseline JPEG is always lossy: 8x8 blocks, a discrete cosine transform, then Huffman coding.
- **Transparency**: WebP has an alpha channel in both modes. JPG has none.
- **Animation**: WebP can hold timed frames. A JPG is one still picture.
- **Color depth**: JPEG keeps 8 bits per channel. The page converts through 8-bit RGBA pixels, so a deeper source loses its extra bits.
- **Largest image**: a WebP side tops out at 16,383 pixels.
- **Quality setting**: Most programs ask for a JPEG quality from 0 to 100, but one value gives different results in different tools. This page has no setting and uses 0.85 for every file.
- **Layers and progressive mode**: JPEG cannot store layers. A progressive JPEG shows a rough preview that sharpens as the rest arrives.
- **Reach**: JPEG opens in all the major browsers, and cameras and scanners commonly save it. Safari 14, Firefox 65, Edge 18 and Chrome 17, along with later releases, show lossy WebP, and elsewhere WebP needs one of the programs above.
- **Metadata**: WebP can carry an ICC profile, Exif and XMP. The JPG made here carries none of them.

The change here is the move to a format without transparency or animation. The page decodes the WebP to pixels and writes a JPG at quality 0.85. See-through areas can't stay see-through, an animation gives its first frame, and the Exif, ICC profile and XMP aren't copied.

### Other ways to convert WebP to JPG

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac and Linux):** open the WebP in GIMP 2.10 or later, then export it as a JPEG from File > Export As.
- **ImageMagick (terminal):** run `magick input.webp output.jpg`, if the installation can read WebP.

### Problems with WebP files

- **Double-clicking does nothing on Windows**: install the WebP Image Extension from the Microsoft Store.
- **An older browser shows nothing**: Edge 18, Chrome 17, Firefox 65 and Safari 14 were the first to show lossy WebP, so earlier releases can't display it.
- **A site or form rejects it**: convert it to JPG here, or to PNG with the [WebP to PNG converter](/webp-to-png/) when transparency must survive.
- **A renamed file still fails**: changing .webp to .jpg leaves WebP data inside. Convert the file instead.
- **Only one frame came out**: a JPG can't animate, so an animated WebP gives its first frame. Keep the WebP if you need the motion.
- **"Image decode failed."**: the browser's decoder couldn't read the file. Download it again from where you found it.
- **The JPG looks soft or blotchy**: a lossy WebP has already lost some detail, and the JPG is compressed again on top. Start from the largest, least compressed copy the site offers.

guide.title: About WebP files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebP file?

Google created WebP for images on the web. The lossy mode is built on the VP8 video codec, and the format also covers lossless compression, alpha transparency and animation. A WebP image can't be larger than 16,383 pixels on either axis. The file is a RIFF container. Lossy files apply VP8 intra-frame coding, whereas lossless files rely on a distinct method that combines LZ77, prefix codes and a color cache. Its image/webp media type comes from RFC 9649, which describes the format. Room exists inside a file for Exif and XMP metadata and an ICC color profile.

PDF has a different job. A form, a portal or a colleague may ask for a document when all you have is one image. Putting the WebP on a PDF page gives them something any PDF reader can open and print. The conversion does not recover the page the picture came from, and it adds no text. It also doesn't change the picture: you can still look at the WebP you started with, and the PDF is a second copy for the cases where a document is required.

### Programs that open WebP files

**Android**

- Android: it decodes WebP from version 4.0, but lossless or transparent files wait until 4.2.1.

**Mac and iPhone**

- Safari: opens WebP from version 14, on macOS Big Sur and iOS 14 onward.

**Windows**

- File Explorer and Photos: Microsoft's WebP Image Extension has to be installed before they show WebP images.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- GIMP: native WebP import and export arrived in GIMP 2.10.
- ImageMagick: reads WebP and writes PDF, which makes it a command-line route between the two.

### WebP and PDF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .webp is image/webp, and .pdf is application/pdf.
- **What they hold**: a WebP is one image, or an animation. A PDF is a document with pages, which can contain images, text and vector drawings. PDF is standardized as ISO 32000.
- **Compression**: WebP is lossy or lossless. The PDF made here stores the decoded pixels as lossless PNG data.
- **Transparency**: WebP has an alpha channel. The PDF keeps it as a soft mask, and no background is added behind the picture.
- **Animation**: WebP can animate, and a PDF page can't. You get the first frame.
- **Layout**: a PDF has fixed pages. This one has a single page sized to the image. It has no margins and isn't set to A4 or Letter.
- **Text**: a picture inside a PDF stays a picture. Selectable text needs a separate OCR step.

The browser decodes the WebP, and the page embeds the pixels without a second lossy step. The pixels travel as 8-bit RGBA, which is why EXIF, ICC and XMP data don't make it into the PDF. Each file you pick is converted on its own.

### Other ways to convert WebP to PDF

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux):** load the WebP, pick File > Export As, and choose the .pdf extension or the PDF file type. In GIMP's PDF dialog, an option can replace transparent areas with the background color, so check it when transparency matters.
- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick input.webp output.pdf`. On a 96 by 96 pixel test image it wrote a 96 by 96 point page.
- **Pillow (Python):** run `python3 -c "from PIL import Image; Image.open('input.webp').convert('RGB').save('output.pdf')"`. Pillow writes an RGB image into a PDF with JPEG encoding, so the picture is compressed again and loses its transparency.

### Problems with WebP files

- **The PDF prints at a surprising size**: pixels are not paper. A page with one point per pixel can be much larger than Letter or A4.
- **Several files downloaded**: each WebP you select makes its own PDF. Combine them afterward if you need one document.
- **The text can't be selected**: lettering in the picture is still image pixels, and the PDF adds no text layer.
- **A moving image became still**: only the first frame of an animated WebP is used. Keep the WebP for the animation.
- **A picture over 16,383 pixels**: WebP cannot be larger than that on either axis, so such a file points to a broken download or another format. Fetch it again.
- **The image won't load**: your browser decodes the WebP, so an old browser without WebP support can't open it.

guide.title: About WebP files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebP file?

Google developed WebP and announced it on 30 September 2010. Lossy files use the VP8 video codec, and a separate lossless method exists. Inside the RIFF container there is room for transparency, animation, an ICC color profile, and Exif and XMP metadata. RFC 9649 documents the format and registers the image/webp media type. Lossless coding relies on LZ77, prefix codes and a color cache, while lossy files reuse VP8's intra-frame coding.

Neither side of a WebP may pass 16,383 pixels. Typical uses are smaller web images, pictures needing transparency, and short animations.

### Programs that open WebP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP has handled WebP natively, for both import and export, since version 2.10.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads WebP, and on the Mac you run it from Terminal.
- **Windows:** File Explorer and Photos show WebP once Microsoft's WebP Image Extension has been added.
- **Web and Mobile:** Google Chrome displays WebP.
- **Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays WebP.
- **Mobile:** Safari displays WebP on phones, as Chrome does.

### WebP and PSD compared

- **Extensions**: .webp and .psd.
- **Purpose**: Photoshop's own document format, PSD, holds layers, masks and text so a design remains editable.
- **Structure**: files start with 8BPS and allow one, eight, 16 or 32 bits for each sample, storing pixels raw, with RLE or with ZIP. Each side tops out at 30,000 pixels.

This page writes the PSD from the decoded picture. It can't rebuild layers from a flat image.

### Other ways to convert WebP to PSD

- **ImageMagick:** `magick site-banner.webp site-banner.psd`. ImageMagick's format list shows WebP and PSD as readable and writable.
- **Photopea (web):** use File > Open to load the WebP, then File > Save as PSD. Photopea's front page lists WebP among the formats it opens.

### Problems with WebP files

- **An old browser**: older browser versions may lack animation support even when they display still WebP.
- **A picture over the limit**: an image beyond 16,383 pixels on either axis exceeds WebP's size limit.
- **ImageMagick can't read it**: a WebP decode may be unavailable in a particular ImageMagick installation, so check its format list.

guide.title: About WebP files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebP file?

Google announced WebP in 2010 as a new image format. For lossy pictures it borrows the key-frame method of VP8, a video codec from On2 Technologies that Google open-sourced in May 2010; a lossless mode came later. Either mode may include transparency and animation. Inside, the file is a RIFF container, and RFC 9649 describes it and registers the image/webp media type. Each side is limited to 16,383 pixels, and the file can store an ICC color profile plus Exif and XMP metadata.

Websites use WebP because it is compact: Google reports lossless files about 26% smaller than PNG and lossy ones about 30% smaller than JPEG. That is why a picture you save from a browser often arrives as .webp. Messaging apps use it as well, since WhatsApp's animated stickers are WebP files.

### Programs that open WebP pictures

**Windows**

- Photos and File Explorer: they display WebP after you install Microsoft's WebP Image Extension.

**Windows and Mac**

- Photoshop: opens and saves WebP from version 23.2.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- GIMP: has supported WebP since version 2.10.
- ImageMagick: reads WebP, if your installation includes the format.
- XnView MP: reads and writes WebP; free for private or educational use.

**Web**

- Lossy WebP shows in Chrome from version 17, Edge from 18, Firefox from 65 and Safari from 14.

**Mobile**

- On Android, WebP decodes from version 4.0, with lossless or transparent files from 4.2.1. iPhone Safari shows it from iOS 14.

### WebP and SVG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .webp with image/webp; .svg with image/svg+xml.
- **What they store**: WebP stores pixels. SVG is written in XML and describes shapes, text and embedded images, which means one SVG can hold drawn artwork or just a picture.
- **Scaling**: a vector SVG stays sharp at any size. A pixel image does not, and neither does an SVG that merely wraps one.
- **Animation**: WebP can hold timed frames. An SVG can animate through CSS or scripts, but that is a different mechanism.
- **Text**: an SVG is plain text, so it can be edited in a text editor and searched, indexed and compressed. A WebP is a RIFF container.
- **Linked pictures**: an SVG can point to a picture in another file and lose it when that file is unavailable. This page avoids that by embedding the picture inside the SVG itself.

This is what the conversion does. The page decodes the WebP and writes an SVG that contains a single image element: your picture, embedded as a base64 PNG, at the picture's own width and height. Nothing is traced into paths. The SVG opens wherever SVG opens, but it scales like the original bitmap, and its colors and shapes can't be edited as objects.

### Other ways to convert WebP to SVG

These routes trace the picture into paths, which is a different job from the embedding this page does. dwebp does not read animated WebP files.

- **Inkscape with dwebp:** run `dwebp input.webp -o input.png`, which writes a PNG. In Inkscape choose File > Import, select the image with the Selector tool, then choose Path > Trace Bitmap, set the options and click OK. Tracing is not a faithful copy, and color tracing makes one object per color, which can be hard to edit.
- **Potrace with dwebp:** run `dwebp input.webp -bmp -o input.bmp`, which writes an uncompressed BMP, then `potrace -s input.bmp -o output.svg`. Potrace reads PBM, PGM, PPM and BMP, and -s selects the SVG backend.

### Problems with WebP files

- **Renaming the file doesn't work**: changing .webp to .svg leaves WebP data inside, and an SVG has to be XML text.
- **It won't open in an older program**: install Microsoft's WebP Image Extension on Windows, or use a recent browser, GIMP or Photoshop.
- **A design tool rejects it**: turn the WebP into a plain bitmap with the [WebP to PNG converter](/webp-to-png/), then bring that in.
- **An old browser shows a still**: an older browser can show a still WebP yet lack animation support. On this page an animated WebP gives its first frame only.
- **The picture is too big for WebP**: WebP limits each side to 16,383 pixels, so a file claiming more is damaged or not a WebP.
- **A decode failure message appears**: the browser could not open the file. Try an up-to-date Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari, or fetch a fresh copy.
- **ImageMagick can't read it**: a WebP decode or encode may be unavailable in a particular installation, so check its format list.

guide.markdown:
### What is a WebP image file?

WebP is Google's open-source image format, announced on 30 September 2010. Its lossy mode borrows from the VP8 video codec: still pictures are compressed the way VP8 compresses key frames. The lossless mode is a different design built on LZ77, prefix codes and a color cache. Inside a RIFF container, both modes can carry transparency and animation. Metadata such as an ICC profile, Exif and XMP can ride along.

### Programs that open WebP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP, which has imported and exported WebP natively since 2.10.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads WebP.
- **Windows:** Microsoft's WebP Image Extension lets File Explorer and Photos open WebP images.
- **Web and Mobile:** Google Chrome displays WebP.
- **Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays WebP.
- **Mobile:** Safari displays WebP.

### WebP and WebP compared

With the same format on both sides, the file is still decoded and then encoded from scratch. Your browser reads the WebP and a canvas writes the new one, or ImageMagick does where the canvas can't produce WebP. Transparency stays. An animated file keeps only its first frame, and EXIF, ICC and XMP data are left behind. Pixels move through at 8 bits per channel. No quality value is passed along.

That makes it useful for turning an animation into a still or for stripping metadata from a file you plan to publish. For a lossless rewrite or a quality of your own, use a desktop tool.

### Other ways to convert WebP to WebP

- **cwebp:** run `cwebp -lossless -exact still.webp -o recoded.webp`. cwebp accepts WebP input if the file is static, and -exact preserves RGB values in transparent areas.
- **GIMP:** load the WebP through File > Open, pick File > Export As, give it a different name ending in .webp and click Export. In the WebP dialog you will find Lossless, Image quality, Alpha quality, Save animation and the metadata switches Save Exif data, Save XMP data and Save color profile.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick still.webp -define webp:lossless=true rewritten.webp` to encode the new file without any quality loss.

### Problems with WebP files

- **Older browsers:** some versions show a still WebP but have no animation support.
- **Too large:** WebP stops at 16,383 pixels along either axis, so a bigger picture can't be stored.
- **ImageMagick without WebP:** ImageMagick needs the WEBP delegate library to read WebP.

guide.title: WMA to AIFF: background and alternatives
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMA file?

Windows Media Audio is the name of four codecs: standard, Professional, Lossless and Voice. Microsoft's ASF container holds their data, and a .wma extension tells you the file is audio alone, not other ASF content. The media type usually associated with it is audio/x-ms-wma. Delivery workflows are one use and intermediate audio storage another, and WMA 9 can encode at a variable bit rate. The extension never tells you which of the four codecs is inside.

### Programs that open WMA files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC media player names ASF/WMA among its inputs, with a number of WMA decoders.
- Audacity brings in unprotected WMA only after its optional FFmpeg library has been added.
- FFmpeg decodes WMA 1, WMA 2, Pro, Voice and Lossless in its support matrix.

### WMA and AIFF compared

AIFF is Apple's creation, a wrapper for audio that descends from the IFF family of Electronic Arts. Most often it stores linear PCM without compression; the AIFF-C variant adds compressed audio. Chunks with names exist for the author, a copyright line and annotations. Pro audio users keep masters and intermediate recordings in it, and audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff are common media types.

Here, FFmpeg works in your browser tab and writes audio-only 16-bit big-endian PCM. PCM can't bring back detail a lossy encoder discarded, and it takes more storage than a compressed copy, so a standard WMA becomes an AIFF that is larger but not better. Before converting, check whether your WMA is the Lossless variant, which keeps all its detail, and whether it is copy-protected. Afterwards, play the AIFF from start to end and compare its length with the original.

### Other ways to convert WMA to AIFF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i take.wma -vn -c:a pcm_s16be take.aiff`. The `.aiff` name selects the AIFF format, `-vn` leaves out video and `pcm_s16be` writes 16-bit big-endian samples.
- **Switch Sound File Converter:** click Add and choose the WMA, open the Output Format field and select AIFF, then click Convert.

### Problems with WMA files

- **Protected files:** copy-protected WMA can't be imported through Audacity's FFmpeg library.
- **Audacity offers no WMA import:** WMA import may be missing until the optional FFmpeg component is installed.
- **One WMA opens and another doesn't:** a program may support one WMA codec but lack another, and the extension does not identify the variant.
- **Adobe Audition:** WMA import works on Windows only, with DLMS Format Support enabled.

WMA 9 supports variable bit rate encoding, and audio/x-ms-wma is the media type commonly tied to the format. It serves delivery workflows and sometimes intermediate audio storage.

### Programs that open WMA files

- **Windows:** VLC plays WMA, since it lists ASF input along with a number of Windows Media Audio decoders.
- **Mac:** Audacity opens a WMA that has no DRM, provided you have added its optional FFmpeg library.
- **Linux:** FFmpeg lists five WMA decoders in its support matrix: version 1, version 2, Pro, Voice and Lossless.

### WMA and FLAC compared

FLAC compresses integer PCM audio without discarding samples, and its specification is open (RFC 9639). A lossy WMA is the opposite: it threw detail away to save space. So the FLAC can be larger and sounds no better.

FLAC allows from one to eight channels and bit depths of 4 to 32, and its metadata blocks can hold seek points, pictures and Vorbis comments. The format description became a standard in RFC 9639 in December 2024, and a native stream is labeled audio/flac.

This page decodes the WMA and writes FLAC with the video switched off. It sets neither the sample rate nor the channel count, and it runs entirely on your device.

### Other ways to convert WMA to FLAC

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i song.wma -vn -c:a flac song.flac` does the same job on the command line.
- **Audacity:** once the FFmpeg library is installed, bring the WMA in through File > Import > Audio, then save it from File > Export Audio with FLAC chosen as the Format.

### Problems with WMA files

An app may support one WMA codec but not another, so a file that fails in one player can open in VLC. Protected WMA can't be imported through Audacity's FFmpeg library, so use an unprotected copy. WMA import may be missing from Audacity until you install the optional FFmpeg component. A damaged WMA can still convert, but the FLAC may be shorter than expected.

Microsoft's Windows Media Audio is a family of codecs, kept in the ASF container. The .wma extension separates audio-only files from other ASF content. Variants include standard, Professional, Lossless and Voice, and WMA 9 supports variable bit rate. The usual media type is audio/x-ms-wma. People use it for delivering music and sometimes for intermediate audio storage.

### Programs that open WMA files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- FFmpeg's support matrix covers decoding the WMA 1 and WMA 2 codecs, as well as Pro, Voice and Lossless.

WMA is a codec family, lossy except for the Lossless variant. Apple adopted the M4A extension, used for MPEG-4 files with audio only, for its unprotected music files. Most M4A files contain AAC, a lossy codec defined in MPEG-4 Part 3 that aims for better sound than MP3 at a comparable bitrate. Apple used it for songs sold through iTunes. - **A protected file**: Audacity cannot import protected WMA through its FFmpeg library.

guide.title: About WMA and MP3 files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMA file?

WMA stands for Windows Media Audio, a family of audio codecs developed by Microsoft. The sound sits inside Microsoft's ASF container, and the .wma ending marks an ASF file that holds audio only. The family has four variants: standard WMA, WMA Professional, WMA Lossless and WMA Voice. WMA 9 supports variable bitrate encoding. The media type usually given is audio/x-ms-wma.

WMA serves delivery workflows and is sometimes used to store audio between editing steps. You find WMA files in Windows media libraries and on older portable music players. The extension does not tell you which of the four variants a file uses, which is why an app can open one WMA and refuse another.

### Programs that open WMA files

**Linux, Mac and Windows**

- VLC media player: its feature list names ASF/WMA input and several Windows Media Audio decoders.
- Audacity: imports unprotected WMA once its optional FFmpeg library is installed.
- FFmpeg: decodes WMA 1 and 2 plus the Pro, Voice and Lossless variants, per its support list.

**Windows**

- Windows Media Player: the format's own player, named in the format reference.

### WMA and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .wma with audio/x-ms-wma, against .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **Container**: WMA is held in an ASF container, while an MP3 is audio frames with ID3 tags attached.
- **Compression**: the standard WMA codec is lossy, and WMA Lossless is not. MP3 is always lossy.
- **Ownership**: WMA is a proprietary Microsoft format. MP3 is an ISO/IEC standard (11172-3) from MPEG, developed at Fraunhofer.
- **Bitrate**: WMA 9 supports variable bitrate. MP3 can be constant or variable and runs from 32 to 320 kbps.
- **Metadata**: the title and artist of a WMA sit in its ASF container. The MP3 written here carries them as ID3 tags when FFmpeg finds them.
- **Reach**: MP3 plays in every major browser and on nearly every device.
- **Typical use**: WMA belongs to Windows media libraries and older portable players; MP3 serves music libraries, podcasts and portable players.

MP3 is lossy, and its encoder uses a model of what people can hear to decide which sounds to leave out. This page decodes the WMA with FFmpeg and asks LAME for 192 kbps, which only sources sampled at 32 kHz or higher can reach. A run on a sample WMA decoded the WMA and wrote a new MP3 stream. The sound is first decoded and then encoded again, so the MP3 is a new file and not a repackaged WMA. A lossless WMA therefore ends up lossy, so keep a WMA Lossless original and make the MP3 as a listening copy.

The download is named after the WMA, with .mp3 in place of .wma. A folder's worth of WMA files can go in together; they are processed one by one, which means an album gives one download per track. No size limit or timeout is set.

### Other ways to convert WMA to MP3

- **FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** type `ffmpeg -i input.wma -c:a libmp3lame output.mp3` in a terminal.
- **Audacity with FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** get Audacity's optional FFmpeg library first, open the WMA, choose File > Export Audio and select MP3 in the Format menu. Protected WMA files do not import.

Audacity's MP3 export lets you set the bit rate mode, and in FFmpeg you can pass -b:a with a rate of your choice. This page offers neither.

### Problems with WMA files

- **Audacity cannot import it**: the optional FFmpeg library may be missing, or the file is copy-protected. Install the library or use an unprotected copy.
- **A player opens one WMA but not another**: an app may decode one WMA codec and not another, and the ending hides which variant a file is.
- **A lower bitrate than 192 kbps**: sources at 16 to 24 kHz are held to 160 kbps by LAME, and sources at 8 to 12 kHz to 64 kbps.
- **The file is cut short**: a damaged or truncated WMA usually still converts, to a shorter MP3.
- **Titles or artists are missing**: FFmpeg copies the WMA's global tags, such as title and artist, when it has them. Fill in the rest with a tag editor.
- **Audition will not import it**: Adobe Audition enables WMA import on Windows only, once DLMS Format Support is switched on.
